```text
1	#Requires -Version 7
2	# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1 — merge a managed overlay into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json so claude-hud (statusline HUD), the pyright-lsp
4	# plugin, and a couple of safe defaults deploy on Windows. Companion to the
5	# parent (macOS/Linux) repo's dot_claude/modify_settings.json; that repo uses a
6	# `modify_` + jq merge, which is unreliable on Windows (invariant #5), so we use
7	# the same run_onchange pwsh-merger idiom as the editor overlays instead.
8	#
9	# Why a merge (not a managed dot_claude/settings.json)? Claude Code rewrites
10	# this file at runtime (plugins it installs, permissions the user grants). A
11	# static managed file would clobber all of that on every apply. We instead
12	# recursively deep-merge only our keys in, preserving every live key.
13	#
14	# Gated on installCodingAgents — no Claude Code, nothing to configure. Re-runs
15	# when the embedded overlay (claude/settings-overlay.json) changes.
16	{{ if .installCodingAgents -}}
17	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'   # best-effort; never abort the apply
18	
19	# Embedded at render time from the (chezmoi-ignored) claude/ source, so this
20	# script is self-contained and re-fires when the overlay changes.
21	$overlayJson = @'
22	{{ include "claude/settings-overlay.json" }}
23	'@
24	
25	$overlay = $overlayJson | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable
26	
27	# --- Completion-feedback hooks, gated on `agentSounds` -----------------------
28	#
29	# Built here rather than in claude/settings-overlay.json because that file is
30	# `include`d verbatim and so cannot carry Go-template conditionals.
31	#
32	# `notify` wires notify.ps1 (apprise -> Windows toast); `peon` wires peon-ping's
33	# game voice lines. Values lifted from a real peon-ping install.ps1 (verified
34	# against upstream source, NOT its README — the README's documented command
35	# shape is wrong on the POSIX side too). Windows specifics that differ from the
36	# macOS/Linux parent repo:
37	#   - command is `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File "<peon.ps1>"`
38	#   - `timeout = 10`, and there is NO `async` field
39	#   - the event set includes PreToolUse and has NO UserPromptSubmit
40	# Parent repo equivalent: dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl.
41	{{- $peon   := or (eq .agentSounds "peon")   (eq .agentSounds "both") }}
42	{{- $notify := or (eq .agentSounds "notify") (eq .agentSounds "both") }}
43	$notifyCmd = 'exec pwsh -NoProfile -File "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hooks/notify.ps1"'
44	# peon-ping is installed with `-OpenPeon`, which reroots its whole tree at the
45	# tool-agnostic ~/.openpeon — so peon.ps1 is NOT under ~/.claude/hooks/.
46	# Wrapped in a Test-Path guard so the hook is a silent no-op on a box where the
47	# install hasn't run (or failed): an unguarded `-File <missing>` makes Claude
48	# Code surface a hook error on every event. Mirrors the mandatory
49	# `command -v workmux` / `[ -x ... ]` guards in the parent repo.
50	$peonPs1   = Join-Path $HOME '.openpeon\hooks\peon-ping\peon.ps1'
51	$peonCmd   = "powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command `"if (Test-Path '$peonPs1') { & '$peonPs1' }`""
52	
53	# Event -> the commands that should be wired for the current tier.
54	$soundHooks = @{}
55	{{- if $notify }}
56	foreach ($evt in @('Notification', 'Stop')) {
57	    $soundHooks[$evt] = @(@{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $notifyCmd }) })
58	}
59	{{- end }}
60	{{- if $peon }}
61	foreach ($evt in @('SessionStart', 'SessionEnd', 'SubagentStart', 'Stop',
62	                   'Notification', 'PermissionRequest', 'PreToolUse',
63	                   'PostToolUseFailure', 'PreCompact')) {
64	    $entry = @{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $peonCmd; timeout = 10 }) }
65	    if ($soundHooks.ContainsKey($evt)) { $soundHooks[$evt] = @($soundHooks[$evt] + $entry) }
66	    else                               { $soundHooks[$evt] = @($entry) }
67	}
68	{{- end }}
69	if ($soundHooks.Count -gt 0) {
70	    if ($overlay['hooks'] -isnot [hashtable]) { $overlay['hooks'] = @{} }
71	    foreach ($evt in $soundHooks.Keys) { $overlay['hooks'][$evt] = $soundHooks[$evt] }
72	}
73	
74	# Commands the CURRENT tier disables — pruned from the live file below. Without
75	# this the additive merge makes agentSounds a one-way ratchet: switching
76	# notify -> none would leave notify.ps1 wired forever, so `none` would not
77	# actually silence a machine that previously had sound. Only OUR OWN
78	# fingerprints are listed, so foreign hook entries can never be touched.
79	# (Upstream's own install.ps1 strips `peon\.(ps1|sh)` / `notify\.sh` the same
80	# way before re-adding, so this matches its behaviour.)
81	$prunePatterns = @(
82	{{- if not $notify }}
83	    'notify\.ps1'
84	{{- end }}
85	{{- if not $peon }}
86	    'peon\.ps1'
87	{{- end }}
88	)
89	
90	# Recursive deep-merge: overlay leaves win; live-only keys are preserved. Unlike
91	# the editor overlay's shallow top-level assign, this keeps the user's nested
92	# state (e.g. permissions.allow/deny arrays, other enabledPlugins) intact.
93	#
94	# The `hooks` object gets special, ADDITIVE handling (see Merge-ClaudeHooks) so
95	# our Notification/Stop notify entries are appended without clobbering hook
96	# entries the user or other tools added. Every other array value is still
97	# replaced wholesale (overlay wins), which is what we want for scalars/plugins.
98	function Merge-Hashtable([hashtable]$base, [hashtable]$overlay) {
99	    foreach ($k in $overlay.Keys) {
100	        if ($k -eq 'hooks' -and ($overlay[$k] -is [hashtable])) {
101	            if ($base[$k] -isnot [hashtable]) { $base[$k] = @{} }
102	            Merge-ClaudeHooks $base[$k] $overlay[$k]
103	        }
104	        elseif ($base.ContainsKey($k) -and ($base[$k] -is [hashtable]) -and ($overlay[$k] -is [hashtable])) {
105	            Merge-Hashtable $base[$k] $overlay[$k]
106	        }
107	        else {
108	            $base[$k] = $overlay[$k]
109	        }
110	    }
111	}
112	
113	# Additive per-event hook merge, mirroring the parent repo's jq reduce in
114	# dot_claude/modify_settings.json: for each event, append only the overlay
115	# entries whose .hooks[0].command isn't already present in the live array,
116	# preserving live entries verbatim. Wholesale-replacing the arrays (the old
117	# behavior) would drop hooks the user / other tools add at runtime. @(...) also
118	# forces array shape so ConvertTo-Json emits a JSON array even for a single
119	# entry (Claude requires hooks.<event> to be an array).
120	function Merge-ClaudeHooks([hashtable]$base, [hashtable]$overlay) {
121	    foreach ($evt in $overlay.Keys) {
122	        # NB: plain two-line assign, NOT `$live = if (...) { @(..) } else { @() }`.
123	        # A single-element @() flowing out of an if-EXPRESSION gets unwrapped back
124	        # to a scalar (here a hashtable), so `$live + $additions` then throws
125	        # "A hash table can only be added to another hash table". Direct `= @(...)`
126	        # keeps the array shape.
127	        $live = @()
128	        if ($null -ne $base[$evt]) { $live = @($base[$evt]) }
129	        $liveCmds = @($live | ForEach-Object { $_.hooks[0].command })
130	        $additions = @($overlay[$evt] | Where-Object {
131	            $cmd = $_.hooks[0].command
132	            (-not $cmd) -or ($liveCmds -notcontains $cmd)
133	        })
134	        $base[$evt] = @($live + $additions)
135	    }
136	}
137	
138	# Respect CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (matches the statusLine command + claude-hud setup).
139	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME '.claude' }
140	$settingsPath = Join-Path $claudeDir 'settings.json'
141	
142	$settings = @{}
143	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
144	    $raw = Get-Content -Raw $settingsPath
145	    if ($raw.Trim()) {
146	        try { $settings = $raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable }
147	        catch { Write-Warning "could not parse $settingsPath; not overwriting"; return }
148	    }
149	}
150	
151	Merge-Hashtable $settings $overlay
152	
153	# Prune our own now-disabled entries (see $prunePatterns above). Runs AFTER the
154	# additive merge so a tier that re-enables something wins. Foreign entries are
155	# never matched. Event keys whose array empties out are removed so turning
156	# everything off doesn't leave `"SessionStart": []` litter behind.
157	if ($prunePatterns.Count -gt 0 -and $settings['hooks'] -is [hashtable]) {
158	    foreach ($evt in @($settings['hooks'].Keys)) {
159	        $kept = @(@($settings['hooks'][$evt]) | Where-Object {
160	            $cmd = $_.hooks[0].command
161	            if (-not $cmd) { return $true }
162	            foreach ($p in $prunePatterns) { if ($cmd -match $p) { return $false } }
163	            return $true
164	        })
165	        if ($kept.Count -gt 0) { $settings['hooks'][$evt] = $kept }
166	        else                   { $settings['hooks'].Remove($evt) }
167	    }
168	}
169	
170	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $claudeDir | Out-Null
171	$settings | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12 | Set-Content -Path $settingsPath -Encoding utf8
172	Write-Host "claude overlay -> $settingsPath"
173	{{ end -}}
174
```

1719	# --- specstory `-c` passthrough (why the base command must come from config) ---
1720	#
1721	# specstory's `-c/--command` REPLACES the provider's configured command — it does
1722	# NOT append to it. The shipped config says as much: "Use of these is equivalent
1723	# to -c \"custom command\"" — same slot, last write wins. So a hardcoded
1724	# `-c "claude $args"` silently drops every flag in `claude_cmd` the moment
1725	# claude-copilot has args to pass through, which made these two disagree:
1726	#
1727	#   claude-copilot-once             -> bypass-permissions  (no -c branch)
1728	#   claude-copilot-once --resume X  -> ~/.claude defaultMode "auto"
1729	#
1730	# Deriving the base command from the config keeps specstory the single source of
1731	# truth for BOTH branches. `--no-specstory` deliberately does NOT inherit it.
1732	
1733	# Effective `claude_cmd`, honouring specstory's own precedence:
1734	#   project ./.specstory/cli/config.toml > user ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml > `claude`
1735	# Matches UNCOMMENTED assignments only — both shipped configs carry a commented
1736	# `# claude_cmd = "claude"` example, and matching that would re-introduce the very
1737	# bug this exists to fix. Handles TOML's double- and single-quoted strings.
1738	function script:Get-SpecstoryClaudeCmd {
1739	    foreach ($f in '.specstory/cli/config.toml', (Join-Path $HOME '.specstory/cli/config.toml')) {
1740	        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $f)) { continue }
1741	        foreach ($line in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $f -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
1742	            if ($line -match '^\s*claude_cmd\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|''([^'']*)'')') {
1743	                $v = if ($Matches[1]) { $Matches[1] } else { $Matches[2] }
1744	                if ($v) { return $v }
1745	            }
1746	        }
1747	    }
1748	    'claude'
1749	}

1751	# Single-quote ONE argument for embedding in specstory's `-c` command STRING.
1752	# specstory shell-splits that string honouring quotes, so quoting is both possible
1753	# and necessary — an unquoted join flattens `-p "two words"` into two arguments.
1754	# POSIX escape for an embedded quote: close, \', reopen.
1755	function script:ConvertTo-CopilotShQuote {
1756	    param([string] $Value)
1757	    "'" + ($Value -replace "'", "'\''") + "'"
1758	}

1761	function claude-copilot {
1762	    [CmdletBinding()]
1763	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
1764	    $ss = 'auto'
1765	    if ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -eq '--no-specstory') { $ss = 'never'; $Argv = $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)] }
1766	    elseif ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -eq '--specstory') { $Argv = $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)] }
1767	    elseif ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -in '-h', '--help') {
1768	        Write-Host "Usage: claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [claude args...]"
1769	        Write-Host "  One-off Claude Code session on the Copilot proxy. Sticky: copilot-here on"
1770	        Write-Host "  Runs claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions (hands-off proxy flow)."

1772	    }
1773	    if ($ss -eq 'auto' -and (Get-Command specstory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
1774	        if ($Argv -and $Argv.Count -gt 0) {

1781	        else { copilot-run specstory run claude }

1	# SpecStory Windows-native CLI (track PR #191)
2	
3	**Status**: P? — blocked on upstream (experimental build available)

7	## Context
8	
9	2026-07. `npm i -g @specstory/cli` 404s — SpecStory has **no npm package** and
10	**no native-Windows CLI release**. Official install is macOS Homebrew
11	(`brew tap specstoryai/tap && brew install specstory`); Linux/WSL get GitHub
12	release binaries. The Copilot module (`claude-copilot`, session auto-save)
13	degrades gracefully when `specstory` is absent, so this is nice-to-have, not
14	blocking.
15	
16	## Investigation (upstream status)
17	
18	- **issue #132** — maintainer initially recommended running Claude Code +
19	  SpecStory under **WSL** on Windows; said native Windows CLI wasn't a
20	  near-term roadmap priority (no Windows users on the team) but "not
21	  impossible", later "We are working on this now."
22	- issue #132 was **closed** because the **VS Code extension** (`1.0.0`) added
23	  Windows support for exporting Claude Code sessions — but the comment
24	  explicitly notes **the CLI is still behind**, pointing at PR #191.
25	- **PR #191** — adds a Windows build target, WSL/SSH remote-workspace
26	  discovery, Cursor/Copilot IDE workspace-URI parsing, `--config-dir`,
27	  `--project-path`, `--git-origin`, etc.
28	- PR #191 state (at time of writing): **open, not merged, not draft,
29	  `mergeable=false`**. Large: ~67 commits, 38 files, +3159/−415. Visible
30	  review is mostly Copilot review comments (naming, unused fn, XML stripping);
31	  reviewer request → `belucid`. No confirmed human-maintainer approval.

33	## Routes (which SpecStory path works on Windows today)

35	| Route | Status |
36	|---|---|
37	| VS Code extension — export Claude Code sessions | supported (per issue #132) |
38	| Cursor / VS Code chat-history extension | should work |
39	| Native `specstory.exe` CLI | **PR #191, unmerged / no release** |
40	| SpecStory CLI under WSL + Claude Code | official stopgap |
41	| Self-build PR #191 | experimental (this repo: `just specstory-build`) |
42	
43	## What this repo does now
44	
45	- **Omitted** `@specstory/cli` from the npm install list (it 404s).
46	- Added an **opt-in experimental build** of PR #191, two ways in:

=== claude-copilot ===

    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
    $ss = 'auto'
    if ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -eq '--no-specstory') { $ss = 'never'; $Argv = $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)] }
    elseif ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -eq '--specstory') { $Argv = $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)] }
    elseif ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -in '-h', '--help') {
        Write-Host "Usage: claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [claude args...]"
        Write-Host "  One-off Claude Code session on the Copilot proxy. Sticky: copilot-here on"
        Write-Host "  Runs claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions (hands-off proxy flow)."
        return
    }
    if ($ss -eq 'auto' -and (Get-Command specstory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        if ($Argv -and $Argv.Count -gt 0) {
            # Rebuild what `-c` clobbers: the configured base command (ITS flags left
            # unquoted so specstory splits them normally) + each of our args quoted.
            $cc = Get-SpecstoryClaudeCmd
            foreach ($a in $Argv) { $cc = "$cc $(ConvertTo-CopilotShQuote $a)" }
            copilot-run specstory run claude -c $cc
        }
        else { copilot-run specstory run claude }
    } else {
        # No specstory on PATH (the Windows default - no native CLI yet): run claude
        # directly, still bypassing permission prompts so behaviour matches the
        # specstory path regardless of whether specstory is installed.
        copilot-run claude --dangerously-skip-permissions @Argv
    }

=== copilot-run ===

    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
    if (-not $Argv -or $Argv.Count -eq 0) { Write-Error 'Usage: copilot-run <cmd> [args...]'; return }
    if (-not (Test-CopilotAlive)) { copilot-proxy start; if (-not (Test-CopilotAlive)) { return } }
    if ((Get-CopilotShimEnabled) -and -not (Test-CopilotShimAlive)) { Start-CopilotShim | Out-Null }

    # Single source of truth - see Get-CopilotEnvBlock.
    $inject = Get-CopilotEnvBlock
    # Scope env to the child process: set, run, restore (equivalent to `env VAR=..`).
    $saved = @{}
    foreach ($k in $inject.Keys) { $saved[$k] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable($k); Set-Item "env:$k" $inject[$k] }
    try {
        $exe = $Argv[0]; $rest = if ($Argv.Count -gt 1) { $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)] } else { @() }
        & $exe @rest
    } finally {
        foreach ($k in $inject.Keys) {
            if ($null -eq $saved[$k]) { Remove-Item "env:$k" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
            else { Set-Item "env:$k" $saved[$k] }
        }
    }

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Assessing PowerShell issue**

I'm inspecting a profile line related to potential issues in `claude-copilot`. It seems slicing with one argument may cause problems. In PowerShell, a range of `1..0` can lead to array indexing issues, resulting in null values. If the argument count is one, it appears that the process outputs null plus the given argument. This suggests a failure mode that should be flagged. I also want to be cautious about how single argument arrays bind, as it might lead to unexpected behavior. 

**Identifying failure in precheck**

I'm noticing another failure: `claude-copilot-once` is checking the proxy and doesn't auto-start, even though `claude-copilot/copy run` does. It seems to trigger Test-CopilotAlive before `copilot-here`, which instructs manual start — that’s concerning. The `wasOn` setting only checks valid JSON with the base URL. If the JSON is malformed, it creates an empty object, potentially destroying the original settings. Also, if any stale pin is refreshed and `copilot-here on` fails, it still might write to settings, which could lead to more issues. 

**Exploring SpecStory behavior**

When running `specstory run claude` without any arguments, I notice that SpecStory can resolve its configuration by itself. However, if there are any arguments included, the wrapper takes over and reads the configuration instead. It's interesting how the mode of operation changes based on whether args are present or not! This distinction seems significant, as it could impact how users interact with the tool and how configurations are managed.
</details></think>

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-17 07:25:07Z)**_

Two additional implementation hazards stand out. First, `create_config.toml` is create-once, so an existing user SpecStory config can keep an older/missing `claude_cmd`; a project-level uncommented `claude_cmd` also outranks it and can silently remove the bypass flag. Second, `claude-copilot-once --no-specstory` with no further arguments uses an unsafe PowerShell slice (`[1..0]`), unlike the corrected Codex wrapper, so the consumed control flag may leak back into Claude.

10	# -Force is required because `reload` dot-sources $PROFILE in the same process.
11	# Without it, PowerShell keeps the old module scriptblocks even after chezmoi has
12	# deployed a fixed Copilot.psm1, which made `copilot-proxy auth` repeat the old
13	# ETARGET-only installer until the entire terminal was restarted.
14	Import-Module Copilot -Force -DisableNameChecking -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
15

```text
145	  On a corporate machine, npm may use an internal pull-through mirror because
146	  `registry.npmjs.org` is blocked. npm honours that configured registry; Bun does
147	  not, so `copilot-proxy` prefers npm for its private prefix. Diagnose the mirror
148	  with `npm view <package>@<version> version`, not `npm ping`; the matching
149	  symptom records are `copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module`
150	  and `packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path` under `pitfalls/`.
151	- **Codex native footer** — chezmoi non-destructively merges a provider-neutral
152	  status line (model/reasoning, fast mode, branch, context, tasks, directory)
153	  into `~/.codex/config.toml`. No fork or PATH shim; see
154	  [Codex status line](codex-status-line.md).
155	- **OpenCode Desktop** — GUI companion to the `opencode-ai` CLI, via scoop
156	  (`extras/opencode-desktop`).
157	- **claude-hud** — a statusline HUD that renders below the Claude Code prompt.
158	  Enabled in `~/.claude/settings.json` by a `run_onchange` merger
159	  (`.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl`) that
160	  additively deep-merges an overlay, preserving your live settings. The plugin
161	  self-installs from its marketplace on first launch and runs on the scoop
162	  `bun`/`node` runtime; the merger also enables the `pyright-lsp` plugin and sets
163	  `permissions.defaultMode: auto` + `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`. **Restart
164	  Claude Code** after `chezmoi apply` to see the HUD. See
165	  [running multiple agents](claude-code-agents.md).
166	- **Desktop notifications** — `apprise` (`uv tool install --with pywin32 apprise`)
167	  fires native Windows toasts on Claude Code's **Notification** (needs your
168	  attention) and **Stop** (task finished) events, via a native-pwsh hook
169	  (`~/.claude/hooks/notify.ps1`) the settings overlay wires into `hooks`. Routing
170	  lives in `~/.config/apprise/apprise.yaml` — the `windows://` backend tagged
171	  `desktop`; add your own remote services (Discord/Slack/…) in the create-once
172	  `~/.config/apprise/custom.yaml`. Port of the parent repo's `notify.sh` +
173	  `apprise.yaml`.
174	
175	The official **ChatGPT** desktop app installs via the Microsoft Store (see GUI
176	apps); **Codex** is the `@openai/codex` npm CLI above, not a Store app. SpecStory
177	has no native-Windows CLI package, so it's omitted here — an experimental build
178	from the unmerged PR #191 is opt-in via the **SpecStory build** init prompt
179	(`installSpecstoryBuild`) or `just specstory-build` (needs git + go).
180	
181	## PowerShell modules (PSGallery)
182	
183	- **PSFzf** — fzf key bindings (Ctrl+t files, Ctrl+r history).
184	- **AudioDeviceCmdlets** — absolute volume + mute for the `sysvol`/`sysmute` helpers.
185	
186	## Opt-in dev stacks
```

+#Requires -Version 7
+# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1 — merge a managed overlay into
+# ~/.claude/settings.json so claude-hud (statusline HUD), the pyright-lsp
+# plugin, and a couple of safe defaults deploy on Windows. Companion to the
+# parent (macOS/Linux) repo's dot_claude/modify_settings.json; that repo uses a
+# `modify_` + jq merge, which is unreliable on Windows (invariant #5), so we use
+# the same run_onchange pwsh-merger idiom as the editor overlays instead.
+#
+# Why a merge (not a managed dot_claude/settings.json)? Claude Code rewrites
+# this file at runtime (plugins it installs, permissions the user grants). A
+# static managed file would clobber all of that on every apply. We instead
+# recursively deep-merge only our keys in, preserving every live key.
+#
+# Gated on installCodingAgents — no Claude Code, nothing to configure. Re-runs
+# when the embedded overlay (claude/settings-overlay.json) changes.
+{{ if .installCodingAgents -}}
+$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'   # best-effort; never abort the apply
+
+# Embedded at render time from the (chezmoi-ignored) claude/ source, so this
+# script is self-contained and re-fires when the overlay changes.
+$overlayJson = @'
+{{ include "claude/settings-overlay.json" }}
+'@
+
+$overlay = $overlayJson | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable
+
+# Recursive deep-merge: overlay leaves win; live-only keys are preserved. Unlike
+# the editor overlay's shallow top-level assign, this keeps the user's nested
+# state (e.g. permissions.allow/deny arrays, other enabledPlugins) intact.
+function Merge-Hashtable([hashtable]$base, [hashtable]$overlay) {
+    foreach ($k in $overlay.Keys) {
+        if ($base.ContainsKey($k) -and ($base[$k] -is [hashtable]) -and ($overlay[$k] -is [hashtable])) {
+            Merge-Hashtable $base[$k] $overlay[$k]
+        } else {
+            $base[$k] = $overlay[$k]
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+# Respect CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (matches the statusLine command + claude-hud setup).
+$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME '.claude' }
+$settingsPath = Join-Path $claudeDir 'settings.json'
+
+$settings = @{}
+if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
+    $raw = Get-Content -Raw $settingsPath
+    if ($raw.Trim()) {
+        try { $settings = $raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable }
+        catch { Write-Warning "could not parse $settingsPath; not overwriting"; return }
+    }
+}
+
+Merge-Hashtable $settings $overlay
+New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $claudeDir | Out-Null
+$settings | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12 | Set-Content -Path $settingsPath -Encoding utf8
+Write-Host "claude overlay -> $settingsPath"
+{{ end -}}
diff --git a/claude/settings-overlay.json b/claude/settings-overlay.json
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..67ead06
--- /dev/null
+++ b/claude/settings-overlay.json
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+{
+  "enabledPlugins": {
+    "claude-hud@claude-hud": true,
+    "pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official": true
+  },
+  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
+    "claude-hud": {
+      "source": {
+        "source": "github",
+        "repo": "jarrodwatts/claude-hud"
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true,
+  "permissions": {
+    "defaultMode": "auto"
+  },
+  "statusLine": {
+    "type": "command",
+    "command": "pwsh -NoProfile -Command \"& { $d = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME '.claude' }; $p = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $d 'plugins\\cache\\claude-hud\\claude-hud') -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match '^\\d+(\\.\\d+)+$' } | Sort-Object { [version]$_.Name } -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).FullName; if (-not $p) { return }; $rt = Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($rt) { & $rt.Source '--env-file' 'NUL' (Join-Path $p 'src\\index.ts'); return }; $rt = Get-Command node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($rt) { & $rt.Source (Join-Path $p 'dist\\index.js') } }\""
+  }
+}

Author: Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>

    feat(claude): agentSounds prompt + peon-ping voice lines (Windows)
    
    Windows counterpart of the cross-platform repo's agentSounds work. Completion
    feedback was unconditional (notify.ps1 -> apprise -> Windows toast, wired from
    the static claude/settings-overlay.json); now it is a four-tier prompt:
    
      none    nothing
      notify  notify.ps1 -> toast          (default on workstation; none on minimal)
      peon    peon-ping voice lines        (sc2_scv -> "Job's finished!")
      both    toast + voice
    
    Gates HOOK WIRING ONLY — the peon CLI installs alongside the coding agents
    regardless, so `peon preview` / `peon packs list` are always available. peon's
    own volume/pack/notification style live in ~/.openpeon/config.json and are NOT
    chezmoi-managed, so tweaking them produces no drift; the installer seeds the
    pack once (guarded on peon.ps1 existing).
    
    The hook entries had to move OUT of claude/settings-overlay.json and into the
    run_onchange: that JSON is `include`d verbatim and cannot carry the
    Go-template conditionals the tiers need. Non-hook keys (statusLine, plugins,
    permissions) stay in the JSON.
    
    Values were lifted from upstream's install.ps1 source, NOT its README — the
    README's documented command shape is already known-wrong on the POSIX side.
    Three things genuinely differ from macOS/Linux and would have been wrong if
    ported by assumption:
    
    - The Windows event set registers PreToolUse and has NO UserPromptSubmit —
      the reverse of POSIX. Both are 9 events.
    - Entries carry `timeout = 10` and no `async` field.
    - With -OpenPeon the tree is rerooted to ~/.openpeon, so peon.ps1 is at
      ~/.openpeon/hooks/peon-ping/peon.ps1 — NOT under ~/.claude. An early draft
      pointed the hook at ~/.claude and would have silently no-opped.
    
    Also: the PowerShell installer's param block has no -NoRc (that is the bash
    install.sh flag) and does not touch $PROFILE, so -OpenPeon alone is enough to
    keep both ~/.claude/settings.json and our profile untouched.
    
    The hook command is wrapped in a Test-Path guard; an unguarded `-File <missing>`
    makes Claude Code surface a hook error on every event on a box where the
    install has not run. Same role as the parent repo's `command -v workmux` guard.
    
    Adds the same narrow prune as the parent repo: entries matching our own
    fingerprints (notify\.ps1, peon\.ps1) are removed when the tier disables them,
    otherwise agentSounds is a one-way ratchet and `none` never silences a machine
    that previously had sound. Foreign entries are untouchable. Upstream's own
    install.ps1 strips the same two fingerprints before re-adding.
    
    Verified on macOS: all four tiers render; all five rendered scripts parse via
    the PowerShell AST parser; and the merge/prune was EXECUTED under pwsh against
    fixtures — at `none` both of ours are pruned while CodeIsland/herdr entries and
    user keys survive; at `peon` all 9 events wire, notify is pruned, hook shape
    matches upstream. mkdocs --strict clean.
    
    NOT verified (needs a Windows host): the peon-ping install itself, toast/voice
    actually firing, and $env:TEMP behaviour. Documented as such in
    docs/agent-sounds.md.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit f7a73eb2d07418d93af0928e15dfc91bc7ff5f16
Author: freyazh <50571823+freyazh@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Sun Jul 12 19:35:18 2026 +0800

    fix(claude): make claude-hud statusLine survive cygwin/msys bash (#6)
    
    The overlay shipped a `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "…"` statusLine. When Claude
    Code invokes the statusline through cygwin/msys bash (OSTYPE=cygwin), bash
    pre-expands the `$` tokens inside the double-quoted pwsh argument before pwsh
    runs — `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` becomes `:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and `$d`/`$p`/`$rt`
    collapse to empty. pwsh then receives a broken script and emits nothing, so the
    HUD renders blank with no error (same class as claude-hud #531).
    
    Replace it with a bash-native command (nothing for bash to mangle): compute
    COLUMNS, select the latest installed version dir via `sort -V`, resolve node
    from PATH, and exec `dist/index.js`.
    
    Trade-off: assumes the statusline is invoked by bash. If a context runs it under
    native cmd/pwsh (no bash), the pwsh form would be needed instead; there is no
    clean single-line command that survives both. On this Windows box Claude Code
    consistently invokes via cygwin bash, so bash-native is correct here.
    
    Fixes #5
    
    Co-authored-by: hanruzhou <hanruzhou+odspmdb@microsoft.com>
    Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

    a chezmoi-ignored overlay source (claude/settings-overlay.json) + a gated
    run_onchange pwsh merger that recursively deep-merges into ~/.claude/settings.json,
    preserving Claude Code's runtime-managed state (plugins, permissions, hooks).
    
    - Overlay: claude-hud + pyright-lsp plugins, claude-hud marketplace,
      permissions.defaultMode=auto, skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt, and a
      Windows-pwsh statusLine (dynamic bun->node detection; the parent's `bash -c`
      form won't run under pwsh). Self-no-ops until the plugin/runtime exist.
    - Gated on the existing installCodingAgents toggle -> no new init prompt.
    - backup: snapshot ~/.claude/settings.json, and fix a pre-existing collision
      where Code/Cursor (and now .claude) settings.json all backed up to the same
      leaf name, silently losing backups -- now mirrors the target path.
    - Docs: claude-hud bullet in tools.md + zh-TW twin; Config surfaces in AGENTS.md.

The native build path has a concrete defect: the apply-time installer fetches `'pull\191\head:pr-191'` with backslashes, while the manual script correctly uses `pull/191/head`. Because native exit codes are not checked and installer errors are nonfatal, the apply-time path may continue after failed fetch/checkout, build the wrong checkout, accept a stale pre-existing executable as success, and then never retry on an unchanged apply.

426	        if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $ssRepo '.git'))) {

436	            Push-Location (Join-Path $ssRepo 'specstory-cli')
437	            try { Info "specstory: go build -> $ssOut"; go build -o $ssOut . } finally { Pop-Location }
438	            if (Test-Path $ssOut) { Info "specstory: built $ssOut" }
439	            else { Register-Failure 'specstory-build (go build produced no binary)' }
440	        } finally { Pop-Location }
441	    } catch {
442	        Write-Warning "specstory-build error: $_"
443	        Register-Failure 'specstory-build'
444	    }

## Launcher failure modes

### Project config can remove the bypass flag

An uncommented project assignment has highest precedence:

```toml
claude_cmd = "claude"
```

That would make the SpecStory path run without bypass, despite the global seed. The checked-in project config does not currently do this because its line is commented.

### Existing create-once global config can be stale

Because `create_config.toml` only seeds absent files, an older global config without the flag survives indefinitely.

### `--no-specstory` single-argument slicing bug

The code uses:

```powershell
$Argv = $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)]
```

at `Copilot.psm1:1765-1766`.

For a one-element array, PowerShell evaluates `1..0` and the consumed flag remains in the result. A read-only shell check confirmed:

```text
["--no-specstory"]
```

Thus:

```powershell
claude-copilot-once --no-specstory
```

can leak `--no-specstory` into the underlying Claude invocation. The Codex wrapper already avoids this pattern by using `Select-Object -Skip 1` at `Copilot.psm1:1639-1641`.

There is no test invoking these wrapper-control cases.

### `--specstory` does not force installation

It only removes the leading token and leaves `$ss = 'auto'`. If `Get-Command specstory` fails, execution still falls back to direct Claude.

### Malformed `.claude/settings.local.json` may be destroyed

- `claude-copilot-once` treats parse failure as “not pinned”: `Copilot.psm1:1803-1805`.
- `copilot-here on` catches invalid JSON and replaces it with an empty object: line `1880`.
- It writes the replacement at line `1889`.
- The one-shot cleanup can then remove the temporary proxy-only file at lines `1909-1914`.

So an invalid pre-existing local settings file can be overwritten or deleted rather than preserved.

# 3. claude-hud `statusLine` generation and merge

## Overlay source

The overlay enables:

- `claude-hud@claude-hud`;
- `pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official`;
- the GitHub marketplace `jarrodwatts/claude-hud`;
- dangerous-mode prompt suppression;
- `permissions.defaultMode = auto`;
- command-backed `statusLine`.

Evidence:

- `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\claude\settings-overlay.json:2-20`

The exact status-line command at line 20 is:

```sh
cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size </dev/tty 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -1d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); exec "$(command -v node)" "${plugin_dir}dist/index.js"
```

It:

1. Uses existing numeric `COLUMNS`, otherwise asks `stty`.
2. Falls back to 120 columns.
3. Subtracts four columns for the HUD.
4. Selects the newest matching plugin cache directory.
5. Executes `dist/index.js` with `node`.

## Why it is POSIX shell on Windows

The repository records that these Claude command strings run under Claude’s Cygwin/MSYS bash:

- `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\.claude\plans\apprise-windows-https-appriseit-com-ser-zany-island.md:128-132`

The git history also records that an earlier `pwsh -Command` version rendered blank because bash expanded its `$` tokens before PowerShell received them. The current POSIX command intentionally assumes Claude’s MSYS/Cygwin shell.

## Overlay embedding and gate

The merger is:

`C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\.chezmoiscripts\run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl`

- Entire script is gated on `installCodingAgents`: lines `14-17`.
- Overlay JSON is embedded at render time: lines `19-25`.
- Therefore a change to `claude/settings-overlay.json` changes the rendered run-onchange script and makes chezmoi rerun it.

`claude/` itself is excluded from direct deployment:

- `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\.chezmoiignore:32-40`

It is an input to the merger, not a target directory.

## Target settings path

The merger honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; otherwise it uses `~/.claude`:

- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl:138-140`

It writes `<claudeDir>/settings.json`.

## Merge semantics

General deep merge:

- lines `90-111`

Rules:

- Overlay scalar leaves win.
- Existing live-only keys survive.
- Nested hashtables are recursively merged.
- `enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`, `permissions`, and `statusLine` therefore preserve unrelated nested keys.
- Arrays outside hooks are replaced wholesale by overlay arrays: lines `94-97`.

Hooks have special additive behavior:

- lines `113-136`

This preserves foreign hooks and avoids adding duplicate commands. Sound-related entries owned by this repository are then selectively pruned based on the `agentSounds` tier:

- lines `153-168`

## Read/write behavior

- Existing JSON is loaded at lines `142-149`.
- Invalid nonempty JSON emits a warning and returns without overwriting: lines `143-148`.
- Merge runs at line `151`.
- Directory creation and JSON rewrite occur at lines `170-172`.

The rewrite serializes the entire resulting object with `ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12`, so values are preserved semantically, but formatting/property ordering are not preserved.

## Plugin installation timing

Documentation says:

- the plugin self-installs from its marketplace on first Claude launch;
- Node/Bun are installed by the repo;
- Claude must be restarted after apply.

Evidence:

- `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\docs\tools.md:157-165`

Node and Bun are baseline Scoop packages, independent of the coding-agent toggle:

- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl:233-243`

## Backup

Before the first apply, when `backupMode != off`, the run-once backup includes `~/.claude/settings.json`:

- `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\.chezmoiscripts\run_once_before_01_backup.ps1.tmpl:1-8`
- target: line `17`
- timestamped path-preserving copy: lines `31-45`

This is only a first/run-once safety net, not a backup before every overlay rewrite.

## HUD failure modes

1. **`installCodingAgents` off:** no merge occurs. Turning it off later also does not remove previously merged HUD/plugin keys.
2. **Claude not restarted:** plugin self-install may not have occurred yet.
3. **Plugin cache absent:** `plugin_dir` becomes empty and the command attempts `node dist/index.js` rather than explicitly no-oping.
4. **Marketplace/network/plugin installation failure:** settings can show the plugin enabled while no usable cache exists.
5. **Node unavailable in Claude’s command environment:** `command -v node` returns empty and the status line fails.
6. **Different command shell:** the command assumes Cygwin/MSYS bash. Native cmd or PowerShell cannot interpret it.
7. **Different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` between apply and runtime:** the merger can update one config root while the running Claude process searches another.
8. **Malformed settings JSON:** the merger safely declines to overwrite, but because this is a successful-returning run-onchange script, an unchanged apply may not retry after the JSON is repaired.
9. **Non-atomic write:** `Set-Content` rewrites the whole file directly; interruption can leave malformed JSON.
10. **Managed conflicts are intentional:** a user’s existing `statusLine.type`, `statusLine.command`, plugin enablement, `permissions.defaultMode`, or matching marketplace fields are overwritten by overlay values.

Failures are nonfatal and an unchanged apply will not rerun the installer:

## Permission flags and settings

### Present

  `Copilot.psm1:1786`

### Absent

There is **no `--permission-mode` command-line flag** in `Copilot.psm1`.

`permissions.defaultMode = "auto"` is settings JSON, not part of the invocation. `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt` suppresses Claude’s dangerous-mode acknowledgement prompt; it does not itself activate dangerous mode.

## Launcher failure modes

### Project config can remove the bypass flag

An uncommented project assignment has highest precedence:

```toml
claude_cmd = "claude"
```

That would make the SpecStory path run without bypass, despite the global seed. The checked-in project config does not currently do this because its line is commented.

### Existing create-once global config can be stale

Because `create_config.toml` only seeds absent files, an older global config without the flag survives indefinitely.

### `--no-specstory` single-argument slicing bug

The code uses:

```powershell
$Argv = $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)]
```

at `Copilot.psm1:1765-1766`.

For a one-element array, PowerShell evaluates `1..0` and the consumed flag remains in the result. A read-only shell check confirmed:

```text
["--no-specstory"]
```

Thus:

```powershell
claude-copilot-once --no-specstory
```

can leak `--no-specstory` into the underlying Claude invocation. The Codex wrapper already avoids this pattern by using `Select-Object -Skip 1` at `Copilot.psm1:1639-1641`.

There is no test invoking these wrapper-control cases.

### `--specstory` does not force installation

It only removes the leading token and leaves `$ss = 'auto'`. If `Get-Command specstory` fails, execution still falls back to direct Claude.

### Malformed `.claude/settings.local.json` may be destroyed

- `claude-copilot-once` treats parse failure as “not pinned”: `Copilot.psm1:1803-1805`.
- `copilot-here on` catches invalid JSON and replaces it with an empty object: line `1880`.
- It writes the replacement at line `1889`.
- The one-shot cleanup can then remove the temporary proxy-only file at lines `1909-1914`.

So an invalid pre-existing local settings file can be overwritten or deleted rather than preserved.

# 3. claude-hud `statusLine` generation and merge

## Overlay source

The overlay enables:

- `claude-hud@claude-hud`;
- `pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official`;
- the GitHub marketplace `jarrodwatts/claude-hud`;
- dangerous-mode prompt suppression;
- `permissions.defaultMode = auto`;
- command-backed `statusLine`.

Evidence:

- `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\claude\settings-overlay.json:2-20`

The exact status-line command at line 20 is:

```sh
cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size &lt;/dev/tty 2&gt;/dev/null | awk '{print $2}');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols &gt; 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -1d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2&gt;/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); exec "$(command -v node)" "${plugin_dir}dist/index.js"
```

It:

1. Uses existing numeric `COLUMNS`, otherwise asks `stty`.
2. Falls back to 120 columns.
3. Subtracts four columns for the HUD.
4. Selects the newest matching plugin cache directory.
5. Executes `dist/index.js` with `node`.

## Why it is POSIX shell on Windows

The repository records that these Claude command strings run under Claude’s Cygwin/MSYS bash:

- `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\.claude\plans\apprise-windows-https-appriseit-com-ser-zany-island.md:128-132`

The git history also records that an earlier `pwsh -Command` version rendered blank because bash expanded its `$` tokens before PowerShell received them. The current POSIX command intentionally assumes Claude’s MSYS/Cygwin shell.

`C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\.chezmoiscripts\run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl`

## Merge semantics

General deep merge:

- lines `90-111`

Rules:

- Overlay scalar leaves win.
- Existing live-only keys survive.
- Nested hashtables are recursively merged.
- `enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`, `permissions`, and `statusLine` therefore preserve unrelated nested keys.
- Arrays outside hooks are replaced wholesale by overlay arrays: lines `94-97`.

Hooks have special additive behavior:

- lines `113-136`

This preserves foreign hooks and avoids adding duplicate commands. Sound-related entries owned by this repository are then selectively pruned based on the `agentSounds` tier:

- lines `153-168`

## Read/write behavior

- Existing JSON is loaded at lines `142-149`.
- Invalid nonempty JSON emits a warning and returns without overwriting: lines `143-148`.
- Merge runs at line `151`.
- Directory creation and JSON rewrite occur at lines `170-172`.

The rewrite serializes the entire resulting object with `ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12`, so values are preserved semantically, but formatting/property ordering are not preserved.

## Backup

Before the first apply, when `backupMode != off`, the run-once backup includes `~/.claude/settings.json`:

- `C:\Users\hanruzhou\.local\share\chezmoi\.chezmoiscripts\run_once_before_01_backup.ps1.tmpl:1-8`
- target: line `17`

This is only a first/run-once safety net, not a backup before every overlay rewrite.

## HUD failure modes

1. **`installCodingAgents` off:** no merge occurs. Turning it off later also does not remove previously merged HUD/plugin keys.
2. **Claude not restarted:** plugin self-install may not have occurred yet.
3. **Plugin cache absent:** `plugin_dir` becomes empty and the command attempts `node dist/index.js` rather than explicitly no-oping.
4. **Marketplace/network/plugin installation failure:** settings can show the plugin enabled while no usable cache exists.
5. **Node unavailable in Claude’s command environment:** `command -v node` returns empty and the status line fails.
6. **Different command shell:** the command assumes Cygwin/MSYS bash. Native cmd or PowerShell cannot interpret it.
7. **Different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` between apply and runtime:** the merger can update one config root while the running Claude process searches another.
8. **Malformed settings JSON:** the merger safely declines to overwrite, but because this is a successful-returning run-onchange script, an unchanged apply may not retry after the JSON is repaired.
9. **Non-atomic write:** `Set-Content` rewrites the whole file directly; interruption can leave malformed JSON.
10. **Managed conflicts are intentional:** a user’s existing `statusLine.type`, `statusLine.command`, plugin enablement, `permissions.defaultMode`, or matching marketplace fields are overwritten by overlay values.

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers — `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here — it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) — only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two — don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation — either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying — write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` — it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025–2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing — the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) — see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) — copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials — stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` → Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

### Language-Specific Feature Support

Every SDK language above supports both the beta Tool Runner and Managed Agents (beta) — Python (`@beta_tool` decorator), TypeScript (`betaZodTool` + Zod), Java (annotated classes), Go (`BetaToolRunner` in the `toolrunner` pkg), Ruby (`BaseTool` + `tool_runner`), C# (`BetaToolRunner` + raw JSON schema), PHP (`BetaRunnableTool` + `toolRunner()`); code entry points are in the Tool Use Patterns quick reference below. cURL is raw HTTP (no SDK features) and supports Managed Agents.

> **Managed Agents code examples**: see the reading guide in the `## Managed Agents (Beta)` section below.

## Which Surface Should I Use?

> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases — only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.

| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** — scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |

> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute — file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice — use the tool runner for the agentic loop — its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) — or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.

> **Cloud-provider access.** **Claude Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity — see `shared/claude-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Claude Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` — that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.

### Building an Agent: Four Approaches

Once you've decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Claude Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* — you still host and deploy them yourself — which is why they're easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.

| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |
|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | **Claude API — manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop — no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner's per-turn hooks don't fit |
| 2 | **Claude API — Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, error interception, result modification (e.g. `cache_control`), retries, streaming, and compaction |
| 3 | **Managed Agents** (REST, beta) | Agent config + your tool results | Anthropic supplies the harness **and** hosts a per-session sandbox (**harness + deployment**) | Anthropic-hosted sandbox (bash, files, code exec) + Skills/MCP + your tools | You want Anthropic to run the loop *and* host the per-session workspace; persisted/versioned configs; long-running sessions |
| 4 | **Claude Agent SDK** — *separate product* (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) | A prompt + options | SDK supplies the Claude Code harness + built-in tools (**harness only**); you host | Built-in Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch + MCP + subagents | You want a batteries-included coding/filesystem agent running on your own infra |

The harness/deployment split is the key mental model: options 1, 2, and 4 all **leave deployment to you**; only option 3 (CMA) adds managed deployment. Options 1–3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs — see the disambiguation below.

> **Tool Runner ≠ Claude Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:
> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. It automates the request → execute → loop cycle *for tools you define*. No built-in tools, no filesystem access, no sandbox — you supply every tool and host the compute. It is option 2 above, a thin helper over `POST /v1/messages`.
> - **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) is Claude Code packaged as a library. It ships built-in tools (file read/write/edit, bash, grep, web search), the full agent loop, context management, hooks, subagents, permissions, and sessions. You call `query(prompt, options)` and it drives everything.
>
> Both are **harness-only — you host and deploy them.** The difference is scope of harness: the Tool Runner loops over tools *you* define (with per-turn hooks for approval, interception, result modification, and retries — but no built-in tools); the Agent SDK is the full Claude Code harness with built-in tools. Neither provides managed deployment — that's what **Managed Agents (CMA)** adds (Anthropic hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox).
>
> **This skill covers the Claude API and Managed Agents (options 1–3); it does not generate Claude Agent SDK code.** If the user actually wants the Claude Agent SDK, point them to its docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk`) — don't substitute the API Tool Runner for it, or vice-versa.

### Should I Build an Agent?

Before choosing the agent tier, check all four criteria:

- **Complexity** — Is the task multi-step and hard to fully specify in advance? (e.g., "turn this design doc into a PR" vs. "extract the title from this PDF")
- **Value** — Does the outcome justify higher cost and latency?
- **Viability** — Is Claude capable at this task type?
- **Cost of error** — Can errors be caught and recovered from? (tests, review, rollback)

If the answer is "no" to any of these, stay at a simpler tier (single call or workflow).

---

## Architecture

Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint — not separate APIs.

**User-defined tools** — You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.

**Server-side tools** — Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.

**Structured outputs** — Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and/or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.

**Supporting endpoints** — Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` — see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` — live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.

### Claude Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`) — most capable widely released model

Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's most capable widely released model, for the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work; everything below also applies to **Claude Mythos 5** (`claude-mythos-5`, Project Glasswing — same capabilities, pricing, and API surface; successor to the invitation-only `claude-mythos-preview`). 1M context window (the maximum is also the default), 128K max output. Key API differences from Opus-tier — see `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Fable 5 for details:

- **Thinking is always on** — omit the `thinking` parameter entirely (or send `{type: "adaptive"}`). Any other explicit configuration is rejected: `{type: "disabled"}` and `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` both return a 400. Control depth with `output_config.effort` (supports `low` through `xhigh` and `max`).
- **The raw chain of thought is never returned** — responses carry regular `thinking` blocks (not `redacted_thinking`): `display: "summarized"` returns a readable summary, `"omitted"` (the default) leaves the `thinking` field as an empty string. Replay rules: pass thinking blocks back unchanged on the same model; other models drop them silently (unbilled — nothing to strip); details in `shared/model-migration.md`.
- **Tokenizer** — same tokenizer as Opus 4.8 (introduced with Opus 4.7). Token counts are roughly unchanged when migrating from Opus 4.7/4.8; per-token pricing differs. Coming from Opus 4.6, Sonnet, Haiku, or older, re-baseline with `count_tokens` (the Opus 4.7 tokenizer uses ~1×–1.35× as many tokens).
- **`refusal` stop reason — handle it, and opt into fallbacks by default** — safety classifiers may decline a request (HTTP 200, `stop_reason: "refusal"`, with a `stop_details` category); always check `stop_reason` before reading `content`. **When you write `claude-fable-5` or `claude-opus-5` code, include the server-side `fallbacks` parameter by default.** Simplest form: `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"]` + `fallbacks: "default"`, which routes by refusal category so you never maintain a model list. (The older array form — `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-06-01"]` + `fallbacks: [{"model": "claude-opus-4-8"}]` — still works; Claude API only — everywhere else, incl. Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry, use the SDKs' client-side `BetaRefusalFallbackMiddleware` + `BetaFallbackState`). Tell the user you've enabled it; drop it only if they decline. Full semantics (billing, mid-stream refusals, credit repricing) in `shared/model-migration.md` → refusal section. **Per-language code examples in `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` § Refusal Fallbacks cover the array form only** — for the `"default"` mode, follow the raw-HTTP shape in `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Opus 5 → New API features and swap `fallbacks: [{...}]` for `fallbacks: "default"` plus the `-2026-07-01` header; the rest of the request is unchanged.
- **No assistant prefill** — same as the rest of the 4.6+ family.
- **30-day data retention required** — Claude Fable 5 is not available under zero data retention; requests from an org whose retention configuration doesn't meet the requirement return `400 invalid_request_error`.
- **Longer turns, different prompting** — single requests on hard tasks can run many minutes (plan timeouts/streaming/progress UX); effort sweeps should include low/medium for routine work; prompts written for prior models are often too prescriptive and reduce output quality. See `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Fable 5 → Behavioral shifts (prompt-tunable) for the recommended prompt snippets.

If any model strings above look unfamiliar, that just means they were released after your training data cutoff — they are real models.

**Live capability lookup:** The table above is cached. When the user asks "what's the context window for X", "does X support vision/thinking/effort", or "which models support Y", query the Models API (`client.models.retrieve(id)` / `client.models.list()`) — see `shared/models.md` for the field reference and capability-filter examples.

## Authentication (Quick Reference)

**An unset `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` does NOT mean there are no credentials.** The SDKs and the `ant` CLI resolve credentials in this order (first match wins): `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` → the `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`-selected or active OAuth profile from `ant auth login` → Workload Identity Federation env vars → the default profile on disk. A bare `Anthropic()` / `new Anthropic()` / `anthropic.NewClient()` works after `ant auth login` with no env var set.

**When you need to call the API and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset, don't ask the user for a key.** First run `ant auth status` — it shows which credential source and profile is active. If it reports an active profile:

- **SDK code or `ant` CLI:** just run it. The zero-arg client constructor and every `ant …` subcommand pick up the profile automatically — no env var needed.
- **Raw `curl` / HTTP:** get a short-lived token with `ant auth print-credentials --access-token` and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` **plus** the header `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` (OAuth tokens go on `Authorization: Bearer`, not `x-api-key:` — converting a curl from an API key is a header change, not a key swap). Always pass `--access-token`; the no-flag form prints JSON, not a bare token.

Only ask the user for a key if `ant auth status` reports no active credential source (or `ant` itself isn't installed). Suggest `ant auth login` as the first option — it stores a profile under `~/.config/anthropic/` that the SDKs read automatically — and an exported `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as the alternative.

Full auth details (named profiles, scopes, the API-key-shadows-profile trap, refresh-token expiry): `shared/anthropic-cli.md`.

## Thinking & Effort (Quick Reference)

Use adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) on every current model — Claude dynamically decides when and how much to think. Per-model rules:

| Model | Thinking config | Omitting `thinking` | `budget_tokens` | Sampling (`temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k`) | Effort levels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fable 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` or omit; explicit `{type: "disabled"}` returns 400 — omit the param instead | Runs adaptive (thinking is always on) | Removed — `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` returns 400 | Removed — 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Claude Opus 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` or omit; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted **only at effort `high` or below** — 400 at `xhigh`/`max`, and see the disabled-thinking pitfall below | Runs **adaptive** (thinking is on by default — unlike Opus 4.8/4.7) | Removed — 400 | Removed — 400 | `low`–`max` (all five) |
| Opus 4.8 / 4.7 | `{type: "adaptive"}` is the only on-mode; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted | Runs **without** thinking — set `{type: "adaptive"}` explicitly | Removed — 400 | Removed — 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Sonnet 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` is the only on-mode; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted | Runs adaptive | Removed — 400 | Removed — 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 | `{type: "adaptive"}` (recommended; auto-enables interleaved thinking, no beta header) | Set `{type: "adaptive"}` explicitly | Deprecated — do not use in new code; transitional escape hatch only (see below) | Allowed | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`max` (`xhigh` arrived with Opus 4.7) |
| Older (Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, …) — only if explicitly requested | `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | No thinking | Required for thinking; must be less than `max_tokens`, minimum 1024 — errors otherwise | Allowed | `effort` works on Opus 4.5 (`low`/`medium`/`high` only — no `xhigh`/`max`); errors on Sonnet 4.5 / Haiku 4.5 |

Opus 4.8 keeps the same request surface as 4.7 (no new breaking changes) — see `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Opus 4.8 for the behavioral re-tuning, and → Migrating to Opus 4.7 for the full breaking-change list when coming from 4.6 or earlier. With `thinking` disabled, Opus 4.8 may write longer reasoning into the visible response — leave adaptive thinking on, or add a final-answer-only instruction (see the migration guide).

- **Effort (GA, no beta header):** `output_config: {effort: "low"|"medium"|"high"|"xhigh"|"max"}` — inside `output_config`, not top-level; default `high` (equivalent to omitting it). Controls thinking depth and overall token spend; combine with adaptive thinking for the best cost-quality tradeoffs. `xhigh` (added on Opus 4.7, between `high` and `max`) is the best setting for most coding and agentic use cases on Fable 5 / Opus 4.7/4.8 / Sonnet 5, and the default in Claude Code; effort matters more on those models than on any prior model in their tier — re-tune it when migrating, and run long-horizon/agentic tasks at `high`/`xhigh` with the full task spec given up front. Use a minimum of `high` for intelligence-sensitive work, `max` when correctness matters more than cost, and `low` for subagents or simple tasks — lower effort means fewer and more-consolidated tool calls, less preamble, and terser confirmations (`high` is often the sweet spot balancing quality and token efficiency).
- **Thinking display — `"omitted"` by default on Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7 / Sonnet 5:** `display: "summarized"` returns a readable summary of the reasoning; `"omitted"` (the default on all six — a silent change from Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, where it was `"summarized"`) streams `thinking` blocks with empty text. `display` controls visibility only — thinking happens and is billed the same under every setting; the raw chain of thought is never exposed on any model. If you stream reasoning to users, the default looks like a long pause before output — set `thinking: {type: "adaptive", display: "summarized"}` explicitly. (Independent of display, echo thinking blocks back unchanged when continuing on the same model; other models silently ignore them — see the migration guide.)
- **When the user asks for "extended thinking", a "thinking budget", or `budget_tokens`:** always use Fable 5, Opus 5, 4.8, 4.7, or 4.6 with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` — the fixed thinking-token-budget concept is deprecated and adaptive thinking replaces it. Do NOT use `budget_tokens` for new 4.6/4.7/4.8 code and do NOT switch to an older model just because the user mentions it. *Gradual-migration carve-out:* `budget_tokens` is still functional on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 only, as a transitional escape hatch for existing code that needs a hard token ceiling before you've tuned `effort` — see `shared/model-migration.md` → Transitional escape hatch. It is fully removed on Fable 5, Opus 5/4.7/4.8, and Sonnet 5.

## Compaction (Quick Reference)

**Beta, Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6.** For long-running conversations that may exceed the 1M context window, enable server-side compaction. The API automatically summarizes earlier context when it approaches the trigger threshold (default: 150K tokens). Requires beta header `compact-2026-01-12`.

**Critical:** Append `response.content` (not just the text) back to your messages on every turn. Compaction blocks in the response must be preserved — the API uses them to replace the compacted history on the next request. Extracting only the text string and appending that will silently lose the compaction state.

See `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` (Compaction section) for code examples. Full docs via WebFetch in `shared/live-sources.md`.

---

## Prompt Caching (Quick Reference)

**Prefix match.** Any byte change anywhere in the prefix invalidates everything after it. Render order is `tools` → `system` → `messages`. Keep stable content first (frozen system prompt, deterministic tool list), put volatile content (timestamps, per-request IDs, varying questions) after the last `cache_control` breakpoint.

**Mid-conversation operator instructions** (Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5; not Claude Sonnet 5; no beta header): append `{"role": "system", ...}` to `messages[]` instead of editing top-level `system`. Preserves the cached history prefix and is the prompt-injection-safe operator channel. See `shared/prompt-caching.md` § Mid-conversation system messages.

**Top-level auto-caching** (`cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}` on `messages.create()`) is the simplest option when you don't need fine-grained placement. Max 4 breakpoints per request. Minimum cacheable prefix is ~1024 tokens — shorter prefixes silently won't cache.

**Verify with `usage.cache_read_input_tokens`** — if it's zero across repeated requests, a silent invalidator is at work (`datetime.now()` in system prompt, unsorted JSON, varying tool set).

For placement patterns, architectural guidance, and the silent-invalidator audit checklist: read `shared/prompt-caching.md`. Language-specific syntax: `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` (Prompt Caching section).

## Fast Mode (Quick Reference)

**Research preview, Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 only** — Claude API and Managed Agents, not Bedrock / Google Cloud / Foundry. Opus 4.7 fast mode has been removed: `speed: "fast"` on 4.7 returns an error. Fast mode on Claude Opus 5 is priced at $10 / $50 per MTok. Fast mode runs the same model at up to 2.5x higher output tokens per second, at premium pricing. Three things are required on every request: use the **beta** messages endpoint (`client.beta.messages.…`), pass the beta flag `fast-mode-2026-02-01`, and set `speed: "fast"` as a top-level request parameter (not a header, not in `extra_body`).

```python
client.beta.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5", max_tokens=4096,
    speed="fast", betas=["fast-mode-2026-02-01"],
    messages=[...],
)
```

| Language | Beta flag | Speed parameter |
|---|---|---|
| Python | `betas=["fast-mode-2026-02-01"]` | `speed="fast"` |
| TypeScript / Ruby | `betas: ["fast-mode-2026-02-01"]` | `speed: "fast"` |
| Go | `[]anthropic.AnthropicBeta{anthropic.AnthropicBetaFastMode2026_02_01}` | `Speed: anthropic.BetaMessageNewParamsSpeedFast` |
| Java | `.addBeta(AnthropicBeta.FAST_MODE_2026_02_01)` | `.speed(MessageCreateParams.Speed.FAST)` |
| C# | `Betas = ["fast-mode-2026-02-01"]` | `Speed = Speed.Fast` (`Anthropic.Models.Beta.Messages`) |
| PHP | `betas: ['fast-mode-2026-02-01']` | `speed: 'fast'` |
| cURL | `anthropic-beta: fast-mode-2026-02-01` header | `"speed": "fast"` in body |

`response.usage.speed` reports which speed was used. Fast mode has its own rate limit separate from standard Opus; on 429, either retry after the `retry-after` delay or drop `speed` and fall back to standard (note: switching speed invalidates prompt cache). Not available with Batch API, Priority Tier, Claude Platform on AWS, or third-party platforms.

**Priority Tier does not cover Claude Opus 5.** It is supported on every other current model, including Claude Fable 5 and Opus 4.8, but Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Mythos 5, and Mythos Preview are excluded — a Priority Tier request naming one of them fails validation.

## Task Budgets (Quick Reference)

**Beta, Claude Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7.** A task budget gives Claude a token ceiling for an agentic loop so it paces itself and finishes gracefully instead of being cut off — distinct from `max_tokens`, which is an enforced per-response ceiling the model is not aware of. Minimum `total`: 20,000. Set `task_budget` inside `output_config` on `client.beta.messages.stream(...)` with beta flag `task-budgets-2026-03-13` — use streaming so the large `max_tokens` doesn't hit HTTP timeouts (full details: `shared/model-migration.md` → Task Budgets):

```python
with client.beta.messages.stream(
    model="claude-opus-5", max_tokens=128000,
    output_config={"effort": "high", "task_budget": {"type": "tokens", "total": 64000}},
    betas=["task-budgets-2026-03-13"],
    messages=[...], tools=[...],
) as stream:
    response = stream.get_final_message()
```

`task_budget` fields: `type` (always `"tokens"`), `total`, and optional `remaining` (defaults to `total`). The server injects a countdown marker Claude sees during generation; the budget counts what Claude generates and the tool results it reads this turn — **not** the full history you resend each request. Not the same thing as **Managed Agents session budgets** — those are hard, dollar-denominated, platform-enforced caps on one CMA session (`shared/managed-agents-core.md` § Session budgets); a task budget is advisory and token-denominated.

**Observing spend:** accumulate `response.usage.output_tokens` (plus the token count of the tool-result blocks you append) across loop iterations if you want to display progress. Leave `remaining` unset in the normal loop — the server tracks the countdown itself, and passing a client-computed `remaining` while also resending full history under-reports the budget. **Only pass `remaining`** when you compact or rewrite history between requests and the server can no longer derive prior spend.
