+    "command": "cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case \"$cols\" in \"\"|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size </dev/tty 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}');; esac; case \"$cols\" in \"\"|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -1d \"${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}\"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); exec \"$(command -v node)\" \"${plugin_dir}dist/index.js\""
   }

29	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
30	$cache = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache") -Directory | ForEach-Object { Test-Path (Join-Path $_.FullName "claude-hud") }) -contains $true
31	$registry = (Get-Content (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\installed_plugins.json") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -match "claude-hud"
32	$temp = Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache\temp_local_*") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
33	Write-Host "Cache: $cache | Registry: $registry | Temp: $($temp.Count) files"
34	```
35	
36	### Interpreting Results
37	
38	| Cache | Registry | Meaning | Action |
39	|-------|----------|---------|--------|
40	| YES | YES | Normal install (may still be broken) | Continue to Step 1 |
41	| YES | NO | Ghost install - cache orphaned | Clean up cache |
42	| NO | YES | Ghost install - registry stale | Clean up registry |
43	| NO | NO | Not installed | Continue to Step 1 |
44	
45	If **temp files exist**, a previous install was interrupted. Clean them up.
46	
47	### Cleanup Commands
48	
49	If ghost installation detected, ask user if they want to reset. If yes:
50	
51	**macOS/Linux**:
52	```bash
53	CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
54	
55	# Remove orphaned cache (handles both direct and marketplace installs)
56	rm -rf "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/cache"/*/claude-hud
57	
58	# Remove temp files from failed installs
59	rm -rf "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/cache/temp_local_"*
60	
61	# Reset registry (removes ALL plugins - warn user first!)
62	# Only run if user confirms they have no other plugins they want to keep:
63	echo '{"version": 2, "plugins": {}}' > "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/installed_plugins.json"
64	```
65	
66	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
67	```powershell
68	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
69	
70	# Remove orphaned cache (handles both direct and marketplace installs)
71	Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache") -Directory | ForEach-Object { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Join-Path $_.FullName "claude-hud") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
72	
73	# Remove temp files
74	Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache\temp_local_*") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
75	
76	# Reset registry (removes ALL plugins - warn user first!)
77	'{"version": 2, "plugins": {}}' | Set-Content (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\installed_plugins.json")
78	```
79	
80	After cleanup, tell user to run `/plugin install claude-hud` again followed by `/reload-plugins` — no restart needed. (Restart Claude Code only if the reinstall still misbehaves; the fresh session re-reads the plugin registry from scratch.)
81	
82	### Linux: Cross-Device Filesystem Check
83	
84	**On Linux only**, if install fails with `EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted`, check whether `/tmp` and home are on different filesystems:
85	```bash
86	[ "$(df --output=source ~ /tmp 2>/dev/null | tail -2 | uniq | wc -l)" = "2" ] && echo "CROSS_DEVICE"
87	```
88	
89	The underlying Claude Code bug ([#14799](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/14799)) has been fixed, so this mostly affects older Claude Code versions — suggest updating Claude Code first. If updating isn't an option and the check outputs `CROSS_DEVICE`, the workaround is:
90	```bash
91	mkdir -p ~/.cache/tmp && TMPDIR=~/.cache/tmp claude /plugin install claude-hud
92	```
93	
94	---
95	
96	## Step 1: Detect Platform, Shell, and Runtime
97	
98	**IMPORTANT**: Use the environment context values (`Platform:` and `Shell:`) as your starting point. On `win32`, also check `$OSTYPE` via the Bash tool. Some Windows sessions report `Shell: powershell` while the command path exposed to Claude Code is Git Bash/MSYS2. When `$OSTYPE` is `msys` or `cygwin`, the PowerShell command format can fail before PowerShell runs because bash expands `$env:VAR`, `$p`, and `$(...)` expressions first (see [#531](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/531)).
99	
100	**On `win32`, run this check first:**
101	```bash
102	echo $OSTYPE
103	```
104	
105	| Platform | Shell | OSTYPE | Command Format |
106	|----------|-------|--------|----------------|
107	| `darwin` | any | any | bash (macOS instructions) |
108	| `linux` | any | any | bash (Linux instructions) |
109	| `win32` | `bash` | any | bash — Windows + Git Bash instructions |
110	| `win32` | `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd` | `msys` or `cygwin` | bash — Windows + Git Bash instructions (the active command environment is MSYS/Cygwin; PowerShell syntax is unsafe here) |
111	| `win32` | `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd` | other / empty | PowerShell — Windows + PowerShell instructions |
112	
113	---
114	
115	**macOS/Linux** (Platform: `darwin` or `linux`):
116	
117	1. Get plugin path (sorted by dotted numeric version, not modification time):
118	   ```bash
119	   ls -d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | awk -F/ '{ print $(NF-1) "\t" $(0) }' | grep -E '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]' | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4n | tail -1 | cut -f2-
120	   ```
121	   If empty, the plugin is not installed. Go back to Step 0 to check for ghost installation or EXDEV issues. If Step 0 was clean, ask the user to install via `/plugin install claude-hud` first.
122	
123	2. Get runtime absolute path:
124	   - On `darwin` or `linux`, prefer bun for performance and fall back to node:
125	     ```bash
126	     command -v bun 2>/dev/null || command -v node 2>/dev/null
127	     ```
128	   - On `win32` + `bash`, require node. Do not fall back to bun on Windows:
129	     ```bash
130	     command -v node 2>/dev/null
131	     ```
132	
133	   If empty, stop setup and explain that the current shell cannot find the required runtime.
134	   - On **Windows + Git Bash/MSYS2**, explicitly explain that the current Git Bash session could not find Node.js, even if Claude Code itself is installed.
135	   - If `winget` is available, recommend:
136	     ```bash
137	     winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS
138	     ```
139	   - On Windows, ask the user to install Node.js LTS from https://nodejs.org/
140	   - On macOS/Linux, ask the user to install one of these:
141	     - Node.js LTS from https://nodejs.org/
142	     - Bun from https://bun.sh/
143	   - After installation, ask the user to restart their shell and re-run `/claude-hud:setup`.
144	
145	3. Verify the runtime exists:
146	   ```bash
147	   ls -la {RUNTIME_PATH}
148	   ```
149	   If it doesn't exist, re-detect or ask user to verify their installation.
150	
151	4. Determine source file based on runtime:
152	   - On `darwin` or `linux`, use `src/index.ts` when the runtime is bun. Otherwise use `dist/index.js`.
153	   - On Windows, always use `dist/index.js`.
154	
155	5. Generate command (quotes around runtime path handle spaces):
156	
157	   The command exports `COLUMNS` so the HUD knows the real terminal width.
158	   Claude Code pipes the subprocess stdout, so `process.stdout.columns` is
159	   unavailable at runtime. Since Claude Code v2.1.153, `COLUMNS` and `LINES`
160	   are set natively to the current terminal dimensions before the statusLine
161	   command runs, so the inherited `COLUMNS` value is the primary source. The
162	   `stty size </dev/tty` probe and the 120 fallback remain for older Claude
163	   Code versions where `COLUMNS` may be absent. The `- 4` accounts for Claude
164	   Code's input area padding (2 columns on each side).
165	
166	   The grep pattern uses `[[:space:]]` rather than `\t` to match the tab
167	   separator emitted by awk. GNU grep (BRE/ERE) does **not** interpret
168	   `\t` as a tab character — it emits `warning: stray \ before t` and
169	   treats the pattern as literal `t`, so the regex never matches the awk
170	   output and `plugin_dir` resolves to an empty string. The runtime then
171	   exits with `Module not found "src/index.ts"` and no HUD appears.
172	   Setup verification can hide this because some shells alias `grep` to
173	   alternatives (e.g. `ugrep`) that *do* expand `\t`, while the actual
174	   `statusLine` subprocess invokes `/usr/bin/grep`. `[[:space:]]` is a
175	   POSIX character class supported by both BSD grep (macOS default) and
176	   GNU grep (Linux default).
177	
178	   **When runtime is bun** - add `--env-file /dev/null` to prevent Bun from auto-loading project `.env` files:
179	   ```
180	   bash -c 'cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '"'"'{print $2}'"'"');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | awk -F/ '"'"'{ print $(NF-1) "\t" $(0) }'"'"' | grep -E '"'"'^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]'"'"' | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4n | tail -1 | cut -f2-); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" --env-file /dev/null "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"'
181	   ```
182	
183	   **When runtime is node**:
184	   ```
185	   bash -c 'cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '"'"'{print $2}'"'"');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | awk -F/ '"'"'{ print $(NF-1) "\t" $(0) }'"'"' | grep -E '"'"'^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]'"'"' | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4n | tail -1 | cut -f2-); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"'
186	   ```
187	
188	**Windows + Git Bash** (Platform: `win32`, Shell: `bash`):
189	
190	Do not use PowerShell commands when the shell is bash. Claude Code invokes statusLine commands through bash, which will interpret PowerShell variables like `$env` and `$p` before PowerShell ever sees them.
191	
192	On Windows require `node` and always use `dist/index.js`.
193	
194	**Important**: Do **not** reuse the macOS/Linux awk-based command on Windows + Git Bash. The `awk` fragment requires `'"'"'` quoting to nest single quotes inside `bash -c '...'`. After JSON encoding and decoding, this quoting breaks on Windows Git Bash, causing a silent syntax error that prevents the HUD process from starting (see [#326](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/326)).
195	
196	Instead, use `sort -V` (GNU version sort, included with Git for Windows) which avoids nested single quotes entirely. Also avoid wrapping the generated command in a second `bash -c ...` layer. Claude Code is already invoking the statusline through bash, so the direct shell command lets `exec` replace that shell instead of spawning an extra bash wrapper first. The command still exports `COLUMNS` so the HUD receives the real terminal width, and it uses the marketplace-aware cache glob:
197	
198	   ```
199	   cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '{print $2}');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -1d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"
200	   ```
201	
202	**Windows + PowerShell** (Platform: `win32`, Shell: `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd`, OSTYPE: other/empty):
203	
204	> **Before proceeding**: if `echo $OSTYPE` returned `msys` or `cygwin`, use the **Windows + Git Bash** instructions above. In that environment, bash can expand PowerShell variables before PowerShell runs.
205	
206	1. Get plugin path:
207	   ```powershell
208	   $claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
209	   (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache\*\claude-hud\*") -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match '^\d+(\.\d+)+$' } | Sort-Object { [version]$_.Name } -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).FullName
210	   ```
211	   The trailing `\*` on the cache glob is required. Without it, `Get-ChildItem` returns the `claude-hud` directory itself, whose name does not match the `^\d+(\.\d+)+$` version pattern, so the lookup resolves to `$null` and any subsequent `Join-Path` throws (see [#521](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/521)).
212	
213	   If empty or errors, the plugin is not installed. Ask the user to install via marketplace first.
214	
215	2. Get runtime absolute path (require node on Windows):
216	   ```powershell
217	   if (Get-Command node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { (Get-Command node).Source } else { Write-Error "Node.js not found" }
218	   ```
219	
220	   If node is not found, stop setup and explain that the current PowerShell session cannot find Node.js.
221	   - If `winget` is available, recommend:
222	     ```powershell
223	     winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS
224	     ```
225	   - Otherwise ask the user to install Node.js LTS, then restart PowerShell and re-run `/claude-hud:setup`.
226	   - On Windows, do not offer Bun for statusLine setup. Use Node.js only.
227	
228	3. Use `dist\index.js`.
229	
230	4. Write the Windows statusline launcher.
231	
232	   Windows PowerShell startup plus `Get-ChildItem | Sort-Object [version]` can exceed Claude Code's render cadence on every statusLine refresh. Write a small Node launcher once during setup, then invoke it through `cmd.exe` on each refresh. The launcher uses the setup-time validated `node.exe`, preserves update discovery by finding the latest installed `claude-hud` version, and prefers inherited `COLUMNS` before falling back to 120.
233	
234	   The launcher file at `$claudeDir/plugins/claude-hud/statusline.mjs` should contain:
235	
236	   ```js
237	   import fs from 'node:fs';
238	   import os from 'node:os';
239	   import path from 'node:path';
240	   import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
241	
242	   const envColumns = Number.parseInt(process.env.COLUMNS ?? '', 10);
243	   const width = Number.isFinite(envColumns) && envColumns > 0 ? envColumns : 120;
244	   process.env.COLUMNS = String(Math.max(1, width - 4));
245	
246	   const claudeDir = process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude');
247	   const cacheDir = path.join(claudeDir, 'plugins', 'cache');
248	
249	   function versionParts(value) {
250	     const match = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+].*)?$/.exec(value);
251	     return match ? match.slice(1, 4).map(Number) : null;
252	   }
253	
254	   function compareVersions(a, b) {
255	     for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {
256	       if (a[i] !== b[i]) return a[i] - b[i];
257	     }
258	     return 0;
259	   }
260	
261	   const candidates = [];
262	   try {
263	     for (const marketplace of fs.readdirSync(cacheDir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
264	       if (!marketplace.isDirectory()) continue;
265	       const pluginRoot = path.join(cacheDir, marketplace.name, 'claude-hud');
266	       let versions = [];
267	       try {
268	         versions = fs.readdirSync(pluginRoot, { withFileTypes: true });
269	       } catch {
270	         continue;
271	       }
272	       for (const version of versions) {
273	         if (!version.isDirectory()) continue;
274	         const parts = versionParts(version.name);
275	         if (!parts) continue;
276	         const dir = path.join(pluginRoot, version.name);
277	         if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'dist', 'index.js'))) {
278	           candidates.push({ dir, parts });
279	         }
280	       }
281	     }
282	   } catch {
283	     process.exit(0);
284	   }
285	
286	   candidates.sort((a, b) => compareVersions(a.parts, b.parts));
287	   const latest = candidates.at(-1);
288	   if (!latest) process.exit(0);
289	
290	   const hud = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(latest.dir, 'dist', 'index.js')).href);
291	   if (typeof hud.main === 'function') {
292	     await hud.main();
293	   }
294	   ```
295	
296	   Write it using `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` with `New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false` so the file is UTF-8 without a BOM:
297	
298	   ```powershell
299	   $wrapperDir = Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\claude-hud"
300	   New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $wrapperDir | Out-Null
301	   $wrapperPath = Join-Path $wrapperDir "statusline.mjs"
302	   $wrapperBody = @'
303	   import fs from 'node:fs';
304	   import os from 'node:os';
305	   import path from 'node:path';
306	   import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
307	
308	   const envColumns = Number.parseInt(process.env.COLUMNS ?? '', 10);
309	   const width = Number.isFinite(envColumns) && envColumns > 0 ? envColumns : 120;
310	   process.env.COLUMNS = String(Math.max(1, width - 4));
311	
312	   const claudeDir = process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude');
313	   const cacheDir = path.join(claudeDir, 'plugins', 'cache');
314	
315	   function versionParts(value) {
316	     const match = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+].*)?$/.exec(value);
317	     return match ? match.slice(1, 4).map(Number) : null;
318	   }
319	
320	   function compareVersions(a, b) {
321	     for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {
322	       if (a[i] !== b[i]) return a[i] - b[i];
323	     }
324	     return 0;
325	   }
326	
327	   const candidates = [];
328	   try {
329	     for (const marketplace of fs.readdirSync(cacheDir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
330	       if (!marketplace.isDirectory()) continue;
331	       const pluginRoot = path.join(cacheDir, marketplace.name, 'claude-hud');
332	       let versions = [];
333	       try {
334	         versions = fs.readdirSync(pluginRoot, { withFileTypes: true });
335	       } catch {
336	         continue;
337	       }
338	       for (const version of versions) {
339	         if (!version.isDirectory()) continue;
340	         const parts = versionParts(version.name);
341	         if (!parts) continue;
342	         const dir = path.join(pluginRoot, version.name);
343	         if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'dist', 'index.js'))) {
344	           candidates.push({ dir, parts });
345	         }
346	       }
347	     }
348	   } catch {
349	     process.exit(0);
350	   }
351	
352	   candidates.sort((a, b) => compareVersions(a.parts, b.parts));
353	   const latest = candidates.at(-1);
354	   if (!latest) process.exit(0);
355	
356	   const hud = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(latest.dir, 'dist', 'index.js')).href);
357	   if (typeof hud.main === 'function') {
358	     await hud.main();
359	   }
360	   '@
361	   [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($wrapperPath, $wrapperBody, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
362	   ```
363	
364	   `$runtimePath` is the value detected in step 2 (the absolute path returned by `(Get-Command node).Source`, typically `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`). `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` on Windows PowerShell 5.1 both emit a UTF-8 BOM. `WriteAllText` + `UTF8Encoding $false` writes without a BOM in both PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+.
365	
366	5. Generate command:
367	
368	   ```
369	   {CMD_PATH} /d /s /c ""{RUNTIME_PATH}" "{WRAPPER_PATH}""
370	   ```
371	
372	   `{CMD_PATH}` is the absolute `cmd.exe` path, preferably `$env:SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe`. `{WRAPPER_PATH}` is the value of `$wrapperPath` from step 4 (typically `C:\Users\<user>\.claude\plugins\claude-hud\statusline.mjs`). If you build the string in PowerShell, use:
373	
374	   ```powershell
375	   $cmdPath = Join-Path $env:SystemRoot "System32\cmd.exe"
376	   if (-not (Test-Path $cmdPath)) { $cmdPath = "cmd.exe" }
377	   $generatedCommand = $cmdPath + ' /d /s /c ""' + $runtimePath + '" "' + $wrapperPath + '""'
378	   ```
379	
380	**WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux)**: If running in WSL, use the macOS/Linux instructions. Ensure the plugin is installed in the Linux environment (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/plugins/...`), not the Windows side.
381	
382	## Step 2: Test Command
383	
384	Run the generated command. It should produce output (the HUD lines) within a few seconds.
385	
386	- If it errors, do not proceed to Step 3.
387	- If it hangs for more than a few seconds, cancel and debug.
388	- This test catches issues like broken runtime binaries, missing plugins, or path problems.
389	
390	## Step 2.5: Detect Existing Statusline and Create Backup
391	
392	Before writing to `settings.json`, check whether a `statusLine` key already exists and protect the user's current configuration. This covers the existing-statusLine overwrite issue tracked in [#547](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/547).
393	
394	### 2.5.1: Read the existing statusLine
395	
396	**macOS/Linux**:
397	```bash
398	SETTINGS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
399	EXISTING_COMMAND=""
400	EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW=""
401	
402	if [ -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
403	  EXISTING_COMMAND=$("{RUNTIME_PATH}" -e '
404	const fs = require("fs");
405	const settingsPath = process.argv[1];
406	
407	try {
408	  const text = fs.readFileSync(settingsPath, "utf8");
409	  if (text.trim() === "") process.exit(0);
410	
411	  const json = JSON.parse(text);
412	  const command = json && json.statusLine && typeof json.statusLine.command === "string"
413	    ? json.statusLine.command
414	    : "";
415	  process.stdout.write(command);
416	} catch (error) {
417	  console.error("Unable to read statusLine.command from settings.json: " + error.message);
418	  process.exit(1);
419	}
420	' "$SETTINGS") || exit 1
421	
422	  EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING_COMMAND" | "{RUNTIME_PATH}" -e '
423	let value = "";
424	process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8");
425	process.stdin.on("data", chunk => { value += chunk; });
426	process.stdin.on("end", () => {
427	  const redacted = value
428	    .replace(/\b(Bearer)\s+["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "$1 [REDACTED]")
429	    .replace(/\b(Authorization\s*:\s*)["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "$1[REDACTED]")
430	    .replace(/\b(token|api[_-]?key|secret|password|pass|auth)(=|:)\s*["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "$1$2[REDACTED]")
431	    .replace(/\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b/g, "sk-[REDACTED]")
432	    .replace(/\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,}\b/g, "[GITHUB_TOKEN_REDACTED]")
433	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
434	    .trim();
435	
436	  process.stdout.write(redacted.length > 160 ? redacted.slice(0, 157) + "..." : redacted);
437	});
438	')
439	fi
440	```
441	
442	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
443	```powershell
444	$settingsPath = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { Join-Path $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR "settings.json" } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude\settings.json" }
445	$existingCommand = ""
446	$existingCommandPreview = ""
447	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
448	  try {
449	    $json = Get-Content $settingsPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
450	    if ($json.statusLine -and $json.statusLine.command) {
451	      $existingCommand = $json.statusLine.command
452	    }

489	**Always** create a backup of `settings.json` before modifying it, regardless of whether a statusline exists. This protects against corruption (see [#315]) and gives users a recovery path.
490	
491	**macOS/Linux**:
492	```bash
493	SETTINGS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
494	BACKUP_TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

497	  BACKUP_PATH="${SETTINGS}.bak.${BACKUP_TIMESTAMP}"
498	  if cp "$SETTINGS" "$BACKUP_PATH"; then
499	    echo "Backup created: $BACKUP_PATH"
500	  else
501	    echo "Failed to create backup at: $BACKUP_PATH" >&2
502	    exit 1
503	  fi
504	fi
505	```

507	**Windows (PowerShell)**:

512	  $backupPath = "${settingsPath}.bak.${timestamp}"

514	  Write-Host "Backup created: $backupPath"

596	- **Platform `darwin` or `linux`, or Platform `win32` + Shell `bash`**: `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json`

604	```json

608	    "command": "{GENERATED_COMMAND}"
609	  }

613	**JSON safety**: Write `settings.json` with a real JSON serializer or editor API, not manual string concatenation.
614	If you must inspect the saved JSON manually, the embedded bash command must preserve escaped backslashes inside the awk fragment.
615	For example, the saved JSON should contain `\\$(NF-1)` and `\\$0`, not `\$(NF-1)` and `\$0`.
616	
617	**Windows PowerShell 5.1 BOM**: on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the default shell on Windows 10/11), `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` emit a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`). RFC 8259 §8.1 forbids BOM in JSON. PowerShell 7+ added `-Encoding utf8NoBOM`, but PS 5.1 did not. Use `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` with `New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false` to write UTF-8 without a BOM from both PS versions:
618	
619	```powershell
620	[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $json, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
621	```
622	
623	Verify the first bytes are `7B 0D 0A` (`{` + CRLF) or `7B 0A` (`{` + LF), not `EF BB BF`:
624	
625	```powershell
626	[System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($path)[0..2]
627	```

677	### Step 4.5: Auto-Refresh (Optional)
678	
679	Claude Code only re-runs the statusline after an interaction (a new assistant message, `/compact` finishing, a permission-mode change, or a vim-mode toggle). Time-based HUD data — session duration, usage reset countdowns, the prompt-cache countdown — therefore goes stale between messages. Claude Code supports an optional `refreshInterval` key (seconds, minimum 1) on the `statusLine` settings object that re-runs the command every N seconds.
680	
681	Of those, only the usage reset countdown is shown by default — session duration and the prompt-cache countdown tick only if the user enabled them (e.g. "Session info" in Step 4, or via config). Mention this if the user seems unsure whether the timer is worth it.
682	
683	Ask with AskUserQuestion:
684	- header: "Auto-refresh"
685	- question: "Re-run the HUD on a timer so time-based info (session duration, usage countdowns) stays current between messages?"
686	- options:
687	  - "Every 5 seconds (Recommended)" — Keeps countdowns fresh with negligible overhead
688	  - "Every 1 second" — Smoothest ticking; re-runs the HUD command far more often
689	  - "No timer" — HUD updates only after interactions (Claude Code's default)
690	
691	**If the user picks an interval**, merge `refreshInterval: <N>` into the **existing** `statusLine` object in `settings.json` — preserve `type`, `command`, and any other keys. Follow the same rules as Step 3: real JSON serializer, no BOM on Windows, retry once on a concurrent-modification error. Do not re-create the backup; the Step 2.5.3 backup already covers this session.
692	
693	**If the user picks "Other" and gives a numeric interval** (e.g. "10" or "10 seconds"), use that value, clamped to a minimum of 1. Treat a non-numeric "Other" answer that declines (skip/none/no) like "No timer".
694	
695	**If the user picks "No timer"**, do not write the key. If a `refreshInterval` key already exists in `statusLine` from a previous run and the user explicitly chose "No timer", remove it.
696	
697	`refreshInterval` lives in `settings.json`, which Claude Code reloads automatically — ticking should start after the user's next interaction. If countdowns don't tick in the current session, tell the user it will take effect after a Claude Code restart; do not treat a non-ticking timer as a setup failure in Step 5.
698	
699	Each refresh re-runs the full HUD command (runtime startup, transcript parse, git status), so 5 seconds is the recommended default; only suggest 1 second when the user wants visibly smooth countdowns.
700

731	
732	   **"command not found" or empty output**:
733	   - Runtime path might be wrong: `ls -la {RUNTIME_PATH}`
734	   - On macOS with mise/nvm/asdf: the absolute path may have changed after a runtime update
735	   - Symlinks may be stale: `command -v node` often returns a symlink that can break after version updates

363	
364	### For New Users (Flow A):
365	1. Apply chosen preset as base
366	2. Apply chosen language
367	3. Apply Turn Off selections (set those items to OFF)
368	4. Apply Turn On selections (set those items to ON)
369	5. Apply chosen layout
370	
371	### For Returning Users (Flow B):
372	1. Start from current config
373	2. Apply Turn Off selections (set to OFF, including usageBarEnabled if selected)
374	3. Apply Turn On selections (set to ON, including usageBarEnabled if selected)
375	4. Apply Git Style selection (if shown)
376	5. If "Reset to [preset]" selected, override with preset values
377	6. If layout change selected, apply it
378	7. If language change selected, apply it

1	# Claude HUD
2	
3	A Claude Code plugin that shows what's happening — context usage, active tools, running agents, and todo progress. Always visible below your input.
4	
5	[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/jarrodwatts/claude-hud?v=2)](LICENSE)
6	[![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/jarrodwatts/claude-hud)](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/stargazers)

8	![Claude HUD in action](claude-hud-preview-5-2.png)
9	
10	> 🌐 English | [中文文档](README.zh.md)
11	
12	## Install
13	
14	Inside a Claude Code instance, run the following commands:
15	
16	**Step 1: Add the marketplace**
17	```
18	/plugin marketplace add jarrodwatts/claude-hud
19	```
20	
21	**Step 2: Install the plugin**
22	
23	<details>
24	<summary><strong>⚠️ Linux users: Click here if install fails with an EXDEV error</strong></summary>
25	
26	On older Claude Code versions, `/tmp` being a separate filesystem (tmpfs) caused plugin installation to fail with:
27	```
28	EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted
29	```
30	
31	This [Claude Code bug](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/14799) has since been fixed — if you hit it, update Claude Code first. If you can't update, set TMPDIR before installing:
32	```bash
33	mkdir -p ~/.cache/tmp && TMPDIR=~/.cache/tmp claude
34	```
35	
36	Then run the install command below in that session.
37	
38	</details>
39	
40	```
41	/plugin install claude-hud
42	```
43	
44	After that, reload plugins (no restart needed):
45	
46	```
47	/reload-plugins
48	```
49	
50	<details>
51	<summary><strong>Prefer the terminal?</strong></summary>
52	
53	Steps 1–2 can also be done outside a session with the Claude Code CLI:
54	```bash
55	claude plugin marketplace add jarrodwatts/claude-hud
56	claude plugin install claude-hud@claude-hud
57	```
58	Then run `/reload-plugins` inside your session (or start a new one).
59	
60	</details>
61	
62	**Step 3: Configure the statusline**
63	```
64	/claude-hud:setup
65	```
66	
67	<details>
68	<summary><strong>⚠️ Windows users: Click here if setup says no JavaScript runtime was found</strong></summary>
69	
70	On Windows, Node.js LTS is the supported runtime for Claude HUD setup. If setup says no JavaScript runtime was found, install Node.js for your shell first:
71	```powershell

74	Then restart your shell and run `/claude-hud:setup` again.

76	</details>

78	Done! Claude Code reloads settings automatically — the HUD appears after your next message, no restart needed. If it doesn't show up, restart Claude Code (older versions require a restart to pick up statusLine changes).

80	---
81	
82	## What is Claude HUD?
83	
84	Claude HUD gives you better insights into what's happening in your Claude Code session.
85	
86	| What You See | Why It Matters |
87	|--------------|----------------|
88	| **Project path** | Know which project you're in (configurable 1-3 directory levels) |
89	| **Context health** | Know exactly how full your context window is before it's too late |
90	| **Tool activity** | Watch Claude read, edit, and search files as it happens |
91	| **Agent tracking** | See which subagents are running and what they're doing |
92	| **Todo progress** | Track task completion in real-time |
93	
94	## What You See
95	
96	### Default (2 lines)
97	```
98	[Opus] │ my-project git:(main*)
99	Context █████░░░░░ 45% │ Usage ██░░░░░░░░ 25% (1h 30m / 5h)
100	```
101	- **Line 1** — Model, provider label when positively identified (for example `Bedrock`, `Vertex`, `MiniMax`), project path, git branch
102	- **Line 2** — Context bar (green → yellow → red) and usage rate limits
103	
104	### Optional lines (enable via `/claude-hud:configure`)
105	```
106	◐ Edit: auth.ts | ✓ Read ×3 | ✓ Grep ×2        ← Tools activity
107	◐ explore [haiku]: Finding auth code (2m 15s)    ← Agent status
108	▸ Fix authentication bug (2/5)                   ← Todo progress
109	```
110	
111	---
112	
113	## How It Works
114	
115	Claude HUD uses Claude Code's native **statusline API** — no separate window, no tmux required, works in any terminal.
116	
117	```
118	Claude Code → stdin JSON → claude-hud → stdout → displayed in your terminal
119	           ↘ transcript JSONL (tools, agents, todos)
120	```
121	
122	**Key features:**
123	- Native token data from Claude Code (not estimated)
124	- Scales with Claude Code's reported context window size, including newer 1M-context sessions
125	- Parses the transcript for tool/agent activity
126	- Re-renders after each interaction (new assistant messages, `/compact`, permission changes, vim-mode toggles), debounced at 300ms
127	
128	---
129	
130	## Configuration
131	
132	Customize your HUD anytime:
133	
134	```
135	/claude-hud:configure
136	```
137	
138	The guided flow handles layout, language, and common display toggles. Advanced overrides such as
139	custom colors and thresholds are preserved there, but you set them by editing the config file directly:
140	
141	- **First time setup**: Choose a preset (Full/Essential/Minimal), pick a label language, then fine-tune individual elements
142	- **Customize anytime**: Toggle items on/off, adjust git display style, switch layouts, or change label language
143	- **Preview before saving**: See exactly how your HUD will look before committing changes
144	
145	### Presets
146	
147	| Preset | What's Shown |
148	|--------|--------------|
149	| **Full** | Everything enabled — tools, agents, todos, git, usage, duration |
150	| **Essential** | Activity lines + git status, minimal info clutter |
151	| **Minimal** | Core only — just model name and context bar |
152	
153	After choosing a preset, you can turn individual elements on or off.
154	
155	### Manual Configuration
156	
157	Edit `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json` directly for advanced settings such as `colors.*`,
158	`pathLevels`, `maxWidth`, threshold overrides, `display.timeFormat`, and `display.promptCacheTtlSeconds`. Running `/claude-hud:configure`
159	preserves those manual settings while still letting you change `language`, layout, and the common
160	guided toggles.
161	
162	Simplified and Traditional Chinese HUD labels are available as explicit opt-ins. English stays the default unless you choose a Chinese locale in `/claude-hud:configure` or set `language` in config. The `zh` alias maps to Simplified Chinese, and `zh-TW` maps to Traditional Chinese. Guided config writes the canonical `zh-Hans` or `zh-Hant` value.
163	
164	### Options
165	
166	| Option | Type | Default | Description |
167	|--------|------|---------|-------------|
168	| `language` | `en` \| `zh` \| `zh-Hans` \| `zh-Hant` \| `zh-TW` | `en` | HUD label language. Use `zh` or `zh-Hans` for Simplified Chinese and `zh-Hant` or `zh-TW` for Traditional Chinese. |
169	| `lineLayout` | string | `expanded` | Layout: `expanded` (multi-line) or `compact` (single line) |
170	| `pathLevels` | 1-3 \| `full` | 1 | Directory levels to show in project path, or `full` to show the entire absolute path |
171	| `maxWidth` | number \| `null` | `null` | Optional fallback width used only when terminal width detection fails completely |
172	| `forceMaxWidth` | boolean | false | Always use `maxWidth` when it is set, even if terminal width detection returns a smaller value |
173	| `elementOrder` | string[] | `["project","addedDirs","context","usage","promptCache","memory","environment","tools","skills","mcp","agents","todos","sessionTime"]` | Expanded-mode element order. Omit entries to hide them in expanded mode. Existing configs keep their explicit order until updated. |
174	| `projectLineOrder` | string[] | `[]` | Optional leading order of segments *within* the first line, in both layouts. Visibility stays with the `display.show*` flags, and omitted segments retain their existing renderer order. `model` covers provider + model + effort (plus the context bar in compact mode); `project` covers path + added dirs + git as one segment. Example: `["project","model"]` puts the project/git block before the model badge. |
175	| `display.mergeGroups` | string[][] | `[["context","usage"]]` | Expanded-mode groups that should share a line when adjacent. Set `[]` to disable merged lines. |
176	| `display.rightAlign` | string[] | `[]` | Starts a right-aligned suffix at the first listed element in a merged row, preserving `elementOrder` and padding the gap with spaces. Requires the anchor to be in a `display.mergeGroups` group that actually renders on one line. Ignored when the terminal width is unknown, the anchor is first, or there is no room for padding. Example: `["context"]` with a `["project","context","usage"]` group keeps project/git left and pins context + usage right. |
177	| `gitStatus.enabled` | boolean | true | Show git branch in HUD |

181	| `gitStatus.pushCriticalThreshold` | number | 0 | Color the ahead count with the critical color at or above this unpushed-commit count (`0` disables it) |

Transcript model values are terminal-sanitized and capped at 80 characters |
189	| `display.showProvider` | boolean | false | Show the provider label *before* the model name, e.g. `[Bedrock \| Opus 4.6]`. Useful when a custom proxy serves identically-named models from different providers. When off, an auto-detected provider still trails the model as before |

Leave unset or `null` to preserve default full-window behavior. |

249	
250	`colors.barFilled` and `colors.barEmpty` accept a single visible grapheme. Control characters, invisible format characters (bidi controls, zero-width joiners, variation selectors), line/paragraph separators, and noncharacters are rejected. Wide characters (emoji, CJK) may affect bar alignment depending on the terminal.
251	
252	Supported color names: `dim`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `magenta`, `cyan`, `brightBlue`, `brightMagenta`. You can also use a 256-color number (`0-255`) or hex (`#rrggbb`).
253	
254	`display.showMemoryUsage` is fully opt-in and only renders in `expanded` layout. It reports approximate system RAM usage from the local machine, not precise memory pressure inside Claude Code or a specific process. The number may overstate actual pressure because reclaimable OS cache and buffers can still be counted as used memory.
255	
256	`display.showCost` is fully opt-in. ClaudeHUD prefers the native `cost.total_cost_usd` field that Claude Code provides on stdin when it is available. If that field is absent or invalid for a direct Anthropic session, ClaudeHUD falls back to the existing local transcript-based estimate so the cost line still works on older payloads. The native field is absent before the first API response in a session, so the cost display may stay hidden until then. ClaudeHUD also keeps the cost hidden for known routed providers such as Bedrock and Vertex AI, because cloud-provider billed sessions may report `$0.00` or omit the field even though the session was not literally free. Set `display.showRoutedCost: true` (alongside `showCost`) to opt into cost for those providers anyway: the native `cost.total_cost_usd` is shown as `Cost` when positive, otherwise ClaudeHUD falls back to a token-based `Est.` from the Anthropic pricing table.
257	
258	Official MiniMax Anthropic-compatible endpoints receive a `MiniMax` provider label. MiniMax M2.7 can use its published token and cache prices for local estimates; M3 pricing depends on each request's context tier, which cumulative session tokens cannot safely infer, so ClaudeHUD does not guess an M3 estimate.
259	
260	`display.showPromptCache` is fully opt-in. When enabled, ClaudeHUD looks at the timestamp of the last assistant response in the local transcript and shows a live countdown until the prompt cache expires. The default TTL is 5 minutes (`300` seconds). Set `display.promptCacheTtlSeconds` to `3600` if you want a 1-hour Max-style window. If the transcript does not have an assistant timestamp yet, the cache element stays hidden.
261	
262	### Usage Limits
263	
264	Usage display is **enabled by default** when Claude Code provides subscriber `rate_limits` data on stdin. It shows your rate limit consumption on line 2 alongside the context bar.
265	
266	Set `display.usageValue` to `remaining` to show quota left instead of quota used. Warning colors and 7-day threshold checks still use the underlying used percentage.
267	
268	ClaudeHUD prefers the official statusline stdin payload for rate-limit windows. If `display.externalUsagePath` points to a fresh local sidecar snapshot, ClaudeHUD can append its `balance_label` alongside stdin windows. If stdin `rate_limits` are missing, the same snapshot can provide fallback usage windows.
269	
270	The fallback snapshot path must be absolute. The snapshot must be fresh enough (`display.externalUsageFreshnessMs`) and include valid `updated_at`, plus a `five_hour` window, `seven_day` window, `balance_label`, or `model_scoped` array. `balance_label` is optional text for prepaid provider balances; it is trimmed, length-limited, and sanitized before display. Relative paths, invalid JSON, stale files, or invalid timestamps are ignored quietly.
271	
272	The snapshot may also carry `model_scoped` windows using the same shape Claude Code defines for stdin (`display_name`, `utilization` on the 0-100 scale, ISO `resets_at`). They render exactly like stdin scoped windows (see the model-scoped usage section) and stdin always wins when it carries its own `model_scoped` data. This lets a local feeder surface per-model weekly quotas (e.g. Fable) that the statusline payload does not include yet:
273	
274	```json
275	{
276	  "updated_at": "2026-07-24T14:12:37Z",
277	  "model_scoped": [
278	    { "display_name": "Fable", "utilization": 89, "resets_at": "2026-07-27T11:00:00Z" }
279	  ]
280	}
281	```
282	
283	One zero-credential way to produce such a snapshot is Claude Code's own `get_usage` control request, which returns `rate_limits.model_scoped` without spending tokens; a scheduled job can pipe it through `jq` into the snapshot file. The HUD itself never fetches anything: it only reads the file.
284	
285	Set `display.externalUsageWritePath` if you want ClaudeHUD to write the official stdin `rate_limits` into a local snapshot for other tools. The path must be absolute, end in `.json`, and live in an existing directory. ClaudeHUD writes the file with private permissions and ignores invalid paths quietly.
286	
287	Free/weekly-only accounts render the weekly window by itself instead of showing a ghost `5h: --` placeholder.
288	
289	The 7-day percentage appears when above the `display.sevenDayThreshold` (default 80%):
290	
291	```
292	Context █████░░░░░ 45% │ Usage ██░░░░░░░░ 25% (1h 30m / 5h) | ██████████ 85% (2d / 7d)
293	```
294	
295	To disable, set `display.showUsage` to `false`.
296	
297	Reset times use relative countdowns by default. Set `display.timeFormat` to `absolute` for wall-clock
298	times, `both` to show both forms, `elapsed` to show how far through each usage window you are, or
299	`elapsedAndAbsolute` to show elapsed window progress plus the wall-clock reset time. This setting is
300	manual-only today; `/claude-hud:configure` preserves it without editing it.
301	
302	Wall-clock reset times (`absolute`/`both`/`elapsedAndAbsolute`) default to your system locale for 12-
303	vs 24-hour formatting. Set `display.hourCycle` to `h23` to force 24-hour time regardless of locale, or
304	to `h12`/`h11` to force 12-hour time with AM/PM. Set `display.showClockSeconds` to `true` to include
305	seconds in the wall-clock time, e.g. `at 14:30:07`.
306	
307	Set `display.showResetLabel` to `false` if you want shorter usage countdowns such as `(3h 17m)` instead of `(resets in 3h 17m)`.
308	
309	Set `display.usageCompact` to `true` if you want the shorter usage-only form, for example `5h: 25% (1h 30m)`. Compact usage takes precedence over `display.usageBarEnabled`.
310	
311	### Security Notes
312	
313	ClaudeHUD is local-only by design. It does not make network requests, scrape credentials, or call undocumented Claude APIs. It reads the statusline JSON from stdin, the current session transcript path supplied by Claude Code, selected Claude configuration files under `~/.claude`, and git metadata for the current workspace.
314	
315	HUD cache files are written under `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud` with private permissions on POSIX filesystems. The cache stores derived display metadata such as context percentages, token counters, activity names, and the resolved Claude Code version.
316	
317	`--extra-cmd` is disabled unless `CLAUDE_HUD_ALLOW_EXTRA_CMD=1` (or `true`, `yes`, `on`) is present in the HUD process environment. Treat this option as arbitrary code execution: it runs the supplied shell command with your user privileges on statusline refreshes. Do not use commands copied from untrusted sources.
318	
319	**Requirements:**
320	- Claude Code must include subscriber `rate_limits` data on stdin for the current session
321	- Not available for API-key-only users
322	
323	**Troubleshooting:** If usage doesn't appear:
324	- Ensure you're logged in with a Claude subscriber account (not API key)
325	- Check `display.showUsage` is not set to `false` in config
326	- API users see no usage display (they have pay-per-token, not rate limits)
327	- AWS Bedrock models display `Bedrock` and hide usage limits (usage is managed in AWS)
328	- Bedrock and Vertex AI models hide cost estimates by default (billing differs from Anthropic direct); opt in with `display.showRoutedCost`
329	- Claude Code may leave `rate_limits` empty until after the first model response in a session
330	- Some Claude Code builds and subscription tiers may still omit `rate_limits`, even after the first response
331	- If you configured `display.externalUsagePath`, ClaudeHUD will try that local snapshot before hiding usage
332	- ClaudeHUD never falls back to credential scraping or undocumented API calls
333	
334	Example fallback snapshot:
335	
336	```json
337	{
338	  "updated_at": "2026-04-20T12:00:00.000Z",
339	  "five_hour": {
340	    "used_percentage": 42,
341	    "resets_at": "2026-04-20T15:00:00.000Z"
342	  },
343	  "seven_day": {
344	    "used_percentage": 84,
345	    "resets_at": "2026-04-27T12:00:00.000Z"
346	  }
347	}
348	```
349

396	### Display Examples
397	
398	**1 level (default):** `[Opus] │ my-project git:(main)`
399	
400	**2 levels:** `[Opus] │ apps/my-project git:(main)`
401	
402	**3 levels:** `[Opus] │ dev/apps/my-project git:(main)`
403	
404	**With dirty indicator:** `[Opus] │ my-project git:(main*)`
405	
406	**With ahead/behind:** `[Opus] │ my-project git:(main ↑2 ↓1)`
407	
408	**With file stats:** `[Opus] │ my-project git:(main* !3 +1 ?2)`
409	- `!` = modified files, `+` = added/staged, `✘` = deleted, `?` = untracked
410	- Counts of 0 are omitted for cleaner display
411	
412	### Jujutsu (jj) support
413	
414	Set `jjStatus.enabled` to `true` to opt in. When a real `.jj` directory is found
415	in (or above) the working directory, the HUD shows jj-native status instead of
416	git — the two are mutually exclusive per invocation, even in a colocated jj+git
417	repo. If jj cannot be queried safely, a colocated repository falls back to its
418	existing git status.
419	
420	**With a bookmark:** `[Opus] │ my-project jj:(mybookmark)`
421	
422	**Anonymous change (no bookmark at `@`):** `[Opus] │ my-project jj:(wrulwzyw)`
423	
424	**Dirty working copy:** `[Opus] │ my-project jj:(mybookmark*)`
425	
426	**Unresolved conflict:** `[Opus] │ my-project jj:(mybookmark !conflict)`
427	
428	Ahead/behind counts and per-file change stats are git-only in this version —
429	jj's equivalent requires more expensive revset queries against
430	`remote_bookmarks()`, so they're left out to keep the jj status fetch to a
431	single subprocess call.
432	
433	The HUD runs jj in prompt-safe, read-only mode: it disables the pager, ignores
434	the live working copy, and reads the current operation without reconciling it.
435	That avoids snapshotting files or mutating repository state during statusline
436	refreshes. As a result, the dirty marker reflects jj's most recent working-copy
437	snapshot and can remain stale until another jj command records new changes.
438	
439	### Auto-Refresh
440	
441	Claude Code only re-runs the statusline after an interaction (a new assistant message, `/compact` finishing, a permission-mode change, or a vim-mode toggle), so time-based HUD info — session duration, usage reset countdowns, the prompt-cache countdown — goes stale between messages. To keep it ticking, add `refreshInterval` (seconds, minimum 1) to the `statusLine` entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`:
442	
443	```json
444	{
445	  "statusLine": {
446	    "type": "command",
447	    "command": "...",
448	    "refreshInterval": 5
449	  }
450	}
451	```
452	
453	`/claude-hud:setup` offers this during installation. Each refresh re-runs the HUD command, so 5 seconds is a good default; use 1 second only if you want visibly smooth countdowns.
454	
455	### Disabling the HUD Temporarily
456	
457	Set the `CLAUDE_HUD_DISABLE` environment variable to launch a session without the HUD — no need to remove the `statusLine` entry from `settings.json`:
458	
459	```bash
460	CLAUDE_HUD_DISABLE=1 claude
461	```
462	
463	Leaving it unset (or setting an explicit negative: `0`, `false`, `off`, `no`) keeps the HUD enabled. When disabled, the HUD exits immediately without reading the transcript or running git, so the statusline simply stays empty for that session.
464	
465	### Troubleshooting
466	
467	**Config not applying?**
468	- Check for JSON syntax errors: invalid JSON silently falls back to defaults
469	- Ensure valid values: `pathLevels` must be 1, 2, 3, or `full`; `lineLayout` must be `expanded` or `compact`; `maxWidth` must be a positive number
470	- Delete config and run `/claude-hud:configure` to regenerate
471	
472	**Git status missing?**
473	- Verify you're in a git repository
474	- Check `gitStatus.enabled` is not `false` in config
475	
476	**jj status missing, or seeing `git:(...)` in a jj repo?**
477	- Verify a `.jj` directory exists at or above the working directory
478	- Set `jjStatus.enabled` to `true` in config (jj support is opt-in)
479	- Verify the `jj` binary is installed and on `PATH`
480	
481	**Tool/skill/MCP/agent/todo lines missing?**
482	- These are hidden by default — enable with `showTools`, `showSkills`, `showMcp`, `showAgents`, `showTodos` in config
483	- They also only appear when there's activity to show
484	
485	**HUD not appearing after setup?**
486	- Send any message — settings reload automatically, but the statusline only renders after your next interaction
487	- If it still doesn't appear, restart Claude Code (fully quit and run `claude` again) — older Claude Code versions require a restart to pick up statusLine changes
488	- Make sure `CLAUDE_HUD_DISABLE` is not set in your environment (e.g. exported from a shell profile) — it silences the HUD entirely, including setup verification
489	
490	---
491	
492	## Requirements
493

## Line references

The supplied GitHub view shows **770 lines (602 logical lines)** but no per-line numbers, so source line numbers are unavailable.

## Setup entry points

The documented commands are:

- “`/claude-hud:setup`”
- “`/plugin install claude-hud`”
- “`/reload-plugins`”

The setup first checks for orphaned plugin state, then detects platform, shell, runtime, and plugin path.

## Generated `statusLine` commands

The source requires these runtime choices:

- “On `darwin` or `linux`, use `src/index.ts` when the runtime is bun.”
- “Otherwise use `dist/index.js`.”
- “On Windows, always use `dist/index.js`.”

### macOS/Linux: Bun

The exact Bun command is represented by these consecutive source fragments; concatenate each set without adding characters:

1. “`bash -c 'cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '"'"'`”
2. “`'{print $2}'"'"');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ?`”
3. “` cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/`”
4. “` 2>/dev/null | awk -F/ '"'"'{ print $(NF-1) "\t" $(0) }'"'"' | grep -E '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]' |`”
5. “` sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4n | tail -1 | cut -f2-); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" --env-file /dev/null`”
6. “` "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"'`”

### macOS/Linux: Node

Fragments 1–4 above are unchanged. The ending is:

- “` sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4n | tail -1 | cut -f2-); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}"`”
- “` "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"'`”

### Windows + Git Bash

The exact command fragments are:

1. “`cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '{print $2}');; esac;`”
2. “` case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 ));`”
3. “` plugin_dir=$(ls -1d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1);`”
4. “` exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"`”

### Windows + PowerShell

The generated launcher invocation is:

- “`{CMD_PATH} /d /s /c ""{RUNTIME_PATH}" "{WRAPPER_PATH}""`”

The wrapper is written as UTF-8 without a BOM using:

- “`[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($wrapperPath, $wrapperBody, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))`”

## Exact `settings.json` content

The required statusline object is:

- “`{`”
- “`  "statusLine": {`”
- “`    "type": "command",`”
- “`    "command": "{GENERATED_COMMAND}"`”
- “`  }`”
- “`}`”

The page instructs setup to merge this object into the existing settings rather than replace unrelated settings. It also says to use:

- “`Write settings.json with a real JSON serializer or editor API, not manual string concatenation.`”

On Windows, the specified no-BOM write is:

- “`[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $json, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))`”

The optional timer adds or removes this property inside `statusLine`:

- “`refreshInterval: <N>`”

## Optional `config.json` content

When extras are selected, setup writes:

- “`plugins/claude-hud/config.json`”

The documented keys are:

- “`display.showTools: true`”
- “`display.showAgents: true, display.showTodos: true`”
- “`display.showDuration: true, display.showConfigCounts: true`”
- “`display.showSessionName: true`”
- “`display.customLine: "<user's text>"`”

Only selected keys are merged; no configuration file is created when nothing is selected.

## Files setup writes or creates

1. **Settings file**  
   “`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json`” on bash-like systems; the equivalent Claude directory is used on PowerShell.

2. **Timestamped settings backup**  
   A pre-existing settings file is copied to a name matching:
   - “`${SETTINGS}.bak.${BACKUP_TIMESTAMP}`”

3. **Previous statusline command**  
   If an existing non-HUD statusline is replaced, setup saves:
   - “`previous-statusline.txt`”

4. **Windows launcher only**  
   Setup creates:
   - “`$claudeDir/plugins/claude-hud/statusline.mjs`”

5. **Optional HUD configuration**  
   Created only when extras are enabled:
   - “`plugins/claude-hud/config.json`”

6. **Plugin registry during confirmed ghost-install reset**  
   The reset operation overwrites:
   - “`installed_plugins.json`”

That reset writes an empty plugin registry and can remove all registered plugins. Plugin-cache and temporary-install files are removed during cleanup rather than written.

 `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md#plugin-caching-and-file-resolution`

```text
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference

> “For security and verification purposes, Claude Code copies *marketplace* plugins to the user's local **plugin cache** (`~/.claude/plugins/cache`) rather than using them in place, except for [`command` sources in link mode](/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces#copy-mode-and-link-mode), which Claude Code uses in place through links in the cache entry.”

Marketplace plugins are copied into the cache when installed or updated. At session start, Claude Code also creates the cached copy if an enabled plugin is not cached:

> “Claude Code runs the install inside the copied version directory each time it creates one: when you install a plugin, when Claude Code updates a plugin to a new version, and at session start when an enabled plugin isn't cached yet, such as on a new machine.”

Additional cache behavior:

> “For copied plugins, each installed version is a separate directory in the cache, grouped by marketplace and plugin and named for the resolved version…”

The main exception is a `command` source operating in link mode; it is used in place via a cache symlink rather than copied.
```
</details></tool-use>

416	} catch (error) {

677	### Step 4.5: Auto-Refresh (Optional)
678	
679	Claude Code only re-runs the statusline after an interaction (a new assistant message, `/compact` finishing, a permission-mode change, or a vim-mode toggle). Time-based HUD data — session duration, usage reset countdowns, the prompt-cache countdown — therefore goes stale between messages. Claude Code supports an optional `refreshInterval` key (seconds, minimum 1) on the `statusLine` settings object that re-runs the command every N seconds.
680	
681	Of those, only the usage reset countdown is shown by default — session duration and the prompt-cache countdown tick only if the user enabled them (e.g. "Session info" in Step 4, or via config). Mention this if the user seems unsure whether the timer is worth it.
682	
683	Ask with AskUserQuestion:

685	- question: "Re-run the HUD on a timer so time-based info (session duration, usage countdowns) stays current between messages?"
686	- options:
687	  - "Every 5 seconds (Recommended)" — Keeps countdowns fresh with negligible overhead
688	  - "Every 1 second" — Smoothest ticking; re-runs the HUD command far more often
689	  - "No timer" — HUD updates only after interactions (Claude Code's default)
690	
691	**If the user picks an interval**, merge `refreshInterval: <N>` into the **existing** `statusLine` object in `settings.json` — preserve `type`, `command`, and any other keys. Follow the same rules as Step 3: real JSON serializer, no BOM on Windows, retry once on a concurrent-modification error. Do not re-create the backup; the Step 2.5.3 backup already covers this session.

693	**If the user picks "Other" and gives a numeric interval** (e.g. "10" or "10 seconds"), use that value, clamped to a minimum of 1. Treat a non-numeric "Other" answer that declines (skip/none/no) like "No timer".

699	Each refresh re-runs the full HUD command (runtime startup, transcript parse, git status), so 5 seconds is the recommended default; only suggest 1 second when the user wants visibly smooth countdowns.

## Install and setup

No line numbers are displayed in the supplied page.

### Inside Claude Code

```text
/plugin marketplace add jarrodwatts/claude-hud
/plugin install claude-hud
/reload-plugins
/claude-hud:setup
```

The first two commands add the marketplace and install the plugin. Reload plugins, then run setup to configure the statusline.

### From a terminal

```text
claude plugin marketplace add jarrodwatts/claude-hud
claude plugin install claude-hud@claude-hud
```

Afterward, run this inside Claude Code:

```text
/reload-plugins
```

The HUD should appear after the next message. Older Claude Code versions may require a restart.

### Linux installation fallback

If installation fails with an `EXDEV` error:

1. Update Claude Code first.
2. If updating is not possible, launch Claude Code with:

```text
mkdir -p ~/.cache/tmp && TMPDIR=~/.cache/tmp claude
```

Then install the plugin in that session.

## Windows runtime notes

- Windows requires Node.js 18 or newer.
- Node.js LTS is the supported runtime for setup.
- If setup reports that no JavaScript runtime exists, run:

```text
winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS
```

- Restart the shell, then run:

```text
/claude-hud:setup
```

## Features

Claude HUD uses Claude Code’s native statusline interface and displays information below the prompt, including:

- Model and provider identification
- Project path and optional added workspace directories
- Git branch, dirty state, ahead/behind counts, and file statistics
- Optional Jujutsu status
- Context-window usage with configurable bars, percentages, tokens, and thresholds
- Subscriber usage windows and reset information
- Active tools, Skills, MCP servers, agents, and todos
- Session duration, output speed, cost, output style, authentication, and session metadata
- Memory usage, prompt-cache countdown, compaction count, advisor model, and Claude Code version
- English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese labels
- Expanded or compact layouts
- Automatic refresh support through `statusLine.refreshInterval`

The implementation reads statusline JSON from standard input and session-transcript JSONL data. It is designed to operate locally and does not make network requests.

## Configuration path

Advanced configuration is stored at:

```text
~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json
```

The guided configuration command is:

```text
/claude-hud:configure
```

Manual settings such as colors, thresholds, path depth, width, time formatting, and prompt-cache TTL are preserved by the guided configurator.

## Configuration schema

The root object supports these fields:

```json
{
  "language": "en",
  "lineLayout": "expanded",
  "pathLevels": 1,
  "maxWidth": null,
  "forceMaxWidth": false,
  "elementOrder": [],
  "projectLineOrder": [],
  "display": {},
  "gitStatus": {},
  "jjStatus": {},
  "colors": {}
}
```

### Root fields

- `language`: `en`, `zh`, `zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant`, or `zh-TW`; default `en`
- `lineLayout`: `expanded` or `compact`; default `expanded`
- `pathLevels`: `1`, `2`, `3`, or `full`; default `1`
- `maxWidth`: positive number or `null`; default `null`
- `forceMaxWidth`: boolean; default `false`
- `elementOrder`: expanded-layout element ordering
- `projectLineOrder`: ordering of the model and project segments on the first line
- `display`: rendering and feature switches
- `gitStatus`: Git behavior
- `jjStatus`: optional Jujutsu behavior
- `colors`: color and progress-bar customization

The default expanded element order is:

```json
[
  "project", "addedDirs", "context", "usage", "promptCache",
  "memory", "environment", "tools", "skills", "mcp",
  "agents", "todos", "sessionTime"
]
```

### `gitStatus`

Fields:

- `enabled`: default `true`
- `showDirty`: default `true`
- `showAheadBehind`: default `false`
- `pushWarningThreshold`: number; default `0`
- `pushCriticalThreshold`: number; default `0`
- `showFileStats`: default `false`
- `branchOverflow`: `truncate` or `wrap`; default `truncate`

### `jjStatus`

Fields:

- `enabled`: default `false`
- `showDirty`: default `true`
- `showConflicts`: default `true`

When enabled and a `.jj` directory is found, Jujutsu replaces Git status for that repository.

### `display`

Supported fields include:

- Layout: `mergeGroups`, `rightAlign`
- Model: `showModel`, `modelSource`, `showProvider`, `providerName`, `showEffortLevel`
- Project: `showAddedDirs`, `addedDirsLayout`
- Context: `showContextBar`, `contextValue`, `autoCompactWindow`, `showTokenBreakdown`
- Usage: `showUsage`, `usageValue`, `usageBarEnabled`, `usageCompact`, `showResetLabel`, `timeFormat`, `hourCycle`, `showClockSeconds`, `sevenDayThreshold`
- External usage: `externalUsagePath`, `externalUsageWritePath`, `externalUsageFreshnessMs`
- Activity: `showTools`, `showSkills`, `showMcp`, `toolNameMaxLength`, `toolsMaxVisible`, `showAgents`, `showTodos`
- Session metadata: `showSessionName`, `showAuth`, `showAuthUser`, `authUserLength`, `showAdvisor`, `advisorOverride`, `showSessionStartDate`, `showLastResponseAt`, `showCompactions`, `showClaudeCodeVersion`
- Metrics: `showConfigCounts`, `showCost`, `showRoutedCost`, `showOutputStyle`, `showDuration`, `showSpeed`, `showMemoryUsage`, `showPromptCache`, `promptCacheTtlSeconds`

Important defaults include:

- `showModel`: `true`
- `modelSource`: `stdin`
- `showContextBar`: `true`
- `contextValue`: `percent`
- `showUsage`: `true`
- `usageValue`: `percent`
- `usageBarEnabled`: `true`
- `showResetLabel`: `true`
- `sevenDayThreshold`: `80`
- `showTokenBreakdown`: `true`
- `showTools`, `showSkills`, `showMcp`, `showAgents`, and `showTodos`: `false`
- `toolsMaxVisible`: `4`
- `authUserLength`: `8`
- `promptCacheTtlSeconds`: `300`

### `colors`

Supported color fields:

```text
context
usage
warning
usageWarning
critical
model
project
git
gitBranch
label
custom
barFilled
barEmpty
```

Named colors include `dim`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `magenta`, `cyan`, `brightBlue`, and `brightMagenta`. Numeric 256-color values and hexadecimal colors are also supported. Progress-bar characters must be single visible graphemes.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
### Agent-oriented installation

1. Check the Claude Code version with `"claude --version"`; version 1.0.80 or newer is required.
2. If necessary, direct the user to `https://claude.ai/code`.
3. Add the marketplace using `"/plugin marketplace add jarrodwatts/claude-hud"`.
4. Install with `"/plugin install claude-hud"`.
5. Reload plugins using `"/reload-plugins"`.
6. Configure the HUD with `"/claude-hud:setup"`.

### Setup and `statusLine` behavior

- The setup command writes a `statusLine` entry to `~/.claude/settings.json`.
- That entry automatically locates the newest installed plugin version, so setup need not be repeated after updates.
- Settings reload automatically; the HUD should appear after the next message. Older Claude Code versions may require a restart.
- Do not star the repository automatically. Ask first, then use the documented `gh repo star` or GitHub API fallback only after explicit consent.

### Runtime invocation

Claude Code runs the plugin after each interaction, with a 300 ms debounce. The plugin:

1. Reads native JSON from standard input.
2. Uses the transcript path from that input to parse the session’s JSONL transcript.
3. Reads Claude configuration files.
4. Produces up to four statusline rows on standard output.

The input can provide model information, context usage, token data, subscription limits and reset times, transcript location, and working directory. Transcript parsing supplies tool activity, agents, todos, completion states, and session timing.

### Configuration paths and sources

- Main user settings: `~/.claude/settings.json`
- Plugin configuration: `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json`
- Plugin metadata: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
- Additional project configuration: `.mcp.json`, project `.claude/` directories, and `CLAUDE.md` files in the working directory or its ancestors

`plugin.json` contains metadata only; the `statusLine` setting belongs in the user settings file.

### Displayed features

The HUD can show:

- Model name and context percentage, with green, yellow, or red threshold coloring
- Git branch and repository state
- Counts of `CLAUDE.md` files, rules, MCP servers, and hooks
- Five-hour and seven-day usage information when supplied
- Session duration
- Running tools and aggregated completed-tool counts
- Active agents, including type, model, description, and elapsed time
- The current todo item and completion count
```
</details></tool-use>

# Customize your status line

> Configure a custom status bar to monitor context window usage, costs, and git status in Claude Code

The status line is a customizable bar at the bottom of Claude Code that runs any shell script you configure. It receives JSON session data on stdin and displays whatever your script prints, giving you a persistent, at-a-glance view of context usage, costs, git status, or anything else you want to track.

Status lines are useful when you:

* Want to monitor context window usage as you work
* Need to track session costs
* Work across multiple sessions and need to distinguish them
* Want git branch and status always visible

The status line renders in its own row above the built-in footer badges and does not replace them. With a custom status line configured, Claude Code stops showing most of the footer's keyboard hints, including `esc to interrupt`, the `? for shortcuts` fallback, and the `hold space to speak` [voice dictation](/docs/en/voice-dictation) hint. To add clickable link badges to the footer when an ID appears in the conversation, without writing a script, configure [`footerLinksRegexes`](/docs/en/settings#footer-link-badges) instead.

Here's an example of a [multi-line status line](#display-multiple-lines) that displays git info on the first line and a color-coded context bar on the second.
