```text
1	# Rationale
2	
3	Why this setup makes the choices it does.
4	
5	## PowerShell 7 default, cmd.exe optional (via Clink)
6	
7	`cmd.exe` (the DOS-lineage shell) has no real scripting story: no functions worth
8	the name, no structured data, awkward quoting. **PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`)** is the
9	modern default on Windows — an object pipeline, real modules, cross-platform, and
10	first-class `init` integration for every tool here (starship, zoxide, atuin,
11	fzf, direnv). Windows PowerShell 5.1 still ships in-box but is frozen; we install
12	and target pwsh 7. Everything in this repo — the `$PROFILE` fragments, aliases,
13	functions, copilot-proxy — is written for pwsh.
14	
15	cmd.exe isn't scripted *against*, but it isn't ignored either: some tools spawn it
16	and muscle memory persists. The **opt-in `installClink` toggle** gives the DOS
17	prompt a starship prompt plus `z` dir-jumping and Ctrl-R/Ctrl-T fzf, via
18	[Clink](https://chrisant996.github.io/clink/) (cmd's PSReadLine analog). It reuses
19	the **same `starship.toml`** and the XDG env already persisted to the User
20	registry — so the *config* is shared; only the shell-activation "script" differs
21	(Clink Lua vs the pwsh profile). This is **prompt + navigation parity, not feature
22	parity**: atuin / direnv / tv and every pwsh function/module stay pwsh-only. pwsh
23	remains the default and primary target; cmd is a scoped secondary. See
24	[Shell → cmd.exe via Clink](shell.md#cmdexe-via-clink).
25	
26	(WSL is great, but it's a Linux environment — handled by the cross-platform
27	dotfiles, not this repo. This repo is about a good *native* Windows shell. The
28	one exception is Docker Desktop's backend: the `installWsl` toggle enables the
29	WSL2 *platform* via `wsl --install --no-distribution` — plumbing for Docker's
30	containers, not a Linux shell — self-elevating with one UAC prompt and a reboot.
31	The optional `installWslUbuntu` toggle goes one step further: it registers an
32	Ubuntu distro and *triggers* the cross-platform repo's own installer inside it
33	(a frozen, non-interactive `chezmoi init` seeded from the Windows-side answers) —
34	even then the Linux config is owned by that repo; this one is just the launcher.)
35	
36	## scoop for CLIs + winget for apps, not Chocolatey
37	
38	| | scoop | winget | Chocolatey |
39	|---|---|---|---|
40	| Admin required | no (user-scoped) | for machine-scope apps | usually yes |
41	| Best at | CLI/dev tools | GUI/Store apps | broad legacy coverage |
42	| Reproducible | `scoop export/import` | `winget export/import` | `packages.config` |
43	| Update model | `scoop update *` | `winget upgrade --all` | `choco upgrade all` |
44	
45	**scoop** installs developer CLIs into a per-user directory with **no UAC prompts**,
46	easy version pinning, and clean uninstalls — ideal for the ~20 shell tools here.
47	**winget** is Microsoft's official manager and has the best catalog for GUI apps
48	and first-party installers (VSCode, PowerToys, Steam, …).
49	
50	**Chocolatey** was the long-time default and still has the broadest package
51	coverage, but it's admin-heavy and less reproducible for a per-user dev setup. It
52	stays a documented fallback for the rare package missing from both scoop and winget.
53	
54	## Runtimes: scoop natives, not mise on Windows
55	
56	The macOS/Linux dotfiles use **mise** to manage language runtimes. On Windows we
57	tried it and backed out — runtimes are installed **natively via scoop** (plus
58	**uv** for Python) instead.
59	
60	Why mise didn't hold up here:
61	
62	- **Shims / activate don't reliably expose global tools.** `mise activate`'s
63	  pwsh prompt-hook and the shims dir both failed to put globally-pinned tools
64	  (`bun`, `go`) on PATH in practice — `mise use -g bun` "succeeded" yet `bun`
65	  wasn't found.
66	- **Arch gaps.** On Windows-on-ARM, `mise use -g bun` records the version but
67	  ships **no windows-arm64 bun binary**, leaving a dead shim.
68	- **It fought the machine's existing node.** A pre-existing `nvm` shadowed
69	  mise's node, so npm used the wrong one.
70	
71	scoop shims live in `~/scoop/shims`, which scoop persists to the user PATH (and
72	`profile.d/00_env.ps1` also prepends) — so `node` (`nodejs-lts`), `bun`, `go`,
73	`rustup`, `ruby` are simply **on PATH**, no activation dance. **Python** is
74	uv-managed (`uv python install --default --preview`), which also drops unversioned
75	`python`/`python3` into `~/.local/bin`.
76	
77	The tradeoff: **no per-project runtime pinning** (mise's headline feature). For a
78	Windows dev box that's a fair trade for "the tools are actually on PATH." If you
79	want per-project versions, `scoop install mise` and use it directly — nothing
80	here depends on it. The full debugging trail lives in
81	`backlog/windows-arm64-managed-machine-rough-edges.md`.
82	
83	## Terminal multiplexer: WezTerm (stable default) + herdr (native beta)
84	
85	`tmux` and `zellij` are **Unix-only** — historically there were no native Windows
86	builds, so they're absent here (you can still run them inside WSL). That's now
87	changing: **herdr** ships an experimental native-Windows beta. The native options:
88	
89	| Option | Splits / tabs | Detach + persist | Notes |
90	|---|---|---|---|
91	| **WezTerm** | yes (panes/tabs, Lua `wezterm.mux`) | yes (mux server + `wezterm connect`) | native Windows; stable default |
92	| **herdr** | yes (mouse-first panes/splits) | yes (persistent sessions, detach/attach) | native Windows, **preview beta**; closest to tmux/zellij — opt-in via `installHerdr` |
93	| Windows Terminal | yes (panes/tabs) | no | great terminal, no session persistence |
94	| Alacritty | no | no | fast, minimal; pair with a multiplexer |
95	| tmux / zellij | — | — | Unix-only; use under WSL |
96	
97	**WezTerm** (`wez.wezterm`) is the stable default: a native Windows terminal with
98	a built-in multiplexer — split panes, tabs, and a persistent mux server you can
99	detach from and reconnect to (`wezterm connect`), plus scriptable layouts via its
100	Lua `wezterm.mux` API. It isn't a 1:1 tmux (the session/persistence model
101	differs), but it's the closest stable native experience.
102	
103	**herdr** (opt-in, `installHerdr`) is the newer, closest-to-tmux/zellij answer: a
104	mouse-first native multiplexer (ConPTY) with panes, splits, persistent sessions,
105	and detach/attach. It has no scoop/winget manifest — it installs via herdr.dev's
106	`irm | iex` script (Windows is preview-only), and its config is managed at
107	`~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (pwsh as the default shell). It's beta, so it stays
108	off by default. Windows Terminal stays installed for its panes/tabs; Alacritty
109	stays as the fast minimal option.
110	
111	## starship, not oh-my-posh
112	
113	Both are prompt engines; running both is redundant. We use **starship** because the
114	exact same `starship.toml` already drives the macOS and Linux dotfiles — one config,
115	one behavior everywhere (`starship init powershell`). oh-my-posh is excellent and
116	very PowerShell-native, but adopting it would mean a second, Windows-only prompt
117	config to maintain for no functional gain here.
118	
119	## A parallel PowerShell tree, not a ported shell layer
120	
121	The macOS/Linux dotfiles have a large POSIX `shell/*.sh` layer. Mechanically
122	translating it to PowerShell would be a maintenance sink (two dialects of the same
123	logic drifting apart). Instead the PowerShell config is written **natively** in
124	`profile.d/*.ps1` — idiomatic pwsh, only the *behaviors* shared, not the code.
125	
126	## Native `copilot-proxy`, not a bash shim
127	
128	The `copilot-proxy` tool series is reimplemented as a real PowerShell module
129	(`Invoke-RestMethod`, `Start-Process`, `ConvertFrom-Json`) rather than shelling out
130	to the original bash. Only the Bun throttle shim (pure JS) is reused verbatim. See
131	[copilot-proxy](copilot-proxy.md).
132	
133	## `run_onchange` pwsh mergers for JSON config, not `modify_` scripts
134	
135	Some JSON config surfaces are **owned by the tool at runtime** — Claude Code
136	rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` (plugins it installs, permissions you grant),
137	VSCode/Cursor rewrite their `settings.json`. Deploying a static managed copy
138	would clobber that live state, so these are **merged**, not overwritten. The
139	macOS/Linux repo merges with a chezmoi **`modify_` script** (a `sh` + `jq`
140	filter: read the live file on stdin, emit the merged result on stdout). On
141	Windows that doesn't hold up:
142	
143	- **Interpreter routing is by the *target's* extension.** chezmoi chooses a
144	  `modify_`/`create_` script's interpreter from the managed file's extension via
145	  `[interpreters.<ext>]`. `modify_settings.json` targets `settings.json` →
146	  `.json`, which maps to no interpreter. On Unix chezmoi falls back to the
147	  script's shebang (`#!/bin/sh`) + exec bit; Windows honors neither, so it can't
148	  run the script reliably — and you can't hand it a `.ps1` extension, because
149	  that's fixed to the target name. Only `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh` is wired up,
150	  and it only helps when the *managed file itself* is a `.ps1`.
151	- **Wrong toolchain.** The parent filter is `sh` + `jq` — not guaranteed on a
152	  pwsh-first box, and rewriting it in pwsh still hits the routing wall above.
153	
154	So each merge is a **`run_onchange_after_*.ps1.tmpl`** in `.chezmoiscripts/`
155	instead: a real `.ps1` that routes cleanly through `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh`,
156	runs natively with no external deps, and recursively deep-merges a
157	chezmoi-ignored overlay (`editors/*.json`, `claude/settings-overlay.json`,
158	embedded via `{{ include }}`) into the live file — preserving every key the tool
159	wrote. This is invariant #5 in `AGENTS.md`.
160	
161	**Tradeoff:** a `modify_` filter re-asserts on *every* apply; `run_onchange` only
162	re-fires when its rendered content (the overlay) changes. If the tool later
163	overwrites a managed key, it isn't restored until the overlay changes or you
164	reset state (`chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=entryState`). The parent needs
165	every-apply enforcement because CodeIsland / workmux keep rewriting
166	`~/.claude/settings.json`; Windows has no such contenders, so the lighter trigger
167	is fine.
168	
169	## XDG paths, not `%APPDATA%`
170	
171	Windows and XDG split directories on different axes — Windows by whether a
172	folder *roams* (`AppData\Roaming` vs `AppData\Local`), XDG by *purpose*
173	(config / data / state / cache) — so `%APPDATA%` is not a clean "Windows XDG".
174	Rather than map onto it, `profile.d/00_env.ps1` sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and
175	friends to Unix-style `~/.config` / `~/.local/share` paths. XDG-aware tools
176	(starship, atuin, zoxide, yazi) then keep a tidy `$HOME` that mirrors the
177	macOS/Linux dotfiles — one mental model, shared configs. Apps that ignore XDG
178	and hard-code `%APPDATA%` (VSCode, Cursor, Alacritty) stay there and are managed
179	at that path. Full mapping, plus the `PATH` mechanics, are in
180	[Shell & environment](shell.md).
181
```

+# SpecStory CLI Configuration
+#
+# This is the user-level config file for SpecStory CLI.
+# Settings here act as global defaults for all projects when you run `specstory`.
+#
+# Project-local `./.specstory/cli/config.toml` settings override these defaults.
+# CLI flags override both user-level and project-level configuration.
+#
+# Uncomment (remove the #) any setting below to change the default behavior.
+# For more information, see:
+# https://docs.specstory.com/integrations/terminal-coding-agents/usage#configuration
+
+[local_sync]
+# Write markdown files locally. (default: true)
+# enabled = false # equivalent to --only-cloud-sync
+
+# Custom output directory for markdown files.
+# Default: ./.specstory/history (relative to the project directory)
+# output_dir = "~/.specstory/history" # equivalent to --output-dir "~/.specstory/history"
+
+# Use local timezone for file name and content timestamps (default: false, UTC)

# Tools

The install set lives in `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl`
(the single source of truth), gated by the init toggles. **scoop** handles CLI
tools; **winget** handles GUI apps.

## CLI tools (scoop)

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| git, gh, glab | version control + GitHub / GitLab CLIs |
| neovim | editor (LazyVim, pre-configured) |
| lazygit | git TUI (delta pager configured) |
| zoxide | smarter `cd` |
| fzf, fd, ripgrep | fuzzy find / file search / grep |
| bat, eza | `cat` / `ls` replacements |
| delta | git diff pager |
| jq | JSON processor |
| yazi, btop | file manager / system monitor |
| television (`tv`) | fuzzy picker / channel launcher |
| tldr (tlrc) | community man-page cheatsheets; `tldrf` adds `zh_TW → zh → en` fallback |
| gh dash | GitHub PR/issue dashboard TUI (gh extension; installs once `gh` is authenticated) |
| starship | prompt |
| node | JS runtime (`nodejs-lts`) |
| uv | Python package/runtime manager |
| bun | JS runtime + package manager (backs copilot-proxy) |
| just | task runner (this repo's `justfile`) |
| make | GNU make |
| zig | C compiler for Neovim tree-sitter parsers |
| gcc | amd64 C compiler (**ARM64 hosts only** — matches the x64-emulated nvim) |
| tree-sitter | tree-sitter CLI (nvim-treesitter `main` branch) |
| win32yank | clipboard provider for Neovim |
| gnupg | `gpg` (git commit signing, verification) |

Runtimes are **native (scoop), not mise** — see [rationale](rationale.md#runtimes-scoop-natives-not-mise-on-windows).
`node` (`nodejs-lts`) and `bun` come from scoop; `go`, `rust` (rustup), `ruby`
are added when **Extra runtimes** is enabled. A default **Python** is uv-managed:
`uv python install --default --preview` puts `python`/`python3` in `~/.local/bin`
(on PATH ahead of the Store's `python.exe` app-alias), so `python`, `uv run`, and
`uv venv` all work without the Microsoft Store.

## GUI apps (winget)

| App | winget id |
|---|---|
| VSCode | `Microsoft.VisualStudioCode` |
| Cursor | `Anysphere.Cursor` |
| Windows Terminal | `Microsoft.WindowsTerminal` |
| Alacritty | `Alacritty.Alacritty` |
| WezTerm | `wez.wezterm` (tmux-like multiplexer; managed `~/.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua` sets pwsh as the shell + Nerd Font) |
| PowerToys | `Microsoft.PowerToys` |
| Raycast | `9PFXXSHC64H3` (msstore) |
| Antigravity | `Google.Antigravity` |
| Docker Desktop | `Docker.DockerDesktop` (WSL2 backend via the `installWsl` toggle — see below) |
| Discord | `Discord.Discord` |
| Claude Desktop | `Anthropic.Claude` |
| ChatGPT | `9PLM9XGG6VKS` (msstore) |
| Chrome | `Google.Chrome` |
| Arc | `TheBrowserCompany.Arc` |
| Zen Browser | `Zen-Team.Zen-Browser` |
| Grammarly | `Grammarly.Grammarly` |
| Steam (gaming) | `Valve.Steam` |

**Docker Desktop's WSL2 backend** (`installWsl` toggle, on for workstation) is set up
by `scripts/enable-wsl.ps1` via `wsl --install --no-distribution` — only the WSL2
platform, not a Linux distro (Docker creates its own `docker-desktop` distro).
`wsl --install` needs admin **and** a reboot, so a non-elevated `chezmoi apply`
self-elevates with a single UAC prompt (like scoop), runs the install, then prints a
restart notice — reboot, then Docker Desktop starts on the WSL2 backend. Re-run or
retry (e.g. if the UAC prompt was declined) with `just enable-wsl`. Already-installed
machines are a no-op (no UAC). On a proxy / corporate / GFW network where the WSL app
download is reset ("connection reset"), the script falls back to enabling the WSL2
features **offline via DISM** and points at the kernel MSI + `wsl --update`. WSL as a
*Linux shell* stays out of scope — see
[rationale](rationale.md#powershell-7-default-cmdexe-optional-via-clink).

**Unattended WSL Ubuntu + dotfiles** (`installWslUbuntu`, off by default) goes further:
`scripts/enable-wsl-ubuntu.ps1` registers `Ubuntu-24.04` with **no OOBE** (creates your
user via `wsl -u root`, passwordless sudo, WSL auto-login), then — in the default
`headless` mode — runs a **frozen-from-Windows** chezmoi one-liner that installs the
cross-platform dotfiles (`daviddwlee84/dotfiles`, `ubuntu_server` profile) with no
prompts inside WSL. `wslUbuntuBootstrap` can instead be `interactive` (the parent repo's
prompts on first login) or `none` (set up the distro only). Requires the WSL2 platform
(`installWsl`) + its reboot first; run or retry with `just enable-wsl-ubuntu`. Linux GUI
apps work out of the box via **WSLg** if you later switch the frozen profile to
`ubuntu_desktop`. This is an opt-in *bridge* — the Linux config lives in the
cross-platform repo, not here.

## Utility apps (winget)

Enabled by **Install utility apps**:

| App | winget id | What |
|---|---|---|
| CPU-Z | `CPUID.CPU-Z` | CPU/mainboard info |
| GPU-Z | `TechPowerUp.GPU-Z` | GPU info + sensors |
| HWiNFO | `REALiX.HWiNFO` | full hardware monitoring |
| TreeSize Free | `JAMSoftware.TreeSize.Free` | disk-usage explorer |
| WinDirStat | `WinDirStat.WinDirStat` | disk-usage treemap |
| Everything | `voidtools.Everything` | instant filename search |
| ShareX | `ShareX.ShareX` | screenshots + screen recording |
| OBS Studio | `OBSProject.OBSStudio` | screen recording / streaming |
| VLC | `VideoLAN.VLC` | media player |
| Rufus | `Rufus.Rufus` | bootable USB creator |
| Tailscale | `Tailscale.Tailscale` | mesh VPN |

!!! note "Launchers & the Alt+Space clash"
    **Raycast** (Microsoft Store, id `9PFXXSHC64H3`) is the default launcher.
    It shares **Alt+Space** with **PowerToys Run** — disable PowerToys Run
    (PowerToys Settings › PowerToys Run › off) or rebind one. Raycast for Windows
    is still a Store beta; if it won't install, fall back to
    [Flow Launcher](https://www.flowlauncher.com/):
    `winget install Flow-Launcher.Flow-Launcher`.

!!! note "Notepad++ is opt-in"
    Dropped from the default set: on Windows-on-ARM its installer is a
    low-reputation binary that Windows Defender / SmartScreen flags as PUA
    (a false positive, aggravated by managed-machine PUA protection), and it's
    redundant with VSCode / Cursor / nvim. Add it yourself if you want it:
    `winget install Notepad++.Notepad++` or `scoop install notepadplusplus`.

!!! note "Managed / corporate machines"
    The **Managed machine** init toggle skips apps that org policy commonly
    blocks — **Grammarly** and **Tailscale** (its MSI fails with exit `1625`
    under policy). Leave the toggle off on a personal machine to install them.

!!! note "Alacritty & Nerd Fonts (machine-wide install)"
    scoop's `nerd-fonts` bucket registers **Hack Nerd Font Mono** *per-user*
    (HKCU). Windows Terminal and WezTerm see per-user fonts, but **Alacritty on
    Windows reads only the machine-wide font collection**, so it can't find the
    font and falls back to a default. Fix (needs admin):
    `just install-fonts-machine-wide` (runs `scoop install -g Hack-NF-Mono Hack-NF`),
    then restart Alacritty. Diagnose the family name with
    `[System.Drawing.FontFamily]::Families.Name | Select-String Hack`.

## AI agents

Enabled by **Install coding agents**:

- **Claude Code** — `Anthropic.ClaudeCode` via **winget** (the native Windows
  build; distinct from `Anthropic.Claude`, the desktop app under GUI apps).
  Upgraded with `just upgrade-winget`, not npm.
- **OpenCode** (`opencode-ai`), **Codex** (`@openai/codex`), **Copilot CLI**
  (`@github/copilot`) — installed globally via **npm** (provided by the scoop `node`).
- **OpenCode Desktop** — GUI companion to the `opencode-ai` CLI, via scoop
  (`extras/opencode-desktop`).
- **claude-hud** — a statusline HUD that renders below the Claude Code prompt.
  Enabled in `~/.claude/settings.json` by a `run_onchange` merger
  (`.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl`) that
  additively deep-merges an overlay, preserving your live settings. The plugin
  self-installs from its marketplace on first launch and runs on the scoop
  `bun`/`node` runtime; the merger also enables the `pyright-lsp` plugin and sets
  `permissions.defaultMode: auto` + `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`. **Restart
  Claude Code** after `chezmoi apply` to see the HUD. See
  [running multiple agents](claude-code-agents.md).

The official **ChatGPT** desktop app installs via the Microsoft Store (see GUI
apps); **Codex** is the `@openai/codex` npm CLI above, not a Store app. SpecStory
has no native-Windows CLI package, so it's omitted here.

## PowerShell modules (PSGallery)

- **PSFzf** — fzf key bindings (Ctrl+t files, Ctrl+r history).
- **AudioDeviceCmdlets** — absolute volume + mute for the `sysvol`/`sysmute` helpers.

## Opt-in dev stacks

Off by default; enable the matching init prompt:

| Toggle | Installs |
|---|---|
| Local LLM tools | Ollama (`Ollama.Ollama`) + LiteLLM (`uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'`) |
| Tunnel tools | ngrok, cloudflared (scoop) |
| IaC tools | Terraform, OpenTofu (scoop) + Azure CLI & the `azure-devops` extension (`az devops`/`az repos`, winget) |
| OpenSSH server | Microsoft OpenSSH Server (sshd): Windows capability + auto-start service + inbound TCP 22 firewall rule, with pwsh as the default shell. Needs admin — set up on an elevated `chezmoi apply`, or run `just enable-sshd` from an elevated pwsh. |
| herdr multiplexer | herdr, a native Windows terminal multiplexer (**preview beta**). No scoop/winget manifest — installs via herdr.dev's `irm \| iex` script; config managed at `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (pwsh as the default shell). See [rationale](rationale.md#terminal-multiplexer-wezterm-stable-default-herdr-native-beta). |
| Clink (cmd.exe) | [Clink](https://chrisant996.github.io/clink/) (scoop `main`) — Bash-style line editing for `cmd.exe`, so **starship** + **zoxide** + **fzf** work in the DOS prompt. Reuses the shared `starship.toml`; registers a per-user cmd AutoRun, deploys our `starship.lua`, and fetches the community `clink-zoxide` / `clink-fzf` bridges into `%LocalAppData%\clink`. pwsh stays the default — this is an opt-in secondary shell with prompt + nav parity only. See [rationale](rationale.md#powershell-7-default-cmdexe-optional-via-clink) & [Shell](shell.md#cmdexe-via-clink). |

**China mirrors** routes pip / npm / cargo / go / node package fetches through GFW
mirrors (Tsinghua / npmmirror / goproxy.cn / rsproxy), applied both at install time
and in the interactive shell (`profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`).

## Television (tv) channels

Custom pickers under `%APPDATA%\television\cable\` (run `tv` to browse, or `tv <name>`):

| Channel | What |
|---|---|
| `aliases` | PowerShell aliases & functions (cached at shell startup) |
| `git-ops` | common git commands → Enter copies to clipboard |
| `ports` | listening TCP ports → Ctrl+K kills the owning process |
| `kill-process` | processes by memory → Enter/Ctrl+K kill, Ctrl+D force-kill |
| `scoop-apps` | installed scoop apps → Enter info, Ctrl+U update, Ctrl+X uninstall |
| `apps` | launch an app from Start Menu shortcuts |
| `channels` | browse every tv channel by description → Enter opens the selected one |

## Upgrades

Install and upgrade are separate. `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing;
upgrades are explicit:

```powershell
just upgrade-scoop     # scoop update *
just upgrade-winget    # winget upgrade --all
```
{
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "claude-hud@claude-hud": true,
    "pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official": true
  },
  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
    "claude-hud": {
      "source": {
        "source": "github",
        "repo": "jarrodwatts/claude-hud"
      }
    }
  },
  "skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true,
  "permissions": {
    "defaultMode": "auto"
  },
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case \"$cols\" in \"\"|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size </dev/tty 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}');; esac; case \"$cols\" in \"\"|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -1d \"${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}\"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); exec \"$(command -v node)\" \"${plugin_dir}dist/index.js\""
  }
}
```

+

+

+

## Verified upstream findings as of 2026-08-17

### Latest verifiable version

The latest verifiable upstream `claude-hud` release is **`v0.7.1`**.

- [Official latest releases page](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/releases/latest)
- [Release `v0.7.1`](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/releases/tag/v0.7.1)
- The current repository manifest also declares version `0.7.1`: [` .claude-plugin/plugin.json`, lines 1–4](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/blob/main/.claude-plugin/plugin.json#L1-L4)

The repository’s current manifest and release page agree on `0.7.1`; I found no authoritative upstream evidence of a newer release.

### What “all features” means

Upstream uses **Full** as the preset described as:

> “Everything enabled (Recommended)”

The README/configuration documentation expands that to:

> “tools, agents, todos, git, usage, duration”

Sources:

- [README — Presets](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/blob/main/README.md#presets)
- [`commands/configure.md`](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/blob/main/commands/configure.md)

This refers to the HUD’s **display feature preset**. It does not mean:

- the plugin installation process automatically runs setup;
- Claude Code automatically invokes `/claude-hud:setup`;
- every optional setting, such as a custom line, is enabled;
- a timer refresh interval is necessarily configured.

The setup documentation separately identifies optional display settings such as:

- `display.showTools`
- `display.showAgents`
- `display.showTodos`
- `display.showDuration`
- `display.showConfigCounts`
- `display.showSessionName`
- `display.customLine`

See [`commands/setup.md`](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/blob/main/commands/setup.md), under **“Configure optional HUD features.”**

### Does enabling the plugin plus `statusLine` automatically run setup?

**No.**

The upstream plugin manifest registers only two commands:

```json
"commands": [
  "./commands/setup.md",
  "./commands/configure.md"
]
```

See [` .claude-plugin/plugin.json`, lines 9–12](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/blob/main/.claude-plugin/plugin.json#L9-L12).

There is no setup hook in that manifest. Consequently:

- enabling `claude-hud` makes its commands available;
- configuring Claude Code’s `statusLine` makes Claude Code execute the configured status-line command;
- neither action invokes the slash command `/claude-hud:setup`.

Upstream explicitly instructs users to run setup as a separate step:

```text
/plugin marketplace add jarrodwatts/claude-hud
/plugin install claude-hud
/reload-plugins
/claude-hud:setup
```

Sources:

- [README — Install](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/blob/main/README.md#install)
- [`commands/setup.md`](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/blob/main/commands/setup.md)
- [Claude Code plugin reference — plugin enable](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-enable)
- [Claude Code plugin reference — skills and commands](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#skills)

A pre-existing, correctly generated `statusLine` command can therefore make the HUD work without running setup, but it does not reproduce setup’s other side effects.

### Exactly what `/claude-hud:setup` writes

The current setup procedure can write or create the following.

#### 1. Claude settings

It backs up the existing settings file before modification, then merges a `statusLine` object into:

```text
${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json
```

The core object is:

```json
{
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "{GENERATED_COMMAND}"
  }
}
```

It preserves unrelated settings rather than replacing the whole file.

On current Claude Code versions, settings reload automatically; the HUD normally appears after the next interaction. A restart is documented only as a fallback.

#### 2. Optional refresh interval

If selected, setup adds:

```json
"refreshInterval": 5
```

Upstream recommends **5 seconds**. The documented minimum is **1 second**. If the user explicitly chooses no timer, setup removes `refreshInterval`.

Source: [README — Auto-Refresh](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/blob/main/README.md#auto-refresh)

#### 3. Windows launcher

On Windows, setup creates:

```text
$claudeDir/plugins/claude-hud/statusline.mjs
```

It writes the file as UTF-8 without a BOM. The launcher:

- uses the detected absolute `node.exe` path;
- searches all marketplace-aware cache locations;
- selects the highest available semantic-version directory containing `dist\index.js`;
- dynamically imports that version;
- calls the plugin’s `main()` function.

The generated `statusLine.command` invokes the launcher through `cmd.exe` using this template:

```text
{CMD_PATH} /d /s /c ""{RUNTIME_PATH}" "{WRAPPER_PATH}""
```

Source: [`commands/setup.md`](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/blob/main/commands/setup.md), under **“Windows + PowerShell”**.

#### 4. Optional HUD configuration

If optional features are selected, setup merges them into:

```text
$claudeDir/plugins/claude-hud/config.json
```

It writes only selected keys and does not create the file when no optional features are selected. It does not write explicit `false` values for unselected features.

#### 5. Backups and status-line preservation

Depending on the existing state, setup also creates:

```text
settings.json.bak.YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS
```

If it replaces an existing non-HUD status line, it saves the previous command privately as:

```text
plugins/claude-hud/previous-statusline.txt
```

The setup procedure also contains “ghost installation” repair logic. If that path is used, it can modify `installed_plugins.json`; that is cleanup behavior, not part of ordinary HUD setup.

### Current recommended `statusLine` command

The current upstream recommendation is **not** a hard-coded path to one cached version.

The generated command should dynamically locate the newest installed `claude-hud` version. This is important because Claude Code’s marketplace cache is versioned and marketplace-aware.

Platform behavior documented in [`commands/setup.md`](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/blob/main/commands/setup.md):

- **macOS/Linux + Bun:** locate the newest cached version and invoke `src/index.ts` with Bun, including `--env-file /dev/null`.
- **macOS/Linux + Node:** locate the newest cached version and invoke `dist/index.js`.
- **Windows Git Bash:** locate the newest cached version and invoke `dist/index.js` with Node.
- **Windows PowerShell:** invoke the generated BOM-free `statusline.mjs` wrapper through `cmd.exe`.

The practical recommended settings shape is therefore:

```json
{
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "<setup-generated dynamic launcher>",
    "refreshInterval": 5
  }
}
```

Do not replace `<setup-generated dynamic launcher>` with a permanent path containing a specific version directory unless you deliberately accept having to update it after every plugin upgrade.

### Why the plugin cache may appear only after Claude Code launches

Claude Code intentionally copies marketplace plugins into its local cache rather than using the marketplace source directly:

```text
~/.claude/plugins/cache
```

The official Claude Code documentation states that cached copies are created:

- when a plugin is installed;
- when Claude Code updates it;
- **at session start when an enabled plugin is not cached yet**, such as on a new machine.

Source: [Claude Code plugin reference — Plugin caching and file resolution](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-caching-and-file-resolution)

This explains the apparent ordering:

1. Plugin enablement or settings deployment records that `claude-hud` should be enabled.
2. No cached plugin directory may exist yet.
3. The first Claude Code launch detects the enabled-but-uncached plugin.
4. Claude Code materializes the marketplace plugin under `~/.claude/plugins/cache`.
5. The setup-generated dynamic status-line launcher can then find the cached version.

Thus, “enabled” and “present in the plugin cache” are not necessarily simultaneous states. The cache can be lazy and session-start materialized. A status-line command that searches the cache may have no executable target before the first Claude Code launch, even though the plugin is already enabled.

## Bottom line

- **Latest upstream version verifiable:** `v0.7.1`.
- **“All features”:** the Full preset—tools, agents, todos, git, usage, and duration.
- **Plugin + `statusLine` does not run `/claude-hud:setup`.**
- **Setup writes:** a merged `settings.json` status-line entry, optional `refreshInterval`, platform-specific launcher on Windows, optional `plugins/claude-hud/config.json`, and backups when applicable.
- **Recommended command:** the setup-generated dynamic launcher that resolves the newest cached plugin version at runtime.
- **Cache timing:** Claude Code may materialize an enabled marketplace plugin only at session start, which is why the cache can appear only after launching Claude Code.

The overlay was intended to enable the default claude-hud status-line experience, not to manage individual HUD display options:

Consequently, the overlay enables whatever claude-hud’s own defaults provide and leaves detailed user customization unmanaged. In current upstream defaults, model/context/usage/token-breakdown displays are enabled, while tools, Skills, MCP, agents, and todos require configuration.

### 2. Why SpecStory uses `create_config.toml`

`private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml` maps to private, create-only `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`.

The file’s own contract is user ownership:

- `private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:3-7` defines it as user-level global defaults and establishes precedence: project settings override it, and CLI flags override both.
- `private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:9-11` invites the user to uncomment and edit settings.

That divergence also shows that the create-only baseline is now older than the project sample: it lacks `[resume]` and `deepseek_cmd`. That is expected under seed-once semantics; updating the source does not retrofit existing targets.

#### Why not a plain managed file?

A plain managed file would overwrite the user’s global defaults and provider customization on each apply, contradicting both:

- the comments at `private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:3-11`, and
- the commit’s explicit use of the word “seed.”

The repository uses the same ownership model elsewhere: `README.md:54,61-67` describes the create-only SSH skeleton and states that an existing target is never overwritten.

#### Why not `modify_`?

`docs/rationale.md:133-159` explains the Windows limitation:

- `docs/rationale.md:143-150`: chezmoi routes a modifier using the target extension. A modifier targeting `config.toml` routes as TOML, not PowerShell.
- Windows cannot rely on a Unix shebang or executable bit.
- `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:61-64` only configures the `.ps1` interpreter.

Thus a PowerShell `modify_config.toml` is not a reliable native-Windows mechanism.

#### Why not a `run_onchange` merger?

A `run_onchange` merger would be technically viable, but its semantics would differ. The repository reserves these mergers for surfaces where it deliberately owns selected keys while preserving surrounding runtime state; see `docs/rationale.md:135-159`.

The SpecStory introduction did not claim such ongoing ownership. It explicitly seeded a user-editable configuration. A merger is justified only if the provider commands are reclassified as enforced repository policy.

**Keep `create_` under the current contract.**

This best matches the commit history, precedence comments, and security implications of the active provider commands:

- `cursor-agent --force`
- `droid --yolo`

These commands define user security posture, not merely cosmetic defaults. Existing user changes should not be silently reasserted by dotfiles.

   - Preserves all post-seed customization.
   - Matches `8f64d91`’s stated intent.
   - Allows project config and CLI flags to override naturally.

2. **If provider commands become explicit managed policy: use a key-level `run_onchange` PowerShell merger.**

## Claude HUD: we did **not** enable the Full preset

The managed overlay currently does only three things:

1. Registers the marketplace.
2. Enables `claude-hud@claude-hud`.
3. Writes a working `statusLine.command`.

See [`claude/settings-overlay.json:2-20`](claude/settings-overlay.json#L2-L20).

It does **not** create Claude HUD’s separate configuration file:

```text
~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json
```

Because that file is absent, HUD 0.7.1 uses its conservative defaults. Those show model/project/context/usage/git, but disable many elements such as:

- tools, skills, MCP activity
- agents and todos
- cost and duration
- session metadata
- memory and prompt-cache information
- compactions, advisor, and several other indicators

The Full preset is defined in the installed plugin at:

```text
~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-hud/claude-hud/0.7.1/commands/configure.md:246-252
```

### Why setup did not run automatically

Plugin enablement does not execute plugin slash commands. The plugin manifest only **registers** `setup` and `configure`; it has no startup hook that runs them:

```text
~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-hud/claude-hud/0.7.1/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:9-12
```

Our implementation intentionally copied the important output of `/claude-hud:setup`—the `statusLine` value—into the chezmoi overlay. It never invokes the setup command itself; the settings merger only edits JSON at [`run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl:138-172`](.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl#L138-L172).

There is also a first-launch ordering issue:

1. Claude reads `enabledPlugins`.
2. Claude materializes the plugin cache during startup.
3. The status line may run before that cache is ready.
4. The current session does not reload the settings/plugin afterward.

That explains why a second Claude launch was required.

### Is 0.7.1 old?

No. Installed `0.7.1` is also the latest verifiable upstream release:

- Installed commit: `e479926c7908b12aec04c54fac6d213b0711fa43`
- Latest release: [jarrodwatts/claude-hud v0.7.1](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/releases/latest)

Our status-line wrapper is slightly behind the latest setup script’s diagnostics, backup behavior, and optional `refreshInterval`, but its actual architecture remains current:

- discovers the latest cached version
- runs `dist/index.js` through Node
- supports `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`
- handles terminal width
- uses Git Bash on this Windows/Cygwin environment

So this is **not a version problem**. It is an incomplete declarative setup: working HUD entrypoint, but no Full display configuration.

### Recommended HUD ownership

Keep chezmoi authoritative rather than running `/claude-hud:setup`, because setup would rewrite `statusLine`, and the next `chezmoi apply` would overwrite it again.

I recommend:

- Continue managing `statusLine` through the existing Claude settings overlay.
- Add a separate deep-merged HUD config overlay for:
  ```text
  ~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json
  ```
- Encode the **Full preset** there while preserving advanced/manual user settings that the overlay does not own.
- Optionally add `statusLine.refreshInterval`.
- Make the status-line command no-op cleanly when the plugin cache is temporarily absent, rather than accidentally running `node dist/index.js` from the current directory.

For a temporary local change, `/claude-hud:configure` → **Full** would work, but the durable dotfiles solution should manage that preset.

## SpecStory: why `create_` was used

It was intentional. Commit history shows the file was introduced as a **one-time seed** for a user-owned config:

[`private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:3-11`](private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml#L3-L11)

Most of the file consists of commented options that the user is expected to customize. `create_` means:

- create `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` when absent;
- never overwrite an existing file;
- preserve cloud sync, logging, analytics, telemetry, resume state, custom providers, and future SpecStory fields.

That is normally the correct policy for a user configuration file.

### Why it failed here

The provider commands at [`create_config.toml:65-83`](private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml#L65-L83) are different from ordinary preferences. They establish behavior relied upon by our wrappers, including:

```toml
claude_cmd = "claude --dangerously-skip-permissions"
```

Because the live config existed before chezmoi tried to seed it, `create_` did nothing. The source said bypass should be enabled, but the live file retained SpecStory’s plain commented defaults.

So we mixed two incompatible ownership models in one file:

- most fields are user-owned preferences;
- provider launch commands are intended dotfiles policy.

### Should we override the SpecStory config?

**Not the whole file.** A plain managed file would repeatedly erase:

- `[local_sync]` and `[cloud_sync]` choices
- telemetry/logging preferences
- CLI-managed `[resume]` state
- custom provider commands
- new fields introduced by future SpecStory versions

Instead, use a **key-level overlay** that owns only selected `[providers]` keys and pulls everything else through unchanged.

Recommended behavior:

```text
Live config
  + enforce providers.claude_cmd
  + optionally enforce the other provider commands already active in our seed
  + preserve every other table, key, comment, and unknown provider
```

Because PowerShell `modify_` routing for a `.toml` target is unreliable on Windows, this should be a fail-closed `run_onchange` PowerShell merger, following the existing Claude/Codex/herdr patterns.

I would also harden `claude-copilot` itself so its documented bypass behavior does not depend solely on external SpecStory configuration. The wrapper should ensure its generated `-c` command contains `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, while direct `specstory run claude` can still follow the managed provider key.

## Recommended change set

1. **HUD**
   - Manage the Full-preset `config.json` as an overlay.
   - Preserve advanced user-only HUD settings.
   - Make missing plugin cache a clean temporary no-op.
   - Update stale Bun wording in [`docs/tools.md:157-164`](docs/tools.md#L157-L164).

2. **SpecStory**
   - Replace seed-only ownership for provider commands with a key-level run-onchange merger.
   - Preserve all non-provider settings and unknown keys.
   - Harden `claude-copilot` to enforce its own bypass contract.
   - Add tests for stale, absent, customized, and future-expanded TOML files.

A full-file SpecStory override is not recommended; a targeted overlay is.

- `docs/tools.md:157-164` continues to describe the result as a HUD below the prompt, deployed through the settings merger.

There is no managed `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json` equivalent in this repository. Consequently, the overlay enables whatever claude-hud’s own defaults provide and leaves detailed user customization unmanaged. In current upstream defaults, model/context/usage/token-breakdown displays are enabled, while tools, Skills, MCP, agents, and todos require configuration.

#### Setup command bypass

It intentionally bypasses executing `/claude-hud:setup`, but does so by reproducing setup’s output:

- `.claude/plans/snazzy-painting-wilkes.md:20-22` explicitly says claude-hud’s Windows setup-generated `statusLine` was “what we port.”
- `.claude/plans/snazzy-painting-wilkes.md:24-26` says chezmoi should merge that configuration directly so the HUD appears after restart.
- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl:2-15` explains why the repository manages this as an overlay rather than as a static settings file.
- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl:19-25,90-109,138-151` embeds the overlay, recursively merges it, respects `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and preserves unrelated runtime state.

Therefore, this is not an accidental omission of setup. It is declarative ownership of the same `statusLine` key that setup would write. Running upstream setup afterward would merely let another writer replace that key.

#### History and current staleness

Relevant commits:

- `fc936fa` — 2026-07-12, `feat(claude): deploy claude-hud via a run_onchange settings merger`
  - Introduced the overlay and merger.

### 2. Why SpecStory uses `create_config.toml`

`private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml` maps to private, create-only `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`.

The file’s own contract is user ownership:

- `private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:3-7` defines it as user-level global defaults and establishes precedence: project settings override it, and CLI flags override both.
- `private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:9-11` invites the user to uncomment and edit settings.
- Most of `:13-63` is a commented customization template.
- Only the provider commands at `:65-83` are active defaults.

The history is unambiguous:

- `8f64d91` — 2026-07-09, `feat: parity toggles, Docker/Discord, mirrors, backup, agent-skill junction`
  - Commit message: “SpecStory: seed `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` (`private_ create_`) mirroring the main repo’s provider commands.”
  - `git blame` attributes all 83 lines to this commit.
  - No subsequent commit modified the global seed.
- `463e8be` — 2026-07-10, `Backup chat history and plan`
  - Added project-local `.specstory/cli/config.toml`.
  - `.specstory/cli/config.toml:1-7` identifies it as project-level.
  - `.specstory/cli/config.toml:61-67` contains runtime-oriented resume state.
  - `.specstory/cli/config.toml:69-90` leaves provider commands commented and adds DeepSeek.

That divergence also shows that the create-only baseline is now older than the project sample: it lacks `[resume]` and `deepseek_cmd`. That is expected under seed-once semantics; updating the source does not retrofit existing targets.

#### Why not a plain managed file?

A plain managed file would overwrite the user’s global defaults and provider customization on each apply, contradicting both:

- the comments at `private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:3-11`, and
- the commit’s explicit use of the word “seed.”

The repository uses the same ownership model elsewhere: `README.md:54,61-67` describes the create-only SSH skeleton and states that an existing target is never overwritten.

#### Why not `modify_`?

`docs/rationale.md:133-159` explains the Windows limitation:

- `docs/rationale.md:143-150`: chezmoi routes a modifier using the target extension. A modifier targeting `config.toml` routes as TOML, not PowerShell.
- Windows cannot rely on a Unix shebang or executable bit.
- `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:61-64` only configures the `.ps1` interpreter.

Thus a PowerShell `modify_config.toml` is not a reliable native-Windows mechanism.

#### Why not a `run_onchange` merger?

A `run_onchange` merger would be technically viable, but its semantics would differ. The repository reserves these mergers for surfaces where it deliberately owns selected keys while preserving surrounding runtime state; see `docs/rationale.md:135-159`.

The SpecStory introduction did not claim such ongoing ownership. It explicitly seeded a user-editable configuration. A merger is justified only if the provider commands are reclassified as enforced repository policy.

### 3. Recommendation

**Keep `create_` under the current contract.**

This best matches the commit history, precedence comments, and security implications of the active provider commands:

- `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`
- Codex with `--ask-for-approval never --sandbox danger-full-access`
- `cursor-agent --force`
- `droid --yolo`
- `gemini --sandbox=none`

These commands define user security posture, not merely cosmetic defaults. Existing user changes should not be silently reasserted by dotfiles.

Recommended order:

1. **Current recommendation: keep `create_`.**
   - Preserves all post-seed customization.
   - Matches `8f64d91`’s stated intent.
   - Allows project config and CLI flags to override naturally.

2. **If provider commands become explicit managed policy: use a key-level `run_onchange` PowerShell merger.**
   - Own only `[providers].claude_cmd`, `codex_cmd`, `cursor_cmd`, `droid_cmd`, and `gemini_cmd`.
   - Preserve every other section and unknown provider, including `[resume]` and DeepSeek.
   - Make overlay-wins behavior and its security implications explicit, preferably behind an opt-in toggle.

3. **Do not use a plain managed override.**
   - It would erase user/runtime additions wholesale.

4. **Do not use `modify_` on Windows.**
   - The repository’s documented interpreter-routing limitation applies directly to a TOML target.

# dotfiles-windows

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)

## Orientation
- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).

## Shell layout (pwsh)
- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).

## Packages
- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.

## copilot-proxy
- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`,
  `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`), `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
  `copilot-here` writes
  only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The pinned copilot-api is

# dotfiles-windows

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —

(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)

## Orientation
- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).

## Shell layout (pwsh)
- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).

## Packages
- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.

## copilot-proxy
- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`,
  `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`), `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
  `copilot-here` writes
  only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The pinned copilot-api is
  installed ONCE into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg` (never `bunx` at launch);
  `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls whether Node fetches the
  GitHub model catalog through the local proxy. Full guide: `docs/copilot-proxy.md`.

1	#Requires -Version 7
2	# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1 — merge a managed overlay into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json so claude-hud (statusline HUD), the pyright-lsp
4	# plugin, and a couple of safe defaults deploy on Windows. Companion to the
5	# parent (macOS/Linux) repo's dot_claude/modify_settings.json; that repo uses a
6	# `modify_` + jq merge, which is unreliable on Windows (invariant #5), so we use
7	# the same run_onchange pwsh-merger idiom as the editor overlays instead.
8	#
9	# Why a merge (not a managed dot_claude/settings.json)? Claude Code rewrites
10	# this file at runtime (plugins it installs, permissions the user grants). A
11	# static managed file would clobber all of that on every apply. We instead
12	# recursively deep-merge only our keys in, preserving every live key.
13	#
14	# Gated on installCodingAgents — no Claude Code, nothing to configure. Re-runs
15	# when the embedded overlay (claude/settings-overlay.json) changes.
16	{{ if .installCodingAgents -}}
17	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'   # best-effort; never abort the apply
18	
19	# Embedded at render time from the (chezmoi-ignored) claude/ source, so this
20	# script is self-contained and re-fires when the overlay changes.
21	$overlayJson = @'
22	{{ include "claude/settings-overlay.json" }}
23	'@
24	
25	$overlay = $overlayJson | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable
26	
27	# --- Completion-feedback hooks, gated on `agentSounds` -----------------------
28	#
29	# Built here rather than in claude/settings-overlay.json because that file is
30	# `include`d verbatim and so cannot carry Go-template conditionals.
31	#
32	# `notify` wires notify.ps1 (apprise -> Windows toast); `peon` wires peon-ping's
33	# game voice lines. Values lifted from a real peon-ping install.ps1 (verified
34	# against upstream source, NOT its README — the README's documented command
35	# shape is wrong on the POSIX side too). Windows specifics that differ from the
36	# macOS/Linux parent repo:
37	#   - command is `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File "<peon.ps1>"`
38	#   - `timeout = 10`, and there is NO `async` field
39	#   - the event set includes PreToolUse and has NO UserPromptSubmit
40	# Parent repo equivalent: dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl.
41	{{- $peon   := or (eq .agentSounds "peon")   (eq .agentSounds "both") }}
42	{{- $notify := or (eq .agentSounds "notify") (eq .agentSounds "both") }}
43	$notifyCmd = 'exec pwsh -NoProfile -File "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hooks/notify.ps1"'
44	# peon-ping is installed with `-OpenPeon`, which reroots its whole tree at the
45	# tool-agnostic ~/.openpeon — so peon.ps1 is NOT under ~/.claude/hooks/.
46	# Wrapped in a Test-Path guard so the hook is a silent no-op on a box where the
47	# install hasn't run (or failed): an unguarded `-File <missing>` makes Claude
48	# Code surface a hook error on every event. Mirrors the mandatory
49	# `command -v workmux` / `[ -x ... ]` guards in the parent repo.
50	$peonPs1   = Join-Path $HOME '.openpeon\hooks\peon-ping\peon.ps1'
51	$peonCmd   = "powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command `"if (Test-Path '$peonPs1') { & '$peonPs1' }`""
52	
53	# Event -> the commands that should be wired for the current tier.
54	$soundHooks = @{}
55	{{- if $notify }}
56	foreach ($evt in @('Notification', 'Stop')) {
57	    $soundHooks[$evt] = @(@{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $notifyCmd }) })
58	}
59	{{- end }}
60	{{- if $peon }}
61	foreach ($evt in @('SessionStart', 'SessionEnd', 'SubagentStart', 'Stop',
62	                   'Notification', 'PermissionRequest', 'PreToolUse',
63	                   'PostToolUseFailure', 'PreCompact')) {
64	    $entry = @{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $peonCmd; timeout = 10 }) }
65	    if ($soundHooks.ContainsKey($evt)) { $soundHooks[$evt] = @($soundHooks[$evt] + $entry) }
66	    else                               { $soundHooks[$evt] = @($entry) }
67	}
68	{{- end }}
69	if ($soundHooks.Count -gt 0) {
70	    if ($overlay['hooks'] -isnot [hashtable]) { $overlay['hooks'] = @{} }
71	    foreach ($evt in $soundHooks.Keys) { $overlay['hooks'][$evt] = $soundHooks[$evt] }
72	}
73	
74	# Commands the CURRENT tier disables — pruned from the live file below. Without
75	# this the additive merge makes agentSounds a one-way ratchet: switching
76	# notify -> none would leave notify.ps1 wired forever, so `none` would not
77	# actually silence a machine that previously had sound. Only OUR OWN
78	# fingerprints are listed, so foreign hook entries can never be touched.
79	# (Upstream's own install.ps1 strips `peon\.(ps1|sh)` / `notify\.sh` the same
80	# way before re-adding, so this matches its behaviour.)
81	$prunePatterns = @(
82	{{- if not $notify }}
83	    'notify\.ps1'
84	{{- end }}
85	{{- if not $peon }}
86	    'peon\.ps1'
87	{{- end }}
88	)
89	
90	# Recursive deep-merge: overlay leaves win; live-only keys are preserved. Unlike
91	# the editor overlay's shallow top-level assign, this keeps the user's nested
92	# state (e.g. permissions.allow/deny arrays, other enabledPlugins) intact.
93	#
94	# The `hooks` object gets special, ADDITIVE handling (see Merge-ClaudeHooks) so
95	# our Notification/Stop notify entries are appended without clobbering hook
96	# entries the user or other tools added. Every other array value is still
97	# replaced wholesale (overlay wins), which is what we want for scalars/plugins.
98	function Merge-Hashtable([hashtable]$base, [hashtable]$overlay) {
99	    foreach ($k in $overlay.Keys) {
100	        if ($k -eq 'hooks' -and ($overlay[$k] -is [hashtable])) {
101	            if ($base[$k] -isnot [hashtable]) { $base[$k] = @{} }
102	            Merge-ClaudeHooks $base[$k] $overlay[$k]
103	        }
104	        elseif ($base.ContainsKey($k) -and ($base[$k] -is [hashtable]) -and ($overlay[$k] -is [hashtable])) {
105	            Merge-Hashtable $base[$k] $overlay[$k]
106	        }
107	        else {
108	            $base[$k] = $overlay[$k]
109	        }
110	    }
111	}
112	
113	# Additive per-event hook merge, mirroring the parent repo's jq reduce in
114	# dot_claude/modify_settings.json: for each event, append only the overlay
115	# entries whose .hooks[0].command isn't already present in the live array,
116	# preserving live entries verbatim. Wholesale-replacing the arrays (the old
117	# behavior) would drop hooks the user / other tools add at runtime. @(...) also
118	# forces array shape so ConvertTo-Json emits a JSON array even for a single
119	# entry (Claude requires hooks.<event> to be an array).
120	function Merge-ClaudeHooks([hashtable]$base, [hashtable]$overlay) {
121	    foreach ($evt in $overlay.Keys) {
122	        # NB: plain two-line assign, NOT `$live = if (...) { @(..) } else { @() }`.
123	        # A single-element @() flowing out of an if-EXPRESSION gets unwrapped back
124	        # to a scalar (here a hashtable), so `$live + $additions` then throws
125	        # "A hash table can only be added to another hash table". Direct `= @(...)`
126	        # keeps the array shape.
127	        $live = @()
128	        if ($null -ne $base[$evt]) { $live = @($base[$evt]) }
129	        $liveCmds = @($live | ForEach-Object { $_.hooks[0].command })
130	        $additions = @($overlay[$evt] | Where-Object {
131	            $cmd = $_.hooks[0].command
132	            (-not $cmd) -or ($liveCmds -notcontains $cmd)
133	        })
134	        $base[$evt] = @($live + $additions)
135	    }
136	}
137	
138	# Respect CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (matches the statusLine command + claude-hud setup).
139	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME '.claude' }
140	$settingsPath = Join-Path $claudeDir 'settings.json'
141	
142	$settings = @{}
143	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
144	    $raw = Get-Content -Raw $settingsPath
145	    if ($raw.Trim()) {
146	        try { $settings = $raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable }
147	        catch { Write-Warning "could not parse $settingsPath; not overwriting"; return }
148	    }
149	}
150	
151	Merge-Hashtable $settings $overlay
152	
153	# Prune our own now-disabled entries (see $prunePatterns above). Runs AFTER the
154	# additive merge so a tier that re-enables something wins. Foreign entries are
155	# never matched. Event keys whose array empties out are removed so turning
156	# everything off doesn't leave `"SessionStart": []` litter behind.
157	if ($prunePatterns.Count -gt 0 -and $settings['hooks'] -is [hashtable]) {
158	    foreach ($evt in @($settings['hooks'].Keys)) {
159	        $kept = @(@($settings['hooks'][$evt]) | Where-Object {
160	            $cmd = $_.hooks[0].command
161	            if (-not $cmd) { return $true }
162	            foreach ($p in $prunePatterns) { if ($cmd -match $p) { return $false } }
163	            return $true
164	        })
165	        if ($kept.Count -gt 0) { $settings['hooks'][$evt] = $kept }
166	        else                   { $settings['hooks'].Remove($evt) }
167	    }
168	}
169	
170	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $claudeDir | Out-Null
171	$settings | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12 | Set-Content -Path $settingsPath -Encoding utf8
172	Write-Host "claude overlay -> $settingsPath"
173	{{ end -}}
174
```

387	function validateAutocompactBuffer(value: unknown): value is AutocompactBufferMode {
388	  return value === 'enabled' || value === 'disabled';

392	  return value === 'truncate' || value === 'wrap';
393	}

396	  return value === 'percent' || value === 'tokens' || value === 'remaining' || value === 'both';
397	}

399	function validateUsageValue(value: unknown): value is UsageValueMode {
400	  return value === 'percent' || value === 'remaining';
401	}

403	function validateLanguage(value: unknown): value is Language {
404	  return value === 'en' || value === 'zh' || value === 'zh-Hans' || value === 'zh-Hant' || value === 'zh-TW';
405	}
406	
407	function validateModelFormat(value: unknown): value is ModelFormatMode {
408	  return value === 'full' || value === 'compact' || value === 'short';
409	}

411	function validateTimeFormat(value: unknown): value is TimeFormatMode {
412	  return value === 'relative'
413	    || value === 'absolute'
414	    || value === 'both'
415	    || value === 'elapsed'
416	    || value === 'elapsedAndAbsolute';

420	  return value === 'first' || value === 'last';

425	}

427	function validateColorName(value: unknown): value is HudColorName {
428	  return value === 'dim'
429	    || value === 'red'
430	    || value === 'green'
431	    || value === 'yellow'
432	    || value === 'magenta'
433	    || value === 'cyan'
434	    || value === 'brightBlue'
435	    || value === 'brightMagenta';
436	}
437	
438	const UNSAFE_CODEPOINT = /[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Variation_Selector}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Cn}]/u;
439	
440	function validateBarChar(value: unknown): value is string {
441	  if (typeof value !== 'string' || value.length === 0) return false;
442	
443	  const segmenter = new Intl.Segmenter(undefined, { granularity: 'grapheme' });
444	  if (Array.from(segmenter.segment(value)).length !== 1) return false;
445	
446	  for (const ch of value) {
447	    if (UNSAFE_CODEPOINT.test(ch)) return false;
448	  }
449	  return true;
450	}
451	
452	const HEX_COLOR_PATTERN = /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/;
453	
454	function validateColorValue(value: unknown): value is HudColorValue {
455	  if (validateColorName(value)) return true;
456	  if (typeof value === 'number' && Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0 && value <= 255) return true;
457	  if (typeof value === 'string' && HEX_COLOR_PATTERN.test(value)) return true;
458	  return false;
459	}
460	
461	function validateElementOrder(value: unknown): HudElement[] {
462	  if (!Array.isArray(value) || value.length === 0) {
463	    return [...DEFAULT_ELEMENT_ORDER];
464	  }
465	
466	  const seen = new Set<HudElement>();
467	  const elementOrder: HudElement[] = [];
468	
469	  for (const item of value) {
470	    if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_ELEMENTS.has(item as HudElement)) {
471	      continue;
472	    }
473	
474	    const element = item as HudElement;
475	    if (seen.has(element)) {
476	      continue;
477	    }
478	
479	    seen.add(element);
480	    elementOrder.push(element);
481	  }
482	
483	  return elementOrder.length > 0 ? elementOrder : [...DEFAULT_ELEMENT_ORDER];
484	}
485	
486	// Unlike `elementOrder`, `projectLineOrder` only reorders segments. A partial
487	// list is preserved as a requested prefix; each renderer appends all remaining
488	// visible parts in its own existing order.
489	function validateProjectLineOrder(value: unknown): FirstLineSegment[] {
490	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
491	    return [...DEFAULT_PROJECT_LINE_ORDER];
492	  }
493	
494	  const seen = new Set<FirstLineSegment>();
495	  const order: FirstLineSegment[] = [];
496	
497	  for (const item of value) {
498	    if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_FIRST_LINE_SEGMENTS.has(item as FirstLineSegment)) {
499	      continue;
500	    }
501	
502	    const segment = item as FirstLineSegment;
503	    if (seen.has(segment)) {
504	      continue;
505	    }
506	
507	    seen.add(segment);
508	    order.push(segment);
509	  }
510	
511	  return order;
512	}
513	
514	function validateRightAlign(value: unknown): HudElement[] {
515	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
516	    return [...DEFAULT_CONFIG.display.rightAlign];
517	  }
518	
519	  const seen = new Set<HudElement>();
520	  const elements: HudElement[] = [];
521	
522	  for (const item of value) {
523	    if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_ELEMENTS.has(item as HudElement)) {
524	      continue;
525	    }
526	
527	    const element = item as HudElement;
528	    if (seen.has(element)) {
529	      continue;
530	    }
531	
532	    seen.add(element);
533	    elements.push(element);
534	  }
535	
536	  return elements;
537	}
538	
539	function validateMergeGroups(value: unknown): HudElement[][] {
540	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
541	    return DEFAULT_MERGE_GROUPS.map(group => [...group]);
542	  }
543	
544	  if (value.length === 0) {
545	    return [];
546	  }
547	
548	  const usedElements = new Set<HudElement>();
549	  const mergeGroups: HudElement[][] = [];
550	
551	  for (const group of value) {
552	    if (!Array.isArray(group)) {
553	      continue;
554	    }
555	
556	    const seenInGroup = new Set<HudElement>();
557	    const normalizedGroup: HudElement[] = [];
558	    const pendingElements: HudElement[] = [];
559	
560	    for (const item of group) {
561	      if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_ELEMENTS.has(item as HudElement)) {
562	        continue;
563	      }
564	
565	      const element = item as HudElement;
566	      if (seenInGroup.has(element) || usedElements.has(element)) {
567	        continue;
568	      }
569	
570	      seenInGroup.add(element);
571	      normalizedGroup.push(element);
572	      pendingElements.push(element);
573	    }
574	
575	    if (normalizedGroup.length >= 2) {
576	      for (const element of pendingElements) {
577	        usedElements.add(element);
578	      }
579	      mergeGroups.push(normalizedGroup);
580	    }
581	  }
582	
583	  return mergeGroups.length > 0
584	    ? mergeGroups
585	    : DEFAULT_MERGE_GROUPS.map(group => [...group]);
586	}

588	interface LegacyConfig {
589	  layout?: 'default' | 'separators' | Record<string, unknown>;
590	}
591	
592	function migrateConfig(userConfig: Partial<HudConfig> & LegacyConfig): Partial<HudConfig> {
593	  const migrated = { ...userConfig } as Partial<HudConfig> & LegacyConfig;
594	
595	  if ('layout' in userConfig && !('lineLayout' in userConfig)) {
596	    if (typeof userConfig.layout === 'string') {
597	      // Legacy string migration (v0.0.x → v0.1.x)
598	      if (userConfig.layout === 'separators') {
599	        migrated.lineLayout = 'compact';
600	        migrated.showSeparators = true;
601	      } else {
602	        migrated.lineLayout = 'compact';
603	        migrated.showSeparators = false;
604	      }
605	    } else if (typeof userConfig.layout === 'object' && userConfig.layout !== null) {
606	      // Object layout written by third-party tools — extract nested fields
607	      const obj = userConfig.layout as Record<string, unknown>;
608	      if (typeof obj.lineLayout === 'string') migrated.lineLayout = obj.lineLayout as any;
609	      if (typeof obj.showSeparators === 'boolean') migrated.showSeparators = obj.showSeparators;
610	      if (typeof obj.pathLevels === 'number' || obj.pathLevels === 'full') migrated.pathLevels = obj.pathLevels as any;
611	    }
612	    delete migrated.layout;
613	  }
614	
615	  return migrated;
616	}

618	function validateThreshold(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
619	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) return fallback;
620	  return Math.max(0, Math.min(100, value));
621	}
622	
623	function validateContextThreshold(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
624	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) return fallback;
625	  return Math.max(0, Math.min(100, value));
626	}
627	
628	function validateCountThreshold(value: unknown): number {
629	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) {
630	    return 0;
631	  }
632	  return Math.max(0, Math.floor(value));
633	}
634	
635	function validateDurationSeconds(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
636	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0) {
637	    return fallback;
638	  }
639	  return Math.floor(value);
640	}
641	
642	function validateNonNegativeInteger(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
643	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(value) || value < 0) {
644	    return fallback;
645	  }
646	  return value;
647	}
648	
649	function validateAutoCompactWindow(value: unknown): number | null {
650	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) || !Number.isInteger(value) || value <= 0) {
651	    return null;
652	  }
653	  return value;
654	}
655	
656	function validateOptionalPath(value: unknown): string {
657	  return typeof value === 'string' ? value.trim() : '';
658	}
659	
660	function validateFreshnessMs(value: unknown): number {
661	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) {
662	    return DEFAULT_CONFIG.display.externalUsageFreshnessMs;
663	  }
664	  return Math.max(0, Math.floor(value));
665	}

20	
21	export function getClaudeConfigJsonPath(homeDir: string): string {
22	  return `${getClaudeConfigDir(homeDir)}.json`;
23	}
24	
25	export function getHudPluginDir(homeDir: string): string {
26	  return path.join(getClaudeConfigDir(homeDir), 'plugins', 'claude-hud');
27	}
28
```
