1	---
2	description: Configure claude-hud as your statusline
3	allowed-tools: Bash, Read, Edit, AskUserQuestion
4	---
5	
6	**Note**: Placeholders like `{RUNTIME_PATH}`, `{SOURCE}`, and `{GENERATED_COMMAND}` should be substituted with actual detected values.
7	
8	## Step 0: Detect Ghost Installation (Run First)
9	
10	Check for inconsistent plugin state that can occur after failed installations:
11	
12	**macOS/Linux**:
13	```bash
14	# Check 1: Cache exists?
15	CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
16	CACHE_EXISTS=$(ls -d "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/cache"/*/claude-hud 2>/dev/null && echo "YES" || echo "NO")
17	
18	# Check 2: Registry entry exists?
19	REGISTRY_EXISTS=$(grep -q "claude-hud" "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/installed_plugins.json" 2>/dev/null && echo "YES" || echo "NO")
20	
21	# Check 3: Temp files left behind?
22	TEMP_FILES=$(ls -d "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/cache/temp_local_"* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
23	
24	echo "Cache: $CACHE_EXISTS | Registry: $REGISTRY_EXISTS | Temp: ${TEMP_FILES:-none}"
25	```
26	
27	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
28	```powershell
29	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
30	$cache = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache") -Directory | ForEach-Object { Test-Path (Join-Path $_.FullName "claude-hud") }) -contains $true
31	$registry = (Get-Content (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\installed_plugins.json") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -match "claude-hud"
32	$temp = Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache\temp_local_*") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
33	Write-Host "Cache: $cache | Registry: $registry | Temp: $($temp.Count) files"
34	```
35	
36	### Interpreting Results
37	
38	| Cache | Registry | Meaning | Action |
39	|-------|----------|---------|--------|
40	| YES | YES | Normal install (may still be broken) | Continue to Step 1 |
41	| YES | NO | Ghost install - cache orphaned | Clean up cache |
42	| NO | YES | Ghost install - registry stale | Clean up registry |
43	| NO | NO | Not installed | Continue to Step 1 |
44	
45	If **temp files exist**, a previous install was interrupted. Clean them up.
46	
47	### Cleanup Commands
48	
49	If ghost installation detected, ask user if they want to reset. If yes:
50	
51	**macOS/Linux**:
52	```bash
53	CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
54	
55	# Remove orphaned cache (handles both direct and marketplace installs)
56	rm -rf "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/cache"/*/claude-hud
57	
58	# Remove temp files from failed installs
59	rm -rf "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/cache/temp_local_"*
60	
61	# Reset registry (removes ALL plugins - warn user first!)
62	# Only run if user confirms they have no other plugins they want to keep:
63	echo '{"version": 2, "plugins": {}}' > "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/installed_plugins.json"
64	```
65	
66	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
67	```powershell
68	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
69	
70	# Remove orphaned cache (handles both direct and marketplace installs)
71	Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache") -Directory | ForEach-Object { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Join-Path $_.FullName "claude-hud") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
72	
73	# Remove temp files
74	Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache\temp_local_*") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
75	
76	# Reset registry (removes ALL plugins - warn user first!)
77	'{"version": 2, "plugins": {}}' | Set-Content (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\installed_plugins.json")
78	```
79	
80	After cleanup, tell user to run `/plugin install claude-hud` again followed by `/reload-plugins` — no restart needed. (Restart Claude Code only if the reinstall still misbehaves; the fresh session re-reads the plugin registry from scratch.)
81	
82	### Linux: Cross-Device Filesystem Check
83	
84	**On Linux only**, if install fails with `EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted`, check whether `/tmp` and home are on different filesystems:
85	```bash
86	[ "$(df --output=source ~ /tmp 2>/dev/null | tail -2 | uniq | wc -l)" = "2" ] && echo "CROSS_DEVICE"
87	```
88	
89	The underlying Claude Code bug ([#14799](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/14799)) has been fixed, so this mostly affects older Claude Code versions — suggest updating Claude Code first. If updating isn't an option and the check outputs `CROSS_DEVICE`, the workaround is:
90	```bash
91	mkdir -p ~/.cache/tmp && TMPDIR=~/.cache/tmp claude /plugin install claude-hud
92	```
93	
94	---
95	
96	## Step 1: Detect Platform, Shell, and Runtime
97	
98	**IMPORTANT**: Use the environment context values (`Platform:` and `Shell:`) as your starting point. On `win32`, also check `$OSTYPE` via the Bash tool. Some Windows sessions report `Shell: powershell` while the command path exposed to Claude Code is Git Bash/MSYS2. When `$OSTYPE` is `msys` or `cygwin`, the PowerShell command format can fail before PowerShell runs because bash expands `$env:VAR`, `$p`, and `$(...)` expressions first (see [#531](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/531)).
99	
100	**On `win32`, run this check first:**
101	```bash
102	echo $OSTYPE
103	```
104	
105	| Platform | Shell | OSTYPE | Command Format |
106	|----------|-------|--------|----------------|
107	| `darwin` | any | any | bash (macOS instructions) |
108	| `linux` | any | any | bash (Linux instructions) |
109	| `win32` | `bash` | any | bash — Windows + Git Bash instructions |
110	| `win32` | `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd` | `msys` or `cygwin` | bash — Windows + Git Bash instructions (the active command environment is MSYS/Cygwin; PowerShell syntax is unsafe here) |
111	| `win32` | `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd` | other / empty | PowerShell — Windows + PowerShell instructions |
112	
113	---
114	
115	**macOS/Linux** (Platform: `darwin` or `linux`):
116	
117	1. Get plugin path (sorted by dotted numeric version, not modification time):
118	   ```bash
119	   ls -d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | awk -F/ '{ print $(NF-1) "\t" $(0) }' | grep -E '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]' | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4n | tail -1 | cut -f2-
120	   ```
121	   If empty, the plugin is not installed. Go back to Step 0 to check for ghost installation or EXDEV issues. If Step 0 was clean, ask the user to install via `/plugin install claude-hud` first.
122	
123	2. Get runtime absolute path:
124	   - On `darwin` or `linux`, prefer bun for performance and fall back to node:
125	     ```bash
126	     command -v bun 2>/dev/null || command -v node 2>/dev/null
127	     ```
128	   - On `win32` + `bash`, require node. Do not fall back to bun on Windows:
129	     ```bash
130	     command -v node 2>/dev/null
131	     ```
132	
133	   If empty, stop setup and explain that the current shell cannot find the required runtime.
134	   - On **Windows + Git Bash/MSYS2**, explicitly explain that the current Git Bash session could not find Node.js, even if Claude Code itself is installed.
135	   - If `winget` is available, recommend:
136	     ```bash
137	     winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS
138	     ```
139	   - On Windows, ask the user to install Node.js LTS from https://nodejs.org/
140	   - On macOS/Linux, ask the user to install one of these:
141	     - Node.js LTS from https://nodejs.org/
142	     - Bun from https://bun.sh/
143	   - After installation, ask the user to restart their shell and re-run `/claude-hud:setup`.
144	
145	3. Verify the runtime exists:
146	   ```bash
147	   ls -la {RUNTIME_PATH}
148	   ```
149	   If it doesn't exist, re-detect or ask user to verify their installation.
150	
151	4. Determine source file based on runtime:
152	   - On `darwin` or `linux`, use `src/index.ts` when the runtime is bun. Otherwise use `dist/index.js`.
153	   - On Windows, always use `dist/index.js`.
154	
155	5. Generate command (quotes around runtime path handle spaces):
156	
157	   The command exports `COLUMNS` so the HUD knows the real terminal width.
158	   Claude Code pipes the subprocess stdout, so `process.stdout.columns` is
159	   unavailable at runtime. Since Claude Code v2.1.153, `COLUMNS` and `LINES`
160	   are set natively to the current terminal dimensions before the statusLine
161	   command runs, so the inherited `COLUMNS` value is the primary source. The
162	   `stty size </dev/tty` probe and the 120 fallback remain for older Claude
163	   Code versions where `COLUMNS` may be absent. The `- 4` accounts for Claude
164	   Code's input area padding (2 columns on each side).
165	
166	   The grep pattern uses `[[:space:]]` rather than `\t` to match the tab
167	   separator emitted by awk. GNU grep (BRE/ERE) does **not** interpret
168	   `\t` as a tab character — it emits `warning: stray \ before t` and
169	   treats the pattern as literal `t`, so the regex never matches the awk
170	   output and `plugin_dir` resolves to an empty string. The runtime then
171	   exits with `Module not found "src/index.ts"` and no HUD appears.
172	   Setup verification can hide this because some shells alias `grep` to
173	   alternatives (e.g. `ugrep`) that *do* expand `\t`, while the actual
174	   `statusLine` subprocess invokes `/usr/bin/grep`. `[[:space:]]` is a
175	   POSIX character class supported by both BSD grep (macOS default) and
176	   GNU grep (Linux default).
177	
178	   **When runtime is bun** - add `--env-file /dev/null` to prevent Bun from auto-loading project `.env` files:
179	   ```
180	   bash -c 'cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '"'"'{print $2}'"'"');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | awk -F/ '"'"'{ print $(NF-1) "\t" $(0) }'"'"' | grep -E '"'"'^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]'"'"' | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4n | tail -1 | cut -f2-); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" --env-file /dev/null "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"'
181	   ```
182	
183	   **When runtime is node**:
184	   ```
185	   bash -c 'cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '"'"'{print $2}'"'"');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | awk -F/ '"'"'{ print $(NF-1) "\t" $(0) }'"'"' | grep -E '"'"'^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]'"'"' | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4n | tail -1 | cut -f2-); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"'
186	   ```
187	
188	**Windows + Git Bash** (Platform: `win32`, Shell: `bash`):
189	
190	Do not use PowerShell commands when the shell is bash. Claude Code invokes statusLine commands through bash, which will interpret PowerShell variables like `$env` and `$p` before PowerShell ever sees them.
191	
192	On Windows require `node` and always use `dist/index.js`.
193	
194	**Important**: Do **not** reuse the macOS/Linux awk-based command on Windows + Git Bash. The `awk` fragment requires `'"'"'` quoting to nest single quotes inside `bash -c '...'`. After JSON encoding and decoding, this quoting breaks on Windows Git Bash, causing a silent syntax error that prevents the HUD process from starting (see [#326](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/326)).
195	
196	Instead, use `sort -V` (GNU version sort, included with Git for Windows) which avoids nested single quotes entirely. Also avoid wrapping the generated command in a second `bash -c ...` layer. Claude Code is already invoking the statusline through bash, so the direct shell command lets `exec` replace that shell instead of spawning an extra bash wrapper first. The command still exports `COLUMNS` so the HUD receives the real terminal width, and it uses the marketplace-aware cache glob:
197	
198	   ```
199	   cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '{print $2}');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -1d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"
200	   ```
201	
202	**Windows + PowerShell** (Platform: `win32`, Shell: `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd`, OSTYPE: other/empty):
203	
204	> **Before proceeding**: if `echo $OSTYPE` returned `msys` or `cygwin`, use the **Windows + Git Bash** instructions above. In that environment, bash can expand PowerShell variables before PowerShell runs.
205	
206	1. Get plugin path:
207	   ```powershell
208	   $claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
209	   (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache\*\claude-hud\*") -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match '^\d+(\.\d+)+$' } | Sort-Object { [version]$_.Name } -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).FullName
210	   ```
211	   The trailing `\*` on the cache glob is required. Without it, `Get-ChildItem` returns the `claude-hud` directory itself, whose name does not match the `^\d+(\.\d+)+$` version pattern, so the lookup resolves to `$null` and any subsequent `Join-Path` throws (see [#521](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/521)).
212	
213	   If empty or errors, the plugin is not installed. Ask the user to install via marketplace first.
214	
215	2. Get runtime absolute path (require node on Windows):
216	   ```powershell
217	   if (Get-Command node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { (Get-Command node).Source } else { Write-Error "Node.js not found" }
218	   ```
219	
220	   If node is not found, stop setup and explain that the current PowerShell session cannot find Node.js.
221	   - If `winget` is available, recommend:
222	     ```powershell
223	     winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS
224	     ```
225	   - Otherwise ask the user to install Node.js LTS, then restart PowerShell and re-run `/claude-hud:setup`.
226	   - On Windows, do not offer Bun for statusLine setup. Use Node.js only.
227	
228	3. Use `dist\index.js`.
229	
230	4. Write the Windows statusline launcher.
231	
232	   Windows PowerShell startup plus `Get-ChildItem | Sort-Object [version]` can exceed Claude Code's render cadence on every statusLine refresh. Write a small Node launcher once during setup, then invoke it through `cmd.exe` on each refresh. The launcher uses the setup-time validated `node.exe`, preserves update discovery by finding the latest installed `claude-hud` version, and prefers inherited `COLUMNS` before falling back to 120.
233	
234	   The launcher file at `$claudeDir/plugins/claude-hud/statusline.mjs` should contain:
235	
236	   ```js
237	   import fs from 'node:fs';
238	   import os from 'node:os';
239	   import path from 'node:path';
240	   import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
241	
242	   const envColumns = Number.parseInt(process.env.COLUMNS ?? '', 10);
243	   const width = Number.isFinite(envColumns) && envColumns > 0 ? envColumns : 120;
244	   process.env.COLUMNS = String(Math.max(1, width - 4));
245	
246	   const claudeDir = process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude');
247	   const cacheDir = path.join(claudeDir, 'plugins', 'cache');
248	
249	   function versionParts(value) {
250	     const match = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+].*)?$/.exec(value);
251	     return match ? match.slice(1, 4).map(Number) : null;
252	   }
253	
254	   function compareVersions(a, b) {
255	     for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {
256	       if (a[i] !== b[i]) return a[i] - b[i];
257	     }
258	     return 0;
259	   }
260	
261	   const candidates = [];
262	   try {
263	     for (const marketplace of fs.readdirSync(cacheDir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
264	       if (!marketplace.isDirectory()) continue;
265	       const pluginRoot = path.join(cacheDir, marketplace.name, 'claude-hud');
266	       let versions = [];
267	       try {
268	         versions = fs.readdirSync(pluginRoot, { withFileTypes: true });
269	       } catch {
270	         continue;
271	       }
272	       for (const version of versions) {
273	         if (!version.isDirectory()) continue;
274	         const parts = versionParts(version.name);
275	         if (!parts) continue;
276	         const dir = path.join(pluginRoot, version.name);
277	         if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'dist', 'index.js'))) {
278	           candidates.push({ dir, parts });
279	         }
280	       }
281	     }
282	   } catch {
283	     process.exit(0);
284	   }
285	
286	   candidates.sort((a, b) => compareVersions(a.parts, b.parts));
287	   const latest = candidates.at(-1);
288	   if (!latest) process.exit(0);
289	
290	   const hud = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(latest.dir, 'dist', 'index.js')).href);
291	   if (typeof hud.main === 'function') {
292	     await hud.main();
293	   }
294	   ```
295	
296	   Write it using `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` with `New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false` so the file is UTF-8 without a BOM:
297	
298	   ```powershell
299	   $wrapperDir = Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\claude-hud"
300	   New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $wrapperDir | Out-Null
301	   $wrapperPath = Join-Path $wrapperDir "statusline.mjs"
302	   $wrapperBody = @'
303	   import fs from 'node:fs';
304	   import os from 'node:os';
305	   import path from 'node:path';
306	   import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
307	
308	   const envColumns = Number.parseInt(process.env.COLUMNS ?? '', 10);
309	   const width = Number.isFinite(envColumns) && envColumns > 0 ? envColumns : 120;
310	   process.env.COLUMNS = String(Math.max(1, width - 4));
311	
312	   const claudeDir = process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude');
313	   const cacheDir = path.join(claudeDir, 'plugins', 'cache');
314	
315	   function versionParts(value) {
316	     const match = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+].*)?$/.exec(value);
317	     return match ? match.slice(1, 4).map(Number) : null;
318	   }
319	
320	   function compareVersions(a, b) {
321	     for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {
322	       if (a[i] !== b[i]) return a[i] - b[i];
323	     }
324	     return 0;
325	   }
326	
327	   const candidates = [];
328	   try {
329	     for (const marketplace of fs.readdirSync(cacheDir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
330	       if (!marketplace.isDirectory()) continue;
331	       const pluginRoot = path.join(cacheDir, marketplace.name, 'claude-hud');
332	       let versions = [];
333	       try {
334	         versions = fs.readdirSync(pluginRoot, { withFileTypes: true });
335	       } catch {
336	         continue;
337	       }
338	       for (const version of versions) {
339	         if (!version.isDirectory()) continue;
340	         const parts = versionParts(version.name);
341	         if (!parts) continue;
342	         const dir = path.join(pluginRoot, version.name);
343	         if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'dist', 'index.js'))) {
344	           candidates.push({ dir, parts });
345	         }
346	       }
347	     }
348	   } catch {
349	     process.exit(0);
350	   }
351	
352	   candidates.sort((a, b) => compareVersions(a.parts, b.parts));
353	   const latest = candidates.at(-1);
354	   if (!latest) process.exit(0);
355	
356	   const hud = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(latest.dir, 'dist', 'index.js')).href);
357	   if (typeof hud.main === 'function') {
358	     await hud.main();
359	   }
360	   '@
361	   [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($wrapperPath, $wrapperBody, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
362	   ```
363	
364	   `$runtimePath` is the value detected in step 2 (the absolute path returned by `(Get-Command node).Source`, typically `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`). `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` on Windows PowerShell 5.1 both emit a UTF-8 BOM. `WriteAllText` + `UTF8Encoding $false` writes without a BOM in both PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+.
365	
366	5. Generate command:
367	
368	   ```
369	   {CMD_PATH} /d /s /c ""{RUNTIME_PATH}" "{WRAPPER_PATH}""
370	   ```
371	
372	   `{CMD_PATH}` is the absolute `cmd.exe` path, preferably `$env:SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe`. `{WRAPPER_PATH}` is the value of `$wrapperPath` from step 4 (typically `C:\Users\<user>\.claude\plugins\claude-hud\statusline.mjs`). If you build the string in PowerShell, use:
373	
374	   ```powershell
375	   $cmdPath = Join-Path $env:SystemRoot "System32\cmd.exe"
376	   if (-not (Test-Path $cmdPath)) { $cmdPath = "cmd.exe" }
377	   $generatedCommand = $cmdPath + ' /d /s /c ""' + $runtimePath + '" "' + $wrapperPath + '""'
378	   ```
379	
380	**WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux)**: If running in WSL, use the macOS/Linux instructions. Ensure the plugin is installed in the Linux environment (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/plugins/...`), not the Windows side.
381	
382	## Step 2: Test Command
383	
384	Run the generated command. It should produce output (the HUD lines) within a few seconds.
385	
386	- If it errors, do not proceed to Step 3.
387	- If it hangs for more than a few seconds, cancel and debug.
388	- This test catches issues like broken runtime binaries, missing plugins, or path problems.
389	
390	## Step 2.5: Detect Existing Statusline and Create Backup
391	
392	Before writing to `settings.json`, check whether a `statusLine` key already exists and protect the user's current configuration. This covers the existing-statusLine overwrite issue tracked in [#547](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/547).
393	
394	### 2.5.1: Read the existing statusLine
395	
396	**macOS/Linux**:
397	```bash
398	SETTINGS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
399	EXISTING_COMMAND=""
400	EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW=""
401	
402	if [ -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
403	  EXISTING_COMMAND=$("{RUNTIME_PATH}" -e '
404	const fs = require("fs");
405	const settingsPath = process.argv[1];
406	
407	try {
408	  const text = fs.readFileSync(settingsPath, "utf8");
409	  if (text.trim() === "") process.exit(0);
410	
411	  const json = JSON.parse(text);
412	  const command = json && json.statusLine && typeof json.statusLine.command === "string"
413	    ? json.statusLine.command
414	    : "";
415	  process.stdout.write(command);
416	} catch (error) {
417	  console.error("Unable to read statusLine.command from settings.json: " + error.message);
418	  process.exit(1);
419	}
420	' "$SETTINGS") || exit 1
421	
422	  EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING_COMMAND" | "{RUNTIME_PATH}" -e '
423	let value = "";
424	process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8");
425	process.stdin.on("data", chunk => { value += chunk; });
426	process.stdin.on("end", () => {
427	  const redacted = value
428	    .replace(/\b(Bearer)\s+["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "$1 [REDACTED]")
429	    .replace(/\b(Authorization\s*:\s*)["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "$1[REDACTED]")
430	    .replace(/\b(token|api[_-]?key|secret|password|pass|auth)(=|:)\s*["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "$1$2[REDACTED]")
431	    .replace(/\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b/g, "sk-[REDACTED]")
432	    .replace(/\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,}\b/g, "[GITHUB_TOKEN_REDACTED]")
433	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
434	    .trim();
435	
436	  process.stdout.write(redacted.length > 160 ? redacted.slice(0, 157) + "..." : redacted);
437	});
438	')
439	fi
440	```
441	
442	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
443	```powershell
444	$settingsPath = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { Join-Path $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR "settings.json" } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude\settings.json" }
445	$existingCommand = ""
446	$existingCommandPreview = ""
447	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
448	  try {
449	    $json = Get-Content $settingsPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
450	    if ($json.statusLine -and $json.statusLine.command) {
451	      $existingCommand = $json.statusLine.command
452	    }
453	  } catch {
454	    Write-Error "Unable to read statusLine.command from settings.json: $($_.Exception.Message)"
455	    throw
456	  }
457	
458	  if ($existingCommand -ne "") {
459	    $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommand `
460	      -replace "(?i)\b(Bearer)\s+[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", '$1 [REDACTED]' `
461	      -replace "(?i)\b(Authorization\s*:\s*)[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", '$1[REDACTED]' `
462	      -replace "(?i)\b(token|api[_-]?key|secret|password|pass|auth)(=|:)\s*[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", '$1$2[REDACTED]' `
463	      -replace "\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b", 'sk-[REDACTED]' `
464	      -replace "\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,}\b", '[GITHUB_TOKEN_REDACTED]' `
465	      -replace "\s+", " "
466	    $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommandPreview.Trim()
467	    if ($existingCommandPreview.Length -gt 160) {
468	      $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommandPreview.Substring(0, 157) + "..."
469	    }
470	  }
471	}
472	```
473	
474	### 2.5.2: Classify the existing statusline
475	
476	If `EXISTING_COMMAND` / `$existingCommand` is non-empty, classify it:
477	
478	| Pattern in command | Classification | Source label |
479	|---|---|---|
480	| Contains `claude-hud` | **Reinstall** (own config) | `claude-hud` |
481	| Contains `claude-pace` | **Known project** | `claude-pace` |
482	| Contains `cc-statusline` or `ccstatusline` | **Known project** | `cc-statusline` |
483	| Contains `statusline.sh` or `statusline.js` or `statusline.py` | **Likely another statusline** | `statusline script` |
484	| Any other non-empty value | **Custom script** | `custom` |
485	| Empty / missing key | **Clean install** | (none) |
486	
487	### 2.5.3: Create a timestamped backup
488	
489	**Always** create a backup of `settings.json` before modifying it, regardless of whether a statusline exists. This protects against corruption (see [#315]) and gives users a recovery path.
490	
491	**macOS/Linux**:
492	```bash
493	SETTINGS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
494	BACKUP_TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
495	BACKUP_PATH=""
496	if [ -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
497	  BACKUP_PATH="${SETTINGS}.bak.${BACKUP_TIMESTAMP}"
498	  if cp "$SETTINGS" "$BACKUP_PATH"; then
499	    echo "Backup created: $BACKUP_PATH"
500	  else
501	    echo "Failed to create backup at: $BACKUP_PATH" >&2
502	    exit 1
503	  fi
504	fi
505	```
506	
507	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
508	```powershell
509	$backupPath = ""
510	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
511	  $timestamp = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'
512	  $backupPath = "${settingsPath}.bak.${timestamp}"
513	  Copy-Item $settingsPath $backupPath -ErrorAction Stop
514	  Write-Host "Backup created: $backupPath"
515	}
516	```
517	
518	### 2.5.4: Prompt the user if a statusline exists
519	
520	**If the statusline is empty (clean install)**: Skip this step. Proceed directly to Step 3.
521	
522	**If the statusline is claude-hud (reinstall)**: Skip this step. The new command replaces the old one — this is an idempotent update. Proceed to Step 3.
523	
524	**If the statusline belongs to a known project or is a custom script**: Use AskUserQuestion to ask the user what to do.
525	
526	Use AskUserQuestion:
527	- header: "Existing statusline detected"
528	- question: "Found an existing statusLine in settings.json:\n\n  command preview: {REDACTED_COMMAND_PREVIEW}\n  source: {SOURCE_LABEL}\n\nWhat would you like to do?"
529	- options:
530	  - "Replace it with claude-hud (your current setup will be backed up)"
531	  - "Keep my current statusline and exit setup (settings stay unchanged)"
532	  - "Cancel setup without changing settings"
533	
534	Set `{REDACTED_COMMAND_PREVIEW}` to `EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW` on macOS/Linux or `$existingCommandPreview` on Windows. Use only the redacted/truncated preview in the prompt and normal output. Do not print the full previous command because it may contain tokens or secrets.
535	
536	**If the user chooses "Keep" or "Cancel"**: Stop setup. The backup from 2.5.3 is still available if one was created. Tell the user:
537	
538	> No changes were made to your settings. Your existing statusline is preserved. Setup created no settings mutation apart from the backup file at `{BACKUP_PATH or $backupPath}` if that value is set.
539	
540	**If the user chooses "Replace"**: Proceed to Step 3. The backup from 2.5.3 ensures the previous configuration can be restored.
541	
542	### 2.5.5: Save the previous command for potential restoration
543	
544	Store the previous `statusLine.command` value in a file alongside the settings backup. This makes it easy to restore if the user later wants to switch back.
545	
546	**macOS/Linux**:
547	```bash
548	CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
549	if [ -n "$EXISTING_COMMAND" ]; then
550	  PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR="$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/claude-hud"
551	  PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH="$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR/previous-statusline.txt"
552	  mkdir -p "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR"
553	  chmod 700 "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
554	  if (
555	    umask 077
556	    printf '%s' "$EXISTING_COMMAND" > "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH"
557	  ); then
558	    chmod 600 "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true
559	    echo "Previous statusline command saved to: $PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH"
560	  else
561	    echo "Failed to save previous statusline command to: $PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH" >&2
562	    exit 1
563	  fi
564	fi
565	```
566	
567	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
568	```powershell
569	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
570	$pluginDir = Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\claude-hud"
571	if (-not (Test-Path $pluginDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $pluginDir | Out-Null }
572	if ($existingCommand -ne "") {
573	  $previousCommandPath = Join-Path $pluginDir "previous-statusline.txt"
574	  [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($previousCommandPath, $existingCommand, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
575	  try {
576	    $acl = Get-Acl $previousCommandPath
577	    $acl.SetAccessRuleProtection($true, $false)
578	    $rule = New-Object System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemAccessRule(
579	      [System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().Name,
580	      "FullControl",
581	      "Allow"
582	    )
583	    $acl.SetAccessRule($rule)
584	    Set-Acl -Path $previousCommandPath -AclObject $acl
585	  } catch {
586	    Write-Warning "Saved previous statusline command, but could not tighten file ACLs: $($_.Exception.Message)"
587	  }
588	}
589	```
590	
591	---
592	
593	## Step 3: Apply Configuration
594	
595	Read the settings file and merge in the statusLine config, preserving all existing settings:
596	- **Platform `darwin` or `linux`, or Platform `win32` + Shell `bash`**: `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json`
597	- **Platform `win32` + Shell `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd`**: `settings.json` inside `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, otherwise `Join-Path $HOME ".claude"`
598	
599	If the file doesn't exist, create it. If it contains invalid JSON, report the error and do not overwrite.
600	If a write fails with `File has been unexpectedly modified`, re-read the file and retry the merge once.
601	
602	**A timestamped backup was already created in Step 2.5.3.** If Step 2.5.4 prompted the user and they chose "Keep" or "Cancel", do not reach this step — setup has already exited.
603	
604	```json
605	{
606	  "statusLine": {
607	    "type": "command",
608	    "command": "{GENERATED_COMMAND}"
609	  }
610	}
611	```
612	
613	**JSON safety**: Write `settings.json` with a real JSON serializer or editor API, not manual string concatenation.
614	If you must inspect the saved JSON manually, the embedded bash command must preserve escaped backslashes inside the awk fragment.
615	For example, the saved JSON should contain `\\$(NF-1)` and `\\$0`, not `\$(NF-1)` and `\$0`.
616	
617	**Windows PowerShell 5.1 BOM**: on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the default shell on Windows 10/11), `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` emit a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`). RFC 8259 §8.1 forbids BOM in JSON. PowerShell 7+ added `-Encoding utf8NoBOM`, but PS 5.1 did not. Use `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` with `New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false` to write UTF-8 without a BOM from both PS versions:
618	
619	```powershell
620	[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $json, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
621	```
622	
623	Verify the first bytes are `7B 0D 0A` (`{` + CRLF) or `7B 0A` (`{` + LF), not `EF BB BF`:
624	
625	```powershell
626	[System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($path)[0..2]
627	```
628	
629	
630	After successfully writing the config, tell the user:
631	
632	> ✅ Config written. Claude Code reloads settings automatically — the HUD should appear below your input field after your next message in this session (no restart needed).
633	> If it doesn't show up after your next interaction, restart Claude Code (quit and run `claude` again) — older Claude Code versions require a restart to pick up statusLine changes.
634	
635	Then continue directly to Step 4 in the same session.
636	
637	**Windows note**: Keep the settings-reload guidance separate from runtime installation guidance.
638	- If the user just installed Node.js, they should restart their shell first so `node` is available in `PATH` — that shell restart is unrelated to Claude Code picking up the statusLine config.
639	- The statusLine config itself reloads automatically on Windows too; a full Claude Code restart is only the fallback if the HUD doesn't appear after the next interaction.
640	
641	**Note**: The generated command dynamically finds and runs the latest installed plugin version. Updates are automatic - no need to re-run setup after plugin updates. If the HUD suddenly stops working, re-run `/claude-hud:setup` to verify the plugin is still installed.
642	
643	**Restoring a previous statusline**: If the user previously had a different statusline and wants to restore it, use the backup path printed in Step 2.5.3. The previous command is stored in `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/previous-statusline.txt`. To restore:
644	1. Find the most recent backup: `ls -t ~/.claude/settings.json.bak.* | head -1`
645	2. Copy it back: `cp ~/.claude/settings.json.bak.{timestamp} ~/.claude/settings.json`
646	3. The restored config applies automatically on the next interaction (restart Claude Code only if it doesn't).
647	
648	## Step 4: Optional Features
649	
650	After the statusLine is applied, ask the user if they'd like to enable additional HUD features beyond the default 2-line display.
651	
652	Use AskUserQuestion:
653	- header: "Extras"
654	- question: "Enable any optional HUD features? (all hidden by default)"
655	- multiSelect: true
656	- options:
657	  - "Tools activity" — Shows running/completed tools (◐ Edit: file.ts | ✓ Read ×3)
658	  - "Agents & Todos" — Shows subagent status and todo progress
659	  - "Session info" — Shows session duration and config counts (CLAUDE.md, rules, MCPs)
660	  - "Session name" — Shows session slug or custom title from /rename
661	  - "Custom line" — Display a custom phrase in the HUD
662	
663	**If user selects any options**, write `plugins/claude-hud/config.json` inside the Claude config directory (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}` on bash, `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `Join-Path $HOME ".claude"` on PowerShell). Create directories if needed:
664	
665	| Selection | Config keys |
666	|-----------|------------|
667	| Tools activity | `display.showTools: true` |
668	| Agents & Todos | `display.showAgents: true, display.showTodos: true` |
669	| Session info | `display.showDuration: true, display.showConfigCounts: true` |
670	| Session name | `display.showSessionName: true` |
671	| Custom line | `display.customLine: "<user's text>"` — ask user for the text (max 80 chars) |
672	
673	Merge with existing config if the file already exists. Only write keys the user selected — don't write `false` for unselected items (defaults handle that).
674	
675	**If user selects nothing** (or picks "Other" and says skip/none), do not create a config file. The defaults are fine.
676	
677	### Step 4.5: Auto-Refresh (Optional)
678	
679	Claude Code only re-runs the statusline after an interaction (a new assistant message, `/compact` finishing, a permission-mode change, or a vim-mode toggle). Time-based HUD data — session duration, usage reset countdowns, the prompt-cache countdown — therefore goes stale between messages. Claude Code supports an optional `refreshInterval` key (seconds, minimum 1) on the `statusLine` settings object that re-runs the command every N seconds.
680	
681	Of those, only the usage reset countdown is shown by default — session duration and the prompt-cache countdown tick only if the user enabled them (e.g. "Session info" in Step 4, or via config). Mention this if the user seems unsure whether the timer is worth it.
682	
683	Ask with AskUserQuestion:
684	- header: "Auto-refresh"
685	- question: "Re-run the HUD on a timer so time-based info (session duration, usage countdowns) stays current between messages?"
686	- options:
687	  - "Every 5 seconds (Recommended)" — Keeps countdowns fresh with negligible overhead
688	  - "Every 1 second" — Smoothest ticking; re-runs the HUD command far more often
689	  - "No timer" — HUD updates only after interactions (Claude Code's default)
690	
691	**If the user picks an interval**, merge `refreshInterval: <N>` into the **existing** `statusLine` object in `settings.json` — preserve `type`, `command`, and any other keys. Follow the same rules as Step 3: real JSON serializer, no BOM on Windows, retry once on a concurrent-modification error. Do not re-create the backup; the Step 2.5.3 backup already covers this session.
692	
693	**If the user picks "Other" and gives a numeric interval** (e.g. "10" or "10 seconds"), use that value, clamped to a minimum of 1. Treat a non-numeric "Other" answer that declines (skip/none/no) like "No timer".
694	
695	**If the user picks "No timer"**, do not write the key. If a `refreshInterval` key already exists in `statusLine` from a previous run and the user explicitly chose "No timer", remove it.
696	
697	`refreshInterval` lives in `settings.json`, which Claude Code reloads automatically — ticking should start after the user's next interaction. If countdowns don't tick in the current session, tell the user it will take effect after a Claude Code restart; do not treat a non-ticking timer as a setup failure in Step 5.
698	
699	Each refresh re-runs the full HUD command (runtime startup, transcript parse, git status), so 5 seconds is the recommended default; only suggest 1 second when the user wants visibly smooth countdowns.
700	
701	---
702	
703	## Step 5: Verify & Finish
704	
705	Settings reload automatically, so the HUD can appear in the same session where setup was run — it renders after the user's next interaction (their answer to the question below counts as one). No restart is needed on current Claude Code versions.
706	
707	Use AskUserQuestion:
708	- Question: "Setup complete! The HUD should appear below your input field. Is it working?"
709	- Options: "Yes, it's working" / "No, something's wrong"
710	
711	**If yes**: Ask the user if they'd like to ⭐ star the claude-hud repository on GitHub to support the project. If they agree and `gh` CLI is available, first check whether their `gh` version supports `gh repo star`. If it does, run `gh repo star jarrodwatts/claude-hud`. Otherwise fall back to `gh api -X PUT /user/starred/jarrodwatts/claude-hud`. Only run the star command if they explicitly say yes.
712	
713	**If no**: Debug systematically:
714	
715	1. **Trigger an interaction, then restart if needed**:
716	    - Settings reload automatically, but the HUD only renders after the next interaction (a new message, `/compact` finishing, a permission-mode change) — sending any message should make it appear
717	    - If it still doesn't appear, restart Claude Code (quit and run `claude` again) — older Claude Code versions require a restart to pick up statusLine changes — then re-run `/claude-hud:setup` to verify
718	    - If you've already restarted, continue below
719	
720	2. **Verify config was applied**:
721	   - Read settings file (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json` on bash, or `settings.json` inside `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, otherwise `Join-Path $HOME ".claude"` on PowerShell)
722	   - Check statusLine.command exists and looks correct
723	   - If command contains a hardcoded version path (not using the dynamic version-lookup command), it may be a stale config from a previous setup
724	
725	3. **Test the command manually** and capture error output:
726	   ```bash
727	   {GENERATED_COMMAND} 2>&1
728	   ```
729	
730	4. **Common issues to check**:
731	
732	   **"command not found" or empty output**:
733	   - Runtime path might be wrong: `ls -la {RUNTIME_PATH}`
734	   - On macOS with mise/nvm/asdf: the absolute path may have changed after a runtime update
735	   - Symlinks may be stale: `command -v node` often returns a symlink that can break after version updates
736	   - Solution: re-detect the runtime path (`command -v node` on Windows, `command -v bun` or `command -v node` on macOS/Linux), and verify with `realpath {RUNTIME_PATH}` (or `readlink -f {RUNTIME_PATH}`) to get the true absolute path
737	
738	   **"No such file or directory" for plugin**:
739	   - Plugin might not be installed: `ls "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/`
740	   - Solution: reinstall plugin via marketplace
741	
742	   **Windows shell mismatch (for example, "bash not recognized")**:
743	   - Command format does not match `Platform:` + `Shell:`
744	   - Solution: re-run Step 1 branch logic and use the matching variant
745	
746	   **Windows: HUD shows only "initializing..." with no error (PowerShell shell, MSYS/Cygwin command environment)**:
747	   - Root cause: `Shell: powershell` with `$OSTYPE=msys` or `$OSTYPE=cygwin`, causing bash to process the command before PowerShell
748	   - Check: run `echo $OSTYPE` in the Bash tool — if it returns `msys` or `cygwin`, this is the issue
749	   - Solution: re-run setup; when OSTYPE is `msys`/`cygwin`, follow the Windows + Git Bash path in Step 1
750	
751	   **Windows + PowerShell: HUD silent or "initializing..." with no error in any log (OSTYPE is not msys/cygwin)**:
752	   - Symptoms: HUD stays at "initializing..." or shows nothing. Running the generated command interactively in a PowerShell prompt produces the expected HUD output, but the version invoked through Claude Code does not.
753	   - Root cause: older setup commands used a PowerShell wrapper on every refresh. That path could fail when `[Console]::WindowWidth` threw `System.IO.IOException: The handle is invalid.`, when the cache glob resolved the `claude-hud` directory instead of a version directory, or when PowerShell startup exceeded the render cadence.
754	   - Check: pipe stdin through `cmd.exe` to mirror Claude Code's invocation:
755	     ```powershell
756	     '{}' | & cmd.exe /c '{GENERATED_COMMAND}'
757	     ```
758	     If you see either error, the existing setup predates the Node launcher format. Re-run `/claude-hud:setup` to regenerate `statusline.mjs` and a `cmd.exe`-launched command. See [#521](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/521).
759	
760	   **Windows: PowerShell execution policy error**:
761	   - Run: `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned`
762	
763	   **Permission denied**:
764	   - Runtime not executable: `chmod +x {RUNTIME_PATH}`
765	
766	   **WSL confusion**:
767	   - If using WSL, ensure plugin is installed in Linux environment, not Windows
768	   - Check: `ls "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/`
769	
770	5. **If still stuck**: Show the user the exact command that was generated and the error, so they can report it or debug further

1	#Requires -Version 7
2	# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1 — merge a managed overlay into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json so claude-hud (statusline HUD), the pyright-lsp
4	# plugin, and a couple of safe defaults deploy on Windows. Companion to the
5	# parent (macOS/Linux) repo's dot_claude/modify_settings.json; that repo uses a
6	# `modify_` + jq merge, which is unreliable on Windows (invariant #5), so we use
7	# the same run_onchange pwsh-merger idiom as the editor overlays instead.
8	#
9	# Why a merge (not a managed dot_claude/settings.json)? Claude Code rewrites
10	# this file at runtime (plugins it installs, permissions the user grants). A
11	# static managed file would clobber all of that on every apply. We instead
12	# recursively deep-merge only our keys in, preserving every live key.
13	#
14	# Gated on installCodingAgents — no Claude Code, nothing to configure. Re-runs
15	# when the embedded overlay (claude/settings-overlay.json) changes.
16	{{ if .installCodingAgents -}}
17	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'   # best-effort; never abort the apply
18	
19	# Embedded at render time from the (chezmoi-ignored) claude/ source, so this
20	# script is self-contained and re-fires when the overlay changes.
21	$overlayJson = @'
22	{{ include "claude/settings-overlay.json" }}
23	'@
24	
25	$overlay = $overlayJson | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable
26	
27	# --- Completion-feedback hooks, gated on `agentSounds` -----------------------
28	#
29	# Built here rather than in claude/settings-overlay.json because that file is
30	# `include`d verbatim and so cannot carry Go-template conditionals.
31	#
32	# `notify` wires notify.ps1 (apprise -> Windows toast); `peon` wires peon-ping's
33	# game voice lines. Values lifted from a real peon-ping install.ps1 (verified
34	# against upstream source, NOT its README — the README's documented command
35	# shape is wrong on the POSIX side too). Windows specifics that differ from the
36	# macOS/Linux parent repo:
37	#   - command is `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File "<peon.ps1>"`
38	#   - `timeout = 10`, and there is NO `async` field
39	#   - the event set includes PreToolUse and has NO UserPromptSubmit
40	# Parent repo equivalent: dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl.
41	{{- $peon   := or (eq .agentSounds "peon")   (eq .agentSounds "both") }}
42	{{- $notify := or (eq .agentSounds "notify") (eq .agentSounds "both") }}
43	$notifyCmd = 'exec pwsh -NoProfile -File "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hooks/notify.ps1"'
44	# peon-ping is installed with `-OpenPeon`, which reroots its whole tree at the
45	# tool-agnostic ~/.openpeon — so peon.ps1 is NOT under ~/.claude/hooks/.
46	# Wrapped in a Test-Path guard so the hook is a silent no-op on a box where the
47	# install hasn't run (or failed): an unguarded `-File <missing>` makes Claude
48	# Code surface a hook error on every event. Mirrors the mandatory
49	# `command -v workmux` / `[ -x ... ]` guards in the parent repo.
50	$peonPs1   = Join-Path $HOME '.openpeon\hooks\peon-ping\peon.ps1'
51	$peonCmd   = "powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command `"if (Test-Path '$peonPs1') { & '$peonPs1' }`""
52	
53	# Event -> the commands that should be wired for the current tier.
54	$soundHooks = @{}
55	{{- if $notify }}
56	foreach ($evt in @('Notification', 'Stop')) {
57	    $soundHooks[$evt] = @(@{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $notifyCmd }) })
58	}
59	{{- end }}
60	{{- if $peon }}
61	foreach ($evt in @('SessionStart', 'SessionEnd', 'SubagentStart', 'Stop',
62	                   'Notification', 'PermissionRequest', 'PreToolUse',
63	                   'PostToolUseFailure', 'PreCompact')) {
64	    $entry = @{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $peonCmd; timeout = 10 }) }
65	    if ($soundHooks.ContainsKey($evt)) { $soundHooks[$evt] = @($soundHooks[$evt] + $entry) }
66	    else                               { $soundHooks[$evt] = @($entry) }
67	}
68	{{- end }}
69	if ($soundHooks.Count -gt 0) {
70	    if ($overlay['hooks'] -isnot [hashtable]) { $overlay['hooks'] = @{} }
71	    foreach ($evt in $soundHooks.Keys) { $overlay['hooks'][$evt] = $soundHooks[$evt] }
72	}
73	
74	# Commands the CURRENT tier disables — pruned from the live file below. Without
75	# this the additive merge makes agentSounds a one-way ratchet: switching
76	# notify -> none would leave notify.ps1 wired forever, so `none` would not
77	# actually silence a machine that previously had sound. Only OUR OWN
78	# fingerprints are listed, so foreign hook entries can never be touched.
79	# (Upstream's own install.ps1 strips `peon\.(ps1|sh)` / `notify\.sh` the same
80	# way before re-adding, so this matches its behaviour.)
81	$prunePatterns = @(
82	{{- if not $notify }}
83	    'notify\.ps1'
84	{{- end }}
85	{{- if not $peon }}
86	    'peon\.ps1'
87	{{- end }}
88	)
89	
90	# Recursive deep-merge: overlay leaves win; live-only keys are preserved. Unlike
91	# the editor overlay's shallow top-level assign, this keeps the user's nested
92	# state (e.g. permissions.allow/deny arrays, other enabledPlugins) intact.
93	#
94	# The `hooks` object gets special, ADDITIVE handling (see Merge-ClaudeHooks) so
95	# our Notification/Stop notify entries are appended without clobbering hook
96	# entries the user or other tools added. Every other array value is still
97	# replaced wholesale (overlay wins), which is what we want for scalars/plugins.
98	function Merge-Hashtable([hashtable]$base, [hashtable]$overlay) {
99	    foreach ($k in $overlay.Keys) {
100	        if ($k -eq 'hooks' -and ($overlay[$k] -is [hashtable])) {
101	            if ($base[$k] -isnot [hashtable]) { $base[$k] = @{} }
102	            Merge-ClaudeHooks $base[$k] $overlay[$k]
103	        }
104	        elseif ($base.ContainsKey($k) -and ($base[$k] -is [hashtable]) -and ($overlay[$k] -is [hashtable])) {
105	            Merge-Hashtable $base[$k] $overlay[$k]
106	        }
107	        else {
108	            $base[$k] = $overlay[$k]
109	        }
110	    }
111	}
112	
113	# Additive per-event hook merge, mirroring the parent repo's jq reduce in
114	# dot_claude/modify_settings.json: for each event, append only the overlay
115	# entries whose .hooks[0].command isn't already present in the live array,
116	# preserving live entries verbatim. Wholesale-replacing the arrays (the old
117	# behavior) would drop hooks the user / other tools add at runtime. @(...) also
118	# forces array shape so ConvertTo-Json emits a JSON array even for a single
119	# entry (Claude requires hooks.<event> to be an array).
120	function Merge-ClaudeHooks([hashtable]$base, [hashtable]$overlay) {
121	    foreach ($evt in $overlay.Keys) {
122	        # NB: plain two-line assign, NOT `$live = if (...) { @(..) } else { @() }`.
123	        # A single-element @() flowing out of an if-EXPRESSION gets unwrapped back
124	        # to a scalar (here a hashtable), so `$live + $additions` then throws
125	        # "A hash table can only be added to another hash table". Direct `= @(...)`
126	        # keeps the array shape.
127	        $live = @()
128	        if ($null -ne $base[$evt]) { $live = @($base[$evt]) }
129	        $liveCmds = @($live | ForEach-Object { $_.hooks[0].command })
130	        $additions = @($overlay[$evt] | Where-Object {
131	            $cmd = $_.hooks[0].command
132	            (-not $cmd) -or ($liveCmds -notcontains $cmd)
133	        })
134	        $base[$evt] = @($live + $additions)
135	    }
136	}
137	
138	# Respect CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (matches the statusLine command + claude-hud setup).
139	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME '.claude' }
140	$settingsPath = Join-Path $claudeDir 'settings.json'
141	
142	$settings = @{}
143	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
144	    $raw = Get-Content -Raw $settingsPath
145	    if ($raw.Trim()) {
146	        try { $settings = $raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable }
147	        catch { Write-Warning "could not parse $settingsPath; not overwriting"; return }
148	    }
149	}
150	
151	Merge-Hashtable $settings $overlay
152	
153	# Prune our own now-disabled entries (see $prunePatterns above). Runs AFTER the
154	# additive merge so a tier that re-enables something wins. Foreign entries are
155	# never matched. Event keys whose array empties out are removed so turning
156	# everything off doesn't leave `"SessionStart": []` litter behind.
157	if ($prunePatterns.Count -gt 0 -and $settings['hooks'] -is [hashtable]) {
158	    foreach ($evt in @($settings['hooks'].Keys)) {
159	        $kept = @(@($settings['hooks'][$evt]) | Where-Object {
160	            $cmd = $_.hooks[0].command
161	            if (-not $cmd) { return $true }
162	            foreach ($p in $prunePatterns) { if ($cmd -match $p) { return $false } }
163	            return $true
164	        })
165	        if ($kept.Count -gt 0) { $settings['hooks'][$evt] = $kept }
166	        else                   { $settings['hooks'].Remove($evt) }
167	    }
168	}
169	
170	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $claudeDir | Out-Null
171	$settings | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12 | Set-Content -Path $settingsPath -Encoding utf8
172	Write-Host "claude overlay -> $settingsPath"
173	{{ end -}}
174

The key inconsistency is now concrete: `claude-copilot` only reconstructs the configured SpecStory command when user arguments are present; with no arguments it delegates directly to `specstory run claude`, so bypass mode depends entirely on mutable project/user configuration. Its `--specstory` and `--no-specstory` prefix removal also uses a range slice that is unsafe for a one-element array, unlike the Codex wrapper’s established `Select-Object -Skip 1` pattern.

1719	# --- specstory `-c` passthrough (why the base command must come from config) ---
1720	#
1721	# specstory's `-c/--command` REPLACES the provider's configured command — it does
1722	# NOT append to it. The shipped config says as much: "Use of these is equivalent
1723	# to -c \"custom command\"" — same slot, last write wins. So a hardcoded
1724	# `-c "claude $args"` silently drops every flag in `claude_cmd` the moment
1725	# claude-copilot has args to pass through, which made these two disagree:
1726	#
1727	#   claude-copilot-once             -> bypass-permissions  (no -c branch)
1728	#   claude-copilot-once --resume X  -> ~/.claude defaultMode "auto"
1729	#
1730	# Deriving the base command from the config keeps specstory the single source of
1731	# truth for BOTH branches. `--no-specstory` deliberately does NOT inherit it.
1732	
1733	# Effective `claude_cmd`, honouring specstory's own precedence:
1734	#   project ./.specstory/cli/config.toml > user ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml > `claude`
1735	# Matches UNCOMMENTED assignments only — both shipped configs carry a commented
1736	# `# claude_cmd = "claude"` example, and matching that would re-introduce the very
1737	# bug this exists to fix. Handles TOML's double- and single-quoted strings.
1738	function script:Get-SpecstoryClaudeCmd {
1739	    foreach ($f in '.specstory/cli/config.toml', (Join-Path $HOME '.specstory/cli/config.toml')) {
1740	        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $f)) { continue }
1741	        foreach ($line in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $f -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
1742	            if ($line -match '^\s*claude_cmd\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|''([^'']*)'')') {
1743	                $v = if ($Matches[1]) { $Matches[1] } else { $Matches[2] }
1744	                if ($v) { return $v }
1745	            }
1746	        }
1747	    }
1748	    'claude'
1749	}
1750	
1751	# Single-quote ONE argument for embedding in specstory's `-c` command STRING.
1752	# specstory shell-splits that string honouring quotes, so quoting is both possible
1753	# and necessary — an unquoted join flattens `-p "two words"` into two arguments.
1754	# POSIX escape for an embedded quote: close, \', reopen.
1755	function script:ConvertTo-CopilotShQuote {
1756	    param([string] $Value)
1757	    "'" + ($Value -replace "'", "'\''") + "'"
1758	}

1	#Requires -Version 7
2	# build-specstory.ps1 — EXPERIMENTAL: build the SpecStory Windows-native CLI
3	# from the still-unmerged PR #191 and drop specstory.exe into ~/.local/bin.
4	#
5	# SpecStory ships no native-Windows CLI release yet; Windows/WSL/SSH support
6	# lives in getspecstory PR #191 (open, mergeable=false at time of writing).
7	# Treat the result as EXPERIMENTAL — behaviour may change or break until the PR
8	# lands. Tracking + revisit criteria: backlog/specstory-windows-native-cli.md
9	#
10	# Needs: git + go (Go toolchain). Enable the "Extra runtimes" init toggle or run
11	# `scoop install go` first. Run via: just specstory-build
12	[CmdletBinding()]
13	param(
14	    [string]$Pr  = '191',
15	    [string]$Ref = 'pull/191/head'
16	)
17	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
18	function Info($m) { Write-Host "==> $m" -ForegroundColor Cyan }
19	
20	foreach ($t in 'git', 'go') {
21	    if (-not (Get-Command $t -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
22	        throw "$t not found. Install it first (go: enable Extra runtimes, or run: scoop install go)."
23	    }
24	}
25	
26	$cache = Join-Path $HOME '.cache\specstory-build'
27	$repo  = Join-Path $cache 'getspecstory'
28	$bin   = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
29	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $cache, $bin | Out-Null
30	
31	if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $repo '.git'))) {
32	    Info 'cloning specstoryai/getspecstory'
33	    git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory.git $repo
34	}
35	
36	Push-Location $repo
37	try {
38	    Info "fetching PR #$Pr"
39	    git fetch origin "${Ref}:pr-$Pr" --force
40	    git checkout --force "pr-$Pr"
41	
42	    $out = Join-Path $bin 'specstory.exe'
43	    Push-Location (Join-Path $repo 'specstory-cli')
44	    try {
45	        Info "go build -> $out"
46	        go build -o $out .
47	    } finally { Pop-Location }
48	
49	    Info "built: $out"
50	    & $out --help | Select-Object -First 5
51	    Write-Host "`nExperimental specstory.exe is in ~/.local/bin (already on PATH). Open a new pwsh and run: specstory --help" -ForegroundColor Green
52	} finally { Pop-Location }
53

1	# SpecStory Windows-native CLI (track PR #191)
2	
3	**Status**: P? — blocked on upstream (experimental build available)
4	**Effort**: M
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` · `scripts/build-specstory.ps1` · `justfile` (`specstory-build`) · `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` (npm block) · `dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/`
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	2026-07. `npm i -g @specstory/cli` 404s — SpecStory has **no npm package** and
10	**no native-Windows CLI release**. Official install is macOS Homebrew
11	(`brew tap specstoryai/tap && brew install specstory`); Linux/WSL get GitHub
12	release binaries. The Copilot module (`claude-copilot`, session auto-save)
13	degrades gracefully when `specstory` is absent, so this is nice-to-have, not
14	blocking.
15	
16	## Investigation (upstream status)
17	
18	- **issue #132** — maintainer initially recommended running Claude Code +
19	  SpecStory under **WSL** on Windows; said native Windows CLI wasn't a
20	  near-term roadmap priority (no Windows users on the team) but "not
21	  impossible", later "We are working on this now."
22	- issue #132 was **closed** because the **VS Code extension** (`1.0.0`) added
23	  Windows support for exporting Claude Code sessions — but the comment
24	  explicitly notes **the CLI is still behind**, pointing at PR #191.
25	- **PR #191** — adds a Windows build target, WSL/SSH remote-workspace
26	  discovery, Cursor/Copilot IDE workspace-URI parsing, `--config-dir`,
27	  `--project-path`, `--git-origin`, etc.
28	- PR #191 state (at time of writing): **open, not merged, not draft,
29	  `mergeable=false`**. Large: ~67 commits, 38 files, +3159/−415. Visible
30	  review is mostly Copilot review comments (naming, unused fn, XML stripping);
31	  reviewer request → `belucid`. No confirmed human-maintainer approval.
32	
33	## Routes (which SpecStory path works on Windows today)
34	
35	| Route | Status |
36	|---|---|
37	| VS Code extension — export Claude Code sessions | supported (per issue #132) |
38	| Cursor / VS Code chat-history extension | should work |
39	| Native `specstory.exe` CLI | **PR #191, unmerged / no release** |
40	| SpecStory CLI under WSL + Claude Code | official stopgap |
41	| Self-build PR #191 | experimental (this repo: `just specstory-build`) |
42	
43	## What this repo does now
44	
45	- **Omitted** `@specstory/cli` from the npm install list (it 404s).
46	- Added an **opt-in experimental build** of PR #191, two ways in:
47	  - the `installSpecstoryBuild` init toggle ("SpecStory build" prompt) runs an
48	    inline build block in `run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` at apply time
49	    (fault-tolerant: Register-Failure if git/go missing, never aborts the apply);
50	  - `just specstory-build` → `scripts/build-specstory.ps1` for a manual one-off.
51	  Both do git clone → fetch `pull/191/head` → `go build` →
52	  `~/.local/bin/specstory.exe`. Needs `git` + `go` (Extra runtimes toggle or
53	  `scoop install go`). Treated as experimental.
54	- `claude-copilot` / `claude-copilot-once` run claude with
55	  `--dangerously-skip-permissions` regardless of whether `specstory` is present,
56	  so the hands-off proxy flow behaves the same before/after this CLI is built.
57	
58	## Revisit criteria (when to promote out of backlog)
59	
60	- **PR #191 merges / a Windows release ships** → replace the experimental build
61	  with the official install (npm if published, else scoop/winget/GitHub
62	  release), re-add to the standard installer, drop `scripts/build-specstory.ps1`
63	  + the `just` recipe + the `installSpecstoryBuild` init toggle (and its
64	  `windows.yml` flag, `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` prompt, and docs/skill mirrors) — or
65	  repoint them at the release, update `docs/tools.md` + `.zh-TW`.
66	- If upstream publishes an **npm package** after all → simplest path: add it
67	  back to the `Npm-InstallGlobal` list.

152	  status line (model/reasoning, fast mode, branch, context, tasks, directory)
153	  into `~/.codex/config.toml`. No fork or PATH shim; see
154	  [Codex status line](codex-status-line.md).

```text
135	Some JSON config surfaces are **owned by the tool at runtime** — Claude Code
136	rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` (plugins it installs, permissions you grant),
137	VSCode/Cursor rewrite their `settings.json`. Deploying a static managed copy
138	would clobber that live state, so these are **merged**, not overwritten. The
139	macOS/Linux repo merges with a chezmoi **`modify_` script** (a `sh` + `jq`
140	filter: read the live file on stdin, emit the merged result on stdout). On
141	Windows that doesn't hold up:
142	
143	- **Interpreter routing is by the *target's* extension.** chezmoi chooses a
144	  `modify_`/`create_` script's interpreter from the managed file's extension via
145	  `[interpreters.<ext>]`. `modify_settings.json` targets `settings.json` →
146	  `.json`, which maps to no interpreter. On Unix chezmoi falls back to the
147	  script's shebang (`#!/bin/sh`) + exec bit; Windows honors neither, so it can't
148	  run the script reliably — and you can't hand it a `.ps1` extension, because
149	  that's fixed to the target name. Only `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh` is wired up,
150	  and it only helps when the *managed file itself* is a `.ps1`.
151	- **Wrong toolchain.** The parent filter is `sh` + `jq` — not guaranteed on a
152	  pwsh-first box, and rewriting it in pwsh still hits the routing wall above.
153	
154	So each merge is a **`run_onchange_after_*.ps1.tmpl`** in `.chezmoiscripts/`
155	instead: a real `.ps1` that routes cleanly through `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh`,
156	runs natively with no external deps, and recursively deep-merges a
157	chezmoi-ignored overlay (`editors/*.json`, `claude/settings-overlay.json`,
158	embedded via `{{ include }}`) into the live file — preserving every key the tool
159	wrote. This is invariant #5 in `AGENTS.md`.
160	
161	**Tradeoff:** a `modify_` filter re-asserts on *every* apply; `run_onchange` only
162	re-fires when its rendered content (the overlay) changes. If the tool later
163	overwrites a managed key, it isn't restored until the overlay changes or you
164	reset state (`chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=entryState`). The parent needs
165	every-apply enforcement because CodeIsland / workmux keep rewriting
166	`~/.claude/settings.json`; Windows has no such contenders, so the lighter trigger
167	is fine.
168	
169	## XDG paths, not `%APPDATA%`
170
```
</details></tool-use>

935	        It 'keeps the Unix and Windows shim implementations byte-identical' {
936	            $unixShim = '/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/copilot-throttle-shim.js'
937	            if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $unixShim)) { Set-ItResult -Skipped -Because 'Unix sibling checkout is unavailable'; return }
938	            $windowsShim = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..' 'dot_config' 'powershell' 'copilot-throttle-shim.js'
939	            (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 $windowsShim).Hash |
940	                Should -Be (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 $unixShim).Hash
941	        }
942	
943	        It 'fills blank MCP descriptions without adding one to a native tool' {
944	            if (-not (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Set-ItResult -Skipped -Because 'bun is unavailable'; return }
945	            $env:COPILOT_SHIM_TEST_PATH = (Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..' 'dot_config' 'powershell' 'copilot-throttle-shim.js')).Path
946	            try {
947	                $json = & bun -e @'
948	import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
949	const { normalizeResponsesToolDescriptions: n } = await import(pathToFileURL(process.env.COPILOT_SHIM_TEST_PATH));
950	const p = { tools: [{ type: "web_search" }], input: [{ type: "plugin_tools", tools: [{ name: "alpha", description: "" }] }] };
951	const r = n(p);
952	console.log(JSON.stringify({ r, p }));

131	
132	Customize your HUD anytime:

138	The guided flow handles layout, language, and common display toggles. Advanced overrides such as

140	
141	- **First time setup**: Choose a preset (Full/Essential/Minimal), pick a label language, then fine-tune individual elements
142	- **Customize anytime**: Toggle items on/off, adjust git display style, switch layouts, or change label language

151	| **Minimal** | Core only — just model name and context bar |

156

Control characters, invisible format characters (bidi controls, zero-width joiners, variation selectors), line/paragraph separators, and noncharacters are rejected. Wide characters (emoji, CJK) may affect bar alignment depending on the terminal.
251	
252	Supported color names: `dim`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `magenta`, `cyan`, `brightBlue`, `brightMagenta`. You can also use a 256-color number (`0-255`) or hex (`#rrggbb`).
253	
254	`display.showMemoryUsage` is fully opt-in and only renders in `expanded` layout. It reports approximate system RAM usage from the local machine, not precise memory pressure inside Claude Code or a specific process. The number may overstate actual pressure because reclaimable OS cache and buffers can still be counted as used memory.
255	
256	`display.showCost` is fully opt-in. ClaudeHUD prefers the native `cost.total_cost_usd` field that Claude Code provides on stdin when it is available. If that field is absent or invalid for a direct Anthropic session, ClaudeHUD falls back to the existing local transcript-based estimate so the cost line still works on older payloads. The native field is absent before the first API response in a session, so the cost display may stay hidden until then. ClaudeHUD also keeps the cost hidden for known routed providers such as Bedrock and Vertex AI, because cloud-provider billed sessions may report `$0.00` or omit the field even though the session was not literally free. Set `display.showRoutedCost: true` (alongside `showCost`) to opt into cost for those providers anyway: the native `cost.total_cost_usd` is shown as `Cost` when positive, otherwise ClaudeHUD falls back to a token-based `Est.` from the Anthropic pricing table.
257	
258	Official MiniMax Anthropic-compatible endpoints receive a `MiniMax` provider label. MiniMax M2.7 can use its published token and cache prices for local estimates; M3 pricing depends on each request's context tier, which cumulative session tokens cannot safely infer, so ClaudeHUD does not guess an M3 estimate.
259	
260	`display.showPromptCache` is fully opt-in. When enabled, ClaudeHUD looks at the timestamp of the last assistant response in the local transcript and shows a live countdown until the prompt cache expires. The default TTL is 5 minutes (`300` seconds). Set `display.promptCacheTtlSeconds` to `3600` if you want a 1-hour Max-style window. If the transcript does not have an assistant timestamp yet, the cache element stays hidden.
261	
262	### Usage Limits
263	
264	Usage display is **enabled by default** when Claude Code provides subscriber `rate_limits` data on stdin. It shows your rate limit consumption on line 2 alongside the context bar.
