```text
1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) and other coding
4	agents when working with code in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to this file.
5	
6	## What this is
7	
8	Standalone, **Windows-only** dotfiles managed by [chezmoi](https://chezmoi.io),
9	targeting **PowerShell 7 (pwsh)**. It is a companion to the cross-platform
10	macOS/Linux repo `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` — the PowerShell layer is written
11	natively, **not** ported from that repo's POSIX shell config. No ansible;
12	packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI). Published at
13	`github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows`.
14	
15	**Dev box vs target:** the deploy target is Windows, but this checkout is usually
16	edited on macOS/Linux. You therefore **cannot execute the `.ps1` run-scripts
17	here** (they call winget / `%APPDATA%`). Validate with the isolated-apply +
18	render/parse pattern below; the `windows-latest` CI is the real gate.
19	
20	## Commands
21	
22	Real machine:
23	
24	- `chezmoi apply` / `chezmoi diff` (or `just apply` / `just diff`)
25	- `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`
26	
27	Validate locally (needs a local pwsh, e.g. installed to `~/.local/bin/pwsh`):
28	
29	- Lint: `pwsh -NoProfile -c "Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path . -Recurse -Settings ./PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1"` (fails only on Error; the excludes are deliberate — see the settings file header)
30	- Tests: `pwsh -NoProfile -c "Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests"` (single file: `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/Copilot.Tests.ps1`)
31	- Docs: `just docs-build` (= `uv run --with mkdocs-material --with mkdocs-static-i18n mkdocs build --strict`)
32	
33	Isolated apply + template render (the core idiom for testing without a Windows
34	box — all chezmoi state is redirected to a temp dir, so it never touches your
35	real setup):
36	
37	```bash
38	TMPD=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$TMPD/home"
39	chezmoi init --source="$PWD" --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --persistent-state="$TMPD/s.db" \
40	  --destination="$TMPD/home" --no-tty \
41	  --promptChoice='Role: workstation (full desktop) or minimal (shell only)=minimal' \
42	  --promptString='Your full name (git)=T' --promptString='Your git email=t@e.com' ...  # EVERY prompt, exact text
43	chezmoi apply --source="$PWD" --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --persistent-state="$TMPD/s.db" \
44	  --destination="$TMPD/home" --exclude=scripts   # scripts can't run off-Windows
45	chezmoi execute-template --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --source="$PWD" < some.ps1.tmpl > r.ps1  # then parse r.ps1 with pwsh
46	```
47	
48	## Architecture (big picture)
49	
50	- **Init** — `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` `[data]` prompts once (`role` → coarse defaults, then `installX` toggles) and sets `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh` so chezmoi runs `.ps1` scripts under pwsh. Prompts are hand-authored here (the parent repo generates them; this repo does not).
51	- **Shell** — `Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1` is a thin `$PROFILE` loader that dot-sources `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in numeric order (env → tool activation → aliases → apps/audio/clipboard → copilot import → yazi → tv cache → psreadline). Add a shell feature = a new numbered fragment. User overrides go in the untracked `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1`.
52	- **Packages** — `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the single source of truth for installs: scoop (CLI), winget (GUI), npm (AI agents), PSGallery (PSFzf / AudioDeviceCmdlets), all gated by init toggles. `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` is the single source for registry environment variables used both by that installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines use company PyPI/npm pull-through feeds; otherwise the China-mirror toggle selects GFW mirrors. Fault-tolerant (see invariants).
53	- **copilot-proxy** — `dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/` is a native PowerShell port of the parent's `43_copilot_proxy.sh` / `44_copilot_embed.sh` (runs the copilot-api fork so GitHub Copilot can back Claude Code and Codex). Reuses the Bun `copilot-throttle-shim.js` verbatim.
54	- **Config surfaces** — Alacritty (`AppData/Roaming/alacritty/`), Windows Terminal (a run_onchange that merges `profiles.defaults` non-destructively), WezTerm (`dot_config/wezterm/wezterm.lua` — sets pwsh as `default_prog`), editors (a run_onchange that deep-merges `editors/*.json` into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`), Claude Code (a run_onchange that recursively deep-merges `claude/settings-overlay.json` — claude-hud statusline, safe defaults, and **additive** `Notification`/`Stop` notify hooks — into `~/.claude/settings.json` non-destructively, gated on `installCodingAgents`), Codex (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` fail-closed-merges only the native `tui.status_line` into `~/.codex/config.toml`, preserving providers/projects/plugins and gated on `installCodingAgents`), apprise desktop notifications (`dot_config/apprise/apprise.yaml` → `~/.config/apprise/`; the `windows://` toast backend behind the Claude notify hook `dot_claude/hooks/notify.ps1`, `installCodingAgents`-gated — the notify hook and peon-ping's voice-line hooks are both gated on the `agentSounds` tier (none|notify|peon|both) and built in the run_onchange, NOT in `claude/settings-overlay.json`; see docs/agent-sounds.md), television channels (`AppData/Roaming/television/`), starship + yazi (`~/.config`, yazi via `YAZI_CONFIG_HOME`), Rime/Weasel (see below), herdr (see below).
55	- **Rime input method** — `installInputMethod`-gated, and the one config surface **shared with the parent repo**. The engine-level YAML lives in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` (`default.custom.yaml`, `luna_pinyin.custom.yaml`) and is kept **byte-identical** to `daviddwlee84/dotfiles`'s copy of the same path — `diff -r` between the two dirs is the drift check, so edit one and copy to the other in the same session. Each platform is a one-line `{{ template "rime/…" . }}` renderer: `AppData/Roaming/Rime/` here, `private_Library/Rime/` (Squirrel) and `dot_config/ibus/rime/` (ibus-rime) there. Only `weasel.custom.yaml` is Windows-specific (`style/` is Weasel's own, `app_options` keys on the EXE name vs. Squirrel's bundle ids, and `global_ascii` doesn't exist on Squirrel). Plain managed files, **not** a `modify_` overlay: Rime persists runtime state to `user.yaml`, never back into `*.custom.yaml`. Two gotchas: a bare silent winget install registers **简体** (hence `--custom '/T'` in `Install-Weasel` — see `pitfalls/weasel-silent-install-registers-simplified-chinese.md`), and config edits need a redeploy, which `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
56	- **herdr** — `dot_config/herdr/` is deployed via `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` and gated on `installHerdr`. `config.toml` is a **`modify_` overlay** (`modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` + `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`), never a plain managed file: herdr rewrites that file at runtime (onboarding flag, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]` bookkeeping) and a plain file clobbers it. The overlay enforces `[theme]`/`[ui]`/`[terminal]`/`[keys]` wholesale, pulls every other top-level key through, and re-asserts the single key `update.channel = "preview"` (the Windows installer rejects `stable`). Helper-script paths in the keymap are baked **absolute at render time** — `pwsh -File` does not expand `~`. Six pwsh helpers (`_common.ps1` + run-command / new-tab-at-space-root / url-pick / path-pick / pane-copy / review-mark) back the `[[keys.command]]` bindings; three `herdr-*` tv channels and the herdr-plus quick-actions are gated by the same toggle. Ported from the parent repo 2026-07-27; the behaviours that still need a real Windows box are listed in [`backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md`](backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md).
57	- **git config** — `~/.gitconfig` is a **`modify_` overlay** (`modify_dot_gitconfig.ps1.tmpl`), never a plain managed file: Git Credential Manager writes `[credential "azrepos:*"]` blocks into it out of band and a plain file would clobber them every apply. The baseline body is `.chezmoitemplates/git/gitconfig` (identity from the existing `.name`/`.email` init prompts); the merge engine is `scripts/gitconfig-merge.ps1`, inlined via `{{ include }}` (the `editors/` idiom) and dot-sourced by `tests/GitConfig.Tests.ps1`. The model is **key-level pull-through**: the baseline owns a fixed set of `section.key` pairs and every other live key is carried over untouched — the inverse of the parent repo's allowlist, which would silently drop `[otel]` and future corp sections. Two hard rules: `core.hooksPath` is **never** emitted (git honours it *instead of* `.git/hooks/`, silently disarming `pre-commit`), and the carry dictionary is **case-sensitive** (`[ordered]@{}` collapses `azrepos:org/O365Exchange` into `azrepos:org/o365exchange`, merging two credential contexts).
58	- **Docs** — bilingual mkdocs-material (`docs/X.md` + `docs/X.zh-TW.md`), deployed to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/docs.yml`. `docs/rationale.md` records the design choices (scoop > Chocolatey, starship > oh-my-posh, pwsh > cmd, native pwsh tree > ported shell layer).
59	- **CI** — `.github/workflows/windows.yml` on `windows-latest` is the real gate: PSScriptAnalyzer, non-interactive `chezmoi init --apply`, render+parse of every `.ps1.tmpl`, and Pester.
60	
61	## Conventions & hard invariants
62	
63	1. **A new/renamed init prompt must update the CI flags in the same commit.** `chezmoi init --promptBool/--promptChoice "<text>=value"` matches the prompt's exact TEXT (3rd arg to `promptXOnce` in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`), used non-interactively by `.github/workflows/windows.yml`. Forget it → CI's init hangs/EOFs (`error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF`; this broke three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds` was added). Corollary: **never put `=` in a prompt's text** — the `name=value` parser splits on the first `=` (this broke the `role` prompt once). Enforced by `tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` (missing flag, stale flag, wrong flag kind, `=` in text), which CI runs *before* `chezmoi init` so the failure names the missing flag instead of EOF-ing — run `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` locally after touching either file.
64	2. **Run-scripts must never abort the apply.** The installer + editor/terminal/backup/skill scripts use `$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'` (+ `PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$false`), collect failures via `Register-Failure`, print a summary, and exit 0. One bad scoop/winget manifest (e.g. btop's stale `.conf`) must not stop the rest.
65	3. **Preserve raw escapes when authoring config with control chars.** Alacritty CSI-u (`[…u`), VSCode `sendSequence`, tv `\t` — hand-typing tends to drop them. Generate via a throwaway Python script and re-parse (`tomllib` / `json`) to confirm the escape landed.
66	4. **tv channel commands are `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "…"` inside TOML literal (`'''…'''`) strings** — runs regardless of tv's shell, sidesteps nested-quote escaping; placeholders `{split: :0}` (space) / `{split:\t:0}` (tab). tv reads config from `%APPDATA%\television\` on Windows.
67	5. **Editors use a run_onchange pwsh merger, not `modify_`** (`modify_` interpreter selection is unreliable on Windows). Overlay sources live in `editors/` (chezmoi-ignored, embedded via `{{ include }}`).
68	6. **The agent skill body lives once** in `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`; both `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/SKILL.md.tmpl` and `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/SKILL.md.tmpl` render it via `{{ "{{" }} template … {{ "}}" }}` → real files at `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/`. Edit the shared template, not the two one-line renderers (no symlink/junction — those need elevation/Developer Mode on Windows).
69	7. **PSScriptAnalyzer exclusions are intentional** (`PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1`): hyphenated command names, `Write-Host`, `Invoke-Expression` for tool init, no-BOM UTF-8. Don't "fix" these; do fix real Errors.
70	
71	### Cross-file mirrors (same commit)
72	
73	- New installer tool → `docs/tools.md` **and** `docs/tools.zh-TW.md`.
74	- New init prompt → `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `windows.yml` flags + `docs/setup.md`/`setup.zh-TW.md` tables + the "What's enabled" block in `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.
75	- New `docs/**/*.md` → its `.zh-TW.md` twin + `nav` + `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`; `just docs-build` must stay green.
76	- Any edit under `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` → copy the file verbatim into the parent repo's `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` (`chezmoi source-path` there, usually `~/.local/share/chezmoi`). They must stay byte-identical; verify with `diff -r`. Frontend-only changes (`weasel.custom.yaml`) do **not** cross over.
77	- `core.autocrlf = input` has **two writers** — `bootstrap.ps1` (runs before chezmoi exists, so scoop's first bucket clone is protected) and `.chezmoitemplates/git/gitconfig` (the managed baseline). Change one → change the other.
78	
79	### `scripts/*.sh` are wrappers, not implementations
80	
81	`scripts/{add-todo,todo-kanban,promote-todo,sweep-inbox}.sh` are byte-identical
82	three-line shims. The real code is vendored at
83	`.agents/skills/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/<same-name>.sh`, and each
84	wrapper derives its target from `$0`, so adding a new helper only needs a copy
85	of an existing wrapper under the new name.
86	
87	They exist because the skill documents its helpers with cwd-relative paths
88	(`scripts/add-todo.sh`) and that prose was copied verbatim into the guidance
89	block below — where `scripts/` means *this* directory. Fixing the prose instead
90	would not survive, because `project-knowledge-harness` regenerates everything
91	between its sentinel markers. **This note is deliberately above the opening
92	sentinel so regeneration cannot erase it.**
93	
94	Not symlinks — invariant 6 (symlinks/junctions need elevation or Developer
95	Mode on Windows).
96	
97	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:agent-guidance -->
98	<!-- Snippet for the project's agent contract file (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md /
99	     similar). The bundled scripts/init.sh appends this between sentinel
100	     markers; safe to re-run. -->
101	
102	### Long-term backlog → `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
103	
104	When the user surfaces an idea explicitly **not** being implemented this
105	session (signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
106	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來"), add an entry to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using
107	the priority + effort tag schema. Do **not** create new `ROADMAP.md` /
108	`IDEAS.md` / `BACKLOG.md` files — `TODO.md` is the single index.
109	
110	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` validates the format. Run it
111	(`scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md`) after editing so syntax
112	drift is caught immediately.
113	
114	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
115	
116	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
117	
118	   ```
119	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
120	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
121	   ```
122	
123	   Inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane and
124	   re-runs the validator. Add `--backlog` to also scaffold
125	   `backlog/<slug>.md` from the bundled template.
126	
127	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
128	
129	   ```
130	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
131	   ```
132	
133	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox", run
134	   `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`. It prompts for the missing fields per loose
135	   line and calls `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs
136	   that only formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
137	
138	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh; run
139	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
140	
141	Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` companion doc when the item meets any of:
142	
143	- carries a `P?` tag (record what was tried so it doesn't need re-investigation)
144	- captures a paused troubleshooting session that you intend to fix later
145	  (preserve the error trace + root cause analysis before context evaporates)
146	- weighs multiple options (record trade-offs, not only the winner)
147	- is `[L]` or `[XL]` (architectural; needs design before code)
148	
149	`[S]` items rarely need a backlog doc — a file path in the `TODO.md` line is
150	usually enough. See [`backlog/README.md`](backlog/README.md) for the full
151	template and "when to add a doc" rules.
152	
153	When implementing a `TODO.md` item, in the same commit:
154	
155	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`
156	   to move the entry into `## Done` with the dated syntax and re-validate.
157	2. Mark the corresponding `backlog/<slug>.md` (if any) `Status: shipped`
158	   and keep it as a historical record (don't delete — future-you may
159	   revisit adjacent decisions).
160	
161	`backlog/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore); it
162	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
163	
164	### Past pitfalls → `pitfalls/`
165	
166	When you spend more than ~15 minutes debugging something that wasn't
167	googleable and the fix is non-obvious, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
168	capturing:
169	
170	1. **Verbatim symptom** — copy-paste error messages exactly, do not
171	   paraphrase (preserves grep-ability for future-you / future agent)
172	2. **Root cause** — why this happens (with source / docs / upstream issue link)
173	3. **Workaround** — copy-pasteable commands or config diff
174	4. **Prevention** — how to avoid stepping on this again
175	
176	Title the doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause (you'll search by what
177	you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned). See
178	[`pitfalls/README.md`](pitfalls/README.md) for the full template and
179	when-to-add rules.
180	
181	**Pitfall vs Hard invariant**: a pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant in
182	this file when it (a) recurs across machines/agents/sessions despite being
183	documented, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround is non-obvious
184	enough that "remember to do X" isn't safe. When graduating, leave the
185	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the new
186	invariant.
187	
188	`pitfalls/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore) and
189	**not** auto-redacted; review for secrets before committing.
190	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:agent-guidance --> (end)

```text
1	# dotfiles-windows
2	
3	Native **Windows + PowerShell 7** dotfiles, managed by [chezmoi](https://chezmoi.io).
4	A self-contained, Windows-only companion to the cross-platform (macOS/Linux)
5	dotfiles at **[daviddwlee84/dotfiles](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles)** —
6	the PowerShell layer is written natively rather than ported from the POSIX shell config.
7	
8	> **Which repo do I install from?**
9	>
10	> | Your machine | Use |
11	> |---|---|
12	> | **Native Windows** (PowerShell) | **this repo** (`dotfiles-windows`) |
13	> | macOS / Linux / WSL | [daviddwlee84/dotfiles](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles) |
14	
15	> Status: work in progress. See [`docs/`](docs/) for the full handbook (bilingual
16	> EN / 繁體中文) once built.
17	
18	## Quick start
19	
20	From a fresh Windows PowerShell (or pwsh) session:
21	
22	```powershell
23	irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows/main/bootstrap.ps1 | iex
24	```
25	
26	This installs [scoop](https://scoop.sh) (CLI tools) + [winget](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/package-manager/)
27	(GUI apps), PowerShell 7, [chezmoi](https://chezmoi.io) and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/),
28	then applies the dotfiles.
29	
30	## What you get
31	
32	- **Shell**: PowerShell 7 with a modular `$PROFILE` (`~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1`).
33	- **Prompt**: [starship](https://starship.rs) (shared config with the macOS/Linux dotfiles).
34	- **CLI tools** (scoop): git, neovim, lazygit, zoxide, fzf, bat, eza, ripgrep, fd, gh, delta, jq, yazi, btop, mise, uv, node, bun.
35	- **AI agents**: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, SpecStory, Antigravity.
36	- **Editors**: VSCode, Cursor, Notepad++ (shared settings/keybindings).
37	- **Apps** (winget): Windows Terminal, Alacritty, Raycast, PowerToys, Steam.
38	- **`copilot-proxy`** tool series, rewritten as a native PowerShell module.
39	
40	## Package manager
41	
42	**scoop for CLIs, winget for GUI apps.** Rationale (why not Chocolatey, why
43	starship not oh-my-posh, why pwsh not cmd) lives in the docs.
44	
45	## Layout
46	
47	| Path | What |
48	|---|---|
49	| `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` | Init prompts (role + feature toggles). |
50	| `Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1` | `$PROFILE` loader. |
51	| `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/` | Modular shell fragments. |
52	| `dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/` | `copilot-proxy` PowerShell module. |
53	| `dot_config/starship.toml` | Prompt config. |
54	| `dot_ssh/` | Create-only `~/.ssh/config` skeleton (`Include config.d/*`) + `config.d/` snippets. |
55	| `.chezmoiscripts/` | Package install + editor-overlay scripts. |
56	| `bootstrap.ps1` | One-line installer. |
57	| `docs/`, `mkdocs.yml` | Bilingual documentation site. |
58	
59	## SSH
60	
61	`dot_ssh/` ships a create-only OpenSSH skeleton, mirrored from the cross-platform
62	dotfiles and adapted for Windows:
63	
64	- `~/.ssh/config` — `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` plus conservative `Host *`
65	  keepalives. **Create-only**: an existing `~/.ssh/config` is never overwritten
66	  (add the `Include` line by hand if so). chezmoi writes it owner-only so
67	  Windows OpenSSH won't reject it with "Bad owner or permissions".
68	- `~/.ssh/config.d/00-defaults` — commented-out global-defaults stub.
69	- `~/.ssh/config.d/01_git` — `github.com` over `ssh.github.com:443` (survives
70	  port-22 filtering) + `gitlab.com`, with commented multi-account / SOCKS5-proxy
71	  examples.
72	
73	Agent handling differs from macOS/Linux: use the Windows **OpenSSH
74	Authentication Agent** service (`Set-Service ssh-agent -StartupType Automatic`;
75	`Start-Service ssh-agent`; `ssh-add`). The client uses the
76	`//./pipe/openssh-ssh-agent` named pipe by default — no `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` needed.
77	
78	## Manual dotfiles ops
79	
80	**First-time install** (fresh machine — no chezmoi yet): run the
81	[Quick start](#quick-start) one-liner. `bootstrap.ps1` installs scoop, git,
82	pwsh, chezmoi and uv, then runs `chezmoi init --apply` (asking the init prompts
83	once). You only do this once per machine.
84	
85	**Day-to-day** (chezmoi already installed): pull the latest and re-apply.
86	
87	```powershell
88	chezmoi update --init   # git pull + apply; --init re-asks any newly-added prompts (noop if none)
89	chezmoi diff            # preview pending changes without applying
90	chezmoi apply           # apply local source edits only (no pull)
91	just upgrade-scoop      # upgrade CLI tools
92	just upgrade-winget     # upgrade GUI apps
93	```
94	
95	Inside a loaded PowerShell session there are shortcuts (see
96	`profile.d/20_aliases.ps1`): **`cau`** = `chezmoi update --init` + reload
97	`$PROFILE`, **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload. Prefer `cau` as the normal
98	"sync my dotfiles" verb.
99	
100	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:readme-roadmap -->
101	<!-- Snippet for project's README.md, placed near other meta sections like
102	     "Customization" or "Contributing". -->
103	
104	## Roadmap & lessons learned
105	
106	Forward-looking work — long-term ideas, deferred items, things needing
107	evaluation — lives in [`TODO.md`](TODO.md), prioritised P1 → P3 with effort
108	estimates (S/M/L/XL). Items with accompanying research, design notes, or paused
109	troubleshooting link to a corresponding [`backlog/<slug>.md`](backlog/) doc.
110	
111	Backward-looking knowledge — past traps and non-obvious debugging — lives in
112	[`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/), titled by symptom so future-you can grep the error
113	message and land on the root cause + workaround instead of re-debugging from
114	scratch.
115	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:readme-roadmap --> (end)
116

10110	# dotfiles-windows
10111	
10112	This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
10113	Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
10114	there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
10115	(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)
10116	
10117	## Orientation
10118	- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
10119	- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
10120	- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
10121	- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
10122	- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).
10123	
10124	## Shell layout (pwsh)
10125	- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
10126	  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
10127	  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
10128	- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
10129	  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
10130	  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
10131	  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
10132	  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).
10133	
10134	## Packages
10135	- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
10136	  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
10137	  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
10138	  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
10139	- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
10140	  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
10141	  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
10142	  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
10143	- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
10144	  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.
10145	
10146	## copilot-proxy
10147	- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
10148	  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
10149	  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`,
10150	  `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`), `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
10151	- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
10152	  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
10153	  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
10154	  `copilot-here` writes
10155	  only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The pinned copilot-api is
10156	  installed ONCE into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg` (never `bunx` at launch);
10157	  `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls whether Node fetches the
10158	  GitHub model catalog through the local proxy. Full guide: `docs/copilot-proxy.md`.
10159	
10160	## Editors / terminal / tv
10161	- VSCode & Cursor settings + keybindings are deep-merged into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`
10162	  by `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_20_editor_overlays.ps1.tmpl` (sources under `editors/`).
10163	- Windows Terminal `profiles.defaults`, Alacritty (`%APPDATA%\alacritty\alacritty.toml`),
10164	  and WezTerm (`~/.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua`, pwsh as default shell) are managed too.
10165	  Television channels live under `%APPDATA%\television\cable\` (`tv <name>`).

10172	
10173	## just recipes
10174	`just --list`: `apply`/`diff`/`update`, `upgrade-scoop`/`upgrade-winget`/`upgrade-translate`, `lint`/`test`,
10175	`docs-serve`/`docs-build`, `enable-sshd` (opt-in OpenSSH server, elevated),
10176	`enable-wsl` (WSL2 for Docker Desktop; self-elevating UAC prompt, reboot after),
10177	`enable-wsl-ubuntu` (WSL2 Ubuntu distro + cross-platform dotfiles; needs enable-wsl first),
10178	`wsl-dotfiles` (bootstrap the cross-platform dotfiles into an existing WSL distro; VPN if behind GFW),
10179	`install-fonts-machine-wide` (Alacritty Nerd Font fix, elevated), and
10180	`docker-up`/`docker-down`/`docker-clean`/`docker-logs`
10181	(the x86-Linux+KVM Windows-in-Docker test harness — see `docker/windows/`).
10182	
10183	## Gotchas
10184	- Windows-only repo — no `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os }}` branching needed.
10185	- Editor settings use a `run_onchange` pwsh merger (not `modify_`) on Windows.
10186	- tmux / zellij are Unix-only and intentionally absent; **WezTerm** (installed) is
10187	  the stable native tmux-like multiplexer, or use Windows Terminal panes. **herdr**
10188	  is an opt-in (`installHerdr`) native-Windows multiplexer in preview beta —
10189	  installed via herdr.dev's `irm|iex` script, config at `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`.
10190	  Runtimes are native via scoop (node/bun/go/rust/ruby) + uv for Python — no mise on Windows.
10191	- **Rime input method** (opt-in `installInputMethod`): Weasel/小狼毫 via winget
10192	  `Rime.Weasel`. Machine-scope NSIS, so applying raises UAC; and a bare silent
10193	  install registers **简体** — `Install-Weasel` passes `--custom '/T'` for 繁體.
10194	  The engine-level YAML in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` is **byte-identical to the
10195	  parent repo's** copy (Squirrel/ibus-rime); only `weasel.custom.yaml` is
10196	  Windows-specific. Edits need a redeploy, which
10197	  `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
10198	  See `docs/input-method.md`.
10199	- **cmd.exe** is opt-in via `installClink`: Clink + starship/zoxide/fzf give the DOS
10200	  prompt parity for **prompt + navigation only** (no pwsh funcs/aliases/modules).
10201	  `starship.lua` is chezmoi-managed at `%LocalAppData%\clink`; the zoxide/fzf Clink
10202	  bridges are fetched from upstream at apply. pwsh stays the default shell.
10203	- **`translate`** (`installTranslate`, on for workstation) is the one tool built from
10204	  source: no scoop/winget manifest, so the packages script runs a version-pinned
10205	  `go install` into `~\.local\bin` (it installs `go` itself). First build takes
10206	  minutes; re-applies no-op via a `--version` check. Upgrade with
10207	  `just upgrade-translate`, not `upgrade-scoop`.
10208	- This skill body is shared: `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/` and
10209	  `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/` both render `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.

13899-I'm inspecting a profile line related to potential issues in `claude-copilot`. It seems slicing with one argument may cause problems. This suggests a failure mode that should be flagged. I also want to be cautious about how single argument arrays bind, as it might lead to unexpected behavior.

13905-**Exploring SpecStory behavior**
13906-
13907-When running `specstory run claude` without any arguments, I notice that SpecStory can resolve its configuration by itself. However, if there are any arguments included, the wrapper takes over and reads the configuration instead. It's interesting how the mode of operation changes based on whether args are present or not! This distinction seems significant, as it could impact how users interact with the tool and how configurations are managed.

13912:Two additional implementation hazards stand out. First, `create_config.toml` is create-once, so an existing user SpecStory config can keep an older/missing `claude_cmd`; a project-level uncommented `claude_cmd` also outranks it and can silently remove the bypass flag. Second, `claude-copilot-once --no-specstory` with no further arguments uses an unsafe PowerShell slice (`[1..0]`), unlike the corrected Codex wrapper, so the consumed control flag may leak back into Claude.

313-## Architecture
314-
315-Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint — not separate APIs.
316-
317-**User-defined tools** — You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.
318-
319-**Server-side tools** — Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.
320-
321-**Structured outputs** — Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and\or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.
322-
323:**Supporting endpoints** — Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` — see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` — live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.

1116-### Refusal Fallbacks (Claude Fable 5) — opt in by default
1117-
1118:Fallbacks are **opt-in**: without them a refused request simply stops. Include the server-side `fallbacks` parameter in `claude-fable-5` code by default — on a policy decline the API re-runs the same request on the fallback model inside the same call. A decline before any output isn't billed (a mid-stream decline bills the streamed partial); the rescue bills at the fallback model's own rates, with cache repricing applied automatically.

This suggests a failure mode that should be flagged. I also want to be cautious about how single argument arrays bind, as it might lead to unexpected behavior. 
13900

13902	
13903	I'm noticing another failure: `claude-copilot-once` is checking the proxy and doesn't auto-start, even though `claude-copilot/copy run` does. It seems to trigger Test-CopilotAlive before `copilot-here`, which instructs manual start — that’s concerning. The `wasOn` setting only checks valid JSON with the base URL. If the JSON is malformed, it creates an empty object, potentially destroying the original settings. Also, if any stale pin is refreshed and `copilot-here on` fails, it still might write to settings, which could lead to more issues. 
13904	
13905	**Exploring SpecStory behavior**
13906	
13907	When running `specstory run claude` without any arguments, I notice that SpecStory can resolve its configuration by itself. However, if there are any arguments included, the wrapper takes over and reads the configuration instead. It's interesting how the mode of operation changes based on whether args are present or not! This distinction seems significant, as it could impact how users interact with the tool and how configurations are managed.

```text
1	# copilot-proxy
2	
3	A native PowerShell port of the `copilot-proxy` tool series. It runs the
4	[`@jeffreycao/copilot-api`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@jeffreycao/copilot-api)
5	fork so a **GitHub Copilot subscription** can back **Claude Code** and other
6	Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible clients.
7	
8	The module is deployed to `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot` and imported by
9	the PowerShell profile. It requires Bun, Node/npm and a Copilot subscription.
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	| Command | What it does |
14	|---|---|
15	| `copilot-proxy auth` | one-time GitHub device login (`copilot-api auth login --provider copilot`; stores but does not display the token) |
16	| `copilot-proxy start` / `stop` / `restart` | manage the local proxy (port 4141) |
17	| `copilot-proxy status` | show raw served count and Claude availability |
18	| `copilot-proxy doctor [--live]` | diagnose package, auth, proxy, catalog, roles, upstream and Codex Apps |
19	| `copilot-proxy logs [N]` | tail the proxy log |
20	| `copilot-proxy shim [on\|off]` | toggle the throttle shim (port 4142) |
21	| `copilot-proxy whoami` | account / plan / quota |
22	| `copilot-proxy reinstall` | wipe and reinstall the pinned package |
23	| `copilot-run <cmd...>` | run a command with the proxy env injected |
24	| `claude-copilot` | one-off Claude Code session on the proxy |
25	| `claude-copilot-once` | pin this project, run once, then restore it |
26	| `codex-copilot` / `codex-copilot-once` | zero-persistence Codex session on the Responses proxy |
27	| `copilot-here [on\|off\|status]` | sticky project pin in `.claude/settings.local.json` |
28	| `copilot-model [<id>\|-l\|-c\|--auto]` | switch or inspect the complete role profile |
29	| `copilot-embed [TEXT\|-]` | embed text through `/v1/embeddings` |
30	| `semsearch index \| <QUERY>` | semantic search over local text |
31	
32	## Quick start
33	
34	```powershell
35	copilot-proxy auth                 # once
36	copilot-proxy start
37	copilot-model --auto              # select from the live catalog
38	copilot-model -c                   # inspect Main/Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku
39	copilot-here on                    # sticky project; or use claude-copilot-once
40	codex-copilot                     # Codex; live OpenAI-first model selection
41	```
42	
43	Existing global and project pins are deliberately not migrated by `chezmoi
44	apply`. Run `copilot-model --auto` once after this upgrade. When `copilot-here`
45	is active, that command refreshes the local role set; otherwise it updates the
46	global one-line main-model state.
47	
48	## How routing works
49	
50	```text
51	Claude Code --Anthropic /v1/messages--> copilot-api (localhost:4141)
52	                                          | Claude: native Messages path
53	                                          | GPT: Anthropic -> Responses translation
54	                                          v
55	                                  GitHub Copilot API
56	```
57	
58	The default package is `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0`. For GPT ids it translates
59	Claude Code requests to Responses, including `output_config.effort` to
60	`reasoning.effort`. This is required for GPT-5.6 and Claude Code's `ultracode`
61	effort setting; the old `1.13.14` path could replace the requested effort with a
62	hard-coded fallback.
63	
64	The package is installed once under `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`. Windows
65	uses `npm.cmd` first because it understands the Azure Artifacts credential
66	provider in `~/.npmrc`; Bun remains the fallback/runtime. Readiness is based on
67	the installed `package.json` name/version, a verified stamp, and a runnable launch
68	path—not merely an old directory or binlink. A failed install cannot restamp or
69	launch stale package contents. `COPILOT_API_PKG` accepts registry package specs
70	(name or `@scope/name` with an optional version/tag/range); npm aliases and
71	local/git/URL specs are rejected before filesystem cleanup. Warm starts do no
72	package network work.
73	
74	On a corporate mirror, `ETARGET` can mean the exact public version has not synced
75	yet. Check the registry that npm is actually using before deleting the working
76	prefix:
77	
78	```powershell
79	npm config get registry
80	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' version
81	# Optional comparison where direct public npm is permitted:
82	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' version --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/
83	```
84	
85	If only the configured mirror is missing the version, wait/request mirror sync or
86	use an approved registry for `copilot-proxy reinstall`. The Windows module also
87	falls back automatically to the exact 2.1.0 runtime files on jsDelivr, verifies a
88	baked SHA-256 for every file, then resolves only its ordinary dependencies through
89	the configured npm registry. This handles a lagging mirror without weakening the
90	pin or bypassing the approved feed for the dependency tree. Do not replace the
91	tested exact pin with `latest`.
92	
93	## Model selection and role profile
94	
95	`copilot-model --auto` requires the live `/v1/models` catalog. It prefers served
96	Claude families (`Fable > Opus > Sonnet > Haiku`), then ranks OpenAI by capability:
97	
98	```text
99	Sol > Terra > GPT-5.5 > GPT-5.4 > GPT-5.3 Codex > Luna > mini > Gemini
100	```
101	
102	Luna follows the older flagships because it is the lightweight tier. This role
103	intent follows OpenAI's [current model guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model).
104	For the normal Claude-less Copilot catalog, the generated profile is:
105	
106	| Claude Code role | Copilot model |
107	|---|---|
108	| Main / Fable / Opus | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
109	| Sonnet | `gpt-5.6-terra` |
110	| Haiku / background / legacy small-fast | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
111	
112	A manually selected OpenAI main remains Main/Fable/Opus; Terra and Luna are used
113	for the lower roles when served. Missing tiers fall back to the selected main,
114	never to an unserved hard-coded id. Native Claude profiles select the strongest
115	served model in each Claude family.
116	
117	The `[1m]` suffix is a Claude Code-only context hint. It is derived from each
118	model's live `max_context_window_tokens` metadata when the value is at least one
119	million. Raw API clients must use the plain id. Offline manual discovery remains
120	available, but offline `--auto` refuses to write a potentially stale pin.
121	
122	Both `copilot-run` and `copilot-here on` inject the same variables:
123	
124	```text
125	ANTHROPIC_MODEL
126	ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL
127	ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL
128	ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL
129	ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL
130	ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL
131	```
132	
133	`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` is intentionally left unset so workflow/frontmatter
134	routing remains authoritative. Restart Claude Code after changing the profile.
135	
136	## Claude Code feature compatibility
137	
138	The useful boundary is local orchestration versus Anthropic cloud services:
139	
140	| Feature | Through Copilot + GPT | Notes |
141	|---|---|---|
142	| CLI, tools, hooks, skills, memory, plugins, MCP, checkpoints, sandboxing | Yes | Local Claude Code features; GPT behavior may differ after prompt/tool translation. |
143	| Subagents and dynamic workflows | Yes | Role variables are provided without overriding workflow-specific subagent routing. See [workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows). |
144	| `ultracode` | Yes on 2.1.0 | It is xhigh effort plus dynamic workflows, not a separate model. |
145	| Thinking/reasoning | Translated | GPT uses Responses reasoning rather than Anthropic-native thinking semantics. |
146	| Web search, fast/auto mode, MCP tool search | Provider-dependent | Availability depends on the Copilot endpoint and gateway translation. |
147	| Ultrareview, Remote Control, Chrome, cloud Code Review, routines, web/mobile/Slack sessions | No | These require Claude.ai authentication/cloud identity; a local API gateway cannot provide it. |
148	
149	See Claude Code's [feature availability](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/feature-availability),
150	[model configuration](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config),
151	[gateway protocol](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol), and
152	[Ultrareview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ultrareview) references.
153	
154	## Network, entitlement and diagnostics
155	
156	- `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=auto` reads the Windows System Proxy or an explicit proxy
157	  environment variable, scopes it to the child and passes `--proxy-env`. Node
158	  otherwise ignores the WinINET system setting.
159	- The proxy refreshes its model cache periodically; a restart forces an immediate
160	  refresh. `COPILOT_PROXY_START_TIMEOUT` defaults to 45 seconds because a
161	  Clash/mihomo hop can make the initial refresh exceed the old 20-second budget.
162	- GitHub can vary the catalog by account, organization policy, rollout and egress.
163	  Claude IDs in `/v1/models` are therefore **advertised aliases**, not proof that
164	  inference is authorized. No Claude IDs is not by itself a broken proxy; use
165	  `copilot-model --auto` when you explicitly want to select another served pin.
166	  There is no automatic Claude-to-OpenAI replay after a failed request.
167	- `copilot-proxy doctor` compares direct and proxied upstream catalogs, validates
168	  the main model plus every role alias, and reports stale local pins. `--live`
169	  also compares direct/proxied reachability of remote ChatGPT `codex_apps`, then
170	  sends one real request to the effective configured main model (or a clearly
171	  labeled catalog fallback when that pin is absent). It never retries another
172	  model. Only this inference request consumes quota; timeout and TLS failures are
173	  reported separately.
174	- HTTP 402 with `billing_not_configured` is account-wide and nonretryable. Select
175	  an organization or enterprise under **Usage billed to** at
176	  <https://github.com/settings/copilot/features>. Model changes,
177	  `copilot-model --auto`, and shim toggles cannot repair that account setting.
178	- `copilot-here` writes only the gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json`, never
179	  committed project settings. `off` removes every env key owned by the helper and
180	  preserves unrelated settings.
181	- `claude-copilot` and `claude-copilot-once` retain the Windows port's trusted
182	  `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and optional SpecStory behavior. Plain `claude`
183	  is unaffected.
184	- The throttle shim remains byte-identical to the macOS/Linux copy and retries
185	  transient 403/429 bursts while limiting concurrent requests. It deliberately
186	  passes HTTP 402 through once; billing configuration is not a throttle failure.
187	
188	State lives under `~/.local/state/copilot-proxy/`; device login stores the GitHub
189	token at `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token` without printing it by default.
190	
191	## Codex through the gateway
192	
193	`codex-copilot` and its identical `codex-copilot-once` alias start the local
194	gateway/shim and pass a `copilot_api` Responses provider through one-invocation
195	Codex `-c` overrides. They do not edit user or project Codex config, so plain
196	`codex` is unaffected. An explicit `-m` / `--model` wins; otherwise the live raw
197	catalog is ranked OpenAI/Codex first (`Sol > Terra > GPT-5.5 > GPT-5.4 > GPT-5.3
198	Codex > Luna > mini`), then Claude, Gemini and other chat models. Disabled and
199	embedding models are excluded.
200	
201	Codex always uses the shim on `localhost:4142`, even when the persisted
202	throttling toggle is off. Besides throttling, that boundary normalizes blank
203	descriptions in Codex `mcp_list_tools` Responses items. GitHub Copilot rejects
204	those with `Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string`, while MCP
205	servers and the native Codex path may omit them. The shim fills only those tool
206	definition fields and leaves prompts, schemas, and tool names unchanged.
207	Codex currently zstd-compresses these requests; the shim decodes only the
208	Responses body it must repair, forwards ordinary JSON, and removes the stale
209	`content-encoding` header.
210	
211	This is a separate picker from Claude Code's `copilot-model --auto`: that path
212	remains Claude-first, while only the Codex launcher is OpenAI-first.
213	
214	SpecStory is automatic when installed. The wrapper preserves the effective
215	`codex_cmd` (project config > user config > bare `codex`) before appending
```
</details></tool-use>

14866	+#Requires -Version 7
14867	+# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1 — merge a managed overlay into
14868	+# ~/.claude/settings.json so claude-hud (statusline HUD), the pyright-lsp
14869	+# plugin, and a couple of safe defaults deploy on Windows. Companion to the
14870	+# parent (macOS/Linux) repo's dot_claude/modify_settings.json; that repo uses a
14871	+# `modify_` + jq merge, which is unreliable on Windows (invariant #5), so we use
14872	+# the same run_onchange pwsh-merger idiom as the editor overlays instead.
14873	+#
14874	+# Why a merge (not a managed dot_claude/settings.json)? Claude Code rewrites
14875	+# this file at runtime (plugins it installs, permissions the user grants). A
14876	+# static managed file would clobber all of that on every apply. We instead
14877	+# recursively deep-merge only our keys in, preserving every live key.
14878	+#
14879	+# Gated on installCodingAgents — no Claude Code, nothing to configure. Re-runs
14880	+# when the embedded overlay (claude/settings-overlay.json) changes.
14881	+{{ if .installCodingAgents -}}
14882	+$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'   # best-effort; never abort the apply
14883	+
14884	+# Embedded at render time from the (chezmoi-ignored) claude/ source, so this
14885	+# script is self-contained and re-fires when the overlay changes.
14886	+$overlayJson = @'
14887	+{{ include "claude/settings-overlay.json" }}
14888	+'@
14889	+
14890	+$overlay = $overlayJson | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable
14891	+
14892	+# Recursive deep-merge: overlay leaves win; live-only keys are preserved. Unlike
14893	+# the editor overlay's shallow top-level assign, this keeps the user's nested
14894	+# state (e.g. permissions.allow/deny arrays, other enabledPlugins) intact.
14895	+function Merge-Hashtable([hashtable]$base, [hashtable]$overlay) {
14896	+    foreach ($k in $overlay.Keys) {
14897	+        if ($base.ContainsKey($k) -and ($base[$k] -is [hashtable]) -and ($overlay[$k] -is [hashtable])) {
14898	+            Merge-Hashtable $base[$k] $overlay[$k]
14899	+        } else {
14900	+            $base[$k] = $overlay[$k]
14901	+        }
14902	+    }
14903	+}
14904	+
14905	+# Respect CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (matches the statusLine command + claude-hud setup).
14906	+$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME '.claude' }
14907	+$settingsPath = Join-Path $claudeDir 'settings.json'

14909	+$settings = @{}

14914	+        catch { Write-Warning "could not parse $settingsPath; not overwriting"; return }
14915	+    }
14916	+}
14917	+
14918	+Merge-Hashtable $settings $overlay

14920	+$settings | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12 | Set-Content -Path $settingsPath -Encoding utf8
14921	+Write-Host "claude overlay -> $settingsPath"
14922	+{{ end -}}

210	
211	This is a separate picker from Claude Code's `copilot-model --auto`: that path
212	remains Claude-first, while only the Codex launcher is OpenAI-first.
213	
214	SpecStory is automatic when installed. The wrapper preserves the effective
215	`codex_cmd` (project config > user config > bare `codex`) before appending
216	provider/model/user arguments; `--no-specstory` runs Codex directly. Claude and
217	Gemini fallback through Responses Lite, which does not support Responses
218	`tool_search`, so native Responses OpenAI models stay ahead of Anthropic.
219	The launcher also enables gateway-backed remote compaction and excludes the
220	`mcp__codex_apps__sites` namespace that depends on unavailable `tool_search`;
221	later explicit `-c` arguments can override either setting per invocation.
222	
223	`codex_apps` itself is not a localhost service and not an Apple-Silicon-only
224	Codex Desktop bridge. It is a remote MCP at
225	`https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/apps`, so startup can fail even while
226	Copilot inference on `localhost:4142` works. Keep Apps enabled and use
227	`copilot-proxy doctor --live` to diagnose that route independently.
228	
229	There is deliberately no Codex equivalent of `copilot-here`: project
230	`.codex/config.toml` cannot override provider definitions, provider selection or
231	auth metadata. The explicit launcher provides project/session scope without
232	changing the user-wide default.
233	
234	### Experimental direct configuration
235	
236	The direct `model_providers.copilot-enterprise` example is documented in the
237	macOS/Linux guide rather than installed. It is not the localhost proxy path, and
238	the pasted `gh auth token` flow is not portable: on the tested EMU account it
239	returned `421`/`403`, while the credential stored by `copilot-proxy auth` plus
240	the normal short-lived Copilot token exchange worked. The supported launcher
241	therefore uses the authenticated local gateway.
242
```

17299	## HUD failure modes
17300	
17301	1. **`installCodingAgents` off:** no merge occurs. Turning it off later also does not remove previously merged HUD/plugin keys.
17302	2. **Claude not restarted:** plugin self-install may not have occurred yet.
17303	3. **Plugin cache absent:** `plugin_dir` becomes empty and the command attempts `node dist/index.js` rather than explicitly no-oping.
17304	4. **Marketplace/network/plugin installation failure:** settings can show the plugin enabled while no usable cache exists.
17305	5. **Node unavailable in Claude’s command environment:** `command -v node` returns empty and the status line fails.
17306	6. **Different command shell:** the command assumes Cygwin/MSYS bash. Native cmd or PowerShell cannot interpret it.
17307	7. **Different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` between apply and runtime:** the merger can update one config root while the running Claude process searches another.
17308	8. **Malformed settings JSON:** the merger safely declines to overwrite, but because this is a successful-returning run-onchange script, an unchanged apply may not retry after the JSON is repaired.
17309	9. **Non-atomic write:** `Set-Content` rewrites the whole file directly; interruption can leave malformed JSON.
17310	10. **Managed conflicts are intentional:** a user’s existing `statusLine.type`, `statusLine.command`, plugin enablement, `permissions.defaultMode`, or matching marketplace fields are overwritten by overlay values.

1	#Requires -Version 7
2	# Guards hard invariant #1 (AGENTS.md): every init prompt in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl
3	# must have a matching non-interactive flag in .github/workflows/windows.yml.
4	#
5	# Why this exists: adding a prompt without the flag does not fail loudly at
6	# authoring time — it fails much later, on the Windows runner, as an opaque
7	#   error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF
8	# because `chezmoi init --no-tty` has no answer for the new question and hits
9	# end-of-input. That broke CI for three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds`
10	# was added. This test turns that into a local `Invoke-Pester` failure with the
11	# exact missing flag line to paste in.
12	#
13	# Matching is on the prompt's TEXT (3rd arg to promptXOnce), because that is
14	# what chezmoi's `--promptBool 'text=value'` parser keys on — not the variable
15	# name.
16	
17	BeforeAll {
18	    $repo = Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent
19	    $tomlTmpl = Join-Path $repo '.chezmoi.toml.tmpl'
20	    $workflow = Join-Path $repo '.github/workflows/windows.yml'
21	
22	    # promptBoolOnce . "varName" "Prompt text" <default>
23	    $script:Prompts = [regex]::Matches(
24	        (Get-Content -Raw $tomlTmpl),
25	        'prompt(?<kind>Bool|String|Choice)Once\s+\.\s+"(?<var>[^"]+)"\s+"(?<text>[^"]+)"'
26	    ) | ForEach-Object {
27	        [pscustomobject]@{
28	            Kind = $_.Groups['kind'].Value
29	            Var  = $_.Groups['var'].Value
30	            Text = $_.Groups['text'].Value
31	        }
32	    }
33	
34	    # '--promptBool','Prompt text=value'
35	    $script:Flags = [regex]::Matches(
36	        (Get-Content -Raw $workflow),
37	        "'--prompt(?<kind>Bool|String|Choice)'\s*,\s*'(?<text>[^=']+)="
38	    ) | ForEach-Object {
39	        [pscustomobject]@{
40	            Kind = $_.Groups['kind'].Value
41	            Text = $_.Groups['text'].Value
42	        }
43	    }
44	}
45	
46	# NB: no angle brackets in Describe/It names — Pester expands `<...>` in test
47	# names as a data placeholder, so a name like "prompts <-> flags" is rewritten
48	# to `$-` and the whole file dies with a bogus CommandNotFoundException.
49	Describe 'init prompts vs CI flags (invariant #1)' {
50	    It 'finds prompts in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl' {
51	        $script:Prompts.Count | Should -BeGreaterThan 10
52	    }
53	
54	    It 'finds prompt flags in windows.yml' {
55	        $script:Flags.Count | Should -BeGreaterThan 10
56	    }
57	
58	    It 'has a CI flag for every init prompt' {
59	        $flagText = @($script:Flags.Text)
60	        $missing = @($script:Prompts | Where-Object { $flagText -notcontains $_.Text })
61	        $hint = ($missing | ForEach-Object {
62	            "            '--prompt$($_.Kind)','$($_.Text)=<value>',   # $($_.Var)"
63	        }) -join "`n"
64	        $missing.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "windows.yml is missing these flags; add to the `$flags array:`n$hint"
65	    }
66	
67	    It 'has no stale CI flag without a matching prompt' {
68	        # Catches the other half of a rename: the prompt text changed but the
69	        # flag did not. chezmoi silently ignores an unmatched flag and then
70	        # blocks on the real prompt, so this would otherwise be invisible.
71	        $promptText = @($script:Prompts.Text)
72	        $stale = @($script:Flags | Where-Object { $promptText -notcontains $_.Text })
73	        $stale.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "these windows.yml flags match no prompt: $($stale.Text -join '; ')"
74	    }
75	
76	    It 'uses the right flag kind for each prompt' {
77	        $byText = @{}
78	        foreach ($f in $script:Flags) { $byText[$f.Text] = $f.Kind }
79	        $wrong = @($script:Prompts | Where-Object {
80	            $byText.ContainsKey($_.Text) -and $byText[$_.Text] -ne $_.Kind
81	        })
82	        $wrong.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "flag kind mismatch for: $($wrong.Var -join '; ')"
83	    }
84	
85	    It 'has no "=" in any prompt text' {
86	        # Invariant #1 corollary: chezmoi's `name=value` parser splits on the
87	        # FIRST "=", so a prompt whose text contains one can never be answered
88	        # non-interactively. This already broke the `role` prompt once.
89	        $bad = @($script:Prompts | Where-Object { $_.Text -match '=' })
90	        $bad.Count | Should -Be 0 -Because "prompt text may not contain '=': $($bad.Var -join '; ')"
91	    }
92	}
93

55	**3. peon-ping lives under `~/.openpeon`, not `~/.claude`.** It is installed
56	with `-OpenPeon`, which reroots its whole tree to a tool-agnostic root so the
57	installer never touches `~/.claude/settings.json` — hook wiring is ours to
58	declare. `peon.ps1` is therefore at
59	`~/.openpeon/hooks/peon-ping/peon.ps1`.
60	
61	Note the installer's parameter block is
62	`param([string[]]$Packs, [switch]$All, [string]$Lang, [switch]$Local, [switch]$Global, [switch]$OpenPeon, [switch]$InitLocalConfig)`
63	— there is **no `-NoRc`** (that is the bash `install.sh` flag), and it does not
64	touch `$PROFILE`.
65	
66	## Where the wiring lives
67	
68	| Concern | File |
69	|---|---|
70	| The prompt | `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` |
71	| Hook entries + prune | `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl` |
72	| Binary install | `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` |
73	| Non-hook overlay (statusLine, plugins) | `claude/settings-overlay.json` |
74	
75	The hook entries had to move **out** of `claude/settings-overlay.json` and into
76	the run_onchange: that JSON is `include`d verbatim, so it cannot carry the
77	Go-template conditionals the tiers need.
78	
79	## The one place we subtract
80	
81	The merge is additive so foreign hook entries (CodeIsland, anything you add by
82	hand) survive. One exception: entries matching **our own** command fingerprints
83	(`notify\.ps1`, `peon\.ps1`) are pruned when the current tier disables them.
84	
85	Without it `agentSounds` is a one-way ratchet — switching `notify` → `none`
86	would leave `notify.ps1` wired forever, so `none` wouldn't actually silence a
87	machine that previously had sound. Upstream's own `install.ps1` strips the same
88	two fingerprints before re-adding, so this matches its behaviour.
89	
90	## peon's config is deliberately unmanaged
91	
92	`peon volume` / `notifications` / `packs use` write `~/.openpeon/config.json` at
93	runtime. chezmoi does not manage that file, so tweaking any of it produces
94	**no** drift. The installer seeds and activates `league_of_legends` once and is skipped on later applies
95	(guarded on `peon.ps1` existing), so a pack you switch to later sticks.
96	
97	## Verify
98

50	它會把整棵樹改根到 tool-agnostic 的位置，這樣安裝器就永遠不會碰
51	`~/.claude/settings.json` —— hook 由我們自己宣告。所以 `peon.ps1` 的位置是
52	`~/.openpeon/hooks/peon-ping/peon.ps1`。
53	
54	順帶一提，安裝器的參數區塊是
55	`param([string[]]$Packs, [switch]$All, [string]$Lang, [switch]$Local, [switch]$Global, [switch]$OpenPeon, [switch]$InitLocalConfig)`
56	—— **沒有 `-NoRc`**（那是 bash `install.sh` 的 flag），而且它不會動 `$PROFILE`。

58	## 接線在哪
59	
60	| 負責什麼 | 檔案 |
61	|---|---|
62	| prompt | `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` |
63	| hook 條目 + prune | `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl` |
64	| 安裝 binary | `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` |
65	| 非 hook overlay（statusLine、plugins） | `claude/settings-overlay.json` |
66	
67	hook 條目必須從 `claude/settings-overlay.json` **搬出來**放進 run_onchange：那個 JSON
68	是被原封不動 `include` 進來的，沒辦法帶 Go-template 條件式。

71	
72	合併是加法式的，所以外部的 hook 條目（CodeIsland、你手動加的）都會保留。只有一個例外：
73	符合**我們自己**指令指紋（`notify\.ps1`、`peon\.ps1`）的條目，會在目前層級關掉它時被移除。

46967	### 2. Why SpecStory uses `create_config.toml`
46968	
46969	`private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml` maps to private, create-only `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`.
46970	
46971	The file’s own contract is user ownership:
46972	
46973	- `private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:3-7` defines it as user-level global defaults and establishes precedence: project settings override it, and CLI flags override both.
46974	- `private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:9-11` invites the user to uncomment and edit settings.
46975	- Most of `:13-63` is a commented customization template.
46976	- Only the provider commands at `:65-83` are active defaults.
46977	
46978	The history is unambiguous:
46979	
46980	- `8f64d91` — 2026-07-09, `feat: parity toggles, Docker/Discord, mirrors, backup, agent-skill junction`
46981	  - Commit message: “SpecStory: seed `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` (`private_ create_`) mirroring the main repo’s provider commands.”
46982	  - `git blame` attributes all 83 lines to this commit.
46983	  - No subsequent commit modified the global seed.
46984	- `463e8be` — 2026-07-10, `Backup chat history and plan`
46985	  - Added project-local `.specstory/cli/config.toml`.
46986	  - `.specstory/cli/config.toml:1-7` identifies it as project-level.
46987	  - `.specstory/cli/config.toml:61-67` contains runtime-oriented resume state.
46988	  - `.specstory/cli/config.toml:69-90` leaves provider commands commented and adds DeepSeek.
46989	
46990	That divergence also shows that the create-only baseline is now older than the project sample: it lacks `[resume]` and `deepseek_cmd`. That is expected under seed-once semantics; updating the source does not retrofit existing targets.
46991	
46992	#### Why not a plain managed file?
46993	
46994	A plain managed file would overwrite the user’s global defaults and provider customization on each apply, contradicting both:
46995	
46996	- the comments at `private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:3-11`, and
46997	- the commit’s explicit use of the word “seed.”
46998	
46999	The repository uses the same ownership model elsewhere: `README.md:54,61-67` describes the create-only SSH skeleton and states that an existing target is never overwritten.
47000	
47001	#### Why not `modify_`?
47002	
47003	`docs/rationale.md:133-159` explains the Windows limitation:
47004	
47005	- `docs/rationale.md:143-150`: chezmoi routes a modifier using the target extension. A modifier targeting `config.toml` routes as TOML, not PowerShell.
47006	- Windows cannot rely on a Unix shebang or executable bit.
47007	- `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:61-64` only configures the `.ps1` interpreter.
47008	
47009	Thus a PowerShell `modify_config.toml` is not a reliable native-Windows mechanism.
47010	
47011	#### Why not a `run_onchange` merger?
47012	
47013	A `run_onchange` merger would be technically viable, but its semantics would differ. The repository reserves these mergers for surfaces where it deliberately owns selected keys while preserving surrounding runtime state; see `docs/rationale.md:135-159`.
47014	
47015	The SpecStory introduction did not claim such ongoing ownership. It explicitly seeded a user-editable configuration. A merger is justified only if the provider commands are reclassified as enforced repository policy.
47016

47019	### 3. Recommendation
47020	
47021	**Keep `create_` under the current contract.**
47022	
47023	This best matches the commit history, precedence comments, and security implications of the active provider commands:
47024	
47025	- `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`
47026	- Codex with `--ask-for-approval never --sandbox danger-full-access`
47027	- `cursor-agent --force`
47028	- `droid --yolo`
47029	- `gemini --sandbox=none`
47030	
47031	These commands define user security posture, not merely cosmetic defaults. Existing user changes should not be silently reasserted by dotfiles.
47032	
47033	Recommended order:
47034	
47035	1. **Current recommendation: keep `create_`.**
47036	   - Preserves all post-seed customization.
47037	   - Matches `8f64d91`’s stated intent.
47038	   - Allows project config and CLI flags to override naturally.
47039	
47040	2. **If provider commands become explicit managed policy: use a key-level `run_onchange` PowerShell merger.**
47041	   - Own only `[providers].claude_cmd`, `codex_cmd`, `cursor_cmd`, `droid_cmd`, and `gemini_cmd`.
47042	   - Preserve every other section and unknown provider, including `[resume]` and DeepSeek.
47043	   - Make overlay-wins behavior and its security implications explicit, preferably behind an opt-in toggle.
47044	
47045	3. **Do not use a plain managed override.**
47046	   - It would erase user/runtime additions wholesale.
47047	
47048	4. **Do not use `modify_` on Windows.**
47049	   - The repository’s documented interpreter-routing limitation applies directly to a TOML target.

47098	### Why setup did not run automatically
47099	
47100	Plugin enablement does not execute plugin slash commands. The plugin manifest only **registers** `setup` and `configure`; it has no startup hook that runs them:
47101	
47102	```text
47103	~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-hud/claude-hud/0.7.1/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:9-12
47104	```
47105	
47106	Our implementation intentionally copied the important output of `/claude-hud:setup`—the `statusLine` value—into the chezmoi overlay. It never invokes the setup command itself; the settings merger only edits JSON at [`run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl:138-172`](.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl#L138-L172).
47107	
47108	There is also a first-launch ordering issue:
47109	
47110	1. Claude reads `enabledPlugins`.
47111	2. Claude materializes the plugin cache during startup.
47112	3. The status line may run before that cache is ready.
47113	4. The current session does not reload the settings/plugin afterward.
47114	
47115	That explains why a second Claude launch was required.

47153	## SpecStory: why `create_` was used
47154	
47155	It was intentional. Commit history shows the file was introduced as a **one-time seed** for a user-owned config:
47156	
47157	[`private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml:3-11`](private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml#L3-L11)
47158	
47159	Most of the file consists of commented options that the user is expected to customize. `create_` means:
47160	
47161	- create `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` when absent;
47162	- never overwrite an existing file;
47163	- preserve cloud sync, logging, analytics, telemetry, resume state, custom providers, and future SpecStory fields.
47164	
47165	That is normally the correct policy for a user configuration file.
47166	
47167	### Why it failed here
47168	
47169	The provider commands at [`create_config.toml:65-83`](private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml#L65-L83) are different from ordinary preferences. They establish behavior relied upon by our wrappers, including:
47170	
47171	```toml
47172	claude_cmd = "claude --dangerously-skip-permissions"
47173	```
47174	
47175	Because the live config existed before chezmoi tried to seed it, `create_` did nothing. The source said bypass should be enabled, but the live file retained SpecStory’s plain commented defaults.
47176	
47177	So we mixed two incompatible ownership models in one file:
47178	
47179	- most fields are user-owned preferences;
47180	- provider launch commands are intended dotfiles policy.
47181	
47182	### Should we override the SpecStory config?
47183	
47184	**Not the whole file.** A plain managed file would repeatedly erase:
47185	
47186	- `[local_sync]` and `[cloud_sync]` choices
47187	- telemetry/logging preferences
47188	- CLI-managed `[resume]` state
47189	- custom provider commands
47190	- new fields introduced by future SpecStory versions
47191	
47192	Instead, use a **key-level overlay** that owns only selected `[providers]` keys and pulls everything else through unchanged.
47193	
47194	Recommended behavior:
47195	
47196	```text
47197	Live config
47198	  + enforce providers.claude_cmd
47199	  + optionally enforce the other provider commands already active in our seed
47200	  + preserve every other table, key, comment, and unknown provider
47201	```
47202	
47203	Because PowerShell `modify_` routing for a `.toml` target is unreliable on Windows, this should be a fail-closed `run_onchange` PowerShell merger, following the existing Claude/Codex/herdr patterns.
47204	
47205	I would also harden `claude-copilot` itself so its documented bypass behavior does not depend solely on external SpecStory configuration. The wrapper should ensure its generated `-c` command contains `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, while direct `specstory run claude` can still follow the managed provider key.
47206	
47207	## Recommended change set
47208	
47209	1. **HUD**
47210	   - Manage the Full-preset `config.json` as an overlay.
47211	   - Preserve advanced user-only HUD settings.
47212	   - Make missing plugin cache a clean temporary no-op.
47213	   - Update stale Bun wording in [`docs/tools.md:157-164`](docs/tools.md#L157-L164).
47214	
47215	2. **SpecStory**
47216	   - Replace seed-only ownership for provider commands with a key-level run-onchange merger.
47217	   - Preserve all non-provider settings and unknown keys.
47218	   - Harden `claude-copilot` to enforce its own bypass contract.
47219	   - Add tests for stale, absent, customized, and future-expanded TOML files.
47220	
47221	A full-file SpecStory override is not recommended; a targeted overlay is.

47459	# dotfiles-windows
47460	
47461	This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
47462	Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
47463	there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
47464	(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)
47465	
47466	## Orientation
47467	- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
47468	- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
47469	- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
47470	- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
47471	- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).
47472	
47473	## Shell layout (pwsh)
47474	- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
47475	  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
47476	  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
47477	- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
47478	  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
47479	  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
47480	  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
47481	  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).
47482	
47483	## Packages
47484	- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the **single source of
47485	  truth** for installs, gated by the init toggles. scoop = CLI tools, winget = GUI
47486	  apps, npm = AI agents, PSGallery = PSFzf/AudioDeviceCmdlets. Fault-tolerant: one
47487	  failed package is collected + reported, never aborts the apply.
47488	- Package sources are defined once in `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` and
47489	  reused by the installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines
47490	  use company PyPI/npm pull-through registries; otherwise the China-mirror toggle
47491	  selects GFW mirrors. Managed-machine policy wins if both toggles are true.
47492	- Install ≠ upgrade: `chezmoi apply` only installs what's missing; upgrade via
47493	  `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`.
47494	
47495	## copilot-proxy
47496	- Module at `~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot`. Commands: `copilot-proxy`
47497	  (`start`/`stop`/`restart`/`status`/`doctor`/`logs`/`shim`/`whoami`/`auth`/`reinstall`),
47498	  `copilot-run`, `claude-copilot`, `claude-copilot-once`, `copilot-here`,
47499	  `copilot-model` (incl. `--auto`), `copilot-embed`, `semsearch`.
47500	- Needs `bun`. Token: `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`. Ports 4141 (proxy) /
47501	  4142 (throttle shim). Default main model `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`; the OpenAI role
47502	  profile maps Fable/Opus to Sol, Sonnet to Terra, and Haiku/background to Luna.
47503	  `copilot-here` writes
47504	  only the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. The pinned copilot-api is
47505	  installed ONCE into `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg` (never `bunx` at launch);
47506	  `COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY` (auto|always|never|URL) controls whether Node fetches the
47507	  GitHub model catalog through the local proxy. Full guide: `docs/copilot-proxy.md`.
47508	
47509	## Editors / terminal / tv
47510	- VSCode & Cursor settings + keybindings are deep-merged into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`
47511	  by `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_20_editor_overlays.ps1.tmpl` (sources under `editors/`).
47512	- Windows Terminal `profiles.defaults`, Alacritty (`%APPDATA%\alacritty\alacritty.toml`),
47513	  and WezTerm (`~/.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua`, pwsh as default shell) are managed too.
47514	  Television channels live under `%APPDATA%\television\cable\` (`tv <name>`).

47519	- Extra runtimes: true · Media: false · LLM: true · Tunnel: false · IaC: false · OpenSSH: false · herdr: true · Clink(cmd): true · try: true · translate: true · Rime/Weasel: false
47520	- China mirrors: false · Backup mode: smart · Vim mode: true · Managed machine: true

47524	`docs-serve`/`docs-build`, `enable-sshd` (opt-in OpenSSH server, elevated),

47532	## Gotchas
47533	- Windows-only repo — no `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os }}` branching needed.
47534	- Editor settings use a `run_onchange` pwsh merger (not `modify_`) on Windows.
47535	- tmux / zellij are Unix-only and intentionally absent; **WezTerm** (installed) is
47536	  the stable native tmux-like multiplexer, or use Windows Terminal panes. **herdr**
47537	  is an opt-in (`installHerdr`) native-Windows multiplexer in preview beta —
47538	  installed via herdr.dev's `irm|iex` script, config at `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`.
47539	  Runtimes are native via scoop (node/bun/go/rust/ruby) + uv for Python — no mise on Windows.
47540	- **Rime input method** (opt-in `installInputMethod`): Weasel/小狼毫 via winget
47541	  `Rime.Weasel`. Machine-scope NSIS, so applying raises UAC; and a bare silent
47542	  install registers **简体** — `Install-Weasel` passes `--custom '/T'` for 繁體.
47543	  The engine-level YAML in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` is **byte-identical to the
47544	  parent repo's** copy (Squirrel/ibus-rime); only `weasel.custom.yaml` is
47545	  Windows-specific. Edits need a redeploy, which
47546	  `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
47547	  See `docs/input-method.md`.
47548	- **cmd.exe** is opt-in via `installClink`: Clink + starship/zoxide/fzf give the DOS
47549	  prompt parity for **prompt + navigation only** (no pwsh funcs/aliases/modules).
47550	  `starship.lua` is chezmoi-managed at `%LocalAppData%\clink`; the zoxide/fzf Clink
47551	  bridges are fetched from upstream at apply. pwsh stays the default shell.
47552	- **`translate`** (`installTranslate`, on for workstation) is the one tool built from
47553	  source: no scoop/winget manifest, so the packages script runs a version-pinned
47554	  `go install` into `~\.local\bin` (it installs `go` itself). First build takes
47555	  minutes; re-applies no-op via a `--version` check. Upgrade with
47556	  `just upgrade-translate`, not `upgrade-scoop`.
47557	- This skill body is shared: `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/` and
47558	  `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/` both render `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.

8	**FIRST**: Use the Read tool to load `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json` if it exists.
9	
10	Store current values and note whether config exists (determines which flow to use).
11	
12	## Core Features (on by default)
13	
14	These default to ON and are what most users keep. They ARE configurable
15	(`display.showModel`, `display.showContextBar`), but the guided flow keeps them
16	enabled — toggle them by editing `config.json` directly if needed:
17	- Model name `[Opus]`
18	- Context bar `████░░░░░░ 45%`
19	
20	Advanced settings such as `colors.*`, `pathLevels`, `maxWidth`, `forceMaxWidth`,
21	`elementOrder`, `projectLineOrder`, `display.mergeGroups`, `display.timeFormat`, `display.contextValue`,
22	`display.modelFormat`, `display.modelOverride`, `display.modelSource`, `display.showProvider`,
23	`display.providerName`, `display.autocompactBuffer`,
24	`display.autoCompactWindow`, `display.promptCacheTtlSeconds`,
25	`display.usageThreshold`, `display.sevenDayThreshold`,
26	`display.environmentThreshold`, `display.contextWarningThreshold`,
27	`display.contextCriticalThreshold`, `display.advisorOverride`,
28	`display.showAuth`, `display.showAuthUser`, `display.authUserLength`, and the
29	`display.externalUsage*` keys, plus `jjStatus.showDirty` and
30	`jjStatus.showConflicts`, are preserved when saving but are not edited by this
31	guided flow.

34	
35	## Two Flows Based on Config State
36	
37	### Flow A: New User (no config)
38	Questions: **Layout → Preset → Language → Turn Off → Turn On → Custom Line**
39	
40	### Flow B: Update Config (config exists)
41	Questions: **Turn Off → Turn On → Git Style → Layout/Reset → Language → Custom Line** (6 questions max)
