246	## Preset Definitions
247	
248	**Full** (everything ON):
249	- Activity: Tools ON, Skills ON, MCP ON, Agents ON, Todos ON
250	- Info: Added Dirs ON, Counts ON, Tokens ON, Usage ON, Reset Label ON, Cost ON, Duration ON, Session Name ON, Session Tokens ON, Reasoning Level ON, Output Style ON, Memory ON, Prompt Cache ON, CC Version ON, Compactions ON, Advisor ON
251	- Git: ON (with dirty indicator, no ahead/behind)
252	- Jujutsu: ON (opted in, with dirty and conflict indicators)
253	
254	**Essential** (activity + git):
255	- Activity: Tools ON, Agents ON, Todos ON
256	- Info: Counts OFF, Tokens OFF, Usage OFF, Duration ON, Session Name OFF, Session Tokens OFF
257	- Git: ON (with dirty indicator)
258	- Jujutsu: OFF
259	
260	**Minimal** (core only — this is the default):
261	- Activity: Tools OFF, Agents OFF, Todos OFF
262	- Info: Counts OFF, Tokens OFF, Usage OFF, Duration OFF, Session Name OFF, Session Tokens OFF
263	- Git: ON (with dirty indicator)
264	- Jujutsu: OFF

345	---
346	
347	## Usage Style Mapping
348	
349	| Option | Config | Example |
350	|--------|--------|---------|
351	| Bar style | `usageBarEnabled: true` | `Usage ██░░ 25% (resets in 1h 30m)` |
352	| Text style | `usageBarEnabled: false` | `Usage 5h 25% (resets in 1h 30m)` |
353	| Compact | `usageCompact: true` | `5h: 25% (1h 30m)` — no "Usage" label, shorter reset format |
354	
355	`usageCompact` takes precedence over `usageBarEnabled` when both are set. Compact mode always uses the text format (no bar).
356	
357	**Note**: Usage style only applies when `display.showUsage: true`. When 7d usage >= 80%, it also shows with the same style.
358	Set `display.usageValue: "remaining"` manually to show remaining quota percentages while keeping warning thresholds based on used quota.
359	
360	---
361	
362	## Processing Logic
363	
364	### For New Users (Flow A):
365	1. Apply chosen preset as base
366	2. Apply chosen language
367	3. Apply Turn Off selections (set those items to OFF)
368	4. Apply Turn On selections (set those items to ON)
369	5. Apply chosen layout
370	
371	### For Returning Users (Flow B):
372	1. Start from current config
373	2. Apply Turn Off selections (set to OFF, including usageBarEnabled if selected)
374	3. Apply Turn On selections (set to ON, including usageBarEnabled if selected)
375	4. Apply Git Style selection (if shown)
376	5. If "Reset to [preset]" selected, override with preset values
377	6. If layout change selected, apply it
378	7. If language change selected, apply it
379	
380	---
381	
382	## Before Writing - Validate & Preview
383	
384	**GUARDS - Do NOT write config if:**
385	- User cancels (Esc) → say "Configuration cancelled."
386	- No changes from current config → say "No changes needed - config unchanged."
387	
388	**Show preview before saving:**
389	
390	1. **Summary of changes:**
391	```
392	Layout: Compact → Expanded
393	Language: English → 中文
394	Git style: Branch + dirty
395	Changes:
396	  - Usage limits: OFF → ON
397	  - Config counts: ON → OFF
398	```
399	
400	2. **Preview of HUD (Expanded layout):**
401	```
402	[Opus | Pro] │ my-project git:(main*)
403	Context ████░░░░░ 45% │ Usage ██░░░░░░░░ 25% (1h 30m / 5h)
404	◐ Edit: file.ts | ✓ Read ×3
405	▸ Fix auth bug (2/5)
406	```
407	
408	**Preview of HUD (Compact layout):**
409	```
410	[Opus | Pro] ████░░░░░ 45% | my-project git:(main*) | 5h: 25% | ⏱️ 5m
411	◐ Edit: file.ts | ✓ Read ×3
412	▸ Fix auth bug (2/5)
413	```
414	
415	3. **Confirm**: "Save these changes?"
416	
417	---
418	
419	## Write Configuration
420	
421	Write to `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json`.
422	
423	Merge with existing config, preserving:
424	- `pathLevels` (not in configure flow)
425	- `display.usageThreshold` (advanced config)
426	- `display.environmentThreshold` (advanced config)
427	- `display.contextWarningThreshold` (advanced config)
428	- `display.contextCriticalThreshold` (advanced config)
429	- `colors` (advanced manual palette overrides)
430	
431	**Migration note**: Old configs with `layout: "default"` or `layout: "separators"` are automatically migrated to the new `lineLayout` + `showSeparators` format on load.
432	
433	---
434	
435	## After Writing
436	
437	Say: "Configuration saved! The HUD will reflect your changes immediately."
438

374	export function getConfigPath(): string {
375	  const homeDir = os.homedir();
376	  return path.join(getHudPluginDir(homeDir), 'config.json');

379	function validatePathLevels(value: unknown): value is PathLevels {
380	  return value === 1 || value === 2 || value === 3 || value === 'full';
381	}
382	
383	function validateLineLayout(value: unknown): value is LineLayoutType {
384	  return value === 'compact' || value === 'expanded';
385	}
386	
387	function validateAutocompactBuffer(value: unknown): value is AutocompactBufferMode {
388	  return value === 'enabled' || value === 'disabled';
389	}
390	
391	function validateGitBranchOverflow(value: unknown): value is GitBranchOverflowMode {
392	  return value === 'truncate' || value === 'wrap';
393	}
394	
395	function validateContextValue(value: unknown): value is ContextValueMode {
396	  return value === 'percent' || value === 'tokens' || value === 'remaining' || value === 'both';
397	}
398	
399	function validateUsageValue(value: unknown): value is UsageValueMode {
400	  return value === 'percent' || value === 'remaining';
401	}
402	
403	function validateLanguage(value: unknown): value is Language {
404	  return value === 'en' || value === 'zh' || value === 'zh-Hans' || value === 'zh-Hant' || value === 'zh-TW';
405	}
406	
407	function validateModelFormat(value: unknown): value is ModelFormatMode {
408	  return value === 'full' || value === 'compact' || value === 'short';
409	}
410	
411	function validateTimeFormat(value: unknown): value is TimeFormatMode {
412	  return value === 'relative'
413	    || value === 'absolute'
414	    || value === 'both'
415	    || value === 'elapsed'
416	    || value === 'elapsedAndAbsolute';
417	}
418	
419	function validateCustomLinePosition(value: unknown): value is CustomLinePosition {
420	  return value === 'first' || value === 'last';
421	}
422	
423	function validateHourCycle(value: unknown): value is HourCycleMode {
424	  return value === 'auto' || value === 'h11' || value === 'h12' || value === 'h23' || value === 'h24';
425	}
426	
427	function validateColorName(value: unknown): value is HudColorName {
428	  return value === 'dim'
429	    || value === 'red'
430	    || value === 'green'
431	    || value === 'yellow'
432	    || value === 'magenta'
433	    || value === 'cyan'
434	    || value === 'brightBlue'
435	    || value === 'brightMagenta';
436	}
437	
438	const UNSAFE_CODEPOINT = /[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Variation_Selector}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Cn}]/u;
439	
440	function validateBarChar(value: unknown): value is string {
441	  if (typeof value !== 'string' || value.length === 0) return false;
442	
443	  const segmenter = new Intl.Segmenter(undefined, { granularity: 'grapheme' });
444	  if (Array.from(segmenter.segment(value)).length !== 1) return false;
445	
446	  for (const ch of value) {
447	    if (UNSAFE_CODEPOINT.test(ch)) return false;
448	  }
449	  return true;
450	}
451	
452	const HEX_COLOR_PATTERN = /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/;
453	
454	function validateColorValue(value: unknown): value is HudColorValue {
455	  if (validateColorName(value)) return true;
456	  if (typeof value === 'number' && Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0 && value <= 255) return true;
457	  if (typeof value === 'string' && HEX_COLOR_PATTERN.test(value)) return true;
458	  return false;
459	}
460	
461	function validateElementOrder(value: unknown): HudElement[] {
462	  if (!Array.isArray(value) || value.length === 0) {
463	    return [...DEFAULT_ELEMENT_ORDER];
464	  }
465	
466	  const seen = new Set<HudElement>();
467	  const elementOrder: HudElement[] = [];
468	
469	  for (const item of value) {
470	    if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_ELEMENTS.has(item as HudElement)) {
471	      continue;
472	    }
473	
474	    const element = item as HudElement;
475	    if (seen.has(element)) {
476	      continue;
477	    }
478	
479	    seen.add(element);
480	    elementOrder.push(element);
481	  }
482	
483	  return elementOrder.length > 0 ? elementOrder : [...DEFAULT_ELEMENT_ORDER];
484	}
485	
486	// Unlike `elementOrder`, `projectLineOrder` only reorders segments. A partial
487	// list is preserved as a requested prefix; each renderer appends all remaining
488	// visible parts in its own existing order.
489	function validateProjectLineOrder(value: unknown): FirstLineSegment[] {
490	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
491	    return [...DEFAULT_PROJECT_LINE_ORDER];
492	  }
493	
494	  const seen = new Set<FirstLineSegment>();
495	  const order: FirstLineSegment[] = [];
496	
497	  for (const item of value) {
498	    if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_FIRST_LINE_SEGMENTS.has(item as FirstLineSegment)) {
499	      continue;
500	    }
501	
502	    const segment = item as FirstLineSegment;
503	    if (seen.has(segment)) {
504	      continue;
505	    }
506	
507	    seen.add(segment);
508	    order.push(segment);
509	  }
510	
511	  return order;
512	}
513	
514	function validateRightAlign(value: unknown): HudElement[] {
515	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
516	    return [...DEFAULT_CONFIG.display.rightAlign];
517	  }
518	
519	  const seen = new Set<HudElement>();
520	  const elements: HudElement[] = [];
521	
522	  for (const item of value) {
523	    if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_ELEMENTS.has(item as HudElement)) {
524	      continue;
525	    }
526	
527	    const element = item as HudElement;
528	    if (seen.has(element)) {
529	      continue;
530	    }
531	
532	    seen.add(element);
533	    elements.push(element);
534	  }
535	
536	  return elements;
537	}
538	
539	function validateMergeGroups(value: unknown): HudElement[][] {
540	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
541	    return DEFAULT_MERGE_GROUPS.map(group => [...group]);
542	  }
543	
544	  if (value.length === 0) {
545	    return [];
546	  }
547	
548	  const usedElements = new Set<HudElement>();
549	  const mergeGroups: HudElement[][] = [];
550	
551	  for (const group of value) {
552	    if (!Array.isArray(group)) {
553	      continue;
554	    }
555	
556	    const seenInGroup = new Set<HudElement>();
557	    const normalizedGroup: HudElement[] = [];
558	    const pendingElements: HudElement[] = [];
559	
560	    for (const item of group) {
561	      if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_ELEMENTS.has(item as HudElement)) {
562	        continue;
563	      }
564	
565	      const element = item as HudElement;
566	      if (seenInGroup.has(element) || usedElements.has(element)) {
567	        continue;
568	      }
569	
570	      seenInGroup.add(element);
571	      normalizedGroup.push(element);
572	      pendingElements.push(element);
573	    }
574	
575	    if (normalizedGroup.length >= 2) {
576	      for (const element of pendingElements) {
577	        usedElements.add(element);
578	      }
579	      mergeGroups.push(normalizedGroup);
580	    }
581	  }
582	
583	  return mergeGroups.length > 0
584	    ? mergeGroups
585	    : DEFAULT_MERGE_GROUPS.map(group => [...group]);
586	}
587	
588	interface LegacyConfig {
589	  layout?: 'default' | 'separators' | Record<string, unknown>;
590	}
591	
592	function migrateConfig(userConfig: Partial<HudConfig> & LegacyConfig): Partial<HudConfig> {
593	  const migrated = { ...userConfig } as Partial<HudConfig> & LegacyConfig;
594	
595	  if ('layout' in userConfig && !('lineLayout' in userConfig)) {
596	    if (typeof userConfig.layout === 'string') {
597	      // Legacy string migration (v0.0.x → v0.1.x)
598	      if (userConfig.layout === 'separators') {
599	        migrated.lineLayout = 'compact';
600	        migrated.showSeparators = true;
601	      } else {
602	        migrated.lineLayout = 'compact';
603	        migrated.showSeparators = false;
604	      }
605	    } else if (typeof userConfig.layout === 'object' && userConfig.layout !== null) {
606	      // Object layout written by third-party tools — extract nested fields
607	      const obj = userConfig.layout as Record<string, unknown>;
608	      if (typeof obj.lineLayout === 'string') migrated.lineLayout = obj.lineLayout as any;
609	      if (typeof obj.showSeparators === 'boolean') migrated.showSeparators = obj.showSeparators;
610	      if (typeof obj.pathLevels === 'number' || obj.pathLevels === 'full') migrated.pathLevels = obj.pathLevels as any;
611	    }
612	    delete migrated.layout;
613	  }
614	
615	  return migrated;
616	}
617	
618	function validateThreshold(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
619	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) return fallback;
620	  return Math.max(0, Math.min(100, value));
621	}
622	
623	function validateContextThreshold(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
624	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) return fallback;
625	  return Math.max(0, Math.min(100, value));
626	}
627	
628	function validateCountThreshold(value: unknown): number {
629	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) {
630	    return 0;
631	  }
632	  return Math.max(0, Math.floor(value));
633	}
634	
635	function validateDurationSeconds(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
636	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0) {
637	    return fallback;
638	  }
639	  return Math.floor(value);
640	}
641	
642	function validateNonNegativeInteger(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
643	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(value) || value < 0) {
644	    return fallback;
645	  }
646	  return value;
647	}
648	
649	function validateAutoCompactWindow(value: unknown): number | null {
650	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) || !Number.isInteger(value) || value <= 0) {
651	    return null;
652	  }
653	  return value;
654	}
655	
656	function validateOptionalPath(value: unknown): string {
657	  return typeof value === 'string' ? value.trim() : '';
658	}
659	
660	function validateFreshnessMs(value: unknown): number {
661	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) {
662	    return DEFAULT_CONFIG.display.externalUsageFreshnessMs;
663	  }
664	  return Math.max(0, Math.floor(value));
665	}
666	
667	export function mergeConfig(userConfig: Partial<HudConfig>): HudConfig {
668	  const migrated = migrateConfig(userConfig);
669	  const language = validateLanguage(migrated.language)
670	    ? migrated.language
671	    : DEFAULT_CONFIG.language;
672	
673	  const lineLayout = validateLineLayout(migrated.lineLayout)
674	    ? migrated.lineLayout
675	    : DEFAULT_CONFIG.lineLayout;
676	
677	  const showSeparators = typeof migrated.showSeparators === 'boolean'
678	    ? migrated.showSeparators
679	    : DEFAULT_CONFIG.showSeparators;
680	
681	  const pathLevels = validatePathLevels(migrated.pathLevels)
682	    ? migrated.pathLevels
683	    : DEFAULT_CONFIG.pathLevels;
684	
685	  const rawMaxWidth = (migrated as Record<string, unknown>).maxWidth;
686	  const maxWidth = (typeof rawMaxWidth === 'number' && Number.isFinite(rawMaxWidth) && rawMaxWidth > 0)
687	    ? Math.min(Math.floor(rawMaxWidth), MAX_TERMINAL_WIDTH)
688	    : null;
689	
690	  const elementOrder = validateElementOrder(migrated.elementOrder);
691	  const projectLineOrder = validateProjectLineOrder(migrated.projectLineOrder);
692	  const forceMaxWidth = typeof (migrated as Record<string, unknown>).forceMaxWidth === 'boolean'
693	    ? (migrated as Record<string, unknown>).forceMaxWidth as boolean
694	    : DEFAULT_CONFIG.forceMaxWidth;
695	
696	  const gitStatus = {
697	    enabled: typeof migrated.gitStatus?.enabled === 'boolean'
698	      ? migrated.gitStatus.enabled
699	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.gitStatus.enabled,
700	    showDirty: typeof migrated.gitStatus?.showDirty === 'boolean'
701	      ? migrated.gitStatus.showDirty
702	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.gitStatus.showDirty,
703	    showAheadBehind: typeof migrated.gitStatus?.showAheadBehind === 'boolean'
704	      ? migrated.gitStatus.showAheadBehind
705	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.gitStatus.showAheadBehind,
706	    showFileStats: typeof migrated.gitStatus?.showFileStats === 'boolean'
707	      ? migrated.gitStatus.showFileStats
708	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.gitStatus.showFileStats,
709	    branchOverflow: validateGitBranchOverflow(migrated.gitStatus?.branchOverflow)
710	      ? migrated.gitStatus.branchOverflow
711	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.gitStatus.branchOverflow,
712	    pushWarningThreshold: validateCountThreshold(migrated.gitStatus?.pushWarningThreshold),
713	    pushCriticalThreshold: validateCountThreshold(migrated.gitStatus?.pushCriticalThreshold),
714	  };
715	
716	  const jjStatus = {
717	    enabled: typeof migrated.jjStatus?.enabled === 'boolean'
718	      ? migrated.jjStatus.enabled
719	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.jjStatus.enabled,
720	    showDirty: typeof migrated.jjStatus?.showDirty === 'boolean'
721	      ? migrated.jjStatus.showDirty
722	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.jjStatus.showDirty,
723	    showConflicts: typeof migrated.jjStatus?.showConflicts === 'boolean'
724	      ? migrated.jjStatus.showConflicts
725	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.jjStatus.showConflicts,
726	  };
727	
728	  const display = {
729	    showModel: typeof migrated.display?.showModel === 'boolean'
730	      ? migrated.display.showModel
731	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.display.showModel,
732	    showProject: typeof migrated.display?.showProject === 'boolean'
733	      ? migrated.display.showProject
734	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.display.showProject,
735	    showAddedDirs: typeof migrated.display?.showAddedDirs === 'boolean'
736	      ? migrated.display.showAddedDirs
737	      : DEFAULT_CONFIG.display.showAddedDirs,
738	    addedDirsLayout: (migrated.display?.addedDirsLayout === 'inline' || migrated.display?.addedDirsLayout === 'line')

325	    && counts.rulesCount >= 0
326	    && typeof counts.mcpCount === 'number'
327	    && Number.isFinite(counts.mcpCount)
328	    && counts.mcpCount >= 0
329	    && typeof counts.hooksCount === 'number'
330	    && Number.isFinite(counts.hooksCount)
331	    && counts.hooksCount >= 0
332	    && (counts.outputStyle === undefined || typeof counts.outputStyle === 'string')
333	  );
334	}
335	
336	function readConfigCache(cacheKey: Pick<ConfigCacheKey, 'cwd' | 'claudeConfigDir'>, homeDir: string): ConfigCacheFile | null {
337	  try {
338	    const cachePath = getConfigCachePath(cacheKey.cwd, cacheKey.claudeConfigDir, homeDir);
339	    const raw = fs.readFileSync(cachePath, 'utf8');
340	    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as ConfigCacheFile;
341	    if (parsed.key?.cwd !== cacheKey.cwd || parsed.key?.claudeConfigDir !== cacheKey.claudeConfigDir) {
342	      return null;
343	    }
344	    if (!isConfigCounts(parsed.data)) {
345	      return null;
346	    }
347	    return parsed;
348	  } catch (err) {
349	    debug('Failed to read config cache:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : err);
350	    return null;
351	  }
352	}
353	
354	function writeConfigCache(key: ConfigCacheKey, data: ConfigCounts, homeDir: string): void {
355	  try {
356	    const cachePath = getConfigCachePath(key.cwd, key.claudeConfigDir, homeDir);
357	    ensurePrivateDir(path.dirname(cachePath));
358	    const payload: ConfigCacheFile = { key, data };
359	    fs.writeFileSync(cachePath, JSON.stringify(payload), { encoding: 'utf8', mode: 0o600 });
360	    try {
361	      fs.chmodSync(cachePath, 0o600);
362	    } catch {
363	      // Best-effort: some filesystems do not support POSIX modes.
364	    }
365	  } catch (err) {
366	    debug('Failed to write config cache:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : err);
367	  }
368	}

370	function computeConfigCountsFresh(cwd?: string): ConfigCounts {
371	  let claudeMdCount = 0;
372	  let rulesCount = 0;
373	  let hooksCount = 0;
374	  let outputStyle: string | undefined;
375	
376	  const homeDir = os.homedir();
377	  const claudeDir = getClaudeConfigDir(homeDir);
378	
379	  // Collect all MCP servers across scopes, then subtract disabled ones
380	  const userMcpServers = new Set<string>();
381	  const projectMcpServers = new Set<string>();
382	
383	  // === USER SCOPE ===
384	
385	  // ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
386	  if (fs.existsSync(path.join(claudeDir, 'CLAUDE.md'))) {
387	    claudeMdCount++;
388	  }
389	
390	  // ~/.claude/rules/*.md
391	  rulesCount += countRulesInDir(path.join(claudeDir, 'rules'));
392	
393	  // ~/.claude/settings.json (MCPs and hooks)
394	  const userSettings = path.join(claudeDir, 'settings.json');
395	  for (const name of getMcpServerNames(userSettings)) {
396	    userMcpServers.add(name);
397	  }
398	  hooksCount += countHooksInFile(userSettings);
399	  outputStyle = readStringSetting(userSettings, 'outputStyle');
400	
401	  const userLocalSettings = path.join(claudeDir, 'settings.local.json');
402	  outputStyle = readStringSetting(userLocalSettings, 'outputStyle') ?? outputStyle;
403

405	  const userClaudeJson = getClaudeConfigJsonPath(homeDir);

407	    userMcpServers.add(name);
408	  }
409	
410	  // Get disabled user-scope MCPs from ~/.claude.json
411	  const disabledUserMcps = getDisabledMcpServers(userClaudeJson, 'disabledMcpServers');
412	  for (const name of disabledUserMcps) {
413	    userMcpServers.delete(name);
414	  }
415	
416	  // === PROJECT SCOPE ===
417	
418	  // Avoid double-counting when project .claude directory is the same location as user scope.
419	  const projectClaudeDir = cwd ? path.join(cwd, '.claude') : null;
420	  const projectClaudeOverlapsUserScope = projectClaudeDir
421	    ? pathsReferToSameLocation(projectClaudeDir, claudeDir)
422	    : false;
423	
424	  if (cwd) {
425	    // {cwd}/CLAUDE.md
426	    if (fs.existsSync(path.join(cwd, 'CLAUDE.md'))) {
427	      claudeMdCount++;
428	    }
429	
430	    // {cwd}/CLAUDE.local.md
431	    if (fs.existsSync(path.join(cwd, 'CLAUDE.local.md'))) {
432	      claudeMdCount++;
433	    }
434	
435	    // {cwd}/.claude/CLAUDE.md (alternative location, skip when it is user scope)
436	    if (!projectClaudeOverlapsUserScope && fs.existsSync(path.join(cwd, '.claude', 'CLAUDE.md'))) {
437	      claudeMdCount++;
438	    }
439	
440	    // {cwd}/.claude/CLAUDE.local.md
441	    if (fs.existsSync(path.join(cwd, '.claude', 'CLAUDE.local.md'))) {
442	      claudeMdCount++;
443	    }
444	
445	    // {cwd}/.claude/rules/*.md (recursive)
446	    // Skip when it overlaps with user-scope rules.
447	    if (!projectClaudeOverlapsUserScope) {
448	      rulesCount += countRulesInDir(path.join(cwd, '.claude', 'rules'));
449	    }
450	
451	    // {cwd}/.mcp.json (project MCP config) - tracked separately for disabled filtering
452	    const mcpJsonServers = getMcpServerNames(path.join(cwd, '.mcp.json'));
453	
454	    // {cwd}/.claude/settings.json (project settings)
455	    // Skip when it overlaps with user-scope settings.
456	    const projectSettings = path.join(cwd, '.claude', 'settings.json');
457	    if (!projectClaudeOverlapsUserScope) {
458	      for (const name of getMcpServerNames(projectSettings)) {
459	        projectMcpServers.add(name);
460	      }
461	      hooksCount += countHooksInFile(projectSettings);
462	      outputStyle = readStringSetting(projectSettings, 'outputStyle') ?? outputStyle;
463	    }
464	
465	    // {cwd}/.claude/settings.local.json (local project settings)
466	    const localSettings = path.join(cwd, '.claude', 'settings.local.json');
467	    for (const name of getMcpServerNames(localSettings)) {
468	      projectMcpServers.add(name);
469	    }
470	    hooksCount += countHooksInFile(localSettings);
471	    outputStyle = readStringSetting(localSettings, 'outputStyle') ?? outputStyle;
472	
473	    // Get disabled .mcp.json servers from settings.local.json
474	    const disabledMcpJsonServers = getDisabledMcpServers(localSettings, 'disabledMcpjsonServers');
475	    for (const name of disabledMcpJsonServers) {
476	      mcpJsonServers.delete(name);
477	    }
478	
479	    // Add remaining .mcp.json servers to project set
480	    for (const name of mcpJsonServers) {
481	      projectMcpServers.add(name);
482	    }
483	  }
484	
485	  // Total MCP count = user servers + project servers
486	  // Note: Deduplication only occurs within each scope, not across scopes.
487	  // A server with the same name in both user and project scope counts as 2 (separate configs).
488	  const mcpCount = userMcpServers.size + projectMcpServers.size;
489	
490	  return { claudeMdCount, rulesCount, mcpCount, hooksCount, outputStyle };
491	}

493	export async function countConfigs(cwd?: string): Promise<ConfigCounts> {
494	  const homeDir = os.homedir();
495	  const claudeDir = getClaudeConfigDir(homeDir);
496	  const claudeConfigJsonPath = getClaudeConfigJsonPath(homeDir);
497	  const normalizedCwd = cwd ? path.resolve(cwd) : null;
498	
499	  const staticSentinelPaths = buildSentinelPaths(claudeDir, claudeConfigJsonPath, normalizedCwd);
500	  const cached = readConfigCache({ cwd: normalizedCwd, claudeConfigDir: claudeDir }, homeDir);
501	  const cacheValidationPaths = cached
502	    ? Array.from(new Set([...staticSentinelPaths, ...Object.keys(cached.key.sentinels)]))
503	    : staticSentinelPaths;
504	  const currentSentinels = statSentinels(cacheValidationPaths);
505	
506	  if (cached && sentinelsMatch(cached.key.sentinels, currentSentinels)) {
507	    return cached.data;
508	  }
509	
510	  const result = computeConfigCountsFresh(cwd);
511	
512	  const ruleSentinelPaths = collectRuleDirectorySentinels(path.join(claudeDir, 'rules'));
513	  const projectClaudeDir = normalizedCwd ? path.join(normalizedCwd, '.claude') : null;
514	  const projectClaudeOverlapsUserScope = projectClaudeDir
515	    ? pathsReferToSameLocation(projectClaudeDir, claudeDir)
516	    : false;
517	  if (normalizedCwd && !projectClaudeOverlapsUserScope) {
518	    ruleSentinelPaths.push(...collectRuleDirectorySentinels(path.join(normalizedCwd, '.claude', 'rules')));
519	  }
520	
521	  const cacheSentinelPaths = Array.from(new Set([...staticSentinelPaths, ...ruleSentinelPaths]));
522	  const cacheKey: ConfigCacheKey = {
523	    cwd: normalizedCwd,
524	    claudeConfigDir: claudeDir,
525	    sentinels: statSentinels(cacheSentinelPaths),
526	  };
527	  writeConfigCache(cacheKey, result, homeDir);
528	  return result;
529	}

200	   ```

202	**Windows + PowerShell** (Platform: `win32`, Shell: `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd`, OSTYPE: other/empty):
203	
204	> **Before proceeding**: if `echo $OSTYPE` returned `msys` or `cygwin`, use the **Windows + Git Bash** instructions above. In that environment, bash can expand PowerShell variables before PowerShell runs.
205	
206	1. Get plugin path:
207	   ```powershell
208	   $claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
209	   (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache\*\claude-hud\*") -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match '^\d+(\.\d+)+$' } | Sort-Object { [version]$_.Name } -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).FullName
210	   ```
211	   The trailing `\*` on the cache glob is required. Without it, `Get-ChildItem` returns the `claude-hud` directory itself, whose name does not match the `^\d+(\.\d+)+$` version pattern, so the lookup resolves to `$null` and any subsequent `Join-Path` throws (see [#521](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/521)).
212	
213	   If empty or errors, the plugin is not installed. Ask the user to install via marketplace first.
214	
215	2. Get runtime absolute path (require node on Windows):
216	   ```powershell
217	   if (Get-Command node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { (Get-Command node).Source } else { Write-Error "Node.js not found" }
218	   ```
219	
220	   If node is not found, stop setup and explain that the current PowerShell session cannot find Node.js.
221	   - If `winget` is available, recommend:
222	     ```powershell
223	     winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS
224	     ```
225	   - Otherwise ask the user to install Node.js LTS, then restart PowerShell and re-run `/claude-hud:setup`.
226	   - On Windows, do not offer Bun for statusLine setup. Use Node.js only.
227	
228	3. Use `dist\index.js`.
229	
230	4. Write the Windows statusline launcher.
231	
232	   Windows PowerShell startup plus `Get-ChildItem | Sort-Object [version]` can exceed Claude Code's render cadence on every statusLine refresh. Write a small Node launcher once during setup, then invoke it through `cmd.exe` on each refresh. The launcher uses the setup-time validated `node.exe`, preserves update discovery by finding the latest installed `claude-hud` version, and prefers inherited `COLUMNS` before falling back to 120.
233	
234	   The launcher file at `$claudeDir/plugins/claude-hud/statusline.mjs` should contain:
235	
236	   ```js
237	   import fs from 'node:fs';
238	   import os from 'node:os';
239	   import path from 'node:path';
240	   import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
241	
242	   const envColumns = Number.parseInt(process.env.COLUMNS ?? '', 10);
243	   const width = Number.isFinite(envColumns) && envColumns > 0 ? envColumns : 120;
244	   process.env.COLUMNS = String(Math.max(1, width - 4));
245	
246	   const claudeDir = process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude');
247	   const cacheDir = path.join(claudeDir, 'plugins', 'cache');
248	
249	   function versionParts(value) {
250	     const match = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+].*)?$/.exec(value);
251	     return match ? match.slice(1, 4).map(Number) : null;
252	   }
253	
254	   function compareVersions(a, b) {
255	     for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {
256	       if (a[i] !== b[i]) return a[i] - b[i];
257	     }
258	     return 0;
259	   }
260	
261	   const candidates = [];
262	   try {
263	     for (const marketplace of fs.readdirSync(cacheDir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
264	       if (!marketplace.isDirectory()) continue;
265	       const pluginRoot = path.join(cacheDir, marketplace.name, 'claude-hud');
266	       let versions = [];
267	       try {
268	         versions = fs.readdirSync(pluginRoot, { withFileTypes: true });
269	       } catch {
270	         continue;
271	       }
272	       for (const version of versions) {
273	         if (!version.isDirectory()) continue;
274	         const parts = versionParts(version.name);
275	         if (!parts) continue;
276	         const dir = path.join(pluginRoot, version.name);
277	         if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'dist', 'index.js'))) {
278	           candidates.push({ dir, parts });
279	         }
280	       }
281	     }
282	   } catch {
283	     process.exit(0);
284	   }
285	
286	   candidates.sort((a, b) => compareVersions(a.parts, b.parts));
287	   const latest = candidates.at(-1);
288	   if (!latest) process.exit(0);
289	
290	   const hud = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(latest.dir, 'dist', 'index.js')).href);
291	   if (typeof hud.main === 'function') {
292	     await hud.main();
293	   }
294	   ```
295	
296	   Write it using `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` with `New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false` so the file is UTF-8 without a BOM:
297	
298	   ```powershell
299	   $wrapperDir = Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\claude-hud"
300	   New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $wrapperDir | Out-Null
301	   $wrapperPath = Join-Path $wrapperDir "statusline.mjs"
302	   $wrapperBody = @'
303	   import fs from 'node:fs';
304	   import os from 'node:os';
305	   import path from 'node:path';
306	   import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
307	
308	   const envColumns = Number.parseInt(process.env.COLUMNS ?? '', 10);
309	   const width = Number.isFinite(envColumns) && envColumns > 0 ? envColumns : 120;
310	   process.env.COLUMNS = String(Math.max(1, width - 4));
311	
312	   const claudeDir = process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude');
313	   const cacheDir = path.join(claudeDir, 'plugins', 'cache');
314	
315	   function versionParts(value) {
316	     const match = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+].*)?$/.exec(value);
317	     return match ? match.slice(1, 4).map(Number) : null;
318	   }
319	
320	   function compareVersions(a, b) {
321	     for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {
322	       if (a[i] !== b[i]) return a[i] - b[i];
323	     }
324	     return 0;
325	   }
326	
327	   const candidates = [];
328	   try {
329	     for (const marketplace of fs.readdirSync(cacheDir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
330	       if (!marketplace.isDirectory()) continue;
331	       const pluginRoot = path.join(cacheDir, marketplace.name, 'claude-hud');
332	       let versions = [];
333	       try {
334	         versions = fs.readdirSync(pluginRoot, { withFileTypes: true });
335	       } catch {
336	         continue;
337	       }
338	       for (const version of versions) {
339	         if (!version.isDirectory()) continue;
340	         const parts = versionParts(version.name);
341	         if (!parts) continue;
342	         const dir = path.join(pluginRoot, version.name);
343	         if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'dist', 'index.js'))) {
344	           candidates.push({ dir, parts });
345	         }
346	       }
347	     }
348	   } catch {
349	     process.exit(0);
350	   }
351	
352	   candidates.sort((a, b) => compareVersions(a.parts, b.parts));
353	   const latest = candidates.at(-1);
354	   if (!latest) process.exit(0);
355	
356	   const hud = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(latest.dir, 'dist', 'index.js')).href);
357	   if (typeof hud.main === 'function') {
358	     await hud.main();
359	   }
360	   '@
361	   [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($wrapperPath, $wrapperBody, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
362	   ```
363	
364	   `$runtimePath` is the value detected in step 2 (the absolute path returned by `(Get-Command node).Source`, typically `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`). `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` on Windows PowerShell 5.1 both emit a UTF-8 BOM. `WriteAllText` + `UTF8Encoding $false` writes without a BOM in both PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+.
365	
366	5. Generate command:
367	
368	   ```
369	   {CMD_PATH} /d /s /c ""{RUNTIME_PATH}" "{WRAPPER_PATH}""
370	   ```
371	
372	   `{CMD_PATH}` is the absolute `cmd.exe` path, preferably `$env:SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe`. `{WRAPPER_PATH}` is the value of `$wrapperPath` from step 4 (typically `C:\Users\<user>\.claude\plugins\claude-hud\statusline.mjs`). If you build the string in PowerShell, use:
373	
374	   ```powershell
375	   $cmdPath = Join-Path $env:SystemRoot "System32\cmd.exe"
376	   if (-not (Test-Path $cmdPath)) { $cmdPath = "cmd.exe" }
377	   $generatedCommand = $cmdPath + ' /d /s /c ""' + $runtimePath + '" "' + $wrapperPath + '""'
378	   ```
379	
380	**WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux)**: If running in WSL, use the macOS/Linux instructions. Ensure the plugin is installed in the Linux environment (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/plugins/...`), not the Windows side.
381	
382	## Step 2: Test Command
383	
384	Run the generated command. It should produce output (the HUD lines) within a few seconds.
385	
386	- If it errors, do not proceed to Step 3.
387	- If it hangs for more than a few seconds, cancel and debug.
388	- This test catches issues like broken runtime binaries, missing plugins, or path problems.
389	
390	## Step 2.5: Detect Existing Statusline and Create Backup
391	
392	Before writing to `settings.json`, check whether a `statusLine` key already exists and protect the user's current configuration. This covers the existing-statusLine overwrite issue tracked in [#547](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/547).
393	
394	### 2.5.1: Read the existing statusLine
395	
396	**macOS/Linux**:
397	```bash
398	SETTINGS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
399	EXISTING_COMMAND=""
400	EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW=""
401	
402	if [ -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
403	  EXISTING_COMMAND=$("{RUNTIME_PATH}" -e '
404	const fs = require("fs");
405	const settingsPath = process.argv[1];
406	
407	try {
408	  const text = fs.readFileSync(settingsPath, "utf8");
409	  if (text.trim() === "") process.exit(0);
410	
411	  const json = JSON.parse(text);
412	  const command = json && json.statusLine && typeof json.statusLine.command === "string"
413	    ? json.statusLine.command
414	    : "";
415	  process.stdout.write(command);
416	} catch (error) {
417	  console.error("Unable to read statusLine.command from settings.json: " + error.message);
418	  process.exit(1);
419	}
420	' "$SETTINGS") || exit 1
421	
422	  EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING_COMMAND" | "{RUNTIME_PATH}" -e '
423	let value = "";
424	process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8");
425	process.stdin.on("data", chunk => { value += chunk; });
426	process.stdin.on("end", () => {
427	  const redacted = value
428	    .replace(/\b(Bearer)\s+["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "$1 [REDACTED]")
429	    .replace(/\b(Authorization\s*:\s*)["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "$1[REDACTED]")
430	    .replace(/\b(token|api[_-]?key|secret|password|pass|auth)(=|:)\s*["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "$1$2[REDACTED]")
431	    .replace(/\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b/g, "sk-[REDACTED]")
432	    .replace(/\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,}\b/g, "[GITHUB_TOKEN_REDACTED]")
433	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
434	    .trim();
435	
436	  process.stdout.write(redacted.length > 160 ? redacted.slice(0, 157) + "..." : redacted);
437	});
438	')
439	fi
440	```
441	
442	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
443	```powershell
444	$settingsPath = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { Join-Path $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR "settings.json" } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude\settings.json" }
445	$existingCommand = ""
446	$existingCommandPreview = ""
447	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
448	  try {
449	    $json = Get-Content $settingsPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
450	    if ($json.statusLine -and $json.statusLine.command) {
451	      $existingCommand = $json.statusLine.command
452	    }
453	  } catch {
454	    Write-Error "Unable to read statusLine.command from settings.json: $($_.Exception.Message)"
455	    throw
456	  }
457	
458	  if ($existingCommand -ne "") {
459	    $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommand `
460	      -replace "(?i)\b(Bearer)\s+[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", '$1 [REDACTED]' `
461	      -replace "(?i)\b(Authorization\s*:\s*)[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", '$1[REDACTED]' `
462	      -replace "(?i)\b(token|api[_-]?key|secret|password|pass|auth)(=|:)\s*[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", '$1$2[REDACTED]' `
463	      -replace "\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b", 'sk-[REDACTED]' `
464	      -replace "\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,}\b", '[GITHUB_TOKEN_REDACTED]' `
465	      -replace "\s+", " "
466	    $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommandPreview.Trim()
467	    if ($existingCommandPreview.Length -gt 160) {
468	      $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommandPreview.Substring(0, 157) + "..."
469	    }
470	  }
471	}
472	```
473	
474	### 2.5.2: Classify the existing statusline
475	
476	If `EXISTING_COMMAND` / `$existingCommand` is non-empty, classify it:
477	
478	| Pattern in command | Classification | Source label |
479	|---|---|---|
480	| Contains `claude-hud` | **Reinstall** (own config) | `claude-hud` |
481	| Contains `claude-pace` | **Known project** | `claude-pace` |
482	| Contains `cc-statusline` or `ccstatusline` | **Known project** | `cc-statusline` |
483	| Contains `statusline.sh` or `statusline.js` or `statusline.py` | **Likely another statusline** | `statusline script` |
484	| Any other non-empty value | **Custom script** | `custom` |
485	| Empty / missing key | **Clean install** | (none) |
486	
487	### 2.5.3: Create a timestamped backup
488	
489	**Always** create a backup of `settings.json` before modifying it, regardless of whether a statusline exists. This protects against corruption (see [#315]) and gives users a recovery path.
490	
491	**macOS/Linux**:
492	```bash
493	SETTINGS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
494	BACKUP_TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
495	BACKUP_PATH=""
496	if [ -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
497	  BACKUP_PATH="${SETTINGS}.bak.${BACKUP_TIMESTAMP}"
498	  if cp "$SETTINGS" "$BACKUP_PATH"; then
499	    echo "Backup created: $BACKUP_PATH"
500	  else
501	    echo "Failed to create backup at: $BACKUP_PATH" >&2
502	    exit 1
503	  fi
504	fi
505	```
506	
507	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
508	```powershell
509	$backupPath = ""
510	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
511	  $timestamp = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'
512	  $backupPath = "${settingsPath}.bak.${timestamp}"
513	  Copy-Item $settingsPath $backupPath -ErrorAction Stop
514	  Write-Host "Backup created: $backupPath"
515	}
516	```
517	
518	### 2.5.4: Prompt the user if a statusline exists
519	
520	**If the statusline is empty (clean install)**: Skip this step. Proceed directly to Step 3.
521	
522	**If the statusline is claude-hud (reinstall)**: Skip this step. The new command replaces the old one — this is an idempotent update. Proceed to Step 3.
523	
524	**If the statusline belongs to a known project or is a custom script**: Use AskUserQuestion to ask the user what to do.
525	
526	Use AskUserQuestion:
527	- header: "Existing statusline detected"
528	- question: "Found an existing statusLine in settings.json:\n\n  command preview: {REDACTED_COMMAND_PREVIEW}\n  source: {SOURCE_LABEL}\n\nWhat would you like to do?"
529	- options:
530	  - "Replace it with claude-hud (your current setup will be backed up)"
531	  - "Keep my current statusline and exit setup (settings stay unchanged)"
532	  - "Cancel setup without changing settings"
533	
534	Set `{REDACTED_COMMAND_PREVIEW}` to `EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW` on macOS/Linux or `$existingCommandPreview` on Windows. Use only the redacted/truncated preview in the prompt and normal output. Do not print the full previous command because it may contain tokens or secrets.
535	
536	**If the user chooses "Keep" or "Cancel"**: Stop setup. The backup from 2.5.3 is still available if one was created. Tell the user:
537	
538	> No changes were made to your settings. Your existing statusline is preserved. Setup created no settings mutation apart from the backup file at `{BACKUP_PATH or $backupPath}` if that value is set.
539	
540	**If the user chooses "Replace"**: Proceed to Step 3. The backup from 2.5.3 ensures the previous configuration can be restored.
541	
542	### 2.5.5: Save the previous command for potential restoration
543	
544	Store the previous `statusLine.command` value in a file alongside the settings backup. This makes it easy to restore if the user later wants to switch back.
545	
546	**macOS/Linux**:
547	```bash
548	CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
549	if [ -n "$EXISTING_COMMAND" ]; then
550	  PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR="$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/claude-hud"
551	  PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH="$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR/previous-statusline.txt"
552	  mkdir -p "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR"
553	  chmod 700 "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
554	  if (
555	    umask 077
556	    printf '%s' "$EXISTING_COMMAND" > "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH"
557	  ); then
558	    chmod 600 "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true
559	    echo "Previous statusline command saved to: $PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH"
560	  else
561	    echo "Failed to save previous statusline command to: $PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH" >&2
562	    exit 1
563	  fi
564	fi
565	```
566	
567	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
568	```powershell
569	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
570	$pluginDir = Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\claude-hud"
571	if (-not (Test-Path $pluginDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $pluginDir | Out-Null }
572	if ($existingCommand -ne "") {
573	  $previousCommandPath = Join-Path $pluginDir "previous-statusline.txt"
574	  [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($previousCommandPath, $existingCommand, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
575	  try {
576	    $acl = Get-Acl $previousCommandPath
577	    $acl.SetAccessRuleProtection($true, $false)
578	    $rule = New-Object System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemAccessRule(
579	      [System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().Name,
580	      "FullControl",
581	      "Allow"
582	    )
583	    $acl.SetAccessRule($rule)
584	    Set-Acl -Path $previousCommandPath -AclObject $acl
585	  } catch {
586	    Write-Warning "Saved previous statusline command, but could not tighten file ACLs: $($_.Exception.Message)"
587	  }
588	}
589	```
590	
591	---
592	
593	## Step 3: Apply Configuration
594	
595	Read the settings file and merge in the statusLine config, preserving all existing settings:
596	- **Platform `darwin` or `linux`, or Platform `win32` + Shell `bash`**: `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json`
597	- **Platform `win32` + Shell `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd`**: `settings.json` inside `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, otherwise `Join-Path $HOME ".claude"`
598	
599	If the file doesn't exist, create it. If it contains invalid JSON, report the error and do not overwrite.
600	If a write fails with `File has been unexpectedly modified`, re-read the file and retry the merge once.
601	
602	**A timestamped backup was already created in Step 2.5.3.** If Step 2.5.4 prompted the user and they chose "Keep" or "Cancel", do not reach this step — setup has already exited.
603	
604	```json
605	{
606	  "statusLine": {
607	    "type": "command",
608	    "command": "{GENERATED_COMMAND}"
609	  }
610	}
611	```
612	
613	**JSON safety**: Write `settings.json` with a real JSON serializer or editor API, not manual string concatenation.
614	If you must inspect the saved JSON manually, the embedded bash command must preserve escaped backslashes inside the awk fragment.
615	For example, the saved JSON should contain `\\$(NF-1)` and `\\$0`, not `\$(NF-1)` and `\$0`.
616	
617	**Windows PowerShell 5.1 BOM**: on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the default shell on Windows 10/11), `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` emit a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`). RFC 8259 §8.1 forbids BOM in JSON. PowerShell 7+ added `-Encoding utf8NoBOM`, but PS 5.1 did not. Use `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` with `New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false` to write UTF-8 without a BOM from both PS versions:
618	
619	```powershell
620	[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $json, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
621	```
622	
623	Verify the first bytes are `7B 0D 0A` (`{` + CRLF) or `7B 0A` (`{` + LF), not `EF BB BF`:
624	
625	```powershell
626	[System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($path)[0..2]
627	```
628	
629	
630	After successfully writing the config, tell the user:
631	
632	> ✅ Config written. Claude Code reloads settings automatically — the HUD should appear below your input field after your next message in this session (no restart needed).
633	> If it doesn't show up after your next interaction, restart Claude Code (quit and run `claude` again) — older Claude Code versions require a restart to pick up statusLine changes.
634	
635	Then continue directly to Step 4 in the same session.
636	
637	**Windows note**: Keep the settings-reload guidance separate from runtime installation guidance.
638	- If the user just installed Node.js, they should restart their shell first so `node` is available in `PATH` — that shell restart is unrelated to Claude Code picking up the statusLine config.
639	- The statusLine config itself reloads automatically on Windows too; a full Claude Code restart is only the fallback if the HUD doesn't appear after the next interaction.
640	
641	**Note**: The generated command dynamically finds and runs the latest installed plugin version. Updates are automatic - no need to re-run setup after plugin updates. If the HUD suddenly stops working, re-run `/claude-hud:setup` to verify the plugin is still installed.
642	
643	**Restoring a previous statusline**: If the user previously had a different statusline and wants to restore it, use the backup path printed in Step 2.5.3. The previous command is stored in `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/previous-statusline.txt`. To restore:
644	1. Find the most recent backup: `ls -t ~/.claude/settings.json.bak.* | head -1`
645	2. Copy it back: `cp ~/.claude/settings.json.bak.{timestamp} ~/.claude/settings.json`
646	3. The restored config applies automatically on the next interaction (restart Claude Code only if it doesn't).
647	
648	## Step 4: Optional Features
649	
650	After the statusLine is applied, ask the user if they'd like to enable additional HUD features beyond the default 2-line display.
651	
652	Use AskUserQuestion:
653	- header: "Extras"
654	- question: "Enable any optional HUD features? (all hidden by default)"
655	- multiSelect: true
656	- options:
657	  - "Tools activity" — Shows running/completed tools (◐ Edit: file.ts | ✓ Read ×3)
658	  - "Agents & Todos" — Shows subagent status and todo progress
659	  - "Session info" — Shows session duration and config counts (CLAUDE.md, rules, MCPs)
660	  - "Session name" — Shows session slug or custom title from /rename
661	  - "Custom line" — Display a custom phrase in the HUD
662	
663	**If user selects any options**, write `plugins/claude-hud/config.json` inside the Claude config directory (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}` on bash, `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `Join-Path $HOME ".claude"` on PowerShell). Create directories if needed:
664	
665	| Selection | Config keys |
666	|-----------|------------|
667	| Tools activity | `display.showTools: true` |
668	| Agents & Todos | `display.showAgents: true, display.showTodos: true` |
669	| Session info | `display.showDuration: true, display.showConfigCounts: true` |
670	| Session name | `display.showSessionName: true` |
671	| Custom line | `display.customLine: "<user's text>"` — ask user for the text (max 80 chars) |
672	
673	Merge with existing config if the file already exists. Only write keys the user selected — don't write `false` for unselected items (defaults handle that).
674	
675	**If user selects nothing** (or picks "Other" and says skip/none), do not create a config file. The defaults are fine.
676	
677	### Step 4.5: Auto-Refresh (Optional)
678	
679	Claude Code only re-runs the statusline after an interaction (a new assistant message, `/compact` finishing, a permission-mode change, or a vim-mode toggle). Time-based HUD data — session duration, usage reset countdowns, the prompt-cache countdown — therefore goes stale between messages. Claude Code supports an optional `refreshInterval` key (seconds, minimum 1) on the `statusLine` settings object that re-runs the command every N seconds.
680	
681	Of those, only the usage reset countdown is shown by default — session duration and the prompt-cache countdown tick only if the user enabled them (e.g. "Session info" in Step 4, or via config). Mention this if the user seems unsure whether the timer is worth it.
682	
683	Ask with AskUserQuestion:
684	- header: "Auto-refresh"
685	- question: "Re-run the HUD on a timer so time-based info (session duration, usage countdowns) stays current between messages?"
686	- options:
687	  - "Every 5 seconds (Recommended)" — Keeps countdowns fresh with negligible overhead
688	  - "Every 1 second" — Smoothest ticking; re-runs the HUD command far more often
689	  - "No timer" — HUD updates only after interactions (Claude Code's default)
690	
691	**If the user picks an interval**, merge `refreshInterval: <N>` into the **existing** `statusLine` object in `settings.json` — preserve `type`, `command`, and any other keys. Follow the same rules as Step 3: real JSON serializer, no BOM on Windows, retry once on a concurrent-modification error. Do not re-create the backup; the Step 2.5.3 backup already covers this session.
692	
693	**If the user picks "Other" and gives a numeric interval** (e.g. "10" or "10 seconds"), use that value, clamped to a minimum of 1. Treat a non-numeric "Other" answer that declines (skip/none/no) like "No timer".
694	
695	**If the user picks "No timer"**, do not write the key. If a `refreshInterval` key already exists in `statusLine` from a previous run and the user explicitly chose "No timer", remove it.
696	
697	`refreshInterval` lives in `settings.json`, which Claude Code reloads automatically — ticking should start after the user's next interaction. If countdowns don't tick in the current session, tell the user it will take effect after a Claude Code restart; do not treat a non-ticking timer as a setup failure in Step 5.
698	
699	Each refresh re-runs the full HUD command (runtime startup, transcript parse, git status), so 5 seconds is the recommended default; only suggest 1 second when the user wants visibly smooth countdowns.
700	
701	---
702	
703	## Step 5: Verify & Finish
704	
705	Settings reload automatically, so the HUD can appear in the same session where setup was run — it renders after the user's next interaction (their answer to the question below counts as one). No restart is needed on current Claude Code versions.
706	
707	Use AskUserQuestion:
708	- Question: "Setup complete! The HUD should appear below your input field. Is it working?"
709	- Options: "Yes, it's working" / "No, something's wrong"
710	
711	**If yes**: Ask the user if they'd like to ⭐ star the claude-hud repository on GitHub to support the project. If they agree and `gh` CLI is available, first check whether their `gh` version supports `gh repo star`. If it does, run `gh repo star jarrodwatts/claude-hud`. Otherwise fall back to `gh api -X PUT /user/starred/jarrodwatts/claude-hud`. Only run the star command if they explicitly say yes.
712	
713	**If no**: Debug systematically:
714	
715	1. **Trigger an interaction, then restart if needed**:
716	    - Settings reload automatically, but the HUD only renders after the next interaction (a new message, `/compact` finishing, a permission-mode change) — sending any message should make it appear
717	    - If it still doesn't appear, restart Claude Code (quit and run `claude` again) — older Claude Code versions require a restart to pick up statusLine changes — then re-run `/claude-hud:setup` to verify
718	    - If you've already restarted, continue below
719	
720	2. **Verify config was applied**:
721	   - Read settings file (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json` on bash, or `settings.json` inside `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, otherwise `Join-Path $HOME ".claude"` on PowerShell)
722	   - Check statusLine.command exists and looks correct
723	   - If command contains a hardcoded version path (not using the dynamic version-lookup command), it may be a stale config from a previous setup
724	
725	3. **Test the command manually** and capture error output:
726	   ```bash
727	   {GENERATED_COMMAND} 2>&1
728	   ```
729	
730	4. **Common issues to check**:
731	
732	   **"command not found" or empty output**:
733	   - Runtime path might be wrong: `ls -la {RUNTIME_PATH}`
734	   - On macOS with mise/nvm/asdf: the absolute path may have changed after a runtime update
735	   - Symlinks may be stale: `command -v node` often returns a symlink that can break after version updates
736	   - Solution: re-detect the runtime path (`command -v node` on Windows, `command -v bun` or `command -v node` on macOS/Linux), and verify with `realpath {RUNTIME_PATH}` (or `readlink -f {RUNTIME_PATH}`) to get the true absolute path
737	
738	   **"No such file or directory" for plugin**:
739	   - Plugin might not be installed: `ls "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/`
740	   - Solution: reinstall plugin via marketplace
741	
742	   **Windows shell mismatch (for example, "bash not recognized")**:
743	   - Command format does not match `Platform:` + `Shell:`
744	   - Solution: re-run Step 1 branch logic and use the matching variant
745	
746	   **Windows: HUD shows only "initializing..." with no error (PowerShell shell, MSYS/Cygwin command environment)**:
747	   - Root cause: `Shell: powershell` with `$OSTYPE=msys` or `$OSTYPE=cygwin`, causing bash to process the command before PowerShell
748	   - Check: run `echo $OSTYPE` in the Bash tool — if it returns `msys` or `cygwin`, this is the issue
749	   - Solution: re-run setup; when OSTYPE is `msys`/`cygwin`, follow the Windows + Git Bash path in Step 1
750	
751	   **Windows + PowerShell: HUD silent or "initializing..." with no error in any log (OSTYPE is not msys/cygwin)**:
752	   - Symptoms: HUD stays at "initializing..." or shows nothing. Running the generated command interactively in a PowerShell prompt produces the expected HUD output, but the version invoked through Claude Code does not.
753	   - Root cause: older setup commands used a PowerShell wrapper on every refresh. That path could fail when `[Console]::WindowWidth` threw `System.IO.IOException: The handle is invalid.`, when the cache glob resolved the `claude-hud` directory instead of a version directory, or when PowerShell startup exceeded the render cadence.
754	   - Check: pipe stdin through `cmd.exe` to mirror Claude Code's invocation:
755	     ```powershell
756	     '{}' | & cmd.exe /c '{GENERATED_COMMAND}'
757	     ```
758	     If you see either error, the existing setup predates the Node launcher format. Re-run `/claude-hud:setup` to regenerate `statusline.mjs` and a `cmd.exe`-launched command. See [#521](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/521).
759	
760	   **Windows: PowerShell execution policy error**:
761	   - Run: `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned`
762	
763	   **Permission denied**:
764	   - Runtime not executable: `chmod +x {RUNTIME_PATH}`
765	
766	   **WSL confusion**:
767	   - If using WSL, ensure plugin is installed in Linux environment, not Windows
768	   - Check: `ls "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/`
769	
770	5. **If still stuck**: Show the user the exact command that was generated and the error, so they can report it or debug further
771

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **chezmoi's `scripts/redact_secrets.py`** — remains the upstream
  source of truth. The skill bundles a copy so non-chezmoi users get
  protection; sync procedure in
  [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`).
2. Writes `scripts/redact_secrets.py` (bundled copy; use
   `--from-chezmoi` to symlink the chezmoi source so fixes propagate).
3. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
4. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
5. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
6. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` + the redactor
  into the current repo, then run `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — bundled copy of chezmoi's
  `scripts/redact_secrets.py`. Chezmoi version is upstream; sync doc
  in `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.

- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each

```text
125	
126	## Native `copilot-proxy`, not a bash shim
127	
128	The `copilot-proxy` tool series is reimplemented as a real PowerShell module
129	(`Invoke-RestMethod`, `Start-Process`, `ConvertFrom-Json`) rather than shelling out
130	to the original bash. Only the Bun throttle shim (pure JS) is reused verbatim. See
131	[copilot-proxy](copilot-proxy.md).
132	
133	## `run_onchange` pwsh mergers for JSON config, not `modify_` scripts
134	
135	Some JSON config surfaces are **owned by the tool at runtime** — Claude Code
136	rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` (plugins it installs, permissions you grant),
137	VSCode/Cursor rewrite their `settings.json`. Deploying a static managed copy
138	would clobber that live state, so these are **merged**, not overwritten. The
139	macOS/Linux repo merges with a chezmoi **`modify_` script** (a `sh` + `jq`
140	filter: read the live file on stdin, emit the merged result on stdout). On
141	Windows that doesn't hold up:
142	
143	- **Interpreter routing is by the *target's* extension.** chezmoi chooses a
144	  `modify_`/`create_` script's interpreter from the managed file's extension via
145	  `[interpreters.<ext>]`. `modify_settings.json` targets `settings.json` →
146	  `.json`, which maps to no interpreter. On Unix chezmoi falls back to the
147	  script's shebang (`#!/bin/sh`) + exec bit; Windows honors neither, so it can't
148	  run the script reliably — and you can't hand it a `.ps1` extension, because
149	  that's fixed to the target name. Only `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh` is wired up,
150	  and it only helps when the *managed file itself* is a `.ps1`.
151	- **Wrong toolchain.** The parent filter is `sh` + `jq` — not guaranteed on a
152	  pwsh-first box, and rewriting it in pwsh still hits the routing wall above.
153	
154	So each merge is a **`run_onchange_after_*.ps1.tmpl`** in `.chezmoiscripts/`
155	instead: a real `.ps1` that routes cleanly through `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh`,
156	runs natively with no external deps, and recursively deep-merges a
157	chezmoi-ignored overlay (`editors/*.json`, `claude/settings-overlay.json`,
158	embedded via `{{ include }}`) into the live file — preserving every key the tool
159	wrote. This is invariant #5 in `AGENTS.md`.
160	
161	**Tradeoff:** a `modify_` filter re-asserts on *every* apply; `run_onchange` only
162	re-fires when its rendered content (the overlay) changes. If the tool later
163	overwrites a managed key, it isn't restored until the overlay changes or you
164	reset state (`chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=entryState`). The parent needs
165	every-apply enforcement because CodeIsland / workmux keep rewriting
166	`~/.claude/settings.json`; Windows has no such contenders, so the lighter trigger
167	is fine.
168	
169	## XDG paths, not `%APPDATA%`
```

The design recommendation is converging on one ignored source overlay and one live merge path: keep `claude/settings-overlay.json` scoped to Claude Code, add a sibling HUD overlay scoped only to Full-owned leaves, and extend the existing run-onchange script with a generic fail-closed JSON-file merge helper. This avoids a directly managed target, avoids duplicating merge logic, and lets malformed `settings.json` and malformed HUD config fail independently rather than blocking each other.
