## Context Editing

Context editing clears stale tool results and thinking blocks from the transcript as a long-running agent accumulates turns. Unlike compaction (which summarizes), context editing prunes — the cleared content is removed, not replaced. Use it when old tool outputs are no longer relevant and you want to keep the transcript lean without losing the conversation structure.

**Beta.** Use `client.beta.messages.*` with beta `context-management-2025-06-27`. Configure via `context_management.edits` with a strategy type of `clear_tool_uses_20250919` (clear old tool results; optional `clear_tool_inputs: true` also clears the tool_use params) or `clear_thinking_20251015` (clear thinking blocks). These are **not** the compaction types — `compact_20260112` with beta `compact-2026-01-12` is the separate compaction feature.

For full documentation, use WebFetch:

- URL: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing`

---

## Server-Side Tools: Advisor (Beta)

The advisor tool pairs a faster, lower-cost **executor** model (the top-level `model` on the request) with a higher-intelligence **advisor** model (the `model` field inside the tool definition) that provides strategic guidance mid-generation. The executor does most of the token generation; the advisor is consulted for planning. Availability: see `shared/platform-availability.md`.

### Tool Definition

```json
{
  "type": "advisor_20260301",
  "name": "advisor",
  "model": "claude-opus-4-8"
}
```

Optional fields on the tool definition:

- `max_uses` — cap on advisor consultations per request. Exceeding it makes the `advisor_tool_result` block's `content` the error object `{"type": "advisor_tool_result_error", "error_code": "max_uses_exceeded"}` — the third member of the content union in the payload-shape table below.
- `max_tokens` — bounds the advisor's total output (thinking + text) per call. At the cap the result block carries `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` and a truncation note is appended to the advice the executor sees; the server also emits a remaining-tokens budget block in the advisor's prompt so it self-shapes toward the cap.
- `caching` — cache-control for the advisor's own prompt, same shape as a cache breakpoint: `"caching": {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "5m"}` (`ttl` is `"5m"` or `"1h"`, default `"5m"`). Each call writes a cache entry at that TTL so later calls in the conversation read the stable prefix. Omitted = advisor prompt not cached.

**The advisor model must be at least as capable as the executor.** An invalid pairing returns `400 invalid_request_error`. Valid pairs:

| Executor (request `model`) | Valid advisor (tool `model`) |
|---|---|
| `claude-haiku-4-5` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` / `claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-opus-4-6` / `claude-opus-4-7` | `claude-opus-5`, `claude-fable-5`, `claude-mythos-5`, `claude-opus-4-8`, or `claude-opus-4-7` |
| `claude-opus-4-8` | `claude-opus-5`, `claude-fable-5`, `claude-mythos-5`, or `claude-opus-4-8` |
| `claude-opus-5` | `claude-opus-5`, `claude-fable-5`, or `claude-mythos-5` |
| `claude-fable-5` | `claude-fable-5` or `claude-opus-5` |
| `claude-mythos-5` | `claude-mythos-5` or `claude-opus-5` |

> ⚠️ **The advisor's payload shape differs by advisor model.** The response block is always `advisor_tool_result`; what varies is its **`content`**, a discriminated union:
>
> | `content` type | Fields | When |
> |---|---|---|
> | `advisor_result` | `text`, `stop_reason` | Advisor returns plaintext (e.g. Opus 4.8) |
> | `advisor_redacted_result` | `encrypted_content`, `stop_reason` | Advisor returns encrypted output — Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5 |
> | `advisor_tool_result_error` | `error_code` | Consultation failed — `max_uses_exceeded`, `prompt_too_long`, `too_many_requests`, `overloaded`, `unavailable`, `execution_time_exceeded`, or `model_not_found` |
>
> So switch on `advisor_tool_result.content` type, not on the block type. Code that reads `.text` unconditionally gets nothing back from an Claude Opus 5 advisor, because the payload is under `encrypted_content` instead — and you cannot read it, only replay it.

Call via `client.beta.messages.create(...)` with `betas=["advisor-tool-2026-03-01"]` (or the `anthropic-beta: advisor-tool-2026-03-01` header). In multi-turn conversations, append the full `response.content` — including any `advisor_tool_result` blocks — back to `messages` on the next turn. If you remove the advisor tool from `tools` on a later turn while the history still contains `advisor_tool_result` blocks, the API returns a 400.

> **Advisor on Managed Agents:** CMA sessions support an advisor too, configured as a `{"type": "advisor", "model"}` entry in the agent's multiagent roster rather than as a tool definition — no `max_uses`/`max_tokens`/`caching` options, and advice is delivered as thread events on the session's event stream rather than `advisor_tool_result` blocks. See `shared/managed-agents-multiagent.md` → Advisor.

---

## Client-Side Tools: Memory

The memory tool enables Claude to store and retrieve information across conversations through a memory file directory. Claude can create, read, update, and delete files that persist between sessions.

### Key Facts

- Client-side tool — you control storage via your implementation
- Supports commands: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `delete`, `rename`
- Operates on files in a `/memories` directory
- The Python, TypeScript, and Java SDKs provide helper classes/functions for implementing the memory backend

> **Security:** Never store API keys, passwords, tokens, or other secrets in memory files. Be cautious with personally identifiable information (PII) — check data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) before persisting user data. The reference implementations have no built-in access control; in multi-user systems, implement per-user memory directories and authentication in your tool handlers.

For full implementation examples, use WebFetch:

- Docs: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool.md`

---

## Client-Side Tools: Bash and Text Editor

The bash and text editor tools are **Anthropic-defined, schema-less** tools. Declare them by `type` and `name` only — the input schema is built into the model and cannot be modified. **Do not pass an `input_schema`**, and do not define a custom tool that happens to be named `"bash"` — that creates a user-defined tool without the built-in behavior.

Both are **client-executed**: Claude returns a `tool_use` block, your code performs the action locally, and you send back a `tool_result`. The API is stateless; your application maintains the shell session or filesystem between turns.

### Bash tool declaration

```json
{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}
```

| Language | Declaration |
|---|---|
| Python / TypeScript / Ruby / cURL | plain object `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` |
| Go | `anthropic.ToolUnionParam{OfBashTool20250124: &anthropic.ToolBash20250124Param{}}` |
| Java | `.addTool(ToolBash20250124.builder().build())` from `com.anthropic.models.messages` |
| C# | `Tools = [new ToolBash20250124()]` from `Anthropic.Models.Messages` |
| PHP | `tools: [new \Anthropic\Messages\ToolBash20250124()]` |

Claude's `tool_use.input` contains either `{"command": "<string>"}` or `{"restart": true}`. Check for `restart` first (reset the session, return a confirmation string); otherwise run `command` and return combined stdout + stderr.

> **Security — commands are untrusted model output.** Run in an isolated environment (container, VM, or restricted user); apply an **allowlist** of permitted executables and reject shell operators (`&&`, `|`, `;`, `` ` ``, `$()`); set timeouts and resource limits; log every command. A blocklist is not sufficient.

### Text editor tool declaration

```json
{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}
```

Optional field: `max_characters` to cap `view` output. Java exposes a typed `ToolTextEditor20250728` builder (`com.anthropic.models.messages`); other statically-typed SDKs follow the same naming pattern — see the Anthropic-Defined Tools section in `{lang}/claude-api/tool-use.md` for the exact class.

> **Security — `path` is untrusted model output. Confine every file operation to a fixed project root.** Before executing any command, resolve the model-supplied `path` to its canonical form and verify it remains within your project root; reject the request if it escapes (`..`, symlinks, absolute paths outside the root, URL-encoded traversal like `%2e%2e%2f`). Use your language's built-in path utilities (e.g., Python `pathlib.Path.resolve()` then check `.is_relative_to(root)`). Never call `open()` / `writeFile` / `unlink` directly on the raw `path` value.

`tool_use.input.command` is one of:

| `command` | Other inputs | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `view` | `path`, optional `view_range` | Return file contents or directory listing |
| `create` | `path`, `file_text` | Create/overwrite file with `file_text`. Create a backup if the file already exists. |
| `str_replace` | `path`, `old_str`, `new_str` | Replace exactly one occurrence; error if 0 or >1 matches |
| `insert` | `path`, `insert_line`, `insert_text` | Insert `insert_text` after line `insert_line` (0 = beginning of file) |

For both tools, on error return `{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "…", "content": "<error text>", "is_error": true}` so Claude can recover.

---

## Structured Outputs

Structured outputs constrain Claude's responses to follow a specific JSON schema, guaranteeing valid, parseable output. This is not a separate tool — it enhances the Messages API response format and/or tool parameter validation.

Two features are available:

- **JSON outputs** (`output_config.format`): Control Claude's response format
- **Strict tool use** (`strict: true`): Guarantee valid tool parameter schemas

**Supported models:** Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Haiku 4.5. Legacy models (Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Opus 4.1) also support structured outputs.

> **Recommended:** Use `client.messages.parse()` which automatically validates responses against your schema. When using `messages.create()` directly, use `output_config: {format: {...}}`. The `output_format` convenience parameter is also accepted by some SDK methods (e.g., `.parse()`), but `output_config.format` is the canonical API-level parameter.

### JSON Schema Limitations

**Supported:**

- Basic types: object, array, string, integer, number, boolean, null
- `enum`, `const`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `$ref`/`$def`
- String formats: `date-time`, `time`, `date`, `duration`, `email`, `hostname`, `uri`, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `uuid`
- `additionalProperties: false` (required for all objects)

**Not supported:**

- Recursive schemas
- Numerical constraints (`minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`)
- String constraints (`minLength`, `maxLength`)
- Complex array constraints
- `additionalProperties` set to anything other than `false`

The Python and TypeScript SDKs automatically handle unsupported constraints by removing them from the schema sent to the API and validating them client-side.

### Important Notes

- **First request latency**: New schemas incur a one-time compilation cost. Subsequent requests with the same schema use a 24-hour cache.
- **Refusals**: If Claude refuses for safety reasons (`stop_reason: "refusal"`), the output may not match your schema.
- **Token limits**: If `stop_reason: "max_tokens"`, output may be incomplete. Increase `max_tokens`.
- **Incompatible with**: Citations (returns 400 error), message prefilling.
- **Works with**: Batches API, streaming, token counting, extended thinking.

---

## Tips for Effective Tool Use

1. **Provide detailed descriptions**: Claude relies heavily on descriptions to understand when and how to use tools
2. **Use specific tool names**: `get_current_weather` is better than `weather`
3. **Validate inputs**: Always validate tool inputs before execution
4. **Handle errors gracefully**: Return informative error messages so Claude can adapt
5. **Limit tool count**: Too many tools can confuse the model — keep the set focused
6. **Test tool interactions**: Verify Claude uses tools correctly in various scenarios

For detailed tool use documentation, use WebFetch:

- URL: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview`
</doc>

## When to Use WebFetch

Use WebFetch to get the latest documentation when:

- User asks for "latest" or "current" information
- Cached data seems incorrect
- User asks about features not covered here

Live documentation URLs are in `shared/live-sources.md`.

## Common Pitfalls

- Don't truncate inputs when passing files or content to the API. If the content is too long to fit in the context window, notify the user and discuss options (chunking, summarization, etc.) rather than silently truncating.
- **Prefill removed (Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Assistant message prefills (last-assistant-turn prefills) return a 400 error on Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6. Use structured outputs (`output_config.format`) or system prompt instructions to control response format instead. (One exception: the fallback-credit prefill claim — when redeeming a credit with `fallback_has_prefill_claim: true`, the server accepts the echoed assistant message; see the migration guide's refusal section.)
- **Confirm migration scope before editing:** When a user asks to migrate code to a newer Claude model without naming a specific file, directory, or file list, **ask which scope to apply first** — the entire working directory, a specific subdirectory, or a specific set of files. Do not start editing until the user confirms. Imperative phrasings like "migrate my codebase", "move my project to X", "upgrade to Sonnet 4.6", or bare "migrate to Opus 4.8" are **still ambiguous** — they tell you what to do but not where, so ask. Proceed without asking only when the prompt names an exact file, a specific directory, or an explicit file list ("migrate `app.py`", "migrate everything under `services/`", "update `a.py` and `b.py`"). See `shared/model-migration.md` Step 0.
- **`max_tokens` defaults:** Don't lowball `max_tokens` — hitting the cap truncates output mid-thought and requires a retry. For non-streaming requests, default to `~16000` (keeps responses under SDK HTTP timeouts). For streaming requests, default to `~64000` (timeouts aren't a concern, so give the model room). Only go lower when you have a hard reason: classification (`~256`), cost caps, deliberately short outputs, or **`max_tokens: 0`** for cache pre-warming (see `shared/prompt-caching.md` → Pre-warming).
- **Disabling thinking on Claude Opus 5 has two failure modes — prefer low/medium effort instead.** Only affects code that explicitly opts out; thinking is on by default, so watch for a disabled-thinking setting carried forward from Opus 4.8. With `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`, the model occasionally writes a tool call into its **visible text** instead of a `tool_use` block: the turn succeeds, the call never runs, no error is raised, and in an agentic loop that text pollutes later turns. It can also leak `<thinking>` tags into the response. Turning thinking on and lowering `effort` fixes both and still cuts cost. If a route must stay thinking-off: add *"You may say a brief sentence before using a tool"*, **delete** any don't-think/don't-reason rule (it makes tag leakage worse), and use a generic *"Do not include internal or system XML tags in your response"* rather than naming thinking tags. Details: `shared/model-migration.md` → Two failure modes when thinking is disabled.
- **128K output tokens:** Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6 support up to 128K `max_tokens`, but the SDKs require streaming for values that large to avoid HTTP timeouts. Use `.stream()` with `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()`.
- **Tool call JSON parsing (Fable 5, Opus 5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6 may produce different JSON string escaping in tool call `input` fields (e.g., Unicode or forward-slash escaping). Always parse tool inputs with `json.loads()` / `JSON.parse()` — never do raw string matching on the serialized input.
- **Structured outputs (all models):** Use `output_config: {format: {...}}` instead of the deprecated `output_format` parameter on `messages.create()`. This is a general API change, not 4.6-specific.
- **Don't reimplement SDK functionality:** The SDK provides high-level helpers — use them instead of building from scratch. Specifically: use `stream.finalMessage()` instead of wrapping `.on()` events in `new Promise()`; use typed exception classes (`Anthropic.RateLimitError`, etc.) instead of string-matching error messages; use SDK types (`Anthropic.MessageParam`, `Anthropic.Tool`, `Anthropic.Message`, etc.) instead of redefining equivalent interfaces.
- **Error handling — catch a chain, not one broad class.** A single `except APIStatusError` / `catch (AnthropicServiceException)` / `rescue APIError` loses the distinction between retryable (429, ≥500, network) and non-retryable (400/404) failures. Write a most-specific-first chain — e.g. `NotFoundError` → `RateLimitError` → `APIStatusError` → `APIConnectionError` (or the Go equivalent: `errors.As` into `*anthropic.Error` then `switch apierr.StatusCode { case 404: …; case 429: …; default: … }`). Per-language class names and namespaces are in `shared/error-codes.md`.
- **Don't research SDK types — write first.** If a type name isn't shown in the documentation included in this skill, write the code file from the namespace/package tables in the language-specific doc and let the compiler's error point you to the right name. Do not spend turns on WebFetch, SDK-repo clones, or compiling-and-running a separate reflection program to discover type names before writing — produce the source file first, then fix what the compiler reports. A quick `strings` / `jar tf` / `javap` against the installed SDK is acceptable for locating names (it returns in seconds), but don't escalate beyond that. A file with a wrong type name is recoverable; a session spent on discovery with no file written is not.
- **Bash and text editor tools are Anthropic-defined, schema-less.** Declare `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` / `{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}` — no `input_schema`. A custom tool with your own schema named `"bash"` is a different tool. Handler paths and security checks are in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Client-Side Tools.
- **Advisor tool model pairing.** The advisor tool's `model` must be at least as capable as the request's top-level `model` — e.g. executor `claude-sonnet-5` → advisor `claude-opus-4-8` or `claude-opus-4-7`. An invalid pair returns 400. Pairing table in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Advisor. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Agent Skills ≠ Managed Agents.** To have Claude generate a `.pptx`/`.xlsx`/etc. via Agent Skills, call `client.beta.messages.create` with `container={"skills": [...]}`, the `code_execution_20260521` tool, and both `code-execution-2025-08-25` + `skills-2025-10-02` betas. Do not use `client.beta.agents` / `sessions` / `environments` here — those are the Managed Agents surface, not Agent Skills.
- **MCP connector needs both halves.** `mcp_servers=[{type:"url", url, name}]` alone is rejected as a validation error — also add `tools=[{type:"mcp_toolset", mcp_server_name:<same name>}]` with beta `mcp-client-2025-11-20`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **`inference_geo` is a direct top-level request parameter** — `client.messages.create(..., inference_geo="us")` / `.inferenceGeo("us")`. Do not put it in `extra_body` / `putAdditionalBodyProperty`. (Messages API only — on Managed Agents, `inference_geo` instead nests inside the agent's `model` object, never top-level; see `shared/managed-agents-core.md` § Pinning inference geography.) Supported on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and later; availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`. `response.usage.inference_geo` reports where inference ran.
- **Fine-grained tool streaming is not a beta feature.** Set `eager_input_streaming: true` on the tool definition and call the regular `client.messages.stream(...)`. There is no beta header and no `client.beta.*` path.
- **Cache diagnostics is beta.** Use `client.beta.messages.*` with beta `cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07`. Pass `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: null}` on the first turn and `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: <previous response id>}` on subsequent turns; the result is on `response.diagnostics`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Memory tool type is `memory_20250818`.** Declare `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}`. Go uses the beta-namespace type `{OfMemoryTool20250818: &anthropic.BetaMemoryTool20250818Param{}}` on `client.Beta.Messages.New`; Python/TypeScript/Ruby/PHP/C# use the non-beta `client.messages.create`; Java has both a non-beta `MemoryTool20250818` and a beta tool-runner path. Python/TypeScript provide `BetaAbstractMemoryTool` / `betaMemoryTool` helpers for implementing the backend.
- **Use a model the feature actually supports.** Some features are restricted to specific model tiers — fast mode is Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 only (and Claude API only), task budgets (Messages API only — Managed Agents session budgets have no model-tier restriction) are Claude Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7 only, and the advisor tool requires a valid executor↔advisor pair. If the user's prompt names a model that the feature doesn't support, use a supported model instead and note the substitution in the output.
- **Don't define custom types for SDK data structures:** The SDK exports types for all API objects. Use `Anthropic.MessageParam` for messages, `Anthropic.Tool` for tool definitions, `Anthropic.ToolUseBlock` / `Anthropic.ToolResultBlockParam` for tool results, `Anthropic.Message` for responses. Defining your own `interface ChatMessage { role: string; content: unknown }` duplicates what the SDK already provides and loses type safety.
- **Report and document output:** For tasks that produce reports, documents, or visualizations, the code execution sandbox has `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `matplotlib`, `pillow`, and `pypdf` pre-installed. Claude can generate formatted files (DOCX, PDF, charts) and return them via the Files API — consider this for "report" or "document" type requests instead of plain stdout text.
- **Server-tool errors don't raise.** Web search and web fetch errors return HTTP 200 with a `web_search_tool_result` / `web_fetch_tool_result` block whose `content` is a single error object (e.g. `{error_code: "max_uses_exceeded"}`) — not a raised exception. For web search, a success `content` is a *list*; an error `content` is an *object* — branch on that before indexing.
- **Code execution output block type:** `code_execution_20260521` returns `bash_code_execution_tool_result` (with `.content.stdout`), **not** the legacy bare `code_execution_tool_result`. Iterate `response.content` and match on the correct type.
- **Tool search: never defer everything.** The search tool itself must not have `defer_loading: true`, and at least one tool in `tools` must be non-deferred, or the API returns 400 `All tools have defer_loading set`.

### Risks and explicit decisions

- **Upstream preset drift:** the overlay is intentionally tied to claude-hud 0.7.1 prose. Review and revise it deliberately when upgrading the plugin rather than inheriting new defaults automatically.

- **Concurrent writers:** atomic replacement prevents partial JSON, but applying chezmoi concurrently with `/claude-hud:configure` can still produce a last-writer-wins race. Do not add locking unless that race is observed.
- **Formatting:** the first successful merge may normalize JSON formatting and ordering; semantic preservation and subsequent byte stability are the guarantees.
- **Command parsing:** bypass detection deliberately supports the seeded unquoted base flag and exact user argument. Do not build a general shell or TOML parser.

1	#Requires -Version 7
2	# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1 — merge a managed overlay into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json so claude-hud (statusline HUD), the pyright-lsp
4	# plugin, and a couple of safe defaults deploy on Windows. Companion to the
5	# parent (macOS/Linux) repo's dot_claude/modify_settings.json; that repo uses a
6	# `modify_` + jq merge, which is unreliable on Windows (invariant #5), so we use
7	# the same run_onchange pwsh-merger idiom as the editor overlays instead.
8	#
9	# Why a merge (not a managed dot_claude/settings.json)? Claude Code rewrites
10	# this file at runtime (plugins it installs, permissions the user grants). A
11	# static managed file would clobber all of that on every apply. We instead
12	# recursively deep-merge only our keys in, preserving every live key.
13	#
14	# Gated on installCodingAgents — no Claude Code, nothing to configure. Re-runs
15	# when the embedded overlay (claude/settings-overlay.json) changes.
16	{{ if .installCodingAgents -}}
17	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'   # best-effort; never abort the apply
18	
19	# Embedded at render time from the (chezmoi-ignored) claude/ source, so this
20	# script is self-contained and re-fires when the overlay changes.
21	$overlayJson = @'
22	{{ include "claude/settings-overlay.json" }}
23	'@
24	
25	$overlay = $overlayJson | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable
26	
27	# --- Completion-feedback hooks, gated on `agentSounds` -----------------------
28	#
29	# Built here rather than in claude/settings-overlay.json because that file is
30	# `include`d verbatim and so cannot carry Go-template conditionals.
31	#
32	# `notify` wires notify.ps1 (apprise -> Windows toast); `peon` wires peon-ping's
33	# game voice lines. Values lifted from a real peon-ping install.ps1 (verified
34	# against upstream source, NOT its README — the README's documented command
35	# shape is wrong on the POSIX side too). Windows specifics that differ from the
36	# macOS/Linux parent repo:
37	#   - command is `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File "<peon.ps1>"`
38	#   - `timeout = 10`, and there is NO `async` field
39	#   - the event set includes PreToolUse and has NO UserPromptSubmit
40	# Parent repo equivalent: dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl.
41	{{- $peon   := or (eq .agentSounds "peon")   (eq .agentSounds "both") }}
42	{{- $notify := or (eq .agentSounds "notify") (eq .agentSounds "both") }}
43	$notifyCmd = 'exec pwsh -NoProfile -File "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hooks/notify.ps1"'
44	# peon-ping is installed with `-OpenPeon`, which reroots its whole tree at the
45	# tool-agnostic ~/.openpeon — so peon.ps1 is NOT under ~/.claude/hooks/.
46	# Wrapped in a Test-Path guard so the hook is a silent no-op on a box where the
47	# install hasn't run (or failed): an unguarded `-File <missing>` makes Claude
48	# Code surface a hook error on every event. Mirrors the mandatory
49	# `command -v workmux` / `[ -x ... ]` guards in the parent repo.
50	$peonPs1   = Join-Path $HOME '.openpeon\hooks\peon-ping\peon.ps1'
51	$peonCmd   = "powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command `"if (Test-Path '$peonPs1') { & '$peonPs1' }`""
52	
53	# Event -> the commands that should be wired for the current tier.
54	$soundHooks = @{}
55	{{- if $notify }}
56	foreach ($evt in @('Notification', 'Stop')) {
57	    $soundHooks[$evt] = @(@{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $notifyCmd }) })
58	}
59	{{- end }}
60	{{- if $peon }}
61	foreach ($evt in @('SessionStart', 'SessionEnd', 'SubagentStart', 'Stop',
62	                   'Notification', 'PermissionRequest', 'PreToolUse',
63	                   'PostToolUseFailure', 'PreCompact')) {
64	    $entry = @{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $peonCmd; timeout = 10 }) }
65	    if ($soundHooks.ContainsKey($evt)) { $soundHooks[$evt] = @($soundHooks[$evt] + $entry) }
66	    else                               { $soundHooks[$evt] = @($entry) }
67	}
68	{{- end }}
69	if ($soundHooks.Count -gt 0) {
70	    if ($overlay['hooks'] -isnot [hashtable]) { $overlay['hooks'] = @{} }
71	    foreach ($evt in $soundHooks.Keys) { $overlay['hooks'][$evt] = $soundHooks[$evt] }
72	}
73	
74	# Commands the CURRENT tier disables — pruned from the live file below. Without
75	# this the additive merge makes agentSounds a one-way ratchet: switching
76	# notify -> none would leave notify.ps1 wired forever, so `none` would not
77	# actually silence a machine that previously had sound. Only OUR OWN
78	# fingerprints are listed, so foreign hook entries can never be touched.
79	# (Upstream's own install.ps1 strips `peon\.(ps1|sh)` / `notify\.sh` the same
80	# way before re-adding, so this matches its behaviour.)
81	$prunePatterns = @(
82	{{- if not $notify }}
83	    'notify\.ps1'
84	{{- end }}
85	{{- if not $peon }}
86	    'peon\.ps1'
87	{{- end }}
88	)
89	
90	# Recursive deep-merge: overlay leaves win; live-only keys are preserved. Unlike
91	# the editor overlay's shallow top-level assign, this keeps the user's nested
92	# state (e.g. permissions.allow/deny arrays, other enabledPlugins) intact.
93	#
94	# The `hooks` object gets special, ADDITIVE handling (see Merge-ClaudeHooks) so
95	# our Notification/Stop notify entries are appended without clobbering hook
96	# entries the user or other tools added. Every other array value is still
97	# replaced wholesale (overlay wins), which is what we want for scalars/plugins.
98	function Merge-Hashtable([hashtable]$base, [hashtable]$overlay) {
99	    foreach ($k in $overlay.Keys) {
100	        if ($k -eq 'hooks' -and ($overlay[$k] -is [hashtable])) {
101	            if ($base[$k] -isnot [hashtable]) { $base[$k] = @{} }
102	            Merge-ClaudeHooks $base[$k] $overlay[$k]
103	        }
104	        elseif ($base.ContainsKey($k) -and ($base[$k] -is [hashtable]) -and ($overlay[$k] -is [hashtable])) {
105	            Merge-Hashtable $base[$k] $overlay[$k]
106	        }
107	        else {
108	            $base[$k] = $overlay[$k]
109	        }
110	    }
111	}
112	
113	# Additive per-event hook merge, mirroring the parent repo's jq reduce in
114	# dot_claude/modify_settings.json: for each event, append only the overlay
115	# entries whose .hooks[0].command isn't already present in the live array,
116	# preserving live entries verbatim. Wholesale-replacing the arrays (the old
117	# behavior) would drop hooks the user / other tools add at runtime. @(...) also
118	# forces array shape so ConvertTo-Json emits a JSON array even for a single
119	# entry (Claude requires hooks.<event> to be an array).
120	function Merge-ClaudeHooks([hashtable]$base, [hashtable]$overlay) {
121	    foreach ($evt in $overlay.Keys) {
122	        # NB: plain two-line assign, NOT `$live = if (...) { @(..) } else { @() }`.
123	        # A single-element @() flowing out of an if-EXPRESSION gets unwrapped back
124	        # to a scalar (here a hashtable), so `$live + $additions` then throws
125	        # "A hash table can only be added to another hash table". Direct `= @(...)`
126	        # keeps the array shape.
127	        $live = @()
128	        if ($null -ne $base[$evt]) { $live = @($base[$evt]) }
129	        $liveCmds = @($live | ForEach-Object { $_.hooks[0].command })
130	        $additions = @($overlay[$evt] | Where-Object {
131	            $cmd = $_.hooks[0].command
132	            (-not $cmd) -or ($liveCmds -notcontains $cmd)
133	        })
134	        $base[$evt] = @($live + $additions)
135	    }
136	}
137	
138	# Respect CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (matches the statusLine command + claude-hud setup).
139	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME '.claude' }
140	$settingsPath = Join-Path $claudeDir 'settings.json'
141	
142	$settings = @{}
143	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
144	    $raw = Get-Content -Raw $settingsPath
145	    if ($raw.Trim()) {
146	        try { $settings = $raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable }
147	        catch { Write-Warning "could not parse $settingsPath; not overwriting"; return }
148	    }
149	}
150	
151	Merge-Hashtable $settings $overlay
152	
153	# Prune our own now-disabled entries (see $prunePatterns above). Runs AFTER the
154	# additive merge so a tier that re-enables something wins. Foreign entries are
155	# never matched. Event keys whose array empties out are removed so turning
156	# everything off doesn't leave `"SessionStart": []` litter behind.
157	if ($prunePatterns.Count -gt 0 -and $settings['hooks'] -is [hashtable]) {
158	    foreach ($evt in @($settings['hooks'].Keys)) {
159	        $kept = @(@($settings['hooks'][$evt]) | Where-Object {
160	            $cmd = $_.hooks[0].command
161	            if (-not $cmd) { return $true }
162	            foreach ($p in $prunePatterns) { if ($cmd -match $p) { return $false } }
163	            return $true
164	        })
165	        if ($kept.Count -gt 0) { $settings['hooks'][$evt] = $kept }
166	        else                   { $settings['hooks'].Remove($evt) }
167	    }
168	}
169	
170	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $claudeDir | Out-Null
171	$settings | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12 | Set-Content -Path $settingsPath -Encoding utf8
172	Write-Host "claude overlay -> $settingsPath"
173	{{ end -}}
174

61	## Conventions & hard invariants
62	
63	1. **A new/renamed init prompt must update the CI flags in the same commit.** `chezmoi init --promptBool/--promptChoice "<text>=value"` matches the prompt's exact TEXT (3rd arg to `promptXOnce` in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`), used non-interactively by `.github/workflows/windows.yml`. Forget it → CI's init hangs/EOFs (`error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF`; this broke three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds` was added). Corollary: **never put `=` in a prompt's text** — the `name=value` parser splits on the first `=` (this broke the `role` prompt once). Enforced by `tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` (missing flag, stale flag, wrong flag kind, `=` in text), which CI runs *before* `chezmoi init` so the failure names the missing flag instead of EOF-ing — run `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` locally after touching either file.
64	2. **Run-scripts must never abort the apply.** The installer + editor/terminal/backup/skill scripts use `$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'` (+ `PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$false`), collect failures via `Register-Failure`, print a summary, and exit 0. 102	### Long-term backlog → `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
103	
104	When the user surfaces an idea explicitly **not** being implemented this
105	session (signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
106	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來"), add an entry to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using
107	the priority + effort tag schema. Do **not** create new `ROADMAP.md` /
108	`IDEAS.md` / `BACKLOG.md` files — `TODO.md` is the single index.
109	
110	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` validates the format. Run it
111	(`scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md`) after editing so syntax
112	drift is caught immediately.
113	
114	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
115	
116	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
117	
118	   ```
119	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
120	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
121	   ```
122	
123	   Inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane and
124	   re-runs the validator. Add `--backlog` to also scaffold
125	   `backlog/<slug>.md` from the bundled template.
126	
127	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
128	
129	   ```
130	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
131	   ```
132	
133	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox", run
134	   `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`. It prompts for the missing fields per loose
135	   line and calls `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs
136	   that only formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
137	
138	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh; run
139	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
140	
141	Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` companion doc when the item meets any of:
142	
143	- carries a `P?` tag (record what was tried so it doesn't need re-investigation)
144	- captures a paused troubleshooting session that you intend to fix later
145	  (preserve the error trace + root cause analysis before context evaporates)
146	- weighs multiple options (record trade-offs, not only the winner)
147	- is `[L]` or `[XL]` (architectural; needs design before code)
148	
149	`[S]` items rarely need a backlog doc — a file path in the `TODO.md` line is
150	usually enough. See [`backlog/README.md`](backlog/README.md) for the full
151	template and "when to add a doc" rules.
152	
153	When implementing a `TODO.md` item, in the same commit:
154	
155	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`
156	   to move the entry into `## Done` with the dated syntax and re-validate.
157	2. Mark the corresponding `backlog/<slug>.md` (if any) `Status: shipped`
158	   and keep it as a historical record (don't delete — future-you may
159	   revisit adjacent decisions).
160	
161	`backlog/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore); it
162	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
163	
164	### Past pitfalls → `pitfalls/`
165	
166	When you spend more than ~15 minutes debugging something that wasn't
167	googleable and the fix is non-obvious, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
168	capturing:
169	
170	1. **Verbatim symptom** — copy-paste error messages exactly, do not
171	   paraphrase (preserves grep-ability for future-you / future agent)
172	2. **Root cause** — why this happens (with source / docs / upstream issue link)
173	3. **Workaround** — copy-pasteable commands or config diff
174	4. **Prevention** — how to avoid stepping on this again
175	
176	Title the doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause (you'll search by what
177	you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned). See
178	[`pitfalls/README.md`](pitfalls/README.md) for the full template and
179	when-to-add rules.
180	
181	**Pitfall vs Hard invariant**: a pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant in
182	this file when it (a) recurs across machines/agents/sessions despite being
183	documented, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround is non-obvious
184	enough that "remember to do X" isn't safe. When graduating, leave the
185	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the new
186	invariant.
187	
188	`pitfalls/` is excluded from chezmoi (see .chezmoiignore) and
189	**not** auto-redacted; review for secrets before committing.

4	# Runs the maintained copilot-api fork (npm @jeffreycao/copilot-api) from a pinned
5	# local install so a GitHub Copilot subscription can back Claude Code and Codex.
6	# The optional Bun throttle shim (copilot-throttle-shim.js) is reused verbatim from
7	# the unix side.

9	# Public commands (exported with their original hyphenated names for muscle
10	# memory — PSUseApprovedVerbs is intentionally waived):
11	#   copilot-proxy [start|stop|restart|status|doctor [--live]|logs [shim|N]|shim [on|off|status]|whoami|auth|reinstall]
12	#   copilot-run <cmd...>            run a command with the proxy env injected
13	#   claude-copilot [args...]        one-off Claude Code session on the proxy
14	#   claude-copilot-once [args...]   pinned one-shot session, auto-reverted
15	#   codex-copilot [args...]         one-off Codex session on Responses proxy
16	#   codex-copilot-once [args...]    identical zero-persistence alias
17	# (claude-copilot / -once run claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions — the
18	#  proxy flow is the trusted, hands-off path; plain `claude` is unaffected.)
19	#   copilot-here [on|off|status]    per-project pin via ./.claude/settings.local.json
20	#   copilot-model [<id>|-l|-c|--auto]  switch the pinned model
21	#   copilot-embed [--model M] [--json] [TEXT|-] | -l
22	#   semsearch index [PATH...] | semsearch <QUERY> [-k N] [--corpus PATH]
23	#
24	# Contract preserved from the unix version: token at
25	# ~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token, ports 4141 (proxy) / 4142 (shim),
26	# state under $XDG_STATE_HOME/copilot-proxy, per-project ./.claude/settings.local.json
27	# pin, default model gpt-5.6-sol[1m], and the ANTHROPIC_* env block.
28	#
29	# The pinned package is INSTALLED ONCE into $XDG_DATA_HOME/copilot-api/pkg and the
30	# proxy runs that binary directly. It deliberately does NOT use `bunx` at launch:
31	# bunx re-resolves the package on every start, and bun stalls forever resolving
32	# through a socks proxy — which wedged `start` at "Resolving dependencies" AND kept
33	# bun's global cache lock, so every retry hung too. Force a re-install with
34	# `copilot-proxy reinstall`.
35	#
36	# Env knobs:
37	#   COPILOT_PROXY_PORT   default 4141    - port the proxy listens on
38	#   COPILOT_PROXY_START_TIMEOUT default 45 - seconds allowed for model refresh
39	#   COPILOT_SHIM_PORT    default 4142    - throttle shim port
40	#   COPILOT_API_PKG      default @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0 - registry spec
41	#                          (name or @scope/name + optional version/tag/range;
42	#                           aliases/local/git/URL specs are rejected before cleanup)
43	#   COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL                 - override the pinned model
44	#   COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET  1               - add the telemetry-suppressing env keys
45	#   COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY 1            - skip straight to the no-proxy install try
46	#   COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY   default auto    - Node->GitHub /models egress:
47	#                          auto   = use the Windows System Proxy (WinINET registry)
48	#                                   or HTTPS_PROXY when either is set; Node ignores
49	#                                   the system setting unless it is passed the env.
50	#                          always = same, but warn when no proxy is found
51	#                          never  = never pass --proxy-env
52	#                          http://127.0.0.1:PORT = force that URL
53	
54	Set-StrictMode -Off
55	
56	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers ---
57	$script:CopilotDefaultPkg = '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0'
58	function script:Get-CopilotPort { if ($env:COPILOT_PROXY_PORT) { $env:COPILOT_PROXY_PORT } else { '4141' } }
59	function script:Get-CopilotPkg  { if ($env:COPILOT_API_PKG)   { $env:COPILOT_API_PKG }   else { $script:CopilotDefaultPkg } }
60	function script:Get-CopilotPkgFlavor {
61	    switch -Regex (Get-CopilotPkg) { '^copilot-api(@.*)?$' { 'original' } default { 'fork' } }
62	}
63	function script:Get-CopilotBase    { "http://localhost:$(Get-CopilotPort)" }
64	function script:Get-CopilotTmp     { if ($env:TEMP) { $env:TEMP } else { [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath() } }
65	function script:Get-CopilotLogFile { Join-Path (Get-CopilotTmp) "copilot-api-$(Get-CopilotPort).log" }
66	function script:Get-CopilotPidFile { Join-Path (Get-CopilotTmp) "copilot-api-$(Get-CopilotPort).pid" }
67	function script:Get-CopilotToken   { Join-Path $HOME '.local/share/copilot-api/github_token' }
68	
69	function script:Get-XdgState { if ($env:XDG_STATE_HOME) { $env:XDG_STATE_HOME } else { Join-Path $HOME '.local/state' } }
70	function script:Get-XdgConfig { if ($env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME) { $env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME } else { Join-Path $HOME '.config' } }
71	function script:Get-XdgData { if ($env:XDG_DATA_HOME) { $env:XDG_DATA_HOME } else { Join-Path $HOME '.local/share' } }
72	
73	# --- pinned package install (run the binary, never `bunx` at launch) -----------
74	#
75	# Why an install prefix instead of `bunx <pkg> start`: bunx re-resolves the
76	# package on EVERY launch, and bun hangs indefinitely resolving through a socks
77	# proxy (a browser/curl through the same proxy is fine, which is what makes it so
78	# confusing). The wedged installer then keeps bun's global install-cache lock, so
79	# every retry hangs identically and stacks another zombie. Installing once and
80	# running the resulting binary removes the per-start resolve entirely — a warm
81	# start does zero network before it binds the port.
82	
83	# Parse only registry package specs: name or @scope/name, optionally followed by
84	# a version/tag/range. npm aliases and local/git/URL selectors are rejected before
85	# their text can reach any filesystem path or destructive cleanup.
86	function script:Get-CopilotPkgSpecInfo {
87	    $spec = Get-CopilotPkg
88	    $match = [regex]::Match(
89	        $spec,
90	        '^(?<name>@[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*|[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)(?:@(?<selector>.+))?$'
91	    )
92	    if (-not $match.Success) { return $null }
93	    $selector = [string]$match.Groups['selector'].Value
94	    if ($selector -and (
95	        $selector -match '^(?:npm:|file:|link:|https?:|git(?:\+[^:]*)?:|github:|gitlab:|bitbucket:)' -or
96	        $selector -match '[\\/]'
97	    )) { return $null }
98	    [pscustomobject]@{
99	        Name     = [string]$match.Groups['name'].Value
100	        Selector = $selector
101	    }
102	}
103	
104	function script:Get-CopilotPkgName {
105	    $info = Get-CopilotPkgSpecInfo
106	    if ($info) { $info.Name } else { $null }
107	}
108	
109	function script:Get-CopilotPkgPrefix { Join-Path (Get-XdgData) 'copilot-api/pkg' }
110	# Records verified installed metadata, so bumping COPILOT_API_PKG (or the pinned
111	# default) re-installs instead of silently running an old or partial tree.
112	function script:Get-CopilotPkgStamp { Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) '.installed-spec' }
113	
114	# Exact registry selectors can be verified against installed package metadata.
115	function script:Get-CopilotPkgExactVersion {
116	    $info = Get-CopilotPkgSpecInfo
117	    if ($info -and $info.Selector -match '^v?(\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?(?:\+[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?)$') {
118	        return $Matches[1]
119	    }
120	    $null
121	}
122	
123	function script:Get-CopilotPkgMetadata {
124	    $name = Get-CopilotPkgName
125	    if (-not $name) { return $null }
126	    $path = Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) "node_modules/$name/package.json"
127	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $path -PathType Leaf)) { return $null }
128	    try {
129	        $json = Get-Content -LiteralPath $path -Raw -ErrorAction Stop | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop
130	        if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$json.name) -or
131	            [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$json.version)) { return $null }
132	        [pscustomobject]@{
133	            Name    = [string]$json.name
134	            Version = [string]$json.version
135	            Path    = $path
136	        }
137	    } catch { $null }
138	}
139	
140	function script:Get-CopilotPkgStampMetadata {
141	    $path = Get-CopilotPkgStamp
142	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $path -PathType Leaf)) { return $null }
143	    try {
144	        $json = Get-Content -LiteralPath $path -Raw -ErrorAction Stop | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop
145	        if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$json.requestedSpec) -or
146	            [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$json.name) -or
147	            [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$json.version)) { return $null }
148	        [pscustomobject]@{
149	            RequestedSpec = [string]$json.requestedSpec
150	            Name          = [string]$json.name
151	            Version       = [string]$json.version
152	        }
153	    } catch { $null }
154	}
155	
156	function script:Get-CopilotPkgLegacyStamp {
157	    $path = Get-CopilotPkgStamp
158	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $path -PathType Leaf)) { return $null }
159	    try {
160	        $raw = (Get-Content -LiteralPath $path -Raw -ErrorAction Stop).Trim()
161	        if ($raw -and -not $raw.StartsWith('{')) { return $raw }
162	    } catch { $null }
163	    $null
164	}
165	
166	function script:Write-CopilotPkgStamp {
167	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] $Metadata)
168	    [ordered]@{
169	        requestedSpec = Get-CopilotPkg
170	        name          = [string]$Metadata.Name
171	        version       = [string]$Metadata.Version
172	    } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Content -Path (Get-CopilotPkgStamp) -Encoding utf8
173	}
174	
175	# The binlink bun wrote, if any. Bun on Windows writes node_modules/.bin/<name>.exe
176	# (plus a .bunx sidecar); the other extensions cover an npm/yarn-populated prefix.
177	# Returns $null when no directly-runnable shim exists — Get-CopilotPkgLaunch then
178	# falls back to `bun run`, which resolves from the local node_modules offline.
179	function script:Get-CopilotPkgBin {
180	    $binDir = Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) 'node_modules/.bin'
181	    foreach ($ext in '.exe', '.cmd', '.bat', '', '.ps1') {
182	        $p = Join-Path $binDir "copilot-api$ext"
183	        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $p -PathType Leaf) { return $p }
184	    }
185	    $null
186	}
187	
188	# How to invoke the installed proxy: @{ Exe; Pre; Cwd }. Cwd is non-null only for
189	# the `bun run` fallback, which must resolve node_modules/.bin from the prefix.
190	#
191	# The prefix is deliberately NOT passed as an argument (`bun run --cwd <path>`):
192	# Start-Process joins -ArgumentList with spaces and does no quoting, so a prefix
193	# under a $HOME containing a space ("C:\Users\Da-Wei Lee\...") would arrive split
194	# across two argv entries. -WorkingDirectory takes the path as a real parameter.
195	function script:Get-CopilotPkgLaunch {
196	    $bin = Get-CopilotPkgBin
197	    # .ps1 can't be Start-Process'd directly, and a bare extensionless shim is a
198	    # shell script — route both through `bun run`, which finds node_modules/.bin.
199	    if ($bin -and [System.IO.Path]::GetExtension($bin) -in '.exe', '.cmd', '.bat') {
200	        return @{ Exe = $bin; Pre = @(); Cwd = $null }
201	    }
202	    if ($bin -and (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
203	        return @{ Exe = 'bun'; Pre = @('run', 'copilot-api'); Cwd = (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) }
204	    }
205	    # The hash-pinned CDN fallback carries the published dist files but no npm
206	    # binlink. Run its declared entry point directly with Bun.
207	    $metadata = Get-CopilotPkgMetadata
208	    $main = if ($metadata) { Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $metadata.Path) 'dist/main.js' } else { $null }
209	    if ($main -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $main -PathType Leaf) -and (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
210	        return @{ Exe = 'bun'; Pre = @($main); Cwd = (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) }
211	    }
212	    $null
213	}
214	
215	function script:Test-CopilotPkgDependencies {
216	    param($Metadata = (Get-CopilotPkgMetadata))
217	    if (-not $Metadata) { return $false }
218	    try {
219	        $package = Get-Content -LiteralPath $Metadata.Path -Raw -ErrorAction Stop | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop
220	        $names = if ($package.dependencies) { @($package.dependencies.PSObject.Properties.Name) } else { @() }
221	        $packageDir = Split-Path -Parent $Metadata.Path
222	        $prefix = Get-CopilotPkgPrefix
223	        foreach ($dependency in $names) {
224	            $local = Join-Path $packageDir "node_modules/$dependency/package.json"
225	            $hoisted = Join-Path $prefix "node_modules/$dependency/package.json"
226	            if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $local -PathType Leaf) -and
227	                -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $hoisted -PathType Leaf)) { return $false }
228	        }
229	        return $true
230	    } catch { return $false }
231	}
232	
233	# Did the requested package actually land in the prefix and remain runnable?
234	# Metadata is authoritative: a stale directory or binlink alone never satisfies
235	# this postcondition. Exact selectors must also match the installed version.
236	function script:Test-CopilotPkgInstalled {
237	    param($Metadata = (Get-CopilotPkgMetadata))
238	    if (-not $Metadata) { return $false }
239	    if ($Metadata.Name -cne (Get-CopilotPkgName)) { return $false }
240	    $exactVersion = Get-CopilotPkgExactVersion
241	    if ($exactVersion -and $Metadata.Version -cne $exactVersion) { return $false }
242	    (Test-CopilotPkgDependencies -Metadata $Metadata) -and $null -ne (Get-CopilotPkgLaunch)
243	}
244	
245	# Is the CURRENT selector installed, stamped with verified metadata and runnable?
246	function script:Test-CopilotPkgReady {
247	    $metadata = Get-CopilotPkgMetadata
248	    if (-not (Test-CopilotPkgInstalled -Metadata $metadata)) { return $false }
249	    $stamp = Get-CopilotPkgStampMetadata
250	    if (-not $stamp) { return $false }
251	    ($stamp.RequestedSpec -ceq (Get-CopilotPkg)) -and
252	        ($stamp.Name -ceq $metadata.Name) -and
253	        ($stamp.Version -ceq $metadata.Version)
254	}
255	
256	# Remove only the requested package and its dedicated launch shims. Resolve and
257	# verify containment before deletion, then require cleanup to be complete: retained
258	# matching files could otherwise certify a failed installer attempt.
259	function script:Clear-CopilotPkgInstallTarget {
260	    $name = Get-CopilotPkgName
261	    if (-not $name) {
262	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: unsupported COPILOT_API_PKG registry spec '$(Get-CopilotPkg)'"
263	        return $false
264	    }
265	
266	    $nodeModules = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) 'node_modules'))
267	    $packageDir = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Join-Path $nodeModules $name))
268	    $trimChars = [char[]]@([System.IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar, [System.IO.Path]::AltDirectorySeparatorChar)
269	    $nodeModulesRoot = $nodeModules.TrimEnd($trimChars) + [System.IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar
270	    $comparison = if ($IsWindows) { [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase } else { [System.StringComparison]::Ordinal }
271	    if (-not $packageDir.StartsWith($nodeModulesRoot, $comparison)) {
272	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: refusing package cleanup outside $nodeModulesRoot"
273	        return $false
274	    }
275	
276	    $binDir = Join-Path $nodeModules '.bin'
277	    try {
278	        if ([System.IO.Directory]::Exists($packageDir)) {
279	            [System.IO.Directory]::Delete($packageDir, $true)
280	        }
281	        if ([System.IO.Directory]::Exists($binDir)) {
282	            foreach ($binPath in [System.IO.Directory]::GetFiles($binDir, 'copilot-api*')) {
283	                [System.IO.File]::Delete($binPath)
284	            }
285	        }
286	    } catch {
287	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: could not clear the previous package target ($_)"
288	        return $false
289	    }
290	
291	    $remainingBin = if ([System.IO.Directory]::Exists($binDir)) {
292	        @([System.IO.Directory]::GetFiles($binDir, 'copilot-api*'))
293	    } else { @() }
294	    if ([System.IO.Directory]::Exists($packageDir) -or $remainingBin.Count -gt 0) {
295	        Write-Error 'copilot-proxy: previous package target is still present after cleanup; refusing to run the installer'
296	        return $false
297	    }
298	    $true
299	}
300	
301	# One package-install attempt in -Dir, bounded by -BudgetSeconds. npm is preferred
302	# because it supports Azure Artifacts' credential-provider token in ~/.npmrc;
303	# Bun does not. -NoProxy strips the proxy env for the child. Returns $true only
304	# when matching metadata and a runnable launch path exist afterwards.
305	#
306	# Success is judged from the FILESYSTEM, not $p.ExitCode: a Start-Process -PassThru
307	# object reports ExitCode 0 even for a child that exited non-zero (verified — the
308	# .Handle-caching workaround does not help either), so trusting it would let a
309	# failed install write the .installed-spec stamp and silently pin a broken prefix.
310	#
311	# The kill on expiry is the load-bearing part: a stalled `bun add` left running
312	# keeps bun's global install-cache lock, and THAT is what made every subsequent
313	# start hang too. Never let one escape.
314	function script:Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry {
315	    param([string] $Dir, [switch] $NoProxy, [int] $BudgetSeconds)
316	
317	    if (-not (Clear-CopilotPkgInstallTarget)) { return $false }
318	    $proxyVars = 'ALL_PROXY', 'all_proxy', 'HTTP_PROXY', 'http_proxy', 'HTTPS_PROXY', 'https_proxy'
319	    $npm = Get-Command npm.cmd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
320	    $installer = if ($npm) {
321	        @{ File = $npm.Source; Args = @('install', '--no-save', '--no-audit', '--no-fund', (Get-CopilotPkg)) }
322	    } else {
323	        Write-Warning 'copilot-proxy: npm.cmd not found; falling back to Bun (authenticated Azure Artifacts feeds require npm).'
324	        @{ File = 'bun'; Args = @('add', (Get-CopilotPkg), '--no-summary') }
325	    }
326	    $saved = @{}
327	    if ($NoProxy) {
328	        foreach ($v in $proxyVars) { $saved[$v] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable($v); Remove-Item "env:$v" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
329	    }
330	    try {
331	        $p = Start-Process -FilePath $installer.File -ArgumentList $installer.Args `
332	            -WorkingDirectory $Dir -PassThru -NoNewWindow -ErrorAction Stop
333	        if ($p.WaitForExit($BudgetSeconds * 1000)) { return (Test-CopilotPkgInstalled) }
334	        Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
335	        # The subshell's child is the one actually holding the install lock.
336	        $name = [regex]::Escape((Get-CopilotPkgName))
337	        Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
338	            Where-Object { $_.Name -in 'bun.exe', 'node.exe' -and $_.CommandLine -match '\b(add|install)\b' -and $_.CommandLine -match $name } |
339	            ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
340	        return $false
341	    } catch {
342	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: could not launch package installer ($_)"; return $false
343	    } finally {
344	        if ($NoProxy) {
345	            foreach ($v in $proxyVars) {
346	                if ($null -eq $saved[$v]) { Remove-Item "env:$v" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
347	                else { Set-Item "env:$v" $saved[$v] }
348	            }
349	        }
350	    }
351	}

382	function script:Get-CopilotSha256Base64 {
383	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path)
384	    $stream = [System.IO.File]::OpenRead($Path)
385	    try {
386	        $sha = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::Create()
387	        try { [Convert]::ToBase64String($sha.ComputeHash($stream)) } finally { $sha.Dispose() }
388	    } finally { $stream.Dispose() }
389	}

391	function script:Install-CopilotPkgDependencies {
392	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $PackageDir, [int] $BudgetSeconds = 120)
393	    $npm = Get-Command npm.cmd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
394	    if (-not $npm) {
395	        Write-Error 'copilot-proxy: npm.cmd is required to install CDN package dependencies through the configured registry'
396	        return $false
397	    }
398	    try {
399	        $npmArgs = @('install', '--omit=dev', '--ignore-scripts', '--no-save', '--package-lock=false', '--no-audit', '--no-fund')
400	        $p = Start-Process -FilePath $npm.Source -ArgumentList $npmArgs -WorkingDirectory $PackageDir -PassThru -NoNewWindow -ErrorAction Stop
401	        if (-not $p.WaitForExit($BudgetSeconds * 1000)) {
402	            Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
403	            return $false
404	        }
405	        return (Test-CopilotPkgDependencies)
406	    } catch {
407	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: could not install CDN package dependencies ($_)"
408	        return $false
409	    }
410	}
411	
412	function script:Install-CopilotPkgFromCdn {
413	    $manifest = Get-CopilotPkgCdnManifest
414	    if (-not $manifest) { return $false }
415	    if (-not (Clear-CopilotPkgInstallTarget)) { return $false }
416	
417	    $packageDir = Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) 'node_modules/@jeffreycao/copilot-api'
418	    $downloadDir = Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) ".cdn-$([guid]::NewGuid())"
419	    try {
420	        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $downloadDir | Out-Null
421	        foreach ($relativePath in $manifest.Files.Keys) {
422	            $downloadPath = Join-Path $downloadDir ($relativePath -replace '/', [System.IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar)
423	            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path -Parent $downloadPath) | Out-Null
424	            Invoke-WebRequest -Uri ($manifest.BaseUrl + $relativePath) -OutFile $downloadPath -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 30 -ErrorAction Stop
425	            $actualHash = Get-CopilotSha256Base64 -Path $downloadPath
426	            if ($actualHash -cne $manifest.Files[$relativePath]) {
427	                throw "hash mismatch for $relativePath"
428	            }
429	        }
430	
431	        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path -Parent $packageDir) | Out-Null
432	        Move-Item -LiteralPath $downloadDir -Destination $packageDir -ErrorAction Stop
433	        $metadata = Get-CopilotPkgMetadata
434	        if (-not $metadata -or $metadata.Name -cne '@jeffreycao/copilot-api' -or $metadata.Version -cne '2.1.0') {
435	            throw 'downloaded package metadata does not identify @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0'
436	        }
437	        if (-not (Install-CopilotPkgDependencies -PackageDir $packageDir)) {
438	            throw 'dependency installation through the configured registry failed'
439	        }
440	        return (Test-CopilotPkgInstalled)
441	    } catch {
442	        Write-Warning "copilot-proxy: pinned CDN fallback failed ($_)"
443	        $null = Clear-CopilotPkgInstallTarget
444	        return $false
445	    } finally {
446	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $downloadDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
447	    }
448	}

450	# Ensure the pinned spec is installed. No-op (and no network) once it is.
451	function script:Install-CopilotPkg {
452	    if (-not (Get-CopilotPkgSpecInfo)) {
453	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: COPILOT_API_PKG must be a registry package spec (name or @scope/name with an optional version/tag/range); aliases and local/git/URL specs are unsupported: $(Get-CopilotPkg)"
454	        return $false
455	    }
456	    if (Test-CopilotPkgReady) { return $true }
457	
458	    # Migrate the old one-line stamp without a network call only when an exact
459	    # selector, the legacy stamp, live package metadata and launch path all agree.
460	    $metadata = Get-CopilotPkgMetadata
461	    if ((Get-CopilotPkgExactVersion) -and
462	        (Get-CopilotPkgLegacyStamp) -ceq (Get-CopilotPkg) -and
463	        (Test-CopilotPkgInstalled -Metadata $metadata)) {
464	        Write-CopilotPkgStamp -Metadata $metadata
465	        return $true
466	    }
467	
468	    if (-not (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
469	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: bun not found (scoop install bun)"; return $false
470	    }
471	    $spec = Get-CopilotPkg; $prefix = Get-CopilotPkgPrefix
472	    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $prefix | Out-Null
473	    # A private package.json keeps `bun add` from walking up and polluting $HOME.
474	    $pkgJson = Join-Path $prefix 'package.json'
475	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $pkgJson)) {
476	        '{"name":"copilot-api-runner","private":true,"version":"0.0.0"}' | Set-Content -Path $pkgJson -Encoding utf8
477	    }
478	
479	    Write-Host "copilot-proxy: installing $spec (one-time — later starts skip this) ..."
480	    # Attempt 1 honours the ambient env: on a host where the npm registry is only
481	    # reachable THROUGH the proxy, stripping it would break the install. Attempt 2
482	    # strips it, which is what rescues the socks stall. COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY=1
483	    # skips straight to attempt 2 (saves the 45s stall on a known-bad host).
484	    $skipFirst = ($env:COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY -eq '1')
485	    if ($skipFirst -or -not (Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry -Dir $prefix -BudgetSeconds 45)) {
486	        if (-not $skipFirst) {
487	            Write-Warning "copilot-proxy: install failed or stalled with the proxy env — retrying without it ..."
488	            # Drop bun's cache lock dir before retrying; the killed attempt may have
489	            # left it behind, and a stale lock hangs the retry for the same reason.
490	            $bunHome = if ($env:BUN_INSTALL) { $env:BUN_INSTALL } else { Join-Path $HOME '.bun' }
491	            Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Join-Path $bunHome 'install/cache/.tmp') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
492	        }
493	        if (-not (Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry -Dir $prefix -NoProxy -BudgetSeconds 90)) {
494	            Write-Warning 'copilot-proxy: configured npm registry did not provide the pin — trying the hash-pinned jsDelivr package copy; dependencies still use the configured registry ...'
495	            if (-not (Install-CopilotPkgFromCdn)) {
496	                Write-Error "copilot-proxy: could not install $spec from the configured registry or pinned CDN fallback — run 'copilot-proxy doctor'."; return $false
497	            }
498	        }
499	    }
500	
501	    $metadata = Get-CopilotPkgMetadata
502	    if (-not (Test-CopilotPkgInstalled -Metadata $metadata)) {
503	        $actual = if ($metadata) { "$($metadata.Name)@$($metadata.Version)" } else { 'no readable package metadata' }
504	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: install finished but $actual does not satisfy $spec with a runnable launch path under $prefix."
505	        return $false
506	    }
507	    Write-CopilotPkgStamp -Metadata $metadata
508	    $true
509	}

511	# Run a copilot-api subcommand (auth / check-usage / debug) in the foreground.
512	# Honours $launch.Cwd so the `bun run` fallback resolves node_modules/.bin.
513	function script:Invoke-CopilotPkgCommand {
514	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argument)
515	    if (-not (Install-CopilotPkg)) {
516	        $global:LASTEXITCODE = 1
517	        throw 'copilot-proxy: package installation or verification failed'
518	    }
519	    $launch = Get-CopilotPkgLaunch
520	    if (-not $launch) {
521	        $global:LASTEXITCODE = 1
522	        throw "copilot-proxy: no runnable copilot-api — try 'copilot-proxy reinstall'"
523	    }
524	    if ($launch.Cwd) { Push-Location $launch.Cwd }
525	    try {
526	        & $launch.Exe @($launch.Pre + $Argument)
527	        $commandExitCode = $LASTEXITCODE
528	        $global:LASTEXITCODE = $commandExitCode
529	        if ($commandExitCode -ne 0) {
530	            throw "copilot-proxy: copilot-api $($Argument -join ' ') failed with exit code $commandExitCode"
531	        }
532	    } finally { if ($launch.Cwd) { Pop-Location } }
533	}

535	# Live `bun add … copilot-api` processes. Install is a one-shot, so a match at
536	# rest is a clean stale-installer signal: a stalled one keeps bun's global
537	# install-cache lock, which wedges every later install too. Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry
538	# bounds and kills its own attempts, so this should stay empty — it remains as a
539	# safety net for a stall we didn't spawn (e.g. a hand-run `bunx @jeffreycao/copilot-api`).
540	function script:Get-CopilotStaleInstaller {
541	    Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name = 'bun.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
542	        Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match '\badd\b' -and $_.CommandLine -match 'copilot-api' }
543	}

555	# --- egress: which proxy should Node use for the GitHub /models fetch? --------
556	#
557	# copilot-api fetches /models at startup and refreshes its cache periodically;
558	# restart forces an immediate refresh. GitHub geo-filters the Claude catalog on
559	# some egress paths. Node does NOT honour the Windows System Proxy on its own — it
560	# only sees HTTP(S)_PROXY — so a host whose browser reaches the unfiltered catalog
561	# could still have the proxy cache a Claude-less list, which then looks exactly
562	# like an entitlement problem. Resolve the URL here and hand it to the child.
563	#
564	# COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY: auto|always|never|<url>. Returns a URL or $null.
565	function script:Resolve-CopilotHttpProxy {
566	    $mode = if ($env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY) { $env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY } else { 'auto' }
567	    switch -Regex ($mode) {
568	        '^(never|off|0|false|no)$' { return $null }
569	        '^(http|https|socks5h?)://' { return $mode }
570	        '^(always|auto|on|1|true|yes)$' { break }
571	        default {
572	            Write-Warning "copilot-proxy: unknown COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY='$mode' (use auto|always|never|http://...)"
573	            return $null
574	        }
575	    }
576	
577	    # The Windows System Proxy (WinINET). This is what Clash Verge / mihomo /
578	    # v2rayN write when their "System Proxy" toggle is on, so reading it covers
579	    # the same ground the unix side gets from its Clash detector.
580	    try {
581	        $key = Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings' -ErrorAction Stop
582	        if ($key.ProxyEnable -eq 1 -and $key.ProxyServer) {
583	            # ProxyServer is either "host:port" or "http=host:port;https=host:port".
584	            $server = $key.ProxyServer
585	            if ($server -match '(?:^|;)\s*https?=([^;]+)') { $server = $Matches[1] }
586	            elseif ($server -match ';') { $server = ($server -split ';')[0] }
587	            if ($server) { return "http://$($server -replace '^https?://', '')" }
588	        }
589	    } catch { $null = $_ }
590	
591	    # Fallback: an explicit env proxy in this shell.
592	    foreach ($v in $env:HTTPS_PROXY, $env:https_proxy, $env:HTTP_PROXY, $env:http_proxy) {
593	        if ($v) { return $v }
594	    }
595	    $null
596	}

598	# Model ids GitHub serves for this account RIGHT NOW, for the direct-vs-proxied
599	# A/B in doctor. -Via: 'direct' forces no proxy, a URL forces that proxy, absent
600	# uses .NET defaults. Returns sorted-unique ids, or $null on any failure.
601	#
602	# Secrets: the ghu_/bearer tokens only ever travel in request headers — never in
603	# a command line, never echoed.
604	function script:Get-CopilotUpstreamModel {
605	    param([string] $Via)
606	
607	    $tokFile = Get-CopilotToken
608	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $tokFile)) { return $null }
609	    $ghu = Get-Content -First 1 $tokFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
610	    if (-not $ghu) { return $null }
611	
612	    $transport = @{}
613	    if ($Via -eq 'direct') { $transport['NoProxy'] = $true }
614	    elseif ($Via) { $transport['Proxy'] = $Via }
615	
616	    try {
617	        $ex = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token' -TimeoutSec 10 `
618	            -Headers @{ 'Authorization' = "token $ghu"; 'user-agent' = 'GitHubCopilotChat/0.26.7' } `
619	            @transport -ErrorAction Stop
620	    } catch { return $null }
621	
622	    $api = if ($ex.endpoints.api) { $ex.endpoints.api } else { 'https://api.githubcopilot.com' }
623	    if (-not $ex.token) { return $null }
624	
625	    try {
626	        $up = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$api/models" -TimeoutSec 12 `
627	            -Headers @{
628	                'Authorization'            = "Bearer $($ex.token)"
629	                'user-agent'               = 'GitHubCopilotChat/0.26.7'
630	                'copilot-integration-id'   = 'vscode-chat'
631	            } @transport -ErrorAction Stop
632	    } catch { return $null }
633	
634	    @($up.data.id | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
635	}

637	# Optional ChatGPT Apps reachability. This is deliberately separate from the
638	# Copilot inference probes: codex_apps is a remote MCP served by chatgpt.com,
639	# not a localhost bridge to Codex.app and not part of GitHub Copilot.
640	function script:Get-CopilotProbeFailureKind {
641	    param($ErrorRecord)
642	
643	    $message = if ($ErrorRecord -is [System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord]) {
644	        $ErrorRecord.Exception.ToString()
645	    } else { [string]$ErrorRecord }
646	
647	    if ($message -match '(?i)timed?\s*out|timeout|operation.*canceled|deadline') { return 'timeout' }
648	    if ($message -match '(?i)certificate|authenticationexception|ssl|tls|secure channel') { return 'tls' }
649	    'network'
650	}

652	function script:Invoke-CopilotOptionalHttpProbe {
653	    param(
654	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Uri,
655	        [string] $Via = 'direct'
656	    )
657	
658	    $transport = @{}
659	    if ($Via -eq 'direct') { $transport['NoProxy'] = $true }
660	    elseif ($Via) { $transport['Proxy'] = $Via }
661	
662	    $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
663	    try {
664	        $response = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $Uri -Method Get -TimeoutSec 12 `
665	            -SkipHttpErrorCheck -Headers @{ 'user-agent' = 'codex-copilot-doctor/1.0' } `
666	            @transport -ErrorAction Stop
667	        $sw.Stop()
668	        [pscustomobject]@{
669	            Reached = $true
670	            Code    = [int]$response.StatusCode
671	            Seconds = [math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 2)
672	            Kind    = $null
673	            Error   = $null
674	        }
675	    } catch {
676	        $sw.Stop()
677	        [pscustomobject]@{
678	            Reached = $false
679	            Code    = 0
680	            Seconds = [math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 2)
681	            Kind    = Get-CopilotProbeFailureKind $_
682	            Error   = ($_.Exception.Message -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
683	        }
684	    }
685	}

711	# Resolve the model: $COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL > state file > default.
712	#
713	#   - HYPHENATED ids (claude-opus-4-8), not dotted (claude-opus-4.8): Claude Code
714	#     only recognizes hyphenated family names — dotted ids fall back to a legacy
715	#     "[Opus 4] retired" label AND a 200k context assumption.
716	#   - "[1m]" suffix: Claude Code uses it to size HUD/compaction for a 1M context
717	#     window. ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel derives it from live /v1/models metadata
718	#     for every provider. Claude Code-only: raw API clients use the plain id.
719	function script:Get-CopilotDefaultModel {
720	    if ($env:COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL) { return $env:COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL }
721	    $sf = Get-CopilotModelState
722	    if (Test-Path $sf) { return (Get-Content -First 1 $sf) }
723	    'gpt-5.6-sol[1m]'
724	}

726	# Every model id the proxy accepts: .id plus the .claude_model_id alias. Callers
727	# with several catalog views pass one snapshot so all decisions share one response.
728	function script:Get-CopilotServedModels {
729	    param($Catalog)
730	    if (-not $PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('Catalog')) { $Catalog = Get-CopilotModelCatalog }
731	    if (-not $Catalog) { return @() }
732	    $ids = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
733	    foreach ($m in $Catalog.data) {
734	        if ($m.id) { $ids.Add([string]$m.id) }
735	        if ($m.claude_model_id) { $ids.Add([string]$m.claude_model_id) }
736	    }
737	    $ids | Sort-Object -Unique
738	}

758	# Pick exactly one live inference target. The configured main wins only when its
759	# raw id is advertised; otherwise the catalog-ranked fallback is explicit.
760	function script:Resolve-CopilotDoctorTarget {
761	    param([string] $ConfiguredMain, [string[]] $RawModel)
762	    $RawModel = @($RawModel | Where-Object { $_ -and $_ -notmatch 'embedding' } | Sort-Object -Unique)
763	    $rawConfigured = Remove-CopilotContextHint $ConfiguredMain
764	    if (-not $rawConfigured) {
765	        return [pscustomobject]@{
766	            Model  = $null
767	            Label  = 'MissingConfiguredMain'
768	            Reason = 'the active project proxy pin has no ANTHROPIC_MODEL'
769	        }
770	    }
771	    if ($RawModel -contains $rawConfigured) {
772	        return [pscustomobject]@{
773	            Model  = $rawConfigured
774	            Label  = 'ConfiguredMain'
775	            Reason = 'configured main is advertised by the live catalog'
776	        }
777	    }
778	
779	    $fallback = Select-CopilotBestModel -Model $RawModel
780	    [pscustomobject]@{
781	        Model  = $fallback
782	        Label  = 'CatalogFallback'
783	        Reason = "configured main '$rawConfigured' is not advertised by the live catalog"
784	    }
785	}

787	function script:ConvertTo-CopilotCompactText {
788	    param($Value, [int] $MaxLength = 320)
789	    $text = if ($Value -is [string]) { $Value } else {
790	        try { $Value | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12 -Compress -ErrorAction Stop } catch { [string]$Value }
791	    }
792	    $text = ($text -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
793	    if ($text.Length -gt $MaxLength) { return $text.Substring(0, $MaxLength - 3) + '...' }
794	    $text
795	}
