250	# Respect CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for both targets, matching Claude Code and claude-hud.
251	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME '.claude' }
252	try { Update-ClaudeSettings -ClaudeDir $claudeDir -OverlayJson $settingsOverlayJson }

254	try { Update-ClaudeHudConfig -ClaudeDir $claudeDir -OverlayJson $hudOverlayJson }
255	catch { Write-Warning "claude-hud overlay skipped; not overwriting: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
256	{{ end -}}

+# Serialize once, validate the candidate, then replace through a same-directory
+# temporary file. Existing normalized bytes are left untouched for idempotence.
+function Write-JsonObjectAtomically {
+    param(
+        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path,
+        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Value,
+        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [bool] $ExpectedExists,
+        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [byte[]] $ExpectedBytes
+    )
+
+    $json = $Value | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 32 -ErrorAction Stop
+    $json = $json.Replace("`r`n", "`n").Replace("`r", "`n").TrimEnd([char[]] "`r`n") + "`n"
+    $null = ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText -Text $json -Label "generated JSON for $Path"
+    $utf8 = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false, $true)
+    [byte[]] $candidate = $utf8.GetBytes($json)
+
+    $currentExists = Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path
+    if ($currentExists -ne $ExpectedExists) {
+        throw "$Path changed while the managed overlay was being prepared"
+    }
+    [byte[]] $current = [byte[]]::new(0)
+    if ($currentExists) {
+        $current = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Path)
+        if ([Convert]::ToBase64String($current) -cne [Convert]::ToBase64String($ExpectedBytes)) {
+            throw "$Path changed while the managed overlay was being prepared"
+        }
+        if ($current.Length -eq $candidate.Length -and
+            [Convert]::ToBase64String($current) -ceq [Convert]::ToBase64String($candidate)) {
+            return $false
+        }
     }
+
+    $directory = Split-Path -Parent $Path
+    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $directory -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
+    $temporary = Join-Path $directory ('.' + [IO.Path]::GetFileName($Path) + '.tmp.' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
+    $backup = "$temporary.backup"
+    try {
+        [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($temporary, $candidate)
+        $null = Read-JsonObject -Path $temporary
+        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path) {
+            # ReplaceFile preserves the destination's Windows metadata (ACLs and
+            # attributes); the non-empty backup path avoids PowerShell binding a
+            # null string as an invalid empty path.
+            [IO.File]::Replace($temporary, $Path, $backup)
+        } else {
+            [IO.File]::Move($temporary, $Path)
+        }
+    } finally {
+        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $temporary -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
+        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $backup -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
+    }
+    $true
 }

2	# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1 — merge managed overlays into

8	# Why merges (not managed files)? Claude Code rewrites settings.json at runtime,
9	# and /claude-hud:configure rewrites the HUD config. Static managed files would
10	# clobber live-only state. Each transaction recursively merges only our owned
11	# leaves and fails closed independently, so one malformed file cannot block the
12	# other or be overwritten.

27	# Parse a JSON string as an object. Arrays/scalars are not valid roots for either
28	# managed surface, because merging them would replace rather than preserve state.
29	function ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText {
30	    param(
31	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Text,
32	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Label
33	    )
34	    try { $value = $Text | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable -ErrorAction Stop }
35	    catch { throw "$Label is invalid JSON: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
36	    if ($value -isnot [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {
37	        throw "$Label root is not a JSON object"
38	    }
39	    $value
40	}
41	
42	# Read strict UTF-8 without normalizing the live bytes first. A single UTF-8 BOM
43	# is accepted for compatibility; successful writes normalize to BOM-free UTF-8.
44	function Read-JsonObject {
45	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path)
46	
47	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return @{} }
48	    [byte[]] $bytes = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Path)
49	    if ($bytes.Length -eq 0) { return @{} }
50	
51	    $offset = 0
52	    if ($bytes.Length -ge 3 -and $bytes[0] -eq 0xEF -and $bytes[1] -eq 0xBB -and $bytes[2] -eq 0xBF) {
53	        $offset = 3
54	    }
55	    try {
56	        $utf8 = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false, $true)
57	        $text = $utf8.GetString($bytes, $offset, $bytes.Length - $offset)
58	    } catch {
59	        throw "$Path is not valid UTF-8: $($_.Exception.Message)"
60	    }
61	    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($text)) { return @{} }
62	    ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText -Text $text -Label $Path
63	}
64	
65	# Recursive object merge: overlay leaves win; live-only/unknown leaves survive.
66	# settings.json opts into its special additive hook merge; HUD config does not.
67	function Merge-JsonObject {
68	    param(
69	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Base,
70	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Overlay,
71	        [switch] $MergeHooks
72	    )
73	    foreach ($key in $Overlay.Keys) {
74	        if ($MergeHooks -and $key -eq 'hooks' -and $Overlay[$key] -is [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {
75	            if ($Base[$key] -isnot [System.Collections.IDictionary]) { $Base[$key] = @{} }
76	            Merge-ClaudeHooks -Base ($Base[$key]) -Overlay ($Overlay[$key])
77	        } elseif ($Base.Contains($key) -and
78	                  $Base[$key] -is [System.Collections.IDictionary] -and
79	                  $Overlay[$key] -is [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {
80	            Merge-JsonObject -Base ($Base[$key]) -Overlay ($Overlay[$key]) -MergeHooks:$MergeHooks
81	        } else {
82	            $Base[$key] = $Overlay[$key]
83	        }
84	    }
85	}
86	
87	# Additive per-event hook merge. Append only entries whose first hook command is
88	# not already present, preserving foreign live entries and forcing array shape.
89	function Merge-ClaudeHooks {
90	    param(
91	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Base,
92	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Overlay
93	    )
94	    foreach ($eventName in $Overlay.Keys) {
95	        $live = @()
96	        if ($null -ne $Base[$eventName]) { $live = @($Base[$eventName]) }
97	        $liveCommands = @($live | ForEach-Object { $_.hooks[0].command })
98	        $additions = @($Overlay[$eventName] | Where-Object {
99	            $command = $_.hooks[0].command
100	            (-not $command) -or ($liveCommands -notcontains $command)
101	        })
102	        $Base[$eventName] = @($live + $additions)
103	    }
104	}

106	# Serialize once, validate the candidate, then replace through a same-directory
107	# temporary file. Existing normalized bytes are left untouched for idempotence.
108	function Write-JsonObjectAtomically {
109	    param(
110	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path,
111	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Value,
112	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [bool] $ExpectedExists,
113	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [byte[]] $ExpectedBytes
114	    )
115	
116	    $json = $Value | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 32 -ErrorAction Stop
117	    $json = $json.Replace("`r`n", "`n").Replace("`r", "`n").TrimEnd([char[]] "`r`n") + "`n"
118	    $null = ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText -Text $json -Label "generated JSON for $Path"
119	    $utf8 = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false, $true)
120	    [byte[]] $candidate = $utf8.GetBytes($json)
121	
122	    $currentExists = Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path
123	    if ($currentExists -ne $ExpectedExists) {
124	        throw "$Path changed while the managed overlay was being prepared"
125	    }
126	    [byte[]] $current = [byte[]]::new(0)
127	    if ($currentExists) {
128	        $current = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Path)
129	        if ([Convert]::ToBase64String($current) -cne [Convert]::ToBase64String($ExpectedBytes)) {
130	            throw "$Path changed while the managed overlay was being prepared"
131	        }
132	        if ($current.Length -eq $candidate.Length -and
133	            [Convert]::ToBase64String($current) -ceq [Convert]::ToBase64String($candidate)) {
134	            return $false
135	        }
136	    }
137	
138	    $directory = Split-Path -Parent $Path
139	    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $directory -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
140	    $temporary = Join-Path $directory ('.' + [IO.Path]::GetFileName($Path) + '.tmp.' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
141	    $backup = "$temporary.backup"
142	    try {
143	        [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($temporary, $candidate)
144	        $null = Read-JsonObject -Path $temporary
145	        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path) {
146	            # ReplaceFile preserves the destination's Windows metadata (ACLs and
147	            # attributes); the non-empty backup path avoids PowerShell binding a
148	            # null string as an invalid empty path.
149	            [IO.File]::Replace($temporary, $Path, $backup)
150	        } else {
151	            [IO.File]::Move($temporary, $Path)
152	        }
153	    } finally {
154	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $temporary -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
155	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $backup -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
156	    }
157	    $true
158	}

187	        else                                      { $soundHooks[$eventName] = @($entry) }
188	    }

```text
1	# Context
2	
3	The current Claude integration enables `claude-hud` and installs a status-line command, but it never manages the plugin’s stable `plugins/claude-hud/config.json`; the machine therefore receives HUD defaults rather than the documented Full display preset. The status-line launcher can also emit errors during the first-launch gap before Claude materializes the plugin cache. Separately, `claude-copilot` promises a hands-off bypass-permissions flow, but its SpecStory zero-argument branch delegates to a create-seeded, user-editable TOML file and can launch plain `claude`. The goal is to make the HUD Full preset deterministic while preserving advanced user settings, and to make the Copilot wrapper enforce its own bypass contract without converting SpecStory’s user config into a fully managed file.
4	
5	## 1. Manage the Claude HUD Full preset as a narrow overlay
6	
7	- Add `claude/hud-full-overlay.json`, embedded into the existing run-onchange script so its content participates in chezmoi’s rendered-script hash (`claude/**` is intentionally ignored as a direct deployment source).
8	- Define and document the owned key set as **“Full as of claude-hud 0.7.1”**, because upstream exposes Full only as prose in `/claude-hud:configure`, not as a JSON Schema or preset constant.
9	- Own only the documented Full leaves:
10	  - core/activity: model, project, added directories, context, tools, skills, MCP, agents, todos;
11	  - information: config counts, token breakdown, usage/reset label, cost, duration, session name/tokens, effort, output style, memory, prompt cache, Claude Code version, compactions, advisor;
12	  - Git: enabled + dirty, with ahead/behind disabled;
13	  - Jujutsu: enabled + dirty/conflicts.
14	- Preserve all advanced and future live keys, including layout/order, colors, thresholds, prompt-cache TTL, routed cost, speed, auth/provider fields, external usage paths, custom text, model/advisor overrides, and unknown nested keys.
15	
16	## 2. Extend and harden the existing Claude JSON merger
17	
18	Modify `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl`; do not add a second run script.
19	
20	- Embed both `claude/settings-overlay.json` and `claude/hud-full-overlay.json` at render time.
21	- Refactor reusable JSON operations into helpers:
22	  - read an absent/blank file as an empty object and reject malformed/non-object JSON;
23	  - recursively merge objects with overlay leaves winning and live-only keys surviving;
24	  - retain the existing special additive/deduplicating `Merge-ClaudeHooks` behavior for `settings.json` only;

7	
8	**FIRST**: Use the Read tool to load `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json` if it exists.

12	## Core Features (on by default)
13	
14	These default to ON and are what most users keep. They ARE configurable
15	(`display.showModel`, `display.showContextBar`), but the guided flow keeps them

20	Advanced settings such as `colors.*`, `pathLevels`, `maxWidth`, `forceMaxWidth`,
21	`elementOrder`, `projectLineOrder`, `display.mergeGroups`, `display.timeFormat`, `display.contextValue`,
22	`display.modelFormat`, `display.modelOverride`, `display.modelSource`, `display.showProvider`,
23	`display.providerName`, `display.autocompactBuffer`,

29	`display.externalUsage*` keys, plus `jjStatus.showDirty` and

31	guided flow.

288	## Git Style Mapping
289	
290	| Option | Config |

294	| Full details | `gitStatus: { enabled: true, showDirty: true, showAheadBehind: true, showFileStats: false }` |
295	| File stats | `gitStatus: { enabled: true, showDirty: true, showAheadBehind: false, showFileStats: true }` |
296	
297	---
298	
299	## Element Mapping
300	
301	| Element | Config Key |
302	|---------|------------|
303	| Model name | `display.showModel` |
304	| Context bar | `display.showContextBar` |
305	| Tools activity | `display.showTools` |
306	| Skills activity | `display.showSkills` |

312	| Git status | `gitStatus.enabled` |
313	| Jujutsu status | `jjStatus.enabled` |
314	| Config counts | `display.showConfigCounts` |
315	| Token breakdown | `display.showTokenBreakdown` |
316	| Output speed | `display.showSpeed` |
317	| Session cost | `display.showCost` |

319	| Usage limits | `display.showUsage` |

324	| Session name | `display.showSessionName` |
325	| Auth method | `display.showAuth` (plan label, e.g. "Claude Max 20x", own segment at end of first line) |
326	| Auth user | `display.showAuthUser` (login account, truncated to `display.authUserLength` chars, 0 = full) |
327	| Session duration | `display.showDuration` |

338	| Custom line | `display.customLine` |
339	| Custom line position | `display.customLinePosition` |
340	
341	**Defaults to ON (configurable booleans, kept enabled by the guided flow):**
342	- `display.showModel` (default `true`)
343	- `display.showContextBar` (default `true`)
344	
345	---
346	
347	## Usage Style Mapping
348	
349	| Option | Config | Example |
350	|--------|--------|---------|
351	| Bar style | `usageBarEnabled: true` | `Usage ██░░ 25% (resets in 1h 30m)` |
352	| Text style | `usageBarEnabled: false` | `Usage 5h 25% (resets in 1h 30m)` |
353	| Compact | `usageCompact: true` | `5h: 25% (1h 30m)` — no "Usage" label, shorter reset format |
354	
355	`usageCompact` takes precedence over `usageBarEnabled` when both are set. Compact mode always uses the text format (no bar).
356	
357	**Note**: Usage style only applies when `display.showUsage: true`. When 7d usage >= 80%, it also shows with the same style.
358	Set `display.usageValue: "remaining"` manually to show remaining quota percentages while keeping warning thresholds based on used quota.
359	
360	---
361	
362	## Processing Logic
363	
364	### For New Users (Flow A):
365	1. Apply chosen preset as base
366	2. Apply chosen language
367	3. Apply Turn Off selections (set those items to OFF)
368	4. Apply Turn On selections (set those items to ON)
369	5. Apply chosen layout
370	
371	### For Returning Users (Flow B):
372	1. Start from current config
373	2. Apply Turn Off selections (set to OFF, including usageBarEnabled if selected)
374	3. Apply Turn On selections (set to ON, including usageBarEnabled if selected)
375	4. Apply Git Style selection (if shown)
376	5. If "Reset to [preset]" selected, override with preset values
377	6. If layout change selected, apply it
378	7. If language change selected, apply it
379	
380	---
381	
382	## Before Writing - Validate & Preview
383	
384	**GUARDS - Do NOT write config if:**
385	- User cancels (Esc) → say "Configuration cancelled."
386	- No changes from current config → say "No changes needed - config unchanged."
387	
388	**Show preview before saving:**
389	
390	1. **Summary of changes:**
391	```
392	Layout: Compact → Expanded
393	Language: English → 中文
394	Git style: Branch + dirty
395	Changes:
396	  - Usage limits: OFF → ON
397	  - Config counts: ON → OFF
398	```
399	
400	2. **Preview of HUD (Expanded layout):**
401	```
402	[Opus | Pro] │ my-project git:(main*)
403	Context ████░░░░░ 45% │ Usage ██░░░░░░░░ 25% (1h 30m / 5h)
404	◐ Edit: file.ts | ✓ Read ×3
405	▸ Fix auth bug (2/5)
406	```
407	
408	**Preview of HUD (Compact layout):**
409	```
410	[Opus | Pro] ████░░░░░ 45% | my-project git:(main*) | 5h: 25% | ⏱️ 5m
411	◐ Edit: file.ts | ✓ Read ×3
412	▸ Fix auth bug (2/5)
413	```
414	
415	3. **Confirm**: "Save these changes?"
416	
417	---
418	
419	## Write Configuration
420	
421	Write to `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json`.
422	
423	Merge with existing config, preserving:
424	- `pathLevels` (not in configure flow)
425	- `display.usageThreshold` (advanced config)
426	- `display.environmentThreshold` (advanced config)
427	- `display.contextWarningThreshold` (advanced config)
428	- `display.contextCriticalThreshold` (advanced config)
429	- `colors` (advanced manual palette overrides)
430	
431	**Migration note**: Old configs with `layout: "default"` or `layout: "separators"` are automatically migrated to the new `lineLayout` + `showSeparators` format on load.
432	
433	---
434	
435	## After Writing
436	
437	Say: "Configuration saved! The HUD will reflect your changes immediately."
438
```

462	  if (!Array.isArray(value) || value.length === 0) {
463	    return [...DEFAULT_ELEMENT_ORDER];
464	  }
465	
466	  const seen = new Set<HudElement>();
467	  const elementOrder: HudElement[] = [];
468	
469	  for (const item of value) {
470	    if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_ELEMENTS.has(item as HudElement)) {
471	      continue;
472	    }
473	
474	    const element = item as HudElement;
475	    if (seen.has(element)) {
476	      continue;
477	    }
478	
479	    seen.add(element);
480	    elementOrder.push(element);
481	  }
482	
483	  return elementOrder.length > 0 ? elementOrder : [...DEFAULT_ELEMENT_ORDER];
484	}
485	
486	// Unlike `elementOrder`, `projectLineOrder` only reorders segments. A partial
487	// list is preserved as a requested prefix; each renderer appends all remaining
488	// visible parts in its own existing order.
489	function validateProjectLineOrder(value: unknown): FirstLineSegment[] {
490	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
491	    return [...DEFAULT_PROJECT_LINE_ORDER];
492	  }
493	
494	  const seen = new Set<FirstLineSegment>();
495	  const order: FirstLineSegment[] = [];
496	
497	  for (const item of value) {
498	    if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_FIRST_LINE_SEGMENTS.has(item as FirstLineSegment)) {
499	      continue;
500	    }
501	
502	    const segment = item as FirstLineSegment;
503	    if (seen.has(segment)) {
504	      continue;
505	    }
506	
507	    seen.add(segment);
508	    order.push(segment);
509	  }
510	
511	  return order;
512	}
513	
514	function validateRightAlign(value: unknown): HudElement[] {
515	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
516	    return [...DEFAULT_CONFIG.display.rightAlign];
517	  }
518	
519	  const seen = new Set<HudElement>();
520	  const elements: HudElement[] = [];
521	
522	  for (const item of value) {
523	    if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_ELEMENTS.has(item as HudElement)) {
524	      continue;
525	    }
526	
527	    const element = item as HudElement;
528	    if (seen.has(element)) {
529	      continue;
530	    }
531	
532	    seen.add(element);
533	    elements.push(element);
534	  }
535	
536	  return elements;
537	}
538	
539	function validateMergeGroups(value: unknown): HudElement[][] {
540	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
541	    return DEFAULT_MERGE_GROUPS.map(group => [...group]);
542	  }
543	
544	  if (value.length === 0) {
545	    return [];
546	  }
547	
548	  const usedElements = new Set<HudElement>();
549	  const mergeGroups: HudElement[][] = [];
550	
551	  for (const group of value) {
552	    if (!Array.isArray(group)) {
553	      continue;
554	    }
555	
556	    const seenInGroup = new Set<HudElement>();
557	    const normalizedGroup: HudElement[] = [];
558	    const pendingElements: HudElement[] = [];
559	
560	    for (const item of group) {
561	      if (typeof item !== 'string' || !KNOWN_ELEMENTS.has(item as HudElement)) {
562	        continue;
563	      }
564	
565	      const element = item as HudElement;
566	      if (seenInGroup.has(element) || usedElements.has(element)) {
567	        continue;
568	      }
569	
570	      seenInGroup.add(element);
571	      normalizedGroup.push(element);
572	      pendingElements.push(element);
573	    }
574	
575	    if (normalizedGroup.length >= 2) {
576	      for (const element of pendingElements) {
577	        usedElements.add(element);
578	      }
579	      mergeGroups.push(normalizedGroup);
580	    }
581	  }
582	
583	  return mergeGroups.length > 0
584	    ? mergeGroups
585	    : DEFAULT_MERGE_GROUPS.map(group => [...group]);
586	}

590	}

592	function migrateConfig(userConfig: Partial<HudConfig> & LegacyConfig): Partial<HudConfig> {
593	  const migrated = { ...userConfig } as Partial<HudConfig> & LegacyConfig;
594	
595	  if ('layout' in userConfig && !('lineLayout' in userConfig)) {
596	    if (typeof userConfig.layout === 'string') {
597	      // Legacy string migration (v0.0.x → v0.1.x)
598	      if (userConfig.layout === 'separators') {
599	        migrated.lineLayout = 'compact';
600	        migrated.showSeparators = true;
601	      } else {
602	        migrated.lineLayout = 'compact';
603	        migrated.showSeparators = false;
604	      }
605	    } else if (typeof userConfig.layout === 'object' && userConfig.layout !== null) {
606	      // Object layout written by third-party tools — extract nested fields
607	      const obj = userConfig.layout as Record<string, unknown>;
608	      if (typeof obj.lineLayout === 'string') migrated.lineLayout = obj.lineLayout as any;
609	      if (typeof obj.showSeparators === 'boolean') migrated.showSeparators = obj.showSeparators;
610	      if (typeof obj.pathLevels === 'number' || obj.pathLevels === 'full') migrated.pathLevels = obj.pathLevels as any;
611	    }
612	    delete migrated.layout;
613	  }
614	
615	  return migrated;

618	function validateThreshold(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
619	  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) return fallback;
620	  return Math.max(0, Math.min(100, value));

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **chezmoi's `scripts/redact_secrets.py`** — remains the upstream
  source of truth. The skill bundles a copy so non-chezmoi users get
  protection; sync procedure in
  [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`).
2. Writes `scripts/redact_secrets.py` (bundled copy; use
   `--from-chezmoi` to symlink the chezmoi source so fixes propagate).
3. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
4. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
5. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
6. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` + the redactor
  into the current repo, then run `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — bundled copy of chezmoi's
  `scripts/redact_secrets.py`. Chezmoi version is upstream; sync doc
  in `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read
  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.
- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.

## Tests

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
regression the suite locks in.

359	+    {{- if $peon }}

363	+        $entry = @{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $peonCommand; timeout = 10 }) }
364	+        if ($soundHooks.ContainsKey($eventName)) { $soundHooks[$eventName] = @($soundHooks[$eventName] + $entry) }
365	+        else                                      { $soundHooks[$eventName] = @($entry) }
366	     }
367	+    {{- end }}
368	+    if ($soundHooks.Count -gt 0) {
369	+        if ($overlay['hooks'] -isnot [System.Collections.IDictionary]) { $overlay['hooks'] = @{} }
370	+        foreach ($eventName in $soundHooks.Keys) { $overlay['hooks'][$eventName] = $soundHooks[$eventName] }
371	+    }

373	+    # Prune only repository-owned hooks disabled by the current sound tier.

The baseline body is `.chezmoitemplates/git/gitconfig` (identity from the existing `.name`/`.email` init prompts); the merge engine is `scripts/gitconfig-merge.ps1`, inlined via `{{ include }}` (the `editors/` idiom) and dot-sourced by `tests/GitConfig.Tests.ps1`. The model is **key-level pull-through**: the baseline owns a fixed set of `section.key` pairs and every other live key is carried over untouched — the inverse of the parent repo's allowlist, which would silently drop `[otel]` and future corp sections. Two hard rules: `core.hooksPath` is **never** emitted (git honours it *instead of* `.git/hooks/`, silently disarming `pre-commit`), and the carry dictionary is **case-sensitive** (`[ordered]@{}` collapses `azrepos:org/O365Exchange` into `azrepos:org/o365exchange`, merging two credential contexts).

11	# leaves and fails closed independently, so one malformed file cannot block the

27	# Parse a JSON string as an object. Arrays/scalars are not valid roots for either
28	# managed surface, because merging them would replace rather than preserve state.
29	function ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText {
30	    param(
31	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Text,
32	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Label
33	    )
34	    try { $value = $Text | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable -ErrorAction Stop }
35	    catch { throw "$Label is invalid JSON: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
36	    if ($value -isnot [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {
37	        throw "$Label root is not a JSON object"
38	    }
39	    $value
40	}
41	
42	# Read strict UTF-8 without normalizing the live bytes first. A single UTF-8 BOM
43	# is accepted for compatibility; successful writes normalize to BOM-free UTF-8.
44	function Read-JsonObject {
45	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path)
46	
47	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return @{} }
48	    [byte[]] $bytes = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Path)
49	    if ($bytes.Length -eq 0) { return @{} }
50	
51	    $offset = 0
52	    if ($bytes.Length -ge 3 -and $bytes[0] -eq 0xEF -and $bytes[1] -eq 0xBB -and $bytes[2] -eq 0xBF) {
53	        $offset = 3
54	    }
55	    try {
56	        $utf8 = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false, $true)
57	        $text = $utf8.GetString($bytes, $offset, $bytes.Length - $offset)
58	    } catch {
59	        throw "$Path is not valid UTF-8: $($_.Exception.Message)"
60	    }
61	    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($text)) { return @{} }
62	    ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText -Text $text -Label $Path
63	}

65	# Recursive object merge: overlay leaves win; live-only/unknown leaves survive.
66	# settings.json opts into its special additive hook merge; HUD config does not.
67	function Merge-JsonObject {
68	    param(
69	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Base,
70	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Overlay,
71	        [switch] $MergeHooks
72	    )
73	    foreach ($key in $Overlay.Keys) {
74	        if ($MergeHooks -and $key -eq 'hooks' -and $Overlay[$key] -is [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {
75	            if ($Base[$key] -isnot [System.Collections.IDictionary]) { $Base[$key] = @{} }
76	            Merge-ClaudeHooks -Base ($Base[$key]) -Overlay ($Overlay[$key])
77	        } elseif ($Base.Contains($key) -and
78	                  $Base[$key] -is [System.Collections.IDictionary] -and
79	                  $Overlay[$key] -is [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {
80	            Merge-JsonObject -Base ($Base[$key]) -Overlay ($Overlay[$key]) -MergeHooks:$MergeHooks
81	        } else {
82	            $Base[$key] = $Overlay[$key]
83	        }
84	    }
85	}

87	# Additive per-event hook merge. Append only entries whose first hook command is
88	# not already present, preserving foreign live entries and forcing array shape.
89	function Merge-ClaudeHooks {
90	    param(
91	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Base,
92	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Overlay
93	    )
94	    foreach ($eventName in $Overlay.Keys) {
95	        $live = @()
96	        if ($null -ne $Base[$eventName]) { $live = @($Base[$eventName]) }
97	        $liveCommands = @($live | ForEach-Object { $_.hooks[0].command })
98	        $additions = @($Overlay[$eventName] | Where-Object {
99	            $command = $_.hooks[0].command
100	            (-not $command) -or ($liveCommands -notcontains $command)
101	        })
102	        $Base[$eventName] = @($live + $additions)
103	    }
104	}

106	# Serialize once, validate the candidate, then replace through a same-directory
107	# temporary file. Existing normalized bytes are left untouched for idempotence.
108	function Write-JsonObjectAtomically {
109	    param(
110	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path,
111	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Value,
112	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [bool] $ExpectedExists,
113	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [byte[]] $ExpectedBytes
114	    )
115	
116	    $json = $Value | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 32 -ErrorAction Stop
117	    $json = $json.Replace("`r`n", "`n").Replace("`r", "`n").TrimEnd([char[]] "`r`n") + "`n"
118	    $null = ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText -Text $json -Label "generated JSON for $Path"
119	    $utf8 = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false, $true)
120	    [byte[]] $candidate = $utf8.GetBytes($json)
121	
122	    $currentExists = Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path
123	    if ($currentExists -ne $ExpectedExists) {
124	        throw "$Path changed while the managed overlay was being prepared"
125	    }
126	    [byte[]] $current = [byte[]]::new(0)
127	    if ($currentExists) {
128	        $current = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Path)
129	        if ([Convert]::ToBase64String($current) -cne [Convert]::ToBase64String($ExpectedBytes)) {
130	            throw "$Path changed while the managed overlay was being prepared"
131	        }
132	        if ($current.Length -eq $candidate.Length -and
133	            [Convert]::ToBase64String($current) -ceq [Convert]::ToBase64String($candidate)) {
134	            return $false
135	        }
136	    }
137	
138	    $directory = Split-Path -Parent $Path
139	    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $directory -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
140	    $temporary = Join-Path $directory ('.' + [IO.Path]::GetFileName($Path) + '.tmp.' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
141	    $backup = "$temporary.backup"
142	    try {
143	        [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($temporary, $candidate)
144	        $null = Read-JsonObject -Path $temporary
145	        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path) {
146	            # ReplaceFile preserves the destination's Windows metadata (ACLs and
147	            # attributes); the non-empty backup path avoids PowerShell binding a
148	            # null string as an invalid empty path.
149	            [IO.File]::Replace($temporary, $Path, $backup)
150	        } else {
151	            [IO.File]::Move($temporary, $Path)
152	        }
153	    } finally {
154	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $temporary -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
155	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $backup -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
156	    }
157	    $true
158	}

188	    }

1	# Context
2	
3	The current Claude integration enables `claude-hud` and installs a status-line command, but it never manages the plugin’s stable `plugins/claude-hud/config.json`; the machine therefore receives HUD defaults rather than the documented Full display preset. The status-line launcher can also emit errors during the first-launch gap before Claude materializes the plugin cache. Separately, `claude-copilot` promises a hands-off bypass-permissions flow, but its SpecStory zero-argument branch delegates to a create-seeded, user-editable TOML file and can launch plain `claude`. The goal is to make the HUD Full preset deterministic while preserving advanced user settings, and to make the Copilot wrapper enforce its own bypass contract without converting SpecStory’s user config into a fully managed file.
4	
5	## 1. Manage the Claude HUD Full preset as a narrow overlay
6	
7	- Add `claude/hud-full-overlay.json`, embedded into the existing run-onchange script so its content participates in chezmoi’s rendered-script hash (`claude/**` is intentionally ignored as a direct deployment source).
8	- Define and document the owned key set as **“Full as of claude-hud 0.7.1”**, because upstream exposes Full only as prose in `/claude-hud:configure`, not as a JSON Schema or preset constant.
9	- Own only the documented Full leaves:
10	  - core/activity: model, project, added directories, context, tools, skills, MCP, agents, todos;
11	  - information: config counts, token breakdown, usage/reset label, cost, duration, session name/tokens, effort, output style, memory, prompt cache, Claude Code version, compactions, advisor;
12	  - Git: enabled + dirty, with ahead/behind disabled;
13	  - Jujutsu: enabled + dirty/conflicts.
14	- Preserve all advanced and future live keys, including layout/order, colors, thresholds, prompt-cache TTL, routed cost, speed, auth/provider fields, external usage paths, custom text, model/advisor overrides, and unknown nested keys.
15	
16	## 2. Extend and harden the existing Claude JSON merger
17	
18	Modify `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl`; do not add a second run script.
19	
20	- Embed both `claude/settings-overlay.json` and `claude/hud-full-overlay.json` at render time.
21	- Refactor reusable JSON operations into helpers:
22	  - read an absent/blank file as an empty object and reject malformed/non-object JSON;
23	  - recursively merge objects with overlay leaves winning and live-only keys surviving;
24	  - retain the existing special additive/deduplicating `Merge-ClaudeHooks` behavior for `settings.json` only;
25	  - serialize, parse-validate, and atomically replace through a same-directory temporary file using BOM-free UTF-8; avoid rewriting when bytes are already normalized.
26	- Process two independent transactions under separate `try/catch` blocks:
27	  1. `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json`, including sound-hook creation/pruning;
28	  2. `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/plugins/claude-hud/config.json`, using ordinary recursive merge.
29	- Fail closed per target: malformed settings must remain byte-for-byte untouched while HUD still updates, and malformed HUD config must not block settings. Warnings remain nonfatal so chezmoi apply never aborts.
30	- Harden both JSON targets with the shared atomic writer rather than leaving the existing direct `Set-Content` path for settings.
31	
32	## 3. Make the status-line launcher safe during plugin bootstrap
33	
34	Update `claude/settings-overlay.json` while retaining its Git Bash/Cygwin, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, semantic-version cache selection, width fallback, and Node behavior.
35	
36	- Silence the whole `/dev/tty`/`stty` probe when no controlling TTY exists.
37	- Resolve Node and the newest cached `claude-hud/dist/index.js` first.
38	- Exit successfully with no output when Node, the cache directory, or `dist/index.js` is missing.
39	- Execute Node only after all prerequisites are present. This turns the first-launch cache race into a temporary blank status line instead of a module-not-found error.
40	
41	## 4. Keep SpecStory config user-owned and harden the wrapper
42	
43	Modify `dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1`; leave `private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml` and project `.specstory/cli/config.toml` unchanged.
44	
45	- Reuse `Get-SpecstoryClaudeCmd` for project → user → `claude` precedence and `ConvertTo-CopilotShQuote` for every appended argument.
46	- Add one private pure command builder that:

144572	
144573	## Which Surface Should I Use?
144574	
144575	> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases — only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.
144576	
144577	| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
144578	| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
144579	| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
144580	| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
144581	| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
144582	| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
144583	| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
144584	| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
144585	| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
144586	| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** — scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |
144587	
144588	> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute — file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice — use the tool runner for the agentic loop — its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) — or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.
144589	
144590	> **Cloud-provider access.** **Claude Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity — see `shared/claude-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Claude Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` — that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.
144591	
144592	### Building an Agent: Four Approaches
144593	
144594	Once you've decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Claude Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* — you still host and deploy them yourself — which is why they're easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.
144595	
144596	| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |
144597	|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|
144598	| 1 | **Claude API — manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop — no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner's per-turn hooks don't fit |
144599	| 2 | **Claude API — Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, error interception, result modification (e.g. `cache_control`), retries, streaming, and compaction |
144600	| 3 | **Managed Agents** (REST, beta) | Agent config + your tool results | Anthropic supplies the harness **and** hosts a per-session sandbox (**harness + deployment**) | Anthropic-hosted sandbox (bash, files, code exec) + Skills/MCP + your tools | You want Anthropic to run the loop *and* host the per-session workspace; persisted/versioned configs; long-running sessions |
144601	| 4 | **Claude Agent SDK** — *separate product* (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) | A prompt + options | SDK supplies the Claude Code harness + built-in tools (**harness only**); you host | Built-in Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch + MCP + subagents | You want a batteries-included coding/filesystem agent running on your own infra |
144602	
144603	The harness/deployment split is the key mental model: options 1, 2, and 4 all **leave deployment to you**; only option 3 (CMA) adds managed deployment. Options 1–3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs — see the disambiguation below.
144604	
144605	> **Tool Runner ≠ Claude Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:
144606	> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. It automates the request → execute → loop cycle *for tools you define*. No built-in tools, no filesystem access, no sandbox — you supply every tool and host the compute. It is option 2 above, a thin helper over `POST /v1/messages`.
144607	> - **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) is Claude Code packaged as a library. It ships built-in tools (file read/write/edit, bash, grep, web search), the full agent loop, context management, hooks, subagents, permissions, and sessions. You call `query(prompt, options)` and it drives everything.
144608	>
144609	> Both are **harness-only — you host and deploy them.** The difference is scope of harness: the Tool Runner loops over tools *you* define (with per-turn hooks for approval, interception, result modification, and retries — but no built-in tools); the Agent SDK is the full Claude Code harness with built-in tools. Neither provides managed deployment — that's what **Managed Agents (CMA)** adds (Anthropic hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox).
144610	>
144611	> **This skill covers the Claude API and Managed Agents (options 1–3); it does not generate Claude Agent SDK code.** If the user actually wants the Claude Agent SDK, point them to its docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk`) — don't substitute the API Tool Runner for it, or vice-versa.
144612	
144613	### Should I Build an Agent?
144614	
144615	Before choosing the agent tier, check all four criteria:
144616	
144617	- **Complexity** — Is the task multi-step and hard to fully specify in advance? (e.g., "turn this design doc into a PR" vs. "extract the title from this PDF")
144618	- **Value** — Does the outcome justify higher cost and latency?
144619	- **Viability** — Is Claude capable at this task type?
144620	- **Cost of error** — Can errors be caught and recovered from? (tests, review, rollback)
144621	
144622	If the answer is "no" to any of these, stay at a simpler tier (single call or workflow).
144623

144625	
144626	## Architecture
144627	
144628	Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint — not separate APIs.
144629	
144630	**User-defined tools** — You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.
144631	
144632	**Server-side tools** — Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.
144633	
144634	**Structured outputs** — Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and/or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.
144635	
144636	**Supporting endpoints** — Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` — see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` — live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.
