         '-c', 'model_providers.copilot_api.requires_openai_auth=true',
         '-c', 'model_providers.copilot_api.supports_websockets=false',
         '-c', 'model_providers.copilot_api.wire_api="responses"',
         '-c', 'model_providers.copilot_api.request_max_retries=3',
         '-c', 'model_providers.copilot_api.stream_max_retries=1',
         '-c', 'model_providers.copilot_api.stream_idle_timeout_ms=300000',
         '-c', 'features.remote_compaction_v2=true',
         '-c', 'features.code_mode.excluded_tool_namespaces=["mcp__codex_apps__sites"]'
     )
     if ($model) {
         $entry = $catalog.data | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $model } | Select-Object -First 1
         if ($entry.capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens) {
             $Argv = @('-c', "model_context_window=$($entry.capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens)") + @($Argv)
         }
         if ($entry.capabilities.limits.max_prompt_tokens) {
             $Argv = @('-c', "model_auto_compact_token_limit=$($entry.capabilities.limits.max_prompt_tokens)") + @($Argv)
         }
     }
 
     $savedKey = $env:GITHUB_COPILOT_API_KEY
     $env:GITHUB_COPILOT_API_KEY = 'dummy'
     try {
         if ($ss -eq 'auto' -and (Get-Command specstory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
             $cc = Get-SpecstoryCodexCmd
             foreach ($a in @($providerArgs) + @($Argv)) { $cc = "$cc $(ConvertTo-CopilotShQuote $a)" }
             specstory run codex -c $cc
         } else { codex @providerArgs @Argv }
     } finally {
         if ($null -eq $savedKey) { Remove-Item env:GITHUB_COPILOT_API_KEY -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
         else { $env:GITHUB_COPILOT_API_KEY = $savedKey }
     }
 }
 
 function codex-copilot-once {
     [CmdletBinding()]
     param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
     codex-copilot @Argv
 }
 
-# --- specstory `-c` passthrough (why the base command must come from config) ---
+# --- specstory `-c` passthrough (configured base + wrapper policy) -----------
 #
 # specstory's `-c/--command` REPLACES the provider's configured command — it does
-# NOT append to it. The shipped config says as much: "Use of these is equivalent
-# to -c \"custom command\"" — same slot, last write wins. So a hardcoded
-# `-c "claude $args"` silently drops every flag in `claude_cmd` the moment
-# claude-copilot has args to pass through, which made these two disagree:
-#
-#   claude-copilot-once             -> bypass-permissions  (no -c branch)
-#   claude-copilot-once --resume X  -> ~/.claude defaultMode "auto"
-#
-# Deriving the base command from the config keeps specstory the single source of
-# truth for BOTH branches. `--no-specstory` deliberately does NOT inherit it.
+# NOT append to it. Build the complete command from the effective `claude_cmd`,
+# then enforce claude-copilot's own bypass-permissions contract and append each
+# user argument with shell-safe quoting. This keeps configured wrapper flags while
+# making zero-argument and argument-bearing sessions behave identically.
+# `--no-specstory` deliberately does not inherit the configured base command.
 
 # Effective `claude_cmd`, honouring specstory's own precedence:
 #   project ./.specstory/cli/config.toml > user ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml > `claude`
 # Matches UNCOMMENTED assignments only — both shipped configs carry a commented
 # `# claude_cmd = "claude"` example, and matching that would re-introduce the very
 # bug this exists to fix. Handles TOML's double- and single-quoted strings.
 function script:Get-SpecstoryClaudeCmd {
     foreach ($f in '.specstory/cli/config.toml', (Join-Path $HOME '.specstory/cli/config.toml')) {
         if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $f)) { continue }
         foreach ($line in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $f -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
-            if ($line -match '^\s*claude_cmd\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|''([^'']*)'')') {
-                $v = if ($Matches[1]) { $Matches[1] } else { $Matches[2] }
-                if ($v) { return $v }
+            if ($line -notmatch '^\s*claude_cmd\s*=\s*("(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|''[^'']*'')\s*(?:#.*)?$') { continue }
+            $raw = $Matches[1]
+            if ($raw[0] -eq '"') {
+                try { $value = $raw | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop }
+                catch { continue }
+            } else {
+                $value = $raw.Substring(1, $raw.Length - 2)
             }
+            if ($value) { return $value }
         }
     }
     'claude'
 }
 
 # Single-quote ONE argument for embedding in specstory's `-c` command STRING.
 # specstory shell-splits that string honouring quotes, so quoting is both possible
 # and necessary — an unquoted join flattens `-p "two words"` into two arguments.
 # POSIX escape for an embedded quote: close, \', reopen.
 function script:ConvertTo-CopilotShQuote {
     param([string] $Value)
     "'" + ($Value -replace "'", "'\''") + "'"
 }
 
+# Build the complete command string passed to `specstory run claude -c`.
+# Recognize the normal unquoted/fully quoted bypass token without pretending to
+# parse arbitrary shell syntax. Exact duplicate wrapper arguments are suppressed;
+# every other argument keeps its original order and multiplicity.
+function script:New-SpecstoryClaudeCommand {
+    param([string[]] $Argv)
+
+    $bypass = '--dangerously-skip-permissions'
+    $command = (Get-SpecstoryClaudeCmd).Trim()
+    $escaped = [regex]::Escape($bypass)
+    $hasBypass = $command -cmatch "(?:^|\s)(?:$escaped|'$escaped'|`"$escaped`")(?=\s|$)"
+    if (-not $hasBypass) { $command = "$command $bypass" }
+    if ($null -ne $Argv) {
+        foreach ($argument in $Argv) {
+            if ($argument -ceq $bypass) { continue }
+            $command = "$command $(ConvertTo-CopilotShQuote $argument)"
+        }
+    }
+    $command
+}
+
 # --------------------------------------------------------- claude-copilot -----
 function claude-copilot {
     [CmdletBinding()]
     param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
     $ss = 'auto'
-    if ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -eq '--no-specstory') { $ss = 'never'; $Argv = $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)] }
-    elseif ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -eq '--specstory') { $Argv = $Argv[1..($Argv.Count - 1)] }
+    if ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -eq '--no-specstory') { $ss = 'never'; $Argv = @($Argv | Select-Object -Skip 1) }
+    elseif ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -eq '--specstory') { $Argv = @($Argv | Select-Object -Skip 1) }
     elseif ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -in '-h', '--help') {
         Write-Host "Usage: claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [claude args...]"
         Write-Host "  One-off Claude Code session on the Copilot proxy. Sticky: copilot-here on"
         Write-Host "  Runs claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions (hands-off proxy flow)."
         return
     }
     if ($ss -eq 'auto' -and (Get-Command specstory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
-        if ($Argv -and $Argv.Count -gt 0) {
-            # Rebuild what `-c` clobbers: the configured base command (ITS flags left
-            # unquoted so specstory splits them normally) + each of our args quoted.
-            $cc = Get-SpecstoryClaudeCmd
-            foreach ($a in $Argv) { $cc = "$cc $(ConvertTo-CopilotShQuote $a)" }
-            copilot-run specstory run claude -c $cc
-        }
-        else { copilot-run specstory run claude }
+        $command = New-SpecstoryClaudeCommand -Argv $Argv
+        copilot-run specstory run claude -c $command
     } else {
         # No specstory on PATH (the Windows default — no native CLI yet): run claude
         # directly, still bypassing permission prompts so behaviour matches the
         # specstory path regardless of whether specstory is installed.
         copilot-run claude --dangerously-skip-permissions @Argv
     }
 }
 
 # --------------------------------------------------- claude-copilot-once ------
 function claude-copilot-once {
     [CmdletBinding()]
     param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
     if ($Argv -and $Argv[0] -in '-h', '--help') {
         Write-Host "Usage: claude-copilot-once [--no-specstory] [claude args...]"
         Write-Host "  Pin this project to the proxy, run one session, auto-unpin (even on Ctrl-C)."
         return
     }
     if (-not (Test-CopilotAlive)) {
         Write-Error "claude-copilot-once: proxy not reachable on port $(Get-CopilotPort). Start it: copilot-proxy start"; return
     }
     $wasOn = $false
     if (Test-Path '.claude/settings.local.json') {
         try { if ((Get-Content -Raw '.claude/settings.local.json' | ConvertFrom-Json).env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) { $wasOn = $true } } catch { $null = $_ }
     }
     if (-not $wasOn) { copilot-here on }
     else {
         # Already pinned here. If the pin drifted from current defaults (model bump,
         # proxy moved, a key added since), offer to refresh it in place; otherwise
         # leave it untouched. Either way it was already ON, so it stays ON on exit.
         $drift = Get-CopilotHereDrift
         if ($drift) {
             Write-Host "claude-copilot-once: this project's copilot-here pin looks stale:"
             $drift | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
             if (Confirm-CopilotAction '  override with current defaults? (keep = default) [y/N]') { copilot-here on }
             else { Write-Host 'claude-copilot-once: kept the existing pin (stays ON on exit).' }
         } else {
             Write-Host "claude-copilot-once: copilot-here already ON here — leaving the pin in place on exit."
         }
     }
     try {
         claude-copilot @Argv
     } finally {
         if (-not $wasOn) { copilot-here off }
         Write-Host "claude-copilot-once: session ended. Proxy still running on $(Get-CopilotBase)."
     }
 }
 
 # ------------------------------------------------------------ copilot-here ----
 $script:CopilotHereKeys = @(
     'ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL', 'ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN', 'ANTHROPIC_MODEL', 'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL', 'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL',
     'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL', 'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL', 'ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL',
     'CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC', 'CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER',
     'CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION', 'CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY', 'DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS'
 )
 
 # y/N prompt. Returns $true only on an explicit yes; a non-interactive host
 # returns $false — the safe default (keep, don't override). Only called right
 # before launching an interactive Claude Code session, so reading input is fine.
 function script:Confirm-CopilotAction {
     param([string] $Message = 'Proceed? [y/N]')
     if (-not [Environment]::UserInteractive -or [Console]::IsInputRedirected) { return $false }
     $ans = Read-Host -Prompt $Message
     $ans -match '^\s*y(es)?\s*$'
 }
 
 # Has THIS project's copilot-here pin drifted from what `copilot-here on` would
 # write now (default model bumped, proxy moved, a key added since the pin was
 # written)? Returns one "  KEY : old -> new" line per drifted key, or nothing.
 #
 # Drift is defined as "the set of keys `copilot-here on` would actually CHANGE",
 # computed by diffing the live file against Get-CopilotEnvBlock — not a hand-picked
 # subset (that is how three keys silently went unchecked). The asymmetry is
 # deliberate: keys present in the file but absent from the want-set are NOT drift,
 # because `on` merges and never removes them (only `off` does).
 function script:Get-CopilotHereDrift {
     $settings = '.claude/settings.local.json'
     if (-not (Test-Path $settings)) { return @() }
     try { $obj = Get-Content -Raw $settings | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { return @() }
     # ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is only set while the pin is ON — absent -> nothing to do.
     if (-not $obj.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) { return @() }

```text
1	#Requires -Version 7
2	# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1 — merge managed overlays into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json.
4	# Companion to the parent (macOS/Linux) repo's dot_claude/modify_settings.json;
5	# that repo uses a `modify_` + jq merge, which is unreliable on Windows
6	# (invariant #5), so we use the editor-overlay run_onchange pwsh idiom instead.
7	#
8	# Why merges (not managed files)? Claude Code rewrites settings.json at runtime,
9	# and /claude-hud:configure rewrites the HUD config. Static managed files would
10	# clobber live-only state. Each transaction recursively merges only our owned
11	# leaves and fails closed independently, so one malformed file cannot block the
12	# other or be overwritten.
13	#
14	# Gated on installCodingAgents. Re-runs when either embedded overlay changes.
15	{{ if .installCodingAgents -}}
16	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'   # best-effort; never abort the apply
17	
18	# Embedded from chezmoi-ignored claude/ sources. Embedding makes this script
19	# self-contained and includes both overlays in the run_onchange content hash.
20	$settingsOverlayJson = @'
21	{{ include "claude/settings-overlay.json" }}
22	'@
23	$hudOverlayJson = @'
24	{{ include "claude/hud-full-overlay.json" }}
25	'@
26	
27	# Parse a JSON string as an object. Arrays/scalars are not valid roots for either
28	# managed surface, because merging them would replace rather than preserve state.
29	function ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText {
30	    param(
31	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Text,
32	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Label
33	    )
34	    try { $value = $Text | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable -ErrorAction Stop }
35	    catch { throw "$Label is invalid JSON: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
36	    if ($value -isnot [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {
37	        throw "$Label root is not a JSON object"
38	    }
39	    $value
40	}
41	
42	# Read strict UTF-8 without normalizing the live bytes first. A single UTF-8 BOM
43	# is accepted for compatibility; successful writes normalize to BOM-free UTF-8.
44	function Read-JsonObject {
45	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path)
46	
47	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return @{} }
48	    [byte[]] $bytes = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Path)
49	    if ($bytes.Length -eq 0) { return @{} }
50	
51	    $offset = 0
52	    if ($bytes.Length -ge 3 -and $bytes[0] -eq 0xEF -and $bytes[1] -eq 0xBB -and $bytes[2] -eq 0xBF) {
53	        $offset = 3
54	    }
55	    try {
56	        $utf8 = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false, $true)
57	        $text = $utf8.GetString($bytes, $offset, $bytes.Length - $offset)
58	    } catch {
59	        throw "$Path is not valid UTF-8: $($_.Exception.Message)"
60	    }
61	    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($text)) { return @{} }
62	    ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText -Text $text -Label $Path
63	}
64	
65	# Recursive object merge: overlay leaves win; live-only/unknown leaves survive.
66	# settings.json opts into its special additive hook merge; HUD config does not.
67	function Merge-JsonObject {
68	    param(
69	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Base,
70	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Overlay,
71	        [switch] $MergeHooks
72	    )
73	    foreach ($key in $Overlay.Keys) {
74	        if ($MergeHooks -and $key -eq 'hooks' -and $Overlay[$key] -is [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {
75	            if ($Base[$key] -isnot [System.Collections.IDictionary]) { $Base[$key] = @{} }
76	            Merge-ClaudeHooks -Base ($Base[$key]) -Overlay ($Overlay[$key])
77	        } elseif ($Base.Contains($key) -and
78	                  $Base[$key] -is [System.Collections.IDictionary] -and
79	                  $Overlay[$key] -is [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {
80	            Merge-JsonObject -Base ($Base[$key]) -Overlay ($Overlay[$key]) -MergeHooks:$MergeHooks
81	        } else {
82	            $Base[$key] = $Overlay[$key]
83	        }
84	    }
85	}
86	
87	# Additive per-event hook merge. Append only entries whose first hook command is
88	# not already present, preserving foreign live entries and forcing array shape.
89	function Merge-ClaudeHooks {
90	    param(
91	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Base,
92	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Overlay
93	    )
94	    foreach ($eventName in $Overlay.Keys) {
95	        $live = @()
96	        if ($null -ne $Base[$eventName]) { $live = @($Base[$eventName]) }
97	        $liveCommands = @($live | ForEach-Object { $_.hooks[0].command })
98	        $additions = @($Overlay[$eventName] | Where-Object {
99	            $command = $_.hooks[0].command
100	            (-not $command) -or ($liveCommands -notcontains $command)
101	        })
102	        $Base[$eventName] = @($live + $additions)

106	# Serialize once, validate the candidate, then replace through a same-directory
107	# temporary file. Existing normalized bytes are left untouched for idempotence.
108	function Write-JsonObjectAtomically {
109	    param(
110	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path,
111	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.IDictionary] $Value,
112	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [bool] $ExpectedExists,
113	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [byte[]] $ExpectedBytes
114	    )
115	
116	    $json = $Value | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 32 -ErrorAction Stop
117	    $json = $json.Replace("`r`n", "`n").Replace("`r", "`n").TrimEnd([char[]] "`r`n") + "`n"
118	    $null = ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText -Text $json -Label "generated JSON for $Path"
119	    $utf8 = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false, $true)
120	    [byte[]] $candidate = $utf8.GetBytes($json)
121	
122	    $currentExists = Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path
123	    if ($currentExists -ne $ExpectedExists) {
124	        throw "$Path changed while the managed overlay was being prepared"
125	    }
126	    [byte[]] $current = [byte[]]::new(0)
127	    if ($currentExists) {
128	        $current = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Path)
129	        if ([Convert]::ToBase64String($current) -cne [Convert]::ToBase64String($ExpectedBytes)) {
130	            throw "$Path changed while the managed overlay was being prepared"
131	        }
132	        if ($current.Length -eq $candidate.Length -and
133	            [Convert]::ToBase64String($current) -ceq [Convert]::ToBase64String($candidate)) {
134	            return $false
135	        }
136	    }
137	
138	    $directory = Split-Path -Parent $Path
139	    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $directory -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
140	    $temporary = Join-Path $directory ('.' + [IO.Path]::GetFileName($Path) + '.tmp.' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
141	    $backup = "$temporary.backup"
142	    try {
143	        [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($temporary, $candidate)
144	        $null = Read-JsonObject -Path $temporary
145	        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path) {
146	            # ReplaceFile preserves the destination's Windows metadata (ACLs and
147	            # attributes); the non-empty backup path avoids PowerShell binding a
148	            # null string as an invalid empty path.
149	            [IO.File]::Replace($temporary, $Path, $backup)
150	        } else {
151	            [IO.File]::Move($temporary, $Path)
152	        }
153	    } finally {
154	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $temporary -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
155	        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $backup -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
156	    }
157	    $true
158	}

160	function Update-ClaudeSettings {
161	    param(
162	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $ClaudeDir,
163	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $OverlayJson
164	    )
165	
166	    $overlay = ConvertFrom-JsonObjectText -Text $OverlayJson -Label 'managed Claude settings overlay'
167	
168	    # Completion-feedback hooks are built here because the embedded JSON cannot
169	    # carry Go-template conditionals. notify = apprise toast; peon = voice lines.
170	    {{- $peon   := or (eq .agentSounds "peon")   (eq .agentSounds "both") }}
171	    {{- $notify := or (eq .agentSounds "notify") (eq .agentSounds "both") }}
172	    $notifyCommand = 'exec pwsh -NoProfile -File "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hooks/notify.ps1"'
173	    $peonPs1 = Join-Path $HOME '.openpeon\hooks\peon-ping\peon.ps1'
174	    $peonCommand = "powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command `"if (Test-Path '$peonPs1') { & '$peonPs1' }`""
175	    $soundHooks = @{}
176	    {{- if $notify }}
177	    foreach ($eventName in @('Notification', 'Stop')) {
178	        $soundHooks[$eventName] = @(@{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $notifyCommand }) })
179	    }
180	    {{- end }}
181	    {{- if $peon }}
182	    foreach ($eventName in @('SessionStart', 'SessionEnd', 'SubagentStart', 'Stop',
183	                              'Notification', 'PermissionRequest', 'PreToolUse',
184	                              'PostToolUseFailure', 'PreCompact')) {
185	        $entry = @{ matcher = ''; hooks = @(@{ type = 'command'; command = $peonCommand; timeout = 10 }) }
186	        if ($soundHooks.ContainsKey($eventName)) { $soundHooks[$eventName] = @($soundHooks[$eventName] + $entry) }
187	        else                                      { $soundHooks[$eventName] = @($entry) }
188	    }
189	    {{- end }}
190	    if ($soundHooks.Count -gt 0) {
191	        if ($overlay['hooks'] -isnot [System.Collections.IDictionary]) { $overlay['hooks'] = @{} }
192	        foreach ($eventName in $soundHooks.Keys) { $overlay['hooks'][$eventName] = $soundHooks[$eventName] }
193	    }
194	
195	    # Prune only repository-owned hooks disabled by the current sound tier.
196	    $prunePatterns = @(
197	    {{- if not $notify }}
198	        'notify\.ps1'
199	    {{- end }}
200	    {{- if not $peon }}
201	        'peon\.ps1'
202	    {{- end }}
203	    )
204	
205	    $settingsPath = Join-Path $ClaudeDir 'settings.json'
206	    $settingsExisted = Test-Path -LiteralPath $settingsPath
207	    [byte[]] $settingsBytes = [byte[]]::new(0)
208	    if ($settingsExisted) { $settingsBytes = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($settingsPath) }
209	    $settings = Read-JsonObject -Path $settingsPath
210	    Merge-JsonObject -Base $settings -Overlay $overlay -MergeHooks
211	
212	    if ($prunePatterns.Count -gt 0 -and $settings['hooks'] -is [System.Collections.IDictionary]) {
213	        foreach ($eventName in @($settings['hooks'].Keys)) {
214	            $kept = @(@($settings['hooks'][$eventName]) | Where-Object {
215	                $command = $_.hooks[0].command
216	                if (-not $command) { return $true }
217	                foreach ($pattern in $prunePatterns) {
218	                    if ($command -match $pattern) { return $false }
219	                }
220	                $true
221	            })
222	            if ($kept.Count -gt 0) { $settings['hooks'][$eventName] = $kept }
223	            else                   { $settings['hooks'].Remove($eventName) }
224	        }
225	    }
226	
227	    $changed = Write-JsonObjectAtomically -Path $settingsPath -Value $settings `
228	        -ExpectedExists $settingsExisted -ExpectedBytes $settingsBytes
229	    if ($changed) { Write-Host "claude overlay -> $settingsPath" }
230	}

235	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $OverlayJson

1721	# specstory's `-c/--command` REPLACES the provider's configured command — it does
1722	# NOT append to it. Build the complete command from the effective `claude_cmd`,
1723	# then enforce claude-copilot's own bypass-permissions contract and append each

1725	# making zero-argument and argument-bearing sessions behave identically.
1726	# `--no-specstory` deliberately does not inherit the configured base command.
1727	
1728	# Effective `claude_cmd`, honouring specstory's own precedence:
1729	#   project ./.specstory/cli/config.toml > user ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml > `claude`
1730	# Matches UNCOMMENTED assignments only — both shipped configs carry a commented
1731	# `# claude_cmd = "claude"` example, and matching that would re-introduce the very
1732	# bug this exists to fix. Handles TOML's double- and single-quoted strings.
1733	function script:Get-SpecstoryClaudeCmd {
1734	    foreach ($f in '.specstory/cli/config.toml', (Join-Path $HOME '.specstory/cli/config.toml')) {
1735	        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $f)) { continue }
1736	        foreach ($line in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $f -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
1737	            if ($line -notmatch '^\s*claude_cmd\s*=\s*("(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|''[^'']*'')\s*(?:#.*)?$') { continue }

```text
130	to the original bash. Only the Bun throttle shim (pure JS) is reused verbatim. See
131	[copilot-proxy](copilot-proxy.md).
132	
133	## `run_onchange` pwsh mergers for JSON config, not `modify_` scripts
134	
135	Some JSON config surfaces are **owned by the tool at runtime** — Claude Code
136	rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` (plugins it installs, permissions you grant),
137	`/claude-hud:configure` rewrites `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json`, and
138	VSCode/Cursor rewrite their `settings.json`. Deploying static managed copies
139	would clobber that live state, so these are **merged**, not overwritten. The
140	macOS/Linux repo merges with a chezmoi **`modify_` script** (a `sh` + `jq`
141	filter: read the live file on stdin, emit the merged result on stdout). On
142	Windows that doesn't hold up:
143	
144	- **Interpreter routing is by the *target's* extension.** chezmoi chooses a
145	  `modify_`/`create_` script's interpreter from the managed file's extension via
146	  `[interpreters.<ext>]`. `modify_settings.json` targets `settings.json` →
147	  `.json`, which maps to no interpreter. On Unix chezmoi falls back to the
148	  script's shebang (`#!/bin/sh`) + exec bit; Windows honors neither, so it can't
149	  run the script reliably — and you can't hand it a `.ps1` extension, because
150	  that's fixed to the target name. Only `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh` is wired up,
151	  and it only helps when the *managed file itself* is a `.ps1`.
152	- **Wrong toolchain.** The parent filter is `sh` + `jq` — not guaranteed on a
153	  pwsh-first box, and rewriting it in pwsh still hits the routing wall above.
154	
155	So each merge is a **`run_onchange_after_*.ps1.tmpl`** in `.chezmoiscripts/`
156	instead: a real `.ps1` that routes cleanly through `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh`,
157	runs natively with no external deps, and recursively deep-merges
158	chezmoi-ignored overlays (`editors/*.json`, `claude/settings-overlay.json`,
159	`claude/hud-full-overlay.json`, embedded via `{{ include }}`) into live files —
160	preserving every key the tool wrote outside the managed leaves. The Claude
161	merger handles settings and HUD config as two independent, fail-closed
162	transactions and commits validated BOM-free JSON through same-directory atomic
163	replacement while preserving Windows metadata. A byte precondition rejects stale
164	read-modify-write results, so malformed input, a concurrent live edit, or a failed
165	write on one target cannot damage or block the other. This is invariant #5 in `AGENTS.md`.
166	
167	**Tradeoff:** a `modify_` filter re-asserts on *every* apply; `run_onchange` only
168	re-fires when its rendered content (the overlay) changes. If the tool later
169	overwrites a managed key (including a Full-preset HUD leaf changed through
170	`/claude-hud:configure`), it isn't restored until the overlay changes or you reset
171	state (`chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=entryState`). The parent needs
172	every-apply enforcement because CodeIsland / workmux keep rewriting
173	`~/.claude/settings.json`; Windows has no such contenders, so the lighter trigger
174	is fine.
175	
176	## XDG paths, not `%APPDATA%`
```

```text
172	  model. Only this inference request consumes quota; timeout and TLS failures are
173	  reported separately.
174	- HTTP 402 with `billing_not_configured` is account-wide and nonretryable. Select
175	  an organization or enterprise under **Usage billed to** at
176	  <https://github.com/settings/copilot/features>. Model changes,
177	  `copilot-model --auto`, and shim toggles cannot repair that account setting.
178	- `copilot-here` writes only the gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json`, never
179	  committed project settings. `off` removes every env key owned by the helper and
180	  preserves unrelated settings.
181	- `claude-copilot` and `claude-copilot-once` retain the Windows port's trusted
182	  `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and optional SpecStory behavior. On the
183	  SpecStory path they resolve the project/user `claude_cmd` as the base, enforce
184	  one bypass flag, quote all user arguments, and always pass the complete command
185	  through `specstory run claude -c` (including zero-argument sessions). The
186	  create-seeded `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` remains user-owned, and direct
187	  `specstory run claude` still follows that user/project configuration. Plain
188	  `claude` is unaffected.
189	- The throttle shim remains byte-identical to the macOS/Linux copy and retries
190	  transient 403/429 bursts while limiting concurrent requests. It deliberately
191	  passes HTTP 402 through once; billing configuration is not a throttle failure.
192	
193	State lives under `~/.local/state/copilot-proxy/`; device login stores the GitHub
194	token at `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token` without printing it by default.
195	
196	## Codex through the gateway
197	
198	`codex-copilot` and its identical `codex-copilot-once` alias start the local
199	gateway/shim and pass a `copilot_api` Responses provider through one-invocation
200	Codex `-c` overrides. They do not edit user or project Codex config, so plain
201	`codex` is unaffected. An explicit `-m` / `--model` wins; otherwise the live raw
202	catalog is ranked OpenAI/Codex first (`Sol > Terra > GPT-5.5 > GPT-5.4 > GPT-5.3
203	Codex > Luna > mini`), then Claude, Gemini and other chat models. Disabled and
204	embedding models are excluded.
205	
206	Codex always uses the shim on `localhost:4142`, even when the persisted
207	throttling toggle is off. Besides throttling, that boundary normalizes blank
208	descriptions in Codex `mcp_list_tools` Responses items. GitHub Copilot rejects
209	those with `Invalid 'input[0].tools[0].description': empty string`, while MCP
210	servers and the native Codex path may omit them. The shim fills only those tool
211	definition fields and leaves prompts, schemas, and tool names unchanged.
212	Codex currently zstd-compresses these requests; the shim decodes only the
213	Responses body it must repair, forwards ordinary JSON, and removes the stale
214	`content-encoding` header.
215	
216	This is a separate picker from Claude Code's `copilot-model --auto`: that path
217	remains Claude-first, while only the Codex launcher is OpenAI-first.
218	
219	SpecStory is automatic when installed. The wrapper preserves the effective
220	`codex_cmd` (project config > user config > bare `codex`) before appending
221	provider/model/user arguments; `--no-specstory` runs Codex directly. Claude and
222	Gemini fallback through Responses Lite, which does not support Responses
223	`tool_search`, so native Responses OpenAI models stay ahead of Anthropic.
224	The launcher also enables gateway-backed remote compaction and excludes the
225	`mcp__codex_apps__sites` namespace that depends on unavailable `tool_search`;
226	later explicit `-c` arguments can override either setting per invocation.

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $tmp
PS

1	package spi

3	import "strings"

5	// SplitCommandLine splits a command line string into arguments, respecting quoted strings.
6	//
7	// Supports both single and double quotes. Quotes can be escaped with backslash.
8	// This is used by providers to parse custom command strings that may contain paths
9	// or arguments with spaces.
10	//
11	// Examples:
12	//   - "claude --debug" -> ["claude", "--debug"]
13	//   - `claude --config "~/My Settings/config.json"` -> ["claude", "--config", "~/My Settings/config.json"]
14	//   - `claude --msg 'It'\”s working'` -> ["claude", "--msg", "It's working"]
15	//   - `claude --path "C:\\Users\\test"` -> ["claude", "--path", "C:\Users\test"]
16	//
17	// Behavior:
18	//   - Single and double quotes are treated equivalently
19	//   - Backslash escapes the next character (including quotes and backslashes)
20	//   - Whitespace (space, tab, newline) outside quotes separates arguments
21	//   - Empty quoted strings are ignored (e.g., `cmd "" --arg` -> ["cmd", "--arg"])
22	//   - Unclosed quotes consume to end of string
23	func SplitCommandLine(s string) []string {
24		var args []string
25		var current strings.Builder
26		var inQuote rune // ' or " when inside quotes, 0 otherwise
27		var escaped bool
28	
29		for _, r := range s {
30			if escaped {
31				// Previous character was backslash, add this character literally
32				current.WriteRune(r)
33				escaped = false
34				continue
35			}
36	
37			if r == '\\' {
38				// Next character will be escaped
39				escaped = true
40				continue
41			}
42	
43			if inQuote != 0 {
44				// Inside quotes
45				if r == inQuote {
46					// End quote
47					inQuote = 0
48				} else {
49					current.WriteRune(r)
50				}
51				continue
52			}
53	
54			// Not inside quotes
55			if r == '"' || r == '\'' {
56				// Start quote
57				inQuote = r
58				continue
59			}
60	
61			if r == ' ' || r == '\t' || r == '\n' {
62				// Whitespace outside quotes - end of argument
63				if current.Len() > 0 {
64					args = append(args, current.String())
65					current.Reset()
66				}
67				continue
68			}
69	
70			// Regular character
71			current.WriteRune(r)
72		}
73	
74		// Add final argument if any
75		if current.Len() > 0 {
76			args = append(args, current.String())
77		}
78	
79		return args
80	}
81

31	func filterWarmupMessages(records []JSONLRecord) []JSONLRecord {
32		// Find first non-sidechain message
33		firstRealMessageIndex := -1
34		for i, record := range records {
35			if isSidechain, ok := record.Data["isSidechain"].(bool); !ok || !isSidechain {
36				firstRealMessageIndex = i
37				break
38			}
39		}

41		// No real messages found
42		if firstRealMessageIndex == -1 {
43			return []JSONLRecord{}
44		}
45	
46		// Return records starting from first real message
47		return records[firstRealMessageIndex:]
48	}

162	// Check verifies Claude Code installation and returns version info
163	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
164		// Parse the command (no resume session for version check)
165		claudeCmd, _ := parseClaudeCommand(customCommand, "")
166	
167		// Determine if custom command was used
168		isCustomCommand := customCommand != ""
169	
170		// Resolve the actual path of the command
171		resolvedPath := claudeCmd
172		if !filepath.IsAbs(claudeCmd) {
173			// Try to find the command in PATH
174			if path, err := exec.LookPath(claudeCmd); err == nil {
175				resolvedPath = path
176			}
177		}
178	
179		// Run claude -v to check version (ignore custom args for version check)
180		cmd := exec.Command(claudeCmd, "-v")
181		var out bytes.Buffer
182		var errOut bytes.Buffer
183		cmd.Stdout = &out
184		cmd.Stderr = &errOut
185	
186		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
187			// Track installation check failure
188			errorType := "unknown"
189	
190			var execErr *exec.Error
191			var pathErr *os.PathError
192	
193			// Check error types in order of specificity
194			switch {
195			case errors.As(err, &execErr) && execErr.Err == exec.ErrNotFound:
196				errorType = "not_found"
197			case errors.As(err, &pathErr):
198				if errors.Is(pathErr.Err, os.ErrNotExist) {
199					errorType = "not_found"
200				} else if errors.Is(pathErr.Err, os.ErrPermission) {
201					errorType = "permission_denied"
202				}
203			case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
204				errorType = "permission_denied"
205			}
206	
207			stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(errOut.String())
208			analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventCheckInstallFailed, analytics.Properties{
209				"provider":       "claude",
210				"custom_command": isCustomCommand,
211				"command_path":   claudeCmd,
212				"error_type":     errorType,
213				"error_message":  err.Error(),
214			})
215	
216			errorMessage := buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, claudeCmd, isCustomCommand, stderrOutput)
217	
218			return spi.CheckResult{
219				Success:      false,
220				Version:      "",
221				Location:     resolvedPath,
222				ErrorMessage: errorMessage,
223			}
224		}
225	
226		// Check if output contains "Claude Code"
227		output := out.String()
228		if !strings.Contains(output, "(Claude Code)") {
229			// Track unexpected output error
230			analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventCheckInstallFailed, analytics.Properties{
231				"provider":       "claude",
232				"custom_command": isCustomCommand,
233				"command_path":   claudeCmd,
234				"error_type":     "unexpected_output",
235				"output":         strings.TrimSpace(output),
236			})
237	
238			errorMessage := buildCheckErrorMessage("unexpected_output", claudeCmd, isCustomCommand, output)
239	
240			return spi.CheckResult{
241				Success:      false,
242				Version:      "",
243				Location:     resolvedPath,
244				ErrorMessage: errorMessage,
245			}
246		}
247	
248		// Success! Track it
249		analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventCheckInstallSuccess, analytics.Properties{
250			"provider":       "claude",
251			"custom_command": isCustomCommand,
252			"command_path":   resolvedPath,
253			"version":        strings.TrimSpace(output),
254		})
255	
256		return spi.CheckResult{
257			Success:      true,
258			Version:      strings.TrimSpace(output),
259			Location:     resolvedPath,
260			ErrorMessage: "",
261		}
262	}

376	func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
377		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: Starting Claude Code execution and monitoring",
378			"projectPath", projectPath,
379			"customCommand", customCommand,
380			"resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID,
381			"debugRaw", debugRaw)

389			}
390			slog.Info("Resuming Claude Code session", "sessionId", resumeSessionID)
391		}
392	
393		// Set up the callback which enables real-time markdown generation and cloud sync during
394		// interactive sessions. As Claude Code writes JSONL updates, the watcher detects
395		// changes and invokes this callback, allowing immediate processing without blocking
396		// the agent's execution. The defer ensures cleanup when the agent exits.
397		SetWatcherCallback(sessionCallback)
398		defer ClearWatcherCallback()
399	
400		// Set debug raw mode for the watcher
401		SetWatcherDebugRaw(debugRaw)
402	
403		// Start watching for project directory in the background
404		slog.Info("Initializing project directory monitoring...")
405	
406		if err := WatchForProjectDir(); err != nil {
407			// Log the error but don't fail - watcher might work later
408			slog.Error("Failed to start project directory watcher", "error", err)
409		}
410	
411		// Execute Claude Code - this blocks until Claude exits
412		slog.Info("Executing Claude Code", "command", customCommand)
413		err := ExecuteClaude(customCommand, resumeSessionID)
414	
415		// Stop the watcher goroutine before returning
416		slog.Info("Claude Code has exited, stopping watcher")
417		StopWatcher()
418	
419		// Return any execution error
420		if err != nil {
421			return fmt.Errorf("claude Code execution failed: %w", err)
422		}
423	
424		return nil
425	}

427	// WatchAgent watches for Claude Code agent activity and calls the callback with AgentChatSession
428	// Does NOT execute the agent - only watches for existing activity

430	func (p *Provider) WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
431		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Starting Claude Code activity monitoring",
432			"projectPath", projectPath,
433			"debugRaw", debugRaw)
434	
435		// The watcher callback directly passes AgentChatSession (which now contains SessionData)
436		wrappedCallback := func(agentChatSession *spi.AgentChatSession) {
437			slog.Debug("WatchAgent: Received AgentChatSession",
438				"sessionID", agentChatSession.SessionID,
439				"hasSessionData", agentChatSession.SessionData != nil)
440	
441			// Call the user's callback with the AgentChatSession
442			sessionCallback(agentChatSession)
443		}
444	
445		// Set up the callback for the watcher
446		SetWatcherCallback(wrappedCallback)
447		defer ClearWatcherCallback()
448	
449		// Set debug raw mode for the watcher
450		SetWatcherDebugRaw(debugRaw)
451	
452		// Get the Claude Code project directory for the specified project path
453		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Initializing project directory monitoring...")
454	
455		claudeProjectDir, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectDir(projectPath)
456		if err != nil {
457			slog.Error("WatchAgent: Failed to get Claude Code project directory", "error", err)
458			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get project directory: %w", err)
459		}
460	
461		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Project directory found", "directory", claudeProjectDir)
462	
463		if err := startProjectWatcher(claudeProjectDir); err != nil {
464			slog.Error("WatchAgent: Failed to start project watcher", "error", err)
465			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start watcher: %w", err)
466		}
467	
468		// Block until context is cancelled
469		// The watcher runs in a background goroutine and will continue
470		// until context is cancelled or the process exits
471		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Watcher started, blocking until context cancelled")
472	
473		// Wait for context cancellation
474		<-ctx.Done()
475	
476		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Context cancelled, stopping watcher")
477		StopWatcher()
478	
479		return ctx.Err()
480	}

482	// isSyntheticMessage checks if a message is synthetic/internal and should be skipped
483	// when looking for the first real user message (e.g. for the session title/slug).
484	// Filters warmup prompts, title-generation prompts, and slash-command noise (the
485	// command invocation, its local stdout/stderr, and the local-command caveat) — these
486	// are conversation scaffolding, not the user's actual prompt. Without this, a session
487	// that opens with a slash command gets an empty title and falls back to its UUID.
488	func isSyntheticMessage(content string) bool {
489		// warmup and the <TEXTBLOCK> title-generation wrapper can be embedded anywhere
490		// in the record, so match them with Contains.
491		if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(content), "warmup") {
492			return true
493		}
494		if strings.Contains(content, "<TEXTBLOCK>") {
495			return true
496		}
497		// The slash-command scaffolding tags (shared with reconstruction via
498		// spi.SyntheticCommandTags) and the interrupt marker REPLACE the prompt, so they
499		// appear at the very START of the record. Match by prefix so a real prompt that
500		// merely mentions a tag mid-sentence is still treated as real. The interrupt
501		// marker's "…for tool use" variant is caught by the same prefix.
502		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(content)
503		for _, marker := range spi.SyntheticCommandTags {
504			if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, marker) {
505				return true
506			}
507		}
508		return strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "[Request interrupted by user")
509	}

511	// cleanSyntheticPrefixes strips known boilerplate prefixes that Claude Code
512	// prepends to user messages (e.g. plan mode). The real user content follows
513	// the prefix, so we strip rather than skip the message entirely.
514	func cleanSyntheticPrefixes(content string) string {
515		prefixes := []string{
516			"Implement the following plan:",
517		}
518		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(content)
519		lower := strings.ToLower(trimmed)
520		for _, prefix := range prefixes {
521			if strings.HasPrefix(lower, strings.ToLower(prefix)) {
522				return strings.TrimSpace(trimmed[len(prefix):])
523			}
524		}
525		// Return the trimmed form in the no-match case too, so callers always get
526		// consistently-trimmed output regardless of whether a prefix was stripped.
527		return trimmed
528	}
529	
530	// extractContentText extracts plain text from a message content field.
531	// The content field may be either a plain string or a JSON array of typed content
532	// blocks (e.g. [{type:"text",text:"..."},{type:"tool_use",...}]).
533	// When it's an array, all "text"-type blocks are joined with newlines.
534	// This handles the Claude Code JSONL format where IDE context tags (e.g.
535	// <ide_opened_file>) are injected as separate text blocks before the real question.
536	func extractContentText(content interface{}) string {
537		switch v := content.(type) {
538		case string:
539			return v
540		case []interface{}:
541			var parts []string
542			for _, block := range v {
543				if m, ok := block.(map[string]interface{}); ok {
544					if t, _ := m["type"].(string); t == "text" {
545						if text, ok := m["text"].(string); ok && text != "" {
546							parts = append(parts, text)
547						}
548					}
549				}
550			}
551			slog.Debug("extractContentText: extracted text from content block array",
552				"blockCount", len(v),
553				"textParts", len(parts))
554			return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
555		default:
556			return ""
557		}
558	}

560	// findFirstUserMessage finds the first user message in a session for slug generation
561	// Returns empty string if no suitable user message is found
562	func findFirstUserMessage(session Session) string {
563		for _, record := range session.Records {
564			// Check if this is a user message
565			if recordType, ok := record.Data["type"].(string); !ok || recordType != "user" {
566				continue
567			}
568	
569			// Skip meta user messages
570			if isMeta, ok := record.Data["isMeta"].(bool); ok && isMeta {
571				continue
572			}
573	
574			// Extract content from message - content may be a string or a list of blocks
575			if message, ok := record.Data["message"].(map[string]interface{}); ok {
576				content := extractContentText(message["content"])
577				if content != "" {
578					// Skip synthetic messages (warmup, title generation prompts, etc.)
579					if isSyntheticMessage(content) {
580						continue
581					}
582					return cleanSyntheticPrefixes(content)
583				}
584			}
585		}
586		return ""
587	}

606	// ListAgentChatSessions retrieves lightweight session metadata without full parsing
607	// This is much faster than GetAgentChatSessions as it only reads minimal data from each session
608	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
609		// Get the Claude Code project directory
610		claudeProjectDir, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectDir(projectPath)
611		if err != nil {
612			return nil, err
613		}
614	
615		// Check if project directory exists
616		if _, err := os.Stat(claudeProjectDir); os.IsNotExist(err) {
617			return []spi.SessionMetadata{}, nil // No sessions if no project
618		}
619	
620		// Collect all JSONL files in the project directory
621		var sessionFiles []string
622		err = filepath.Walk(claudeProjectDir, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error) error {
623			if err != nil {
624				return err
625			}
626			if info.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(path, ".jsonl") {
627				return nil
628			}
629			sessionFiles = append(sessionFiles, path)
630			return nil
631		})
632		if err != nil {
633			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to scan project directory: %w", err)
634		}
635	
636		// Extract metadata from each session file
637		sessions := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(sessionFiles))
638		for _, filePath := range sessionFiles {

640			if err != nil {
641				slog.Warn("Failed to extract session metadata",
642					"file", filePath,
643					"error", err)
644				continue
645			}
646	
647			// Skip warmup-only sessions (no metadata means warmup-only)
648			if metadata == nil {
649				slog.Debug("Skipping warmup-only session", "file", filePath)
650				continue
651			}
652	
653			sessions = append(sessions, *metadata)
654		}
655	
656		return sessions, nil
657	}

659	// claudeSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one pass:
660	// identity + first-message metadata, plus the originating cwd (Claude Code stamps a
661	// top-level "cwd" on every conversational record). foundRealMessage is false for
662	// warmup-only sessions (no real messages).
663	type claudeSessionScan struct {
664		sessionID        string
665		timestamp        string
666		firstUserMessage string
667		commandFallback  string // slash command title when there is no free-text prompt
668		cwd              string
669		foundRealMessage bool
670	}
671	
672	// scanClaudeSession reads minimal data from a session file: session id, first-real
673	// timestamp, first user message, and originating cwd. Shared by the project-scoped
674	// metadata path and the global enumeration (ListAllAgentChatSessions).
675	func scanClaudeSession(filePath string) (*claudeSessionScan, error) {
676		file, err := os.Open(filePath)
677		if err != nil {
678			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open session file: %w", err)
679		}
680		defer func() {
681			_ = file.Close()
682		}()
683	
684		reader := bufio.NewReader(file)
685		scan := &claudeSessionScan{}
686	
687		// Read records until we find everything we need.
688		// Why: ReadString can return data AND io.EOF on the last line (no trailing newline),
689		// so we always process the line first, then check for EOF once at the bottom.
690		lineNum := 0
691		for {
692			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
693			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
694				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read line: %w", readErr)
695			}
696	
697			lineNum++
698			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
699	
700			if line != "" {
701				// Parse JSON record
702				var record map[string]interface{}
703				if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &record); jsonErr != nil {
704					slog.Warn("Skipping malformed JSONL line",
705						"file", filepath.Base(filePath),
706						"line", lineNum,
707						"error", jsonErr)
708				} else {
709					// Extract session ID (from any record)
710					if scan.sessionID == "" {
711						if sid, ok := record["sessionId"].(string); ok {
712							scan.sessionID = sid
713						}
714					}
715	
716					// Capture the originating cwd (first record that carries one). This is
717					// the input to project-identity resolution for the restore index.
718					if scan.cwd == "" {
719						if cwd, ok := record["cwd"].(string); ok && cwd != "" {
720							scan.cwd = cwd
721						}
722					}
723	
724					// Only process non-sidechain, non-system records for message extraction
725					isSidechain, _ := record["isSidechain"].(bool)
726					recordType, hasType := record["type"].(string)
727					isSystemRecord := hasType && (recordType == "file-history-snapshot" || recordType == "file-change")
728	
729					if !isSidechain && !isSystemRecord {
730						scan.foundRealMessage = true
731						// created_at = the first real record that actually carries a timestamp.
732						// (The leading {mode,sessionId,type} record has none, so we can't gate
733						// timestamp capture on "first real record" — it would stay empty.)
734						if scan.timestamp == "" {
735							if ts, ok := record["timestamp"].(string); ok && ts != "" {
736								scan.timestamp = ts
737							}
738						}
739	
740						// Extract first user message for slug (if this is a user message)
741						// Content may be a string or a list of typed blocks (see extractContentText)
742						if scan.firstUserMessage == "" && hasType && recordType == "user" {
743							isMeta, _ := record["isMeta"].(bool)
744							if !isMeta {
745								if message, ok := record["message"].(map[string]interface{}); ok {
746									content := extractContentText(message["content"])
747									if content != "" {
748										if isSyntheticMessage(content) {
749											// A slash-command session may have no free-text prompt;
750											// remember the command name as a fallback title.
751											if scan.commandFallback == "" {
752												scan.commandFallback = extractCommandName(content)
753											}
754										} else {
755											scan.firstUserMessage = content
756										}
757									}
758								}
759							}
760						}
761					}
762				}
763			}
764	
765			// Single exit: found everything we need, or reached end of file
766			if (scan.sessionID != "" && scan.timestamp != "" && scan.firstUserMessage != "" && scan.cwd != "") || readErr == io.EOF {
767				break
768			}
769		}
770	
771		// Fall back to the slash command when there was no real user prompt (so a
772		// command-only session shows e.g. "/code-review" instead of its UUID).
773		if scan.firstUserMessage == "" {
774			scan.firstUserMessage = scan.commandFallback
775		}
776		return scan, nil
777	}
778	
779	// extractCommandName pulls the slash command from a Claude Code command record, e.g.
780	// "<command-name>/code-review</command-name>…" -> "/code-review". Falls back to the
781	// bare command-message name (prefixed with "/"). Returns "" when none is present.
782	func extractCommandName(content string) string {
783		if c := between(content, "<command-name>", "</command-name>"); c != "" {
784			return c
785		}
786		if c := between(content, "<command-message>", "</command-message>"); c != "" {
787			return "/" + c
788		}
789		return ""
790	}
791	
792	// between returns the text between the first open/close markers, trimmed, or "".
793	func between(s, openTag, closeTag string) string {
794		_, after, ok := strings.Cut(s, openTag)
795		if !ok {
796			return ""
797		}
798		inner, _, ok := strings.Cut(after, closeTag)
799		if !ok {
800			return ""
801		}
802		return strings.TrimSpace(inner)
803	}
804	
805	// extractSessionMetadata reads minimal data from a session file to extract metadata
806	// Returns nil if the session is warmup-only (no real messages)
807	func extractSessionMetadata(filePath string) (*spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
808		scan, err := scanClaudeSession(filePath)
809		if err != nil {
810			return nil, err
811		}
812	
813		// If no real message was found, this is a warmup-only session
814		if !scan.foundRealMessage {
815			return nil, nil
816		}
817	
818		return &spi.SessionMetadata{
819			SessionID: scan.sessionID,
820			CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
821			Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
822			Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
823		}, nil
824	}

826	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every Claude Code session across all projects. It is the

829		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)

832	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates every Claude Code session across all projects by
833	// walking ~/.claude/projects/*/ for *.jsonl (the originating cwd comes from inside each session;
834	// the project directory name is a lossy, irreversible encoding of the path), reporting scan
835	// progress into r (nil-safe). Headers are scanned in parallel across CPUs; output order is
836	// irrelevant (reindex dedups and sorts later). Implements spi.ProgressEnumerator. See
837	// docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
838	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
839		projectsDir, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectsDir()
840		if err != nil {
841			// No projects directory yet → nothing to enumerate (not an error).
842			return []spi.GlobalSessionRef{}, nil
843		}
844	
845		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(projectsDir, "claude", r, func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
846			scan, scanErr := scanClaudeSession(path)

848				return nil, scanErr
849			}
850			if !scan.foundRealMessage {

852			}
853			return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
854				SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
855				CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
856				Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
857				Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
858				NativePath: path,
859				OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
860			}, nil
861		})
862	}

59	func expandTilde(path string) string {

69	// parseClaudeCommand parses a custom command string into executable and arguments.
70	// If customCommand is empty, returns the default command.
71	// If resumeSessionId is provided, appends "--resume <sessionId>" to the arguments.
72	// Supports quoted strings with spaces: claude --arg "value with spaces"
73	// Example: "claude --model gpt-4" returns ("claude", ["--model", "gpt-4"])
74	func parseClaudeCommand(customCommand string, resumeSessionId string) (string, []string) {
75		var cmd string
76		var args []string
77	
78		if customCommand == "" {
79			cmd = getDefaultClaudeCommand()
80			args = nil
81		} else {
82			parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
83			if len(parts) == 0 {
84				cmd = getDefaultClaudeCommand()
85				args = nil
86			} else {
87				// Expand tilde in the command path
88				cmd = expandTilde(parts[0])
89				args = parts[1:]
90			}
91		}
92	
93		// Append --resume flag if sessionId is provided
94		if resumeSessionId != "" {
95			args = append(args, "--resume", resumeSessionId)
96		}
97	
98		return cmd, args
99	}

101	// ExecuteClaude runs the Claude CLI with the given arguments
102	func ExecuteClaude(customCommand string, resumeSessionId string) error {
103		// Parse the command and any custom arguments
104		claudeCmd, customArgs := parseClaudeCommand(customCommand, resumeSessionId)
105	
106		// Log if resuming a session
107		if resumeSessionId != "" {
108			slog.Info("ExecuteClaude: Resuming session", "sessionId", resumeSessionId)
109		}
110	
111		// Create the command
112		cmd := exec.Command(claudeCmd, customArgs...)
113	
114		// Set up stdin/stdout/stderr to match the parent process
115		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
116		cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
117		cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
118	
119		// Start the command
120		slog.Info("ExecuteClaude: Starting Claude Code process")
121		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
122			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start claude: %v", err)
123		}
124	
125		// Wait for the command to complete
126		slog.Info("ExecuteClaude: Waiting for Claude Code to exit")
127		if err := cmd.Wait(); err != nil {
128			// Don't return error if the command exited with a non-zero status
129			// This is normal for many CLI applications
130			if exitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
131				exitCode := exitErr.ExitCode()
132				slog.Info("ExecuteClaude: Claude Code exited", "exitCode", exitCode)
133				os.Exit(exitCode)
134			}
135			return fmt.Errorf("claude execution failed: %v", err)
136		}
137	
138		slog.Info("ExecuteClaude: Claude Code exited normally", "exitCode", 0)
139		return nil
140	}

609				continue
610			}
611			result.UnknownKeys = append(result.UnknownKeys, key.String())
612		}
613	
614		return result
615	}

145	  On a corporate machine, npm may use an internal pull-through mirror because
146	  `registry.npmjs.org` is blocked. npm honours that configured registry; Bun does
147	  not, so `copilot-proxy` prefers npm for its private prefix. Diagnose the mirror
148	  with `npm view <package>@<version> version`, not `npm ping`; the matching
149	  symptom records are `copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module`
150	  and `packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path` under `pitfalls/`.
151	- **Codex native footer** — chezmoi non-destructively merges a provider-neutral
152	  status line (model/reasoning, fast mode, branch, context, tasks, directory)
153	  into `~/.codex/config.toml`. No fork or PATH shim; see
154	  [Codex status line](codex-status-line.md).
155	- **OpenCode Desktop** — GUI companion to the `opencode-ai` CLI, via scoop
156	  (`extras/opencode-desktop`).
157	- **claude-hud** — a statusline HUD below the Claude Code prompt. One
158	  `run_onchange` merger (`.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl`)
159	  independently deep-merges `~/.claude/settings.json` and the stable
160	  `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json`, preserving live-only state in each.
161	  The latter enforces the documented **Full preset as of claude-hud 0.7.1**
162	  (activity plus token/usage/cost/session/memory/cache/version indicators) while
163	  leaving advanced colors, layout, thresholds, provider/auth fields and future
164	  keys user-owned. The plugin self-installs from its marketplace on first launch;
165	  its guarded Git Bash status-line command runs with scoop's `node` and silently
166	  no-ops until the plugin cache exists. The settings overlay also enables
167	  `pyright-lsp` and sets `permissions.defaultMode: auto` plus
168	  `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`. **Restart Claude Code** after
169	  `chezmoi apply` to load a newly installed plugin. See
170	  [running multiple agents](claude-code-agents.md).
171	- **Desktop notifications** — `apprise` (`uv tool install --with pywin32 apprise`)
172	  fires native Windows toasts on Claude Code's **Notification** (needs your
173	  attention) and **Stop** (task finished) events, via a native-pwsh hook
174	  (`~/.claude/hooks/notify.ps1`) the settings overlay wires into `hooks`. Routing
175	  lives in `~/.config/apprise/apprise.yaml` — the `windows://` backend tagged
176	  `desktop`; add your own remote services (Discord/Slack/…) in the create-once
177	  `~/.config/apprise/custom.yaml`. Port of the parent repo's `notify.sh` +
178	  `apprise.yaml`.
179	
180	The official **ChatGPT** desktop app installs via the Microsoft Store (see GUI
181	apps); **Codex** is the `@openai/codex` npm CLI above, not a Store app. SpecStory
182	has no native-Windows CLI package, so it's omitted here — an experimental build
183	from the unmerged PR #191 is opt-in via the **SpecStory build** init prompt
184	(`installSpecstoryBuild`) or `just specstory-build` (needs git + go).

110	（純 JS）原封不動沿用。見 [copilot-proxy](copilot-proxy.md)。
111	
112	## JSON 設定用 `run_onchange` pwsh 合併器，而非 `modify_` 腳本
113	
114	有些 JSON 設定面是**由工具在執行期擁有**的 —— Claude Code 會改寫
115	`~/.claude/settings.json`（它安裝的外掛、你授予的權限），`/claude-hud:configure` 會改寫
116	`~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json`，VSCode/Cursor 也會改寫各自的
117	`settings.json`。直接部署靜態受管副本會蓋掉這些即時狀態，所以它們是用**合併**、
118	而非覆寫。macOS/Linux repo 用 chezmoi 的 **`modify_` 腳本**來合併（一個 `sh` + `jq`
119	過濾器：從 stdin 讀入 live 檔，把合併結果吐到 stdout）。在 Windows 上這行不通：
120	
121	- **直譯器是用「目標檔」的副檔名決定的。** chezmoi 依受管檔的副檔名從
122	  `[interpreters.<ext>]` 選 `modify_`/`create_` 腳本的直譯器。`modify_settings.json`
123	  的目標是 `settings.json` → `.json`，查不到任何直譯器。Unix 上 chezmoi 會退回用腳本的
124	  shebang（`#!/bin/sh`）+ 執行位元；Windows 兩者都不吃，所以無法可靠執行 —— 而且你
125	  沒辦法給它 `.ps1` 副檔名，因為那綁死在目標名上。這裡只接了
126	  `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh`，而它只有在「受管檔本身就是 `.ps1`」時才幫得上忙。
127	- **工具鏈不對。** 父 repo 的過濾器是 `sh` + `jq` —— 在 pwsh 為主的機器上不保證存在，
128	  就算改寫成 pwsh 也還是撞上上面的路由問題。
129	
130	所以每個合併改成放在 `.chezmoiscripts/` 的 **`run_onchange_after_*.ps1.tmpl`**：一個
131	真正的 `.ps1`，乾淨地走 `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh`、原生執行、零外部依賴，並把
132	chezmoi 忽略的 overlays（`editors/*.json`、`claude/settings-overlay.json`、
133	`claude/hud-full-overlay.json`，經 `{{ include }}` 內嵌）遞迴深度合併進 live 檔 ——
134	除了明確受管的 leaves 外，都保留工具寫入的 key。Claude merger 會把 settings 與 HUD
135	config 當成兩個彼此獨立、fail-closed 的 transaction，先驗證 BOM-free JSON，再透過同一
136	目錄、保留 Windows metadata 的 atomic replacement 提交。byte precondition 會拒絕 stale
137	read-modify-write 結果；其中一個 target 的輸入損壞、同時發生的 live edit 或寫入失敗，
138	不會破壞或阻擋另一個。
139	這就是 `AGENTS.md` 的 invariant #5。
140	
141	**取捨：** `modify_` 過濾器每次 apply 都會重新套用；`run_onchange` 只在其 render 後
142	內容（即 overlay）改變時才重跑。若工具之後覆蓋了某個受管 key，它不會被還原，直到
143	overlay 改變或你重置狀態（`chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=entryState`）；透過
144	`/claude-hud:configure` 改掉受管的 Full-preset HUD leaf 也一樣。父 repo 需要每次 apply
145	都強制，是因為 CodeIsland / workmux 會一直改寫
146	`~/.claude/settings.json`；Windows 沒有這種對手，所以較輕的觸發就夠了。
147	
148	## XDG 路徑，而非 `%APPDATA%`
149	
150	Windows 與 XDG 用不同的軸切目錄 —— Windows 看資料夾是否*漫遊*
```

 Isolated apply + template render (the core idiom for testing without a Windows

 chezmoi init --source="$PWD" --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --persistent-state="$TMPD/s.db" \

 ## Architecture (big picture)
 
 - **Init** — `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` `[data]` prompts once (`role` → coarse defaults, then `installX` toggles) and sets `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh` so chezmoi runs `.ps1` scripts under pwsh. Prompts are hand-authored here (the parent repo generates them; this repo does not).
 - **Shell** — `Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1` is a thin `$PROFILE` loader that dot-sources `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in numeric order (env → tool activation → aliases → apps/audio/clipboard → copilot import → yazi → tv cache → psreadline). Add a shell feature = a new numbered fragment. User overrides go in the untracked `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1`.
 - **Packages** — `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the single source of truth for installs: scoop (CLI), winget (GUI), npm (AI agents), PSGallery (PSFzf / AudioDeviceCmdlets), all gated by init toggles. `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` is the single source for registry environment variables used both by that installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines use company PyPI/npm pull-through feeds; otherwise the China-mirror toggle selects GFW mirrors. Fault-tolerant (see invariants).
 - **copilot-proxy** — `dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/` is a native PowerShell port of the parent's `43_copilot_proxy.sh` / `44_copilot_embed.sh` (runs the copilot-api fork so GitHub Copilot can back Claude Code and Codex). Reuses the Bun `copilot-throttle-shim.js` verbatim.
-- **Config surfaces** — Alacritty (`AppData/Roaming/alacritty/`), Windows Terminal (a run_onchange that merges `profiles.defaults` non-destructively), WezTerm (`dot_config/wezterm/wezterm.lua` — sets pwsh as `default_prog`), editors (a run_onchange that deep-merges `editors/*.json` into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`), Claude Code (a run_onchange that recursively deep-merges `claude/settings-overlay.json` — claude-hud statusline, safe defaults, and **additive** `Notification`/`Stop` notify hooks — into `~/.claude/settings.json` non-destructively, gated on `installCodingAgents`), Codex (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` fail-closed-merges only the native `tui.status_line` into `~/.codex/config.toml`, preserving providers/projects/plugins and gated on `installCodingAgents`), apprise desktop notifications (`dot_config/apprise/apprise.yaml` → `~/.config/apprise/`; the `windows://` toast backend behind the Claude notify hook `dot_claude/hooks/notify.ps1`, `installCodingAgents`-gated — the notify hook and peon-ping's voice-line hooks are both gated on the `agentSounds` tier (none|notify|peon|both) and built in the run_onchange, NOT in `claude/settings-overlay.json`; see docs/agent-sounds.md), television channels (`AppData/Roaming/television/`), starship + yazi (`~/.config`, yazi via `YAZI_CONFIG_HOME`), Rime/Weasel (see below), herdr (see below).
+- **Config surfaces** — Alacritty (`AppData/Roaming/alacritty/`), Windows Terminal (a run_onchange that merges `profiles.defaults` non-destructively), WezTerm (`dot_config/wezterm/wezterm.lua` — sets pwsh as `default_prog`), editors (a run_onchange that deep-merges `editors/*.json` into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`), Claude Code (one `installCodingAgents`-gated run_onchange performs failure-isolated, atomic recursive merges of `claude/settings-overlay.json` into `~/.claude/settings.json` — guarded claude-hud statusline, safe defaults, and **additive** sound hooks — and the narrow Full-0.7.1 `claude/hud-full-overlay.json` into `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json`, preserving user-owned advanced/unknown leaves), Codex (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` fail-closed-merges only the native `tui.status_line` into `~/.codex/config.toml`, preserving providers/projects/plugins and gated on `installCodingAgents`), apprise desktop notifications (`dot_config/apprise/apprise.yaml` → `~/.config/apprise/`; the `windows://` toast backend behind the Claude notify hook `dot_claude/hooks/notify.ps1`, `installCodingAgents`-gated — the notify hook and peon-ping's voice-line hooks are both gated on the `agentSounds` tier (none|notify|peon|both) and built in the run_onchange, NOT in `claude/settings-overlay.json`; see docs/agent-sounds.md), television channels (`AppData/Roaming/television/`), starship + yazi (`~/.config`, yazi via `YAZI_CONFIG_HOME`), Rime/Weasel (see below), herdr (see below).
 - **Rime input method** — `installInputMethod`-gated, and the one config surface **shared with the parent repo**. The engine-level YAML lives in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` (`default.custom.yaml`, `luna_pinyin.custom.yaml`) and is kept **byte-identical** to `daviddwlee84/dotfiles`'s copy of the same path — `diff -r` between the two dirs is the drift check, so edit one and copy to the other in the same session. Each platform is a one-line `{{ template "rime/…" . }}` renderer: `AppData/Roaming/Rime/` here, `private_Library/Rime/` (Squirrel) and `dot_config/ibus/rime/` (ibus-rime) there. Only `weasel.custom.yaml` is Windows-specific (`style/` is Weasel's own, `app_options` keys on the EXE name vs. Squirrel's bundle ids, and `global_ascii` doesn't exist on Squirrel). Plain managed files, **not** a `modify_` overlay: Rime persists runtime state to `user.yaml`, never back into `*.custom.yaml`. Two gotchas: a bare silent winget install registers **简体** (hence `--custom '/T'` in `Install-Weasel` — see `pitfalls/weasel-silent-install-registers-simplified-chinese.md`), and config edits need a redeploy, which `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
 - **herdr** — `dot_config/herdr/` is deployed via `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` and gated on `installHerdr`. `config.toml` is a **`modify_` overlay** (`modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` + `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`), never a plain managed file: herdr rewrites that file at runtime (onboarding flag, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]` bookkeeping) and a plain file clobbers it. The overlay enforces `[theme]`/`[ui]`/`[terminal]`/`[keys]` wholesale, pulls every other top-level key through, and re-asserts the single key `update.channel = "preview"` (the Windows installer rejects `stable`). Helper-script paths in the keymap are baked **absolute at render time** — `pwsh -File` does not expand `~`. Six pwsh helpers (`_common.ps1` + run-command / new-tab-at-space-root / url-pick / path-pick / pane-copy / review-mark) back the `[[keys.command]]` bindings; three `herdr-*` tv channels and the herdr-plus quick-actions are gated by the same toggle. Ported from the parent repo 2026-07-27; the behaviours that still need a real Windows box are listed in [`backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md`](backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md).
 - **git config** — `~/.gitconfig` is a **`modify_` overlay** (`modify_dot_gitconfig.ps1.tmpl`), never a plain managed file: Git Credential Manager writes `[credential "azrepos:*"]` blocks into it out of band and a plain file would clobber them every apply. The baseline body is `.chezmoitemplates/git/gitconfig` (identity from the existing `.name`/`.email` init prompts); the merge engine is `scripts/gitconfig-merge.ps1`, inlined via `{{ include }}` (the `editors/` idiom) and dot-sourced by `tests/GitConfig.Tests.ps1`. The model is **key-level pull-through**: the baseline owns a fixed set of `section.key` pairs and every other live key is carried over untouched — the inverse of the parent repo's allowlist, which would silently drop `[otel]` and future corp sections. Two hard rules: `core.hooksPath` is **never** emitted (git honours it *instead of* `.git/hooks/`, silently disarming `pre-commit`), and the carry dictionary is **case-sensitive** (`[ordered]@{}` collapses `azrepos:org/O365Exchange` into `azrepos:org/o365exchange`, merging two credential contexts).
 - **Docs** — bilingual mkdocs-material (`docs/X.md` + `docs/X.zh-TW.md`), deployed to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/docs.yml`. `docs/rationale.md` records the design choices (scoop > Chocolatey, starship > oh-my-posh, pwsh > cmd, native pwsh tree > ported shell layer).
 - **CI** — `.github/workflows/windows.yml` on `windows-latest` is the real gate: PSScriptAnalyzer, non-interactive `chezmoi init --apply`, render+parse of every `.ps1.tmpl`, and Pester.
 
 ## Conventions & hard invariants
 
 1. **A new/renamed init prompt must update the CI flags in the same commit.** `chezmoi init --promptBool/--promptChoice "<text>=value"` matches the prompt's exact TEXT (3rd arg to `promptXOnce` in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`), used non-interactively by `.github/workflows/windows.yml`. Forget it → CI's init hangs/EOFs (`error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF`; this broke three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds` was added). Corollary: **never put `=` in a prompt's text** — the `name=value` parser splits on the first `=` (this broke the `role` prompt once). Enforced by `tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` (missing flag, stale flag, wrong flag kind, `=` in text), which CI runs *before* `chezmoi init` so the failure names the missing flag instead of EOF-ing — run `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` locally after touching either file.
 2. **Run-scripts must never abort the apply.** The installer + editor/terminal/backup/skill scripts use `$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'` (+ `PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$false`), collect failures via `Register-Failure`, print a summary, and exit 0. One bad scoop/winget manifest (e.g. btop's stale `.conf`) must not stop the rest.
 3. **Preserve raw escapes when authoring config with control chars.** Alacritty CSI-u (`[…u`), VSCode `sendSequence`, tv `\t` — hand-typing tends to drop them. Generate via a throwaway Python script and re-parse (`tomllib` / `json`) to confirm the escape landed.
 4. **tv channel commands are `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "…"` inside TOML literal (`'''…'''`) strings** — runs regardless of tv's shell, sidesteps nested-quote escaping; placeholders `{split: :0}` (space) / `{split:\t:0}` (tab). tv reads config from `%APPDATA%\television\` on Windows.
 5. **Editors use a run_onchange pwsh merger, not `modify_`** (`modify_` interpreter selection is unreliable on Windows). Overlay sources live in `editors/` (chezmoi-ignored, embedded via `{{ include }}`).
 6. **The agent skill body lives once** in `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`; both `dot_agents/skills/dotfiles-windows/SKILL.md.tmpl` and `dot_claude/skills/dotfiles-windows/SKILL.md.tmpl` render it via `{{ "{{" }} template … {{ "}}" }}` → real files at `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/`. Edit the shared template, not the two one-line renderers (no symlink/junction — those need elevation/Developer Mode on Windows).
 7. **PSScriptAnalyzer exclusions are intentional** (`PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1`): hyphenated command names, `Write-Host`, `Invoke-Expression` for tool init, no-BOM UTF-8. Don't "fix" these; do fix real Errors.
 
 ### Cross-file mirrors (same commit)
 
 - New installer tool → `docs/tools.md` **and** `docs/tools.zh-TW.md`.
 - New init prompt → `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `windows.yml` flags + `docs/setup.md`/`setup.zh-TW.md` tables + the "What's enabled" block in `.chezmoitemplates/dotfiles-windows-skill.md`.
 - New `docs/**/*.md` → its `.zh-TW.md` twin + `nav` + `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`; `just docs-build` must stay green.
 - Any edit under `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` → copy the file verbatim into the parent repo's `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` (`chezmoi source-path` there, usually `~/.local/share/chezmoi`). They must stay byte-identical; verify with `diff -r`. Frontend-only changes (`weasel.custom.yaml`) do **not** cross over.
 - `core.autocrlf = input` has **two writers** — `bootstrap.ps1` (runs before chezmoi exists, so scoop's first bucket clone is protected) and `.chezmoitemplates/git/gitconfig` (the managed baseline). Change one → change the other.
 
 ### `scripts/*.sh` are wrappers, not implementations
 
 `scripts/{add-todo,todo-kanban,promote-todo,sweep-inbox}.sh` are byte-identical
 three-line shims. The real code is vendored at
 `.agents/skills/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/<same-name>.sh`, and each
 wrapper derives its target from `$0`, so adding a new helper only needs a copy
```

_**User (2026-08-20 04:56:56Z)**_

Review target: `Review the current uncommitted HUD/SpecStory implementation for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups. Apply only safe quality improvements; preserve behavior and tests. Do not touch existing .specstory artifacts or the unrelated Codex baseline issue.`

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).
